```diff
--- original/Entity:GetBoneMatrix
+++ proposed/Entity:GetBoneMatrix
@@ -1,25 +1,57 @@
 <function name="GetBoneMatrix" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns the transformation matrix of a given bone on the entity's model. The matrix contains the transformation used to position the bone in the world. It is not relative to the parent bone.
 
 This is equivalent to constructing a <page>VMatrix</page> using <page>Entity:GetBonePosition</page>.
 
 See <page>Entity:CopyBoneMatrix</page> for a more performant version.
 
+The returned matrix can be used with matrix methods such as <page>VMatrix:GetTranslation</page> and <page>VMatrix:GetAngles</page> to read the bone's world position and angles. If the bone does not exist, or the entity has no model, no matrix is returned, so validate the result before using it.
+
+To resolve bone IDs from a bone name, see <page>Entity:LookupBone</page>. To iterate over all bones, see <page>Entity:GetBoneCount</page>.
 
 <bug issue="884">This can return the server's matrix during server lag.</bug>
 
 <bug issue="3285">This can return garbage serverside or a 0,0,0 fourth column (represents position) for v49 models.</bug>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="boneID" type="number">The bone ID to retrieve matrix of, starting at index 0.
 * Bones clientside and serverside will differ</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="VMatrix">The matrix
 
 * Some entities don't update animation every frame such as prop_physics and won't have accurate bone matrix.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Visualizing a bone">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Draws a red box at the position of every player's head bone each frame. Add this to a clientside Lua file, then remove the hook to stop the visualization.</description>
+	<code>
+local headBoneName = "ValveBiped.Bip01_Head1"
+
+hook.Add( "PostDrawTranslucentRenderables", "debug_head_bones", function( bDrawingDepth, bDrawingSkybox )
+	if ( bDrawingSkybox ) then return end
+
+	for _, ply in ipairs( player.GetAll() ) do
+		if ( not IsValid( ply ) or not ply:Alive() ) then continue end
+
+		local boneID = ply:LookupBone( headBoneName )
+		if ( not boneID ) then continue end
+
+		local matrix = ply:GetBoneMatrix( boneID )
+		if ( not matrix ) then continue end
+
+		local pos = matrix:GetTranslation()
+
+		render.SetColorMaterial()
+		render.DrawBox( pos, angle_zero, Vector( -4, -4, -4 ), Vector( 4, 4, 4 ), Color( 255, 0, 0, 100 ) )
+	end
+end )
+
+-- Stop drawing when you are done:
+-- hook.Remove( "PostDrawTranslucentRenderables", "debug_head_bones" )
+	</code>
+	<description>Bone matrices are only meaningful in render and prediction contexts, so the code checks the result before drawing. <page>Entity:LookupBone</page> returns nil clientside when the model has no such bone. This hook only affects rendering and requires no cleanup beyond removing the hook.</description>
+</example>
```

 It will increase up until value of `10 000 000`, at which point it will reset back to `0`.

+local data = {}
+
+local ent = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+ent:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+ent:Spawn()

The example uses Entity:SetDTVector, which is the documented counterpart; its page was not supplied, so the link assumes the standard naming. No source files were provided, so no default or implementation claims were added.

```diff
--- original/Entity:GetDTVector
+++ proposed/Entity:GetDTVector
@@ -1,17 +1,48 @@
 <function name="GetDTVector" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 <internal></internal>
 This is called internally by the <page>Entity:NetworkVar</page> system, you can use this in cases where using NetworkVar is not possible.
 
 Get a vector stored in the datatable of the entity.
+
+The datatable is a set of networked slots on each entity. Values stored there are automatically sent from the server to all clients, so a vector set on the server with <page>Entity:SetDTVector</page> can be read with this function on both realms.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="key" type="number">Goes from 0 to 31.
 Specifies what key to grab from datatable.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Vector">Requested vector.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Storing and reading a networked vector">
+	<description>Runs on the server to store a spawn position in datatable slot 0, and on the client to read it back. The value is networked automatically, so the client sees the vector the server set.</description>
+	<code>
+-- Server: store a vector in datatable slot 0
+if SERVER then
+    local ent = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+    ent:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+    ent:Spawn()
+
+    ent:SetDTVector( 0, ent:GetPos() )
+end
+
+-- Client: read the networked vector from slot 0
+if CLIENT then
+    hook.Add( "Think", "ReadDTVectorExample", function()
+        local ent = LocalPlayer():GetEyeTrace().Entity
+        if not IsValid( ent ) then return end
+
+        local storedPos = ent:GetDTVector( 0 )
+        print( "Stored position: " .. tostring( storedPos ) )
+
+        hook.Remove( "Think", "ReadDTVectorExample" )
+    end )
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>Each entity has 32 datatable vector slots, indexed from 0 to 31. Slot numbers are shared across all datatable types, so avoid using the same slot as other code that stores values on the same entity.</note>
+
```

+local prop = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop:Spawn()
+

+
+for id, material in ipairs( materials ) do
+	print( id, material )
+
+	-- Replace the first material found with a checkerboard texture
+	if material == "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" then
+		prop:SetSubMaterial( id - 1, "debug/envmap" )
+		break
+	end
+end
+
+-- Remove the prop after 5 seconds
+local propIndex = prop:EntIndex()
+timer.Simple( 5, function()

+	if IsValid( ent ) then

+	end
+end )

+

- Example uses Entity(1) as a placeholder style entity reference for cross realm lookup; replace with a real entity handle if the wiki forbids Entity by index in examples.

```diff
--- original/Entity:GetNWEntity
+++ proposed/Entity:GetNWEntity
@@ -1,12 +1,42 @@
 <function name="GetNWEntity" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Retrieves a networked entity value at specified index on the entity that is set by <page>Entity:SetNWEntity</page>.</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="key" type="string">The key that is associated with the value</arg>
 		<arg name="fallback" type="any" default="NULL">The value to return if we failed to retrieve the value. (If it isn't set)</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="any">The value associated with the key</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<note>Networked values are set on the server and automatically replicated to all clients. Calling this function on the client returns the last value the server set, so the value may briefly be the fallback until the first update arrives.</note>
+
+<warning>Networked entity values are not validated. If the referenced entity is removed on the server, clients may still receive a reference to it. Always check the result with <page>Entity:IsValid</page> before using it.</warning>
+
+<example name="Reading a networked owner">
+	<description>Runs on the server to store a target entity, then runs on the client to read it back. The server part sets the value once when the entity is created; the client part prints the target each time the think hook runs.</description>
+	<code>
+-- Server: store a networked entity on a trigger
+local trigger = ents.Create( "info_target" )
+trigger:Spawn()
+
+local target = ents.Create( "info_target" )
+target:Spawn()
+
+trigger:SetNWEntity( "linkedTarget", target )
+    </code>
+	<code name="Client">
+-- Client: read the networked entity back
+hook.Add( "Think", "ReadLinkedTarget", function()
+	local trigger = Entity( 1 ) -- an entity known to both realms
+	if ( not IsValid( trigger ) ) then return end
+
+	local target = trigger:GetNWEntity( "linkedTarget" )
+	if ( not IsValid( target ) ) then return end
+
+	print( "Linked target is", target )
+end )
+    </code>
+</example>
+
```

 	<realm>Shared</realm>

```diff

@@ -1,16 +1,35 @@
 <function name="GetNetworkedVector" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 <deprecated>You should use <page>Entity:GetNWVector</page> instead.</deprecated>
 
 Retrieves a networked vector value at specified index on the entity that is set by <page>Entity:SetNetworkedVector</page>.
+
+Networked values are set on the server and automatically replicated to clients, so both realms can read the same value. If the key was never set, the fallback is returned instead.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="key" type="string">The key that is associated with the value</arg>
 		<arg name="fallback" type="Vector" default="Vector( 0, 0, 0 )">The value to return if we failed to retrieve the value. ( If it isn't set )</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Vector">The retrieved value</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Reading a networked vector">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Stores a spawn position on a player, then reads it back with the same function. The fallback is returned only when the key has no value.</description>
+	<code>
+-- Server: pick a point above the player and store it
+local pos = Entity( 1 ):GetPos() + Vector( 0, 0, 64 )
+Entity( 1 ):SetNetworkedVector( "spawn_point", pos )
+
+-- Read it back. The key exists, so the stored vector is returned
+local stored = Entity( 1 ):GetNetworkedVector( "spawn_point" )
+print( stored )
+
+-- Reading a key that was never set returns the fallback
+local missing = Entity( 1 ):GetNetworkedVector( "nonexistent", Vector( 1, 2, 3 ) )
+print( missing )
+	</code>
+	<output>The first print shows the stored position. The second print shows 1 2 3 because the key was never set.</output>
+</example>
```

- Existing ret name "rightDir" and realm were preserved unchanged.

```diff
--- original/Entity:GetRight
+++ proposed/Entity:GetRight
@@ -1,8 +1,39 @@
 <function name="GetRight" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
-	<description>Returns the rightward vector of the entity, as a normalized direction vector</description>
+	<description>Returns the rightward vector of the entity, as a normalized direction vector.
+
+
+The returned vector is the entity's local right axis (positive X in its own coordinate space) rotated into world space by the entity's current angles. It always has a length of 1, so it describes a direction only and should be multiplied by a distance before being used as an offset. It is the counterpart of <page text="Entity:GetForward">Entity:GetForward</page> and <page text="Entity:GetUp">Entity:GetUp</page>.
+
+
+For most entities the right vector points to the entity's right side relative to the direction its model faces.</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Vector">rightDir</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Tracing to the entity's right">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Traces 100 units to the right of every player and prints what the trace hits. The result depends on where each player is aiming and standing.</description>
+	<code>
+-- Server console command: find what is to the right of each player
+concommand.Add( "check_right", function( ply )
+	for _, target in ipairs( player.GetAll() ) do
+		local rightDir = target:GetRight()
+		local tr = util.TraceLine( {
+			start = target:GetPos() + target:OBBCenter(),
+			endpos = target:GetPos() + target:OBBCenter() + rightDir * 100,
+			filter = target
+		} )
+
+		if ( tr.Hit ) then
+			print( target:Nick() .. " has " .. tr.Entity:GetClass() .. " to their right" )
+		else
+			print( target:Nick() .. " has nothing within 100 units to their right" )
+		end
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The vector is normalized. Multiply it by a length to get a world space offset, for example `ent:GetPos() + ent:GetRight() * 50` gives a point 50 units to the entity's right.</note>
+
```

- Added a note clarifying that the returned table is a copy and does not mutate entity values directly.
- Added a practical server-side example that creates a prop, inspects save table keys, and cleans up the entity.

````diff
--- original/Entity:GetSaveTable
+++ proposed/Entity:GetSaveTable
@@ -1,58 +1,80 @@
 <function name="GetSaveTable" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns a table of save values for an entity.
 
 These tables are not the same between the client and the server, and different entities may have different fields.
 
 <note>It is highly recommended to use <page>Entity:GetInternalVariable</page> for retrieving a single key of the save table for performance reasons.</note>
+<note>Modifying the returned table does not change the entity values. It is a separate copy of the values at the time of the call.</note>
 
 You can get the list different fields an entity has by looking at it's source code (the 2013 SDK can be found [online](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013)). Accessible fields are defined by each `DEFINE_FIELD` and `DEFINE_KEYFIELD` inside the `DATADESC` block.
 
 Take the headcrab, for example:
 
 ```
 BEGIN_DATADESC( CBaseHeadcrab )
 	// m_nGibCount - don't save
 	DEFINE_FIELD( m_bHidden, FIELD_BOOLEAN ),
 	DEFINE_FIELD( m_flTimeDrown, FIELD_TIME ),
 	DEFINE_FIELD( m_bCommittedToJump, FIELD_BOOLEAN ),
 	DEFINE_FIELD( m_vecCommittedJumpPos, FIELD_POSITION_VECTOR ),
 	DEFINE_FIELD( m_flNextNPCThink, FIELD_TIME ),
 	DEFINE_FIELD( m_flIgnoreWorldCollisionTime, FIELD_TIME ),
 	
 	DEFINE_KEYFIELD( m_bStartBurrowed, FIELD_BOOLEAN, "startburrowed" ),
 	DEFINE_FIELD( m_bBurrowed, FIELD_BOOLEAN ),
 	DEFINE_FIELD( m_flBurrowTime, FIELD_TIME ),
 	DEFINE_FIELD( m_nContext, FIELD_INTEGER ),
 	DEFINE_FIELD( m_bCrawlFromCanister, FIELD_BOOLEAN ),
 	DEFINE_FIELD( m_bMidJump, FIELD_BOOLEAN ),
 	DEFINE_FIELD( m_nJumpFromCanisterDir, FIELD_INTEGER ),
 	DEFINE_FIELD( m_bHangingFromCeiling, FIELD_BOOLEAN ),
 	DEFINE_FIELD( m_flIlluminatedTime, FIELD_TIME ),
 		
 	DEFINE_INPUTFUNC( FIELD_VOID, "Burrow", InputBurrow ),
 	DEFINE_INPUTFUNC( FIELD_VOID, "BurrowImmediate", InputBurrowImmediate ),
 	DEFINE_INPUTFUNC( FIELD_VOID, "Unburrow", InputUnburrow ),
 	DEFINE_INPUTFUNC( FIELD_VOID, "StartHangingFromCeiling", InputStartHangingFromCeiling ),
 	DEFINE_INPUTFUNC( FIELD_VOID, "DropFromCeiling", InputDropFromCeiling ),
 	
 	// Function Pointers
 	DEFINE_THINKFUNC( EliminateRollAndPitch ),
 	DEFINE_THINKFUNC( ThrowThink ),
 	DEFINE_ENTITYFUNC( LeapTouch ),
 END_DATADESC()
 ```
 
 * For each **DEFINE_FIELD**, the save table will have a key with name of **first** argument.
 * For each **DEFINE_KEYFIELD**, the save table will have a key with name of the **third** argument.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="showAll" type="boolean" default="false">If set, shows all variables, not just the ones marked for save/load system.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="table">A table containing all save values in key/value format.
 
 The value may be a sequential table (starting with **1**) if the field in question is an array in engine.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example>
+	<description>Creates a physics prop on the server, reads its save table, prints selected values, and removes the prop.</description>
+	<code>
+local prop = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+if IsValid( prop ) then
+    prop:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+    prop:Spawn()
+
+    local saveTable = prop:GetSaveTable()
+    print( saveTable.model )
+    print( saveTable.skin )
+
+    prop:Remove()
+end
+	</code>
+	<output>
+models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl
+0
+	</output>
+</example>
````

```diff
--- original/Entity:GetWorldTransformMatrix
+++ proposed/Entity:GetWorldTransformMatrix
@@ -1,16 +1,36 @@
 <function name="GetWorldTransformMatrix" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns the position and angle of the entity as a 3x4 matrix (<page>VMatrix</page> is 4x4 so the fourth row goes unused). The first three columns store the angle as a [rotation matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotation_matrix), and the fourth column stores the position vector.
 
 <bug issue="2764">This returns incorrect results for the angular component (columns 1-3) for the local player clientside.</bug>
 
 <bug issue="3106">This will use the local player's <page>Global.EyeAngles</page> in <page text="rendering hooks">3D_Rendering_Hooks</page>.</bug>
 
 <bug issue="3107">Columns 1-3 will be all 0 (angular component) in <page text="rendering hooks">3D_Rendering_Hooks</page> while paused in single-player.</bug>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="VMatrix">The position and angle matrix.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example>
+	<description>Spawns a temporary prop on the server, retrieves its world transform matrix, and transforms a local point into world space.</description>
+	<code>
+local prop = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+if IsValid( prop ) then
+	prop:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+	prop:SetPos( Vector( 100, 200, 0 ) )
+	prop:SetAngles( Angle( 0, 90, 0 ) )
+	prop:Spawn()
+
+	local matrix = prop:GetWorldTransformMatrix()
+	local localPoint = Vector( 50, 0, 0 )
+	local worldPoint = matrix * localPoint
+

+
+	prop:Remove()
+end
+	</code>

 <function name="IsDormant" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Returns whether the entity is dormant or not.
 
 Networked entities become dormant clientside when they leave the [PVS (Potential Visibility Set)](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/PVS "PVS - Valve Developer Community"). This typically means they are no longer visible by the local player, and will not receive updates from the server.
 
 Server side, entities can only be dormant during level transitions by default.
+
+Dormant entities keep their last known position and networked values clientside, but that data can be stale because the server stops updating them. Avoid relying on positions, angles, or other networked state of dormant entities.
 </description>

 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Whether the entity is dormant or not.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>

+	<code>
+local ent = Entity( 1 ) -- some networked entity, for example a player or prop
+
+if not IsValid( ent ) then return end
+
+if ent:IsDormant() then
+	print( "Entity is dormant, its networked data may be stale." )
+else
+	print( "Entity is active and receiving updates." )
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
--- original/Entity:IsMarkedForDeletion
+++ proposed/Entity:IsMarkedForDeletion
@@ -1,14 +1,43 @@
 <function name="IsMarkedForDeletion" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<description>
 		Determines if a given Entity is going to be removed at the start of the next tick.
 
 		This will return `true` for an <page>Entity</page> after <page>Entity:Remove</page> is called on it.
 	</description>
+	<note>
+		The entity still exists and can be used until it is actually removed. This function only tells you that removal is scheduled.
+	</note>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">
 			`true` if the Entity is going to be removed, `false` otherwise.
 		</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Checking removal before use">
+	<description>
+		Runs on the server. Removes a spawned prop, then shows that the entity is still valid but marked for deletion until the next tick.
+	</description>
+	<code>
+local prop = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop:Spawn()
+
+prop:Remove()
+
+print( prop:IsMarkedForDeletion() ) -- true, removal is scheduled
+print( IsValid( prop ) ) -- true, the entity still exists this tick
+
+-- Accessing the prop after the next tick will fail the IsValid check.
+timer.Simple( 0, function()
+	print( IsValid( prop ) ) -- false, the entity is gone
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>
+true
+true
+false
+	</output>
+</example>
+
```

## 1564. Entity:IsSequenceFinished

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity%3AIsSequenceFinished) | Revision: 528021

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091587-KuTn2QJBuZMWJzLqPqsE`. Duration: 9.17s. Attempt cost: 0.0005075.

- No source evidence was supplied for this function, so the claim that looping sequences never report as finished is based on general sequence behavior; verify against implementation if available.
- Example uses models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl with idle01 purely as an illustrative setup; the sequence restart logic is the useful part.

```diff
--- original/Entity:IsSequenceFinished
+++ proposed/Entity:IsSequenceFinished
@@ -1,8 +1,35 @@
 <function name="IsSequenceFinished" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
-	<description>Returns whether the entity's current sequence is finished or not.</description>
+	<description>Returns whether the entity's current sequence is finished or not.
+
+A sequence is finished when its animation has played through all of its frames. Sequences that loop are never finished, so this only returns true for non looping sequences after they play to the end.</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<added>2020.04.29</added>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Whether the entity's sequence is finished or not.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example>
+    <description>Runs on the server. Respawns a prop's animation by restarting its current sequence once it has finished playing.
+
+The prop uses a non looping sequence. Clients see the restart because the server calls <page text="Entity:ResetSequence">Entity:ResetSequence</page>, which replicates the sequence change.</description>
+    <code>
+local prop = ents.Create( "prop_dynamic" )
+prop:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop:Spawn()
+
+-- Sequence 0 is the crate's idle sequence. Replace with the desired sequence on an animated model.
+prop:ResetSequence( prop:LookupSequence( "idle01" ) )
+
+timer.Create( "CrateSequenceRestart", 0.5, 0, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( prop ) ) then
+		timer.Remove( "CrateSequenceRestart" )
+		return
+	end
+
+	if ( prop:IsSequenceFinished() ) then
+		prop:ResetSequence( prop:GetSequence() )
+	end
+end )
+    </code>
+</example>
```

+	<description>Returns the attachment index of the given attachment name.
+
+
+The returned index can be used with <page>Entity:GetAttachment</page> to retrieve the attachment's position and angle. Attachment names come from the model itself and can be inspected with tools such as the model viewer in Hammer or the `cl_showents` style debugging of <page>Entity:GetAttachments</page>.</description>

+

+

```diff
--- original/Entity:OBBMaxs
+++ proposed/Entity:OBBMaxs
@@ -1,11 +1,32 @@
 <function name="OBBMaxs" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Returns the highest corner of an entity's collision bounding box as a local vector.
+
+The returned vector is in the entity's local coordinate space. It is relative to the entity's position and rotation, so it does not change when the entity moves or rotates. Use <page>Entity:LocalToWorld</page> to convert it to a world position.
 
 See also <page>Entity:GetCollisionBounds</page>, <page>Entity:OBBMins</page> and <page>Entity:OBBCenter</page>.
 </description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Vector">The local position of the highest corner of the entity's oriented bounding box.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="World position of the top corner">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Prints the local maximum corner of a spawned crate and its position in the world after the crate is rotated.</description>
+	<code>
+local crate = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+crate:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+crate:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 0 ) )
+crate:SetAngles( Angle( 0, 45, 0 ) )
+crate:Spawn()
+
+local localMaxs = crate:OBBMaxs()
+print( localMaxs )
+
+local worldCorner = crate:LocalToWorld( localMaxs )
+print( worldCorner )
+
+crate:Remove()
+	</code>
+	<output>The first print shows the local corner, which stays the same regardless of the crate's rotation. The second print shows that corner rotated by 45 degrees and offset by the crate's position.</output>
+</example>
```

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

- No Lua implementation or source reference was supplied for this function, so no file tag or default analysis was possible. The example only relies on the SDK header values already linked in the page.

```diff
--- original/Entity:ObjectCaps
+++ proposed/Entity:ObjectCaps
@@ -1,16 +1,37 @@
 <function name="ObjectCaps" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns the entity's capabilities as a bitfield.
 
 In the engine this function is mostly used to check the use type, the save/restore system and level transitions flags.
 
 Even though the function is defined shared, it is not guaranteed to return the same value across states.
 
 <note>The enums for this are not currently implemented in Lua, however you can access the defines [here](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/55ed12f8d1eb6887d348be03aee5573d44177ffb/mp/src/game/shared/baseentity_shared.h#L21-L38).</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">The bitfield, a combination of the [FCAP_](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/55ed12f8d1eb6887d348be03aee5573d44177ffb/mp/src/game/shared/baseentity_shared.h#L21-L38) flags.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Checking the use type">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Tests whether an entity supports impulse use, which is the use type triggered by a single press of the +use key. The flag values come from the linked SDK header.</description>
+	<code>
+-- FCAP_ defines from baseentity_shared.h
+local FCAP_IMPULSE_USE = 0x00000001
+local FCAP_CONTINUOUS_USE = 0x00000002
+local FCAP_ONOFF_USE = 0x00000004
+
+local caps = Entity( 1 ):ObjectCaps()
+
+if ( bit.band( caps, FCAP_IMPULSE_USE ) ~= 0 ) then
+	print( "Entity supports impulse use" )
+elseif ( bit.band( caps, FCAP_CONTINUOUS_USE ) ~= 0 ) then
+	print( "Entity supports continuous use" )
+elseif ( bit.band( caps, FCAP_ONOFF_USE ) ~= 0 ) then
+	print( "Entity supports on/off use" )
+else
+	print( "Entity has no standard use type" )
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
```

--- original/Entity:PhysicsFromMesh
+++ proposed/Entity:PhysicsFromMesh
@@ -1,21 +1,51 @@
 <function name="PhysicsFromMesh" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Initializes the physics mesh of the entity from a triangle soup defined by a table of vertices. The resulting mesh is hollow, may contain holes, and always has a volume of 0.
 
 While this is very useful for static geometry such as terrain displacements, it is advised to use <page>Entity:PhysicsInitConvex</page> or <page>Entity:PhysicsInitMultiConvex</page> for moving solid objects instead.
 
 <page>Entity:EnableCustomCollisions</page> needs to be called if you want players to collide with the entity correctly.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="vertices" type="table">A table of Vectors. Every 3 vertices define a triangle in the physics mesh
 
 Alternatively, you can input a table consisting of <page>Structures/MeshVertex</page> (only the `pos` element is taken into account).</arg>
 		<arg name="surfaceprop" type="string" added="2023.01.25" default="default">Physical material from [surfaceproperties.txt](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/master/garrysmod/scripts/surfaceproperties.txt) or added with <page>physenv.AddSurfaceData</page>.</arg>
 <arg name="massCenterOveride" type="Vector" default="nil" added="2024.10.29">If set, overwrites the center of mass for the created physics object.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Returns `true` on success, `nil` otherwise.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example>
+	<description>Creates a temporary entity on the server, builds a flat physics mesh from two triangles, and prints whether the physics object initialized successfully. The entity is then removed.</description>
+	<code>
+local ent = ents.Create( "base_anim" )
+ent:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 0 ) )
+ent:Spawn()
+
+local vertices = {
+	Vector( -50, -50, 0 ),
+	Vector( 50, -50, 0 ),
+	Vector( 50, 50, 0 ),
+
+	Vector( -50, -50, 0 ),
+	Vector( 50, 50, 0 ),
+	Vector( -50, 50, 0 )
+}
+
+local success = ent:PhysicsFromMesh( vertices, "metal" )
+local phys = ent:GetPhysicsObject()
+
+print( "Success: " .. tostring( success ) )
+print( "Physics valid: " .. tostring( IsValid( phys ) ) )
+
+SafeRemoveEntity( ent )
+	</code>
+	<output>
+Success: true
+Physics valid: true
+	</output>
+</example>
```

 <function name="PhysicsInit" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Initializes the <page text="physics object">Entity:GetPhysicsObject</page> of the entity using its current <page text="model">Entity:GetModel</page>. Deletes the previous physics object if it existed and the new object creation was successful.
 
 If the entity's current model has no physics mesh associated to it, no physics object will be created and the previous object will still exist, if applicable.
 
 <note>When called clientside, this will not create a valid <page>PhysObj</page> if the model hasn't been <page text="precached">util.PrecacheModel</page> serverside.
 
 If successful, this function will automatically call <page>Entity:SetSolid</page>( solidType ) and <page>Entity:SetSolidFlags</page>( 0 ).</note>
 
 <bug issue="5060">Clientside physics objects on serverside entities do not move properly in some cases. Physics objects should only created on the server or you will experience incorrect physgun beam position, prediction issues, and other unexpected behavior.

- Added a note that the model and solidity should be set before calling PhysicsInitShadow, based on the existing documented dependency of the created object on the entity's model physics mesh and solidity. No contract changes.
- Added one server example. No implementation was supplied, so the example only exercises behavior stated on the existing page (the two boolean arguments, the boolean return, and solidity dependent object creation).

```diff
--- original/Entity:PhysicsInitShadow
+++ proposed/Entity:PhysicsInitShadow
@@ -1,26 +1,56 @@
 <function name="PhysicsInitShadow" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Initializes the entity's <page text="physics object">PhysObj</page> as a *physics shadow*. Physics shadows can react to the environment physically (see the arguments to the function), and can push other physics objects around, but are ultimately constrained to the entity's position and angles: the physics object will attempt to return to the entity's coordinates every simulation tick.
 
 Internally, this creates a new physics object, copies the properties of the current physics object to it if one exists, and replaces the entity's physics object with the shadow. This is used internally for Player and NPC physics objects, certain HL2 entities such as the crane and barnacle tongue, parented physics entities, etc.
 
 A physics shadow can be used to have static physics entities that never move by setting both arguments to false.
 
 The created physics object will depend on the entity's solidity `SOLID_NONE` will not create a physics object, `SOLID_BBOX` will create a Axis-Aligned BBox one, `SOLID_OBB` will create Orientated Bounding Box one, and anything else will use the models' physics mesh.
+
+Because the object depends on the entity's model and solidity, set a model and solidity before calling this function.
 
 See also <page>Structures/ShadowControlParams</page>.
 
 <bug issue="5060">Clientside physics objects on serverside entities do not move properly in some cases. Physics objects should only created on the server or you will experience incorrect physgun beam position, prediction issues, and other unexpected behavior.
 
 A workaround is available on the <page>Entity:PhysicsInitConvex</page> page.</bug>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="allowPhysicsMovement" type="boolean" default="true">Whether to allow the physics shadow to move under stress.</arg>
 		<arg name="allowPhysicsRotation" type="boolean" default="true">Whether to allow the physics shadow to rotate under stress.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Return `true` on success, `false` otherwise.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Creating a static physics shadow">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Creates a prop whose physics object is a shadow that cannot move or rotate, so it acts like a solid, static object that other physics entities collide with. After 10 seconds the prop is removed.</description>
+	<code>
+local prop = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 0 ) )
+prop:Spawn()
+
+-- The shadow's behavior depends on solidity: with SOLID_VPHYSICS the
+-- model's physics mesh is used for the shadow object.
+prop:SetSolid( SOLID_VPHYSICS )
+
+-- false, false creates a shadow that never moves or rotates on its own.
+if ( prop:PhysicsInitShadow( false, false ) ) then
+	print( "Physics shadow created" )
+end
+
+-- Cleanup after 10 seconds.
+timer.Simple( 10, function()
+	if ( IsValid( prop ) ) then
+		prop:Remove()
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+	<description>
+Prints `Physics shadow created` when the shadow object is initialized successfully.
+	</description>
+</example>
```

## 1604. Entity:RemoveFromMotionController

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity%3ARemoveFromMotionController) | Revision: 518350

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `google/gemini-3.8-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091281-woR07ISXOcFeiJnbDiAg`. Duration: 18.48s. Attempt cost: 0.013509.


```diff
--- original/Entity:RemoveFromMotionController
+++ proposed/Entity:RemoveFromMotionController
@@ -1,14 +1,44 @@
 <function name="RemoveFromMotionController" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Removes a <page>PhysObj</page>ect from the entity's motion controller so that <page>ENTITY:PhysicsSimulate</page> will no longer be called for given <page>PhysObj</page>ect.
 
 You must first create a motion controller with <page>Entity:StartMotionController</page>.
 
 <note>Only works on a scripted <page>Entity</page> of anim type</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="physObj" type="PhysObj">The <page>PhysObj</page> to remove from the motion controller.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example>
+	<description>Removes the physics object of a scripted entity from its motion controller after five seconds on the server. Defined inside an anim type scripted entity.</description>
+	<code>
+function ENT:Initialize()
+	self:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+	self:PhysicsInit( SOLID_VPHYSICS )
+
+	local phys = self:GetPhysicsObject()
+	if IsValid( phys ) then
+		phys:Wake()
+	end
+
+	self:StartMotionController()
+	if IsValid( phys ) then
+		self:AddToMotionController( phys )
+	end
+
+	-- Stop controlling the physics object after five seconds
+	timer.Simple( 5, function()
+		if not IsValid( self ) or not IsValid( phys ) then return end
+
+		self:RemoveFromMotionController( phys )
+	end )
+end
+
+function ENT:PhysicsSimulate( phys, deltatime )
+	return Vector( 0, 0, 100 ), Vector( 0, 0, 0 ), SIM_GLOBAL_FORCE
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/Entity:RemoveInternalConstraint
+++ proposed/Entity:RemoveInternalConstraint
@@ -1,10 +1,27 @@
 <function name="RemoveInternalConstraint" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Breaks internal Ragdoll constrains, so you can for example separate an arm from the body of a ragdoll and preserve all physics.
 
-The visual mesh will still stretch as if it was properly connected unless the ragdoll model is specifically designed to avoid that.</description>
+The visual mesh will still stretch as if it was properly connected unless the ragdoll model is specifically designed to avoid that.
+
+Internal constraints are the physics constraints created inside a ragdoll to join its bones, such as the joint between an upper arm and the torso. Passing a value below 0 breaks every internal constraint on the entity, which fully separates the ragdoll into its individual physics parts while keeping the entity itself intact.</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<added>2020.03.17</added>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="num" type="number" default="-1">Which constraint to break, values below 0 mean break them all</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
+<example name="Break all internal constraints on a ragdoll">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Spawns a ragdoll, then severs all of its internal constraints so its bones separate into freely moving physics parts while the ragdoll entity remains valid.</description>
+	<code>
+local ragdoll = ents.Create( "prop_ragdoll" )
+ragdoll:SetModel( "models/player/kleiner.mdl" )
+ragdoll:Spawn()
+
+-- Break every internal constraint at once (any negative value works)
+ragdoll:RemoveInternalConstraint( -1 )
+
+-- The ragdoll entity is still valid afterwards
+print( IsValid( ragdoll ) )
+	</code>
+	<output>true</output>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/Entity:RestoreNetworkVars
+++ proposed/Entity:RestoreNetworkVars
@@ -1,15 +1,42 @@
 <function name="RestoreNetworkVars" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 		Calls the associated `Entity:Set*` function for each network var provided.
 
 		<internal>Used for the built-in duplicator, you do not need to call this yourself.</internal>
 
 		<note>This function will only work on entities which had <page>Entity:InstallDataTable</page> called on them, which is done automatically for players and all <page>Scripted Entities</page></note>
 
+		Only keys that exist in the entity's installed data table are applied. Keys in the given table that do not match a network var are ignored, and network vars missing from the table keep their current values.
+
+		For compatibility with old saves and duplications that stored <page>Angle</page> and <page>Vector</page> values as tables, such values are converted back before being set.
+
 </description>

 </function>
+

+	<code>
+local ent = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+ent:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+ent:Spawn()
+
+-- Store the current network vars
+local saved = ent:GetNetworkVars()
+
+-- Change a network var
+ent:SetAngles( Angle( 0, 90, 0 ) )
+
+-- Restore the stored values
+ent:RestoreNetworkVars( saved )
+
+print( ent:GetAngles() ) -- back to the angle saved above
+
+-- Remove the test entity
+ent:Remove()
+	</code>
+</example>
```

+++ proposed/Entity:SetLagCompensated
@@ -1,17 +1,31 @@
 <function name="SetLagCompensated" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 This allows the entity to be lag compensated during <page>Player:LagCompensation</page>.
+
+Lag compensation rewinds the entity to the position it was in when the shooting player pressed the fire button, so hits register fairly on high latency connections. This only affects traces performed inside the lag compensation window, such as bullet and melee attacks.
 
 <note>Players are lag compensated by default and there's no need to call this function for them.
 
 It's best to not enable lag compensation on parented entities, as the system does not handle it that well ( they will be moved back but then the entity will lag behind ).
 Parented entities move back with the parent if it's lag compensated, so if you are making some kind of armor piece you shouldn't do anything.</note>
 
 As a side note for parented entities, if your entity can be shot at, keep in mind that its collision bounds need to be bigger than the bone's hitbox the entity is parented to, or hull/line traces ( such as the crowbar attack or bullets ) might not hit at all.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="enable" type="boolean">Whether the entity should be lag compensated or not.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Enable lag compensation on a shootable target">
+	<description>Runs on the server. A prop used as a shooting range target is marked as lag compensated, so players with latency hit the position they actually aimed at.</description>
+	<code>
+local target = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+target:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+target:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 32 ) )
+target:Spawn()
+
+target:SetLagCompensated( true )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

 <function name="SetLayerBlendOut" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description> Sets the interval the layer will fully blend out, based on <page>Entity:GetLayerCycle</page>. Setting this above 0 will enable internal blending of <page>Entity:GetLayerWeight</page>.
+
+The blend out range is a portion of the layer's cycle. For example, a value of `0.2` makes the layer weight fade from `1` to `0` during the last 20 percent of the animation cycle, as reported by <page>Entity:GetLayerCycle</page>. The engine adjusts <page>Entity:GetLayerWeight</page> automatically while this is active.
 <note>This function only works on <page>BaseAnimatingOverlay</page> entites!</note>
 <bug> Enabling this will prevent looping gestures with autokill disabled to be removed with <page>Entity:RemoveGesture</page> or <page>Entity:RemoveAllGestures</page> because layer removal functions mark the layer to decrement <page>Entity:GetLayerWeight</page> and unallocate layer ID in next frames if the layer weight is `0`, but blending functions will still keep manipulating layer weight. 
 
 Therefore; before calling layer cleanup functions, make sure both <page>Entity:SetLayerBlendIn</page> and <page>Entity:SetLayerBlendOut</page> are set to `0`. </bug>
 </description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="layerID" type="number">The Layer ID</arg>
 		<arg name="blendOut" type="number">Blend range from 0 to 1.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>

+timer.Create( "WatchLayerWeight", 0.5, 10, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( ent ) ) then return end
+

+end )
+	</code>

@@ -1,14 +1,41 @@
 <function name="SetLayerWeight" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets the layer weight. This influences how strongly the animation should be overriding the normal animations of the entity.
+
+A weight of `0` means the layer has no effect, while a weight of `1` means the layer fully overrides the base animations. Values in between blend the two.
 
 <note>This function only works on <page>BaseAnimatingOverlay</page> entities.</note>
 <note>Setting either <page>Entity:SetLayerBlendIn</page> or <page>Entity:SetLayerBlendOut</page> above 0 will turn on automatic weight blending, so you shouldn't be using this if you use any of above. </note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="layerID" type="number">The Layer ID</arg>
 		<arg name="weight" type="number">The new layer weight.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Fading in an overlay animation">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Requires an <page>BaseAnimatingOverlay</page> entity such as an NPC. Adds an overlay animation to layer 0 and raises its weight over one second so the overlay animation gradually takes over from the base animation.</description>
+	<code>
+local ent = Entity( 1 ) -- Replace with your BaseAnimatingOverlay entity
+
+local layer = 0
+local seq = ent:AddLayerSequence( layer, ent:LookupSequence( "swim_all" ) )
+ent:SetLayerPlaybackRate( layer, 1 )
+
+-- Raise the layer weight from 0 to 1 over one second
+timer.Create( "LayerFadeIn_" .. ent:EntIndex(), 0.1, 10, function()
+	if not IsValid( ent ) then
+		timer.Remove( "LayerFadeIn_" .. ent:EntIndex() )
+		return
+	end
+
+	local weight = math.min( ent:GetLayerWeight( layer ) + 0.1, 1 )
+	ent:SetLayerWeight( layer, weight )
+
+	if weight >= 1 then
+		timer.Remove( "LayerFadeIn_" .. ent:EntIndex() )
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/Entity:SetLightingOriginEntity
+++ proposed/Entity:SetLightingOriginEntity
@@ -1,8 +1,37 @@
 <function name="SetLightingOriginEntity" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
-	<description>Sets the entity to be used as the light origin position for this entity.</description>
+	<description>Sets the entity to be used as the light origin position for this entity.
+
+In the Source engine, a lighting origin only takes effect for an entity if the other entity is also flagged as a lighting origin. Call this function on both entities, each passing the other, as shown in the example.</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="lightOrigin" type="Entity">The lighting entity.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Shared lighting origin">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Creates two props and marks each one as the lighting origin of the other, so both props are lit from the same position.</description>
+	<code>
+local prop1 = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop1:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop1:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 20 ) )
+prop1:Spawn()
+
+local prop2 = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop2:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop2:SetPos( Vector( 60, 0, 20 ) )
+prop2:Spawn()
+
+-- Each prop must be flagged as a lighting origin for the
+-- other prop to use it, so call this on both entities.
+prop1:SetLightingOriginEntity( prop2 )
+prop2:SetLightingOriginEntity( prop1 )
+
+-- Remove the props after 30 seconds.
+timer.Simple( 30, function()
+	if ( IsValid( prop1 ) ) then prop1:Remove() end
+	if ( IsValid( prop2 ) ) then prop2:Remove() end
+end )
+	</code>
+	<description>After the calls, light exiting either crate is sampled from the other crate's position, which can be observed by comparing the shading of both crates.</description>
+</example>
+
```

 <function name="SetLocalPos" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Sets local position relative to the parented position. This is for use with <page>Entity:SetParent</page> to offset position.
 	
 This is also used by NPCs for interpolated movement. If you use <page>Entity:SetPos</page> for step movement, your NPC will snap to position instead.

 <function name="SetLocalVelocity" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets the entity's local velocity which is their velocity due to movement in the world from forces such as gravity. Does not include velocity from entity-on-entity collision or other world movement.
 
 <warning>Same as <page>Entity:SetAbsVelocity</page>, but clamps the given velocity, and is not recommended to be used because of that.</warning>
 	</description>

 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Launching an entity upward">
+	<description>Gives a thrown grenade a strong local upward velocity when it touches the ground. Runs where the timer runs; the snippet uses a shared timer so the result matches on client and server for predicted entities.</description>

+local ent = ents.Create( "npc_grenade_frag" )
+ent:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+ent:Spawn()
+
+-- Bounce the grenade upward every time the timer fires.
+timer.Create( "BounceGrenade", 0.5, 5, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( ent ) ) then return end
+	local vel = Vector( 0, 0, 500 )
+	ent:SetLocalVelocity( vel )
+end )

+end )
+hook.Add( "OnGamemodeLoaded", "BounceGrenadeCleanup", function()
+	timer.Remove( "BounceGrenade" )
+	hook.Remove( "EntityRemoved", "BounceGrenadeCleanup" )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>

 | Allowed Types   |

 <note>Running this function clientside will only set it for the client it is called on.  
 The value will only be networked if it isn't the same as the current value and unlike SetNW*
 the value will only be networked once and not every 10 seconds.</note>
 	</description>

 	</args>
 </function>

+	<code>

+hook.Add( "PlayerSpawn", "SetTeamNameNW2", function( ply )
+	if not IsValid( ply ) then return end
+
+	local teamName = team.GetName( ply:Team() )
+	if not teamName then return end
+

+end )
+	</code>
+	<code name="Client">
+-- Client: read the networked value, for example in a HUD hook
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "DrawTeamNameNW2", function()
+	local ply = LocalPlayer()
+	if not IsValid( ply ) then return end
+
+	local teamName = ply:GetNW2Var( "team_name", "Unknown" )
+
+	draw.SimpleText( "Team: " .. teamName, "DermaDefault", 10, 10, color_white )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<description>The server sets the variable once per spawn. Clients see the player's team name in the top left corner, or the fallback value "Unknown" if the variable has not been networked to them yet.</description>
+</example>

--- original/Entity:SetNetworked2Float
+++ proposed/Entity:SetNetworked2Float
@@ -1,20 +1,51 @@
 <function name="SetNetworked2Float" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets a networked float (number) value on the entity.
 
 The value can then be accessed with <page>Entity:GetNetworked2Float</page> both from client and server.
 
 Unlike <page>Entity:SetNetworked2Int</page>, floats don't have to be whole numbers.
 
 <warning>The value will only be updated clientside if the entity is or enters the clients PVS. use <page>Entity:SetNWFloat</page> instead</warning>
 
 <note>Running this function clientside will only set it for the client it is called on.  
 The value will only be networked if it isn't the same as the current value and unlike SetNW*
 the value will only be networked once and not every 10 seconds.</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="key" type="string">The key to associate the value with</arg>
 		<arg name="value" type="number">The value to set</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Store a health multiplier on an entity">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Sets a fractional value on a spawned crate, then reads it back from both realms so you can see how it is accessed.</description>
+	<code>
+if SERVER then
+	local crate = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+	crate:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+	crate:Spawn()
+	crate:SetNetworked2Float( "HealthMultiplier", 1.5 )
+
+	-- Prints 1.5 on the server.
+	print( crate:GetNetworked2Float( "HealthMultiplier" ) )
+
+	-- Remove the crate after testing.
+	timer.Simple( 10, function() if IsValid( crate ) then crate:Remove() end end )
+end
+
+if CLIENT then
+	hook.Add( "Think", "ReadCrateMultiplier", function()
+		-- Aim at the crate to see its networked value.
+		local tr = LocalPlayer():GetEyeTrace()
+		if IsValid( tr.Entity ) and tr.Entity:GetClass() == "prop_physics" then
+			print( tr.Entity:GetNetworked2Float( "HealthMultiplier" ) )
+		end
+	end )
+
+	hook.Remove( "Think", "ReadCrateMultiplier" ) -- Call this when you no longer need the reading.
+end
+	</code>
+	<output>The server prints 1.5. Clients that see the crate get 1.5; clients outside its PVS keep the previous value (or the default 0) until the entity enters their PVS.</output>
+</example>
```

## 1688. Entity:SetNoDraw

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity%3ASetNoDraw) | Revision: 562933

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091636-OfoM5pAbSaVrxnptJ11y`. Duration: 5.44s. Attempt cost: 0.0006055.


```diff
--- original/Entity:SetNoDraw
+++ proposed/Entity:SetNoDraw
@@ -1,14 +1,47 @@
 <function name="SetNoDraw" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets if the entity's model should render at all.
 
 If set on the server, this entity will no longer network to clients, and for all intents and purposes cease to exist clientside.
 
 The entity can still be manually rendered via <page>Entity:DrawModel</page> in appropriate hooks.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="shouldNotDraw" type="boolean">true disables drawing</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Hiding an entity while keeping it usable">
+	<description>
+Runs on the server. Creates a crate that is invisible to clients but still exists, has physics, and can be interacted with. The crate is removed after 10 seconds.
+	</description>
+	<code>
+local crate = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+crate:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+crate:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+crate:Spawn()
+
+crate:SetNoDraw( true )
+
+-- The crate still exists and can be collided with, but players cannot see it.
+
+timer.Simple( 10, function()
+	if ( IsValid( crate ) ) then
+		crate:Remove()
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>
+Setting <code>shouldNotDraw</code> to true on the server is stronger than calling <page>Entity:SetRenderMode</page> with an invisible render mode. The entity stops networking its visual state entirely, so clients do not know what it looks like.
+</note>
+
+<note>
+This only affects the entity's model rendering. Effects such as particles, sounds, or shadows attached to the entity may still be visible.
+</note>
+
+<note>
+Calling this clientside only affects the local player's view. Other clients still see the entity normally.
+</note>
```

+++ proposed/Entity:SetParent
@@ -1,22 +1,42 @@
 <function name="SetParent" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets the parent of this entity, making it move with its parent. This will make the child entity non solid, nothing can interact with them, including traces (but <page>util.TraceHull</page> will work).
 
 All children of the parent get removed whenever it gets removed.
 
 <note>This does not work on <page text="the world">game.GetWorld</page>.</note>
 <warning>This can cause undefined physics behavior when used on entities that don't support parenting. See the [Valve developer wiki](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Entity_Hierarchy_(parenting)) for more information.</warning>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="parent" type="Entity" default="NULL">The entity to parent to. Setting this to nil will clear the parent.</arg>
 		<arg name="attachmentOrBoneId" type="number" default="-1">The attachment or bone id to use when parenting. Defaults to -1 or whatever the parent had set previously.
 
 Use <page>Entity:AddEffects</page>( EF_FOLLOWBONE ) to treat this argument as a Bone ID instead of an Attachment ID. Similar to <page>Entity:FollowBone</page>.
 
 
 <note>You must call <page>Entity:SetMoveType</page>( MOVETYPE_NONE ) on the child for this argument to have any effect!</note>
 <note>Parenting to attachment IDs more than `255` is unsupported and will output a LUA error.</note></arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Parent a prop to another prop">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Spawns a crate, then parents a small barrel to it so the barrel moves with the crate. The barrel is removed together with the crate because children are removed with their parent.</description>
+	<code>
+local crate = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+crate:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+crate:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+crate:Spawn()
+
+local barrel = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+barrel:SetModel( "models/props_c17/oildrum001.mdl" )
+barrel:SetPos( crate:GetPos() + Vector( 0, 0, 50 ) )
+barrel:Spawn()
+
+-- The barrel now moves, rotates and is removed together with the crate.
+barrel:SetParent( crate )
+
+-- To detach the barrel later without removing it:
+-- barrel:SetParent( nil )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

 <function name="SetParentPhysNum" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets the parent of an entity to another entity with the given physics bone number. Similar to <page>Entity:SetParent</page>, except it is parented to a physbone. This function is useful mainly for ragdolls.
+
+The child entity then moves and rotates with the chosen physics bone of the parent, instead of following the parent's origin and angles as <page>Entity:SetParent</page> does.
 
 <note>Despite this function being available server side, it doesn't actually do anything server side.</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="bone" type="number">Physics bone number to attach to. Use 0 for objects with only one physics bone. (See <page>Entity:GetPhysicsObjectNum</page>)</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Attaching an entity to a ragdoll bone">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a clientside model and parents it to the head bone of the first ragdoll found, so it follows the head as the ragdoll moves. The bone number 10 is the head for standard HL2 ragdolls. The clientside model is removed when the ragdoll disappears.</description>
+	<code>
+local ragdoll = nil
+for _, ent in ipairs( ents.GetAll() ) do
+	if ent:GetClass() == "prop_ragdoll" then
+		ragdoll = ent
+		break
+	end
+end
+
+if not IsValid( ragdoll ) then return end
+
+local hat = ClientsideModel( "models/props_junk/PopCan01a.mdl", RENDERGROUP_OPAQUE )
+if not IsValid( hat ) then return end
+
+hat:SetParent( ragdoll )
+hat:SetParentPhysNum( 10 )
+hat:SetLocalPos( vector_origin )
+hat:SetLocalAngles( angle_zero )
+
+-- Remove the clientside model when the ragdoll goes away
+hook.Add( "Think", "RemoveAttachedHat", function()
+	if not IsValid( ragdoll ) then
+		hook.Remove( "Think", "RemoveAttachedHat" )
+		if IsValid( hat ) then hat:Remove() end
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
--- original/Entity:SetPersistent
+++ proposed/Entity:SetPersistent
@@ -1,14 +1,38 @@
 <function name="SetPersistent" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets whether or not the given entity is persistent. A persistent entity will be saved on server shutdown and loaded back when the server starts up. Additionally, by default persistent entities cannot be grabbed with the physgun and tools cannot be used on them.
 
 In sandbox, this can be set on an entity by opening the context menu, right clicking the entity, and choosing `"Make Persistent"`.
 
 <note>Persistence can only be enabled with the sbox_persist convar, which works as an identifier for the current set of persistent entities. An empty identifier (which is the default value) disables this feature.</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="persist" type="boolean">Whether or not the entity should be persistent.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Making a spawned prop persistent">
+    <description>Runs on the server. Spawns a wooden crate in front of the first player, marks it as persistent, and confirms that persistence is only enabled when the sbox_persist convar holds a nonempty identifier.
+
+The crate is not removed afterward, since the point of the example is to see it saved and loaded across a server restart with a nonempty sbox_persist value.</description>
+    <code>
+hook.Add( "InitPostEntity", "SpawnPersistentCrateExample", function()
+    local ply = player.GetAll()[ 1 ]
+    if ( not IsValid( ply ) ) then return end
+
+    local crate = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+    crate:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+    crate:SetPos( ply:GetPos() + ply:GetForward() * 100 + Vector( 0, 0, 32 ) )
+    crate:Spawn()
+
+    crate:SetPersistent( true )
+
+    -- A nonempty sbox_persist identifier is required for persistence to work,
+    -- otherwise entities marked as persistent are not saved on shutdown.
+    local persistId = GetConVar( "sbox_persist" ):GetString()
+    print( "crate persistent: ", crate:GetPersistent(), ", sbox_persist: ", persistId )
+end )
+    </code>
+</example>
+
```

 <function name="SetPhysicsAttacker" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets the player who gets credit if this entity kills something with physics damage within the time limit.
 
 <note>Only functional on props, "anim" type SENTs, vehicles and a few other select entities.</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="ent" type="Player">Player who gets the kills. Setting this to a non-player entity will not work.</arg>
 		<arg name="timeLimit" type="number" default="5">Time in seconds until the entity forgets its physics attacker and prevents it from getting the kill credit.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Credit a player for physics kills">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Creates a physics prop, assigns the first player as its physics attacker for 10 seconds, and throws the prop at the world spawn point. Any NPC killed by the prop's physics damage within those 10 seconds is credited to that player.</description>
+	<code>
+local prop = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+prop:Spawn()
+

+if IsValid( phys ) then
+	phys:ApplyForceCenter( Vector( 0, 0, 5000 ) )

```diff
--- original/Entity:SetPredictable
+++ proposed/Entity:SetPredictable
@@ -1,21 +1,55 @@
 <function name="SetPredictable" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets whether an entity should be predictable or not.
 When an entity is set as predictable, its DT vars can be changed during predicted hooks. This is useful for entities which can be controlled by player input.
 
 Any datatable value that mismatches from the server will be overridden and a prediction error will be spewed.
 
 Weapons are predictable by default, and the drive system uses this function to make the controlled prop predictable as well.
 
 Visit  for a list of all predicted hooks, and the <page>Prediction</page> page.
 For further technical information on the subject, visit [valve's wiki](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Prediction).
 
 <note>This function resets the datatable variables everytime it's called, it should ideally be called when a player starts using the entity and when he stops</note>
 <note>Entities set as predictable with this function will be unmarked when the user lags and receives a full packet update, to handle such case visit <page>GM:NotifyShouldTransmit</page></note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="setPredictable" type="boolean">whether to make this entity predictable or not.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Making an entity predictable while it is used">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Marks the entity the local player is looking at as predictable while the use key is held, so its datatable variables can be changed during predicted hooks. The entity is unmarked when the key is released or the entity becomes invalid.</description>
+	<code>
+local marked = nil
+
+hook.Add( "Think", "PredictableTarget", function()
+	local ply = LocalPlayer()
+	if ( not IsValid( ply ) ) then return end
+
+	local using = ply:KeyDown( IN_USE )
+	local target = ply:GetEyeTrace().Entity
+
+	if ( using and IsValid( target ) and target ~= marked ) then
+		-- Unmark the previous entity first, if any
+		if ( IsValid( marked ) ) then
+			marked:SetPredictable( false )
+		end
+
+		marked = target
+		marked:SetPredictable( true )
+	elseif ( not using and IsValid( marked ) ) then
+		marked:SetPredictable( false )
+		marked = nil
+	elseif ( not IsValid( marked ) ) then
+		marked = nil
+	end
+end )
+
+-- Remove the hook when the local player leaves or the map changes
+hook.Add( "OnGamemodeLoaded", "PredictableTargetCleanup", function()
+	hook.Remove( "Think", "PredictableTarget" )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

 	<description>
 Sets if entity should create a server ragdoll on death or a client one.
+
+By default most entities use a client side ragdoll, which only exists visually on each client. A server side ragdoll is a real <page>Entity</page> created on the server, so it can be manipulated, damaged, and removed like any other entity.
 
 <note>
 This is reset for players when they respawn (<page>Entity:Spawn</page>).
 
 Player ragdolls created with this enabled will have an owner set, see <page>Entity:SetOwner</page> for more information on what effects this has.
 </note>

+    <code>
+-- Enable server ragdolls for every player
+for _, ply in ipairs( player.GetAll() ) do
+    ply:SetShouldServerRagdoll( true )
+end
+
+-- Damage a player so they die and produce a ragdoll
+local victim = player.GetAll()[ 1 ]
+victim:Kill()
+
+-- The dead player becomes a server side ragdoll entity
+-- Requires a short delay, the ragdoll is created on death
+timer.Simple( 0.1, function()
+    for _, ent in ipairs( ents.GetAll() ) do
+        if ( ent:GetClass() == "prop_ragdoll" ) then
+            print( "Server ragdoll created: " .. tostring( ent ) )
+
+            -- Clean up the ragdoll after 5 seconds
+            timer.Simple( 5, function()

+    end
+end )

-Changes the table that can be accessed by indexing an entity. Each entity starts with its own table by default.</description>
+Changes the table that can be accessed by indexing an entity. Each entity starts with its own table by default.
+
+The new table replaces the old one entirely. Any values stored on the previous table, including values set by the engine or addons, are no longer reachable through the entity. The previous table is not modified or cleared, so it can be kept and restored later.

+

+

Verify this is acceptable or adjust to a clientside entity if player mutation is undesirable.

```diff
--- original/Entity:SetupBones
+++ proposed/Entity:SetupBones
@@ -1,9 +1,43 @@
 <function name="SetupBones" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Forces the entity to reconfigure its bones. You might need to call this after changing your model's scales or when manually drawing the entity multiple times at different positions.
+
+When an entity is drawn in a render hook, its bone positions are cached between frames. Calling this function invalidates that cache, so subsequent <page>Entity:DrawModel</page> calls use the changed bone matrix setup instead of the cached one.
 
 <note>This calls the BuildBonePositions callback added via <page>Entity:AddCallback</page>, so avoid calling this function inside it to prevent an infinite loop.</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example>
+	<description>Runs on the client in a rendering hook. Finds the first player and draws them a second time, shifted upward and with main bones scaled down. <page>Entity:SetupBones</page> is called between the draws so the second draw uses its own bone setup instead of reusing the cached one.</description>
+	<code>
+-- Files elsewhere: a script in lua/autorun/client/setupbones_example.lua
+hook.Add( "PostDrawOpaqueRenderables", "SetupBonesExample", function()
+	local ply = Entity( 1 ) -- the local player on a listen server, for demonstration
+	if ( not IsValid( ply ) or not ply:Alive() ) then return end
+
+	local pos = ply:GetPos()
+	local ang = ply:GetAngles()
+
+	-- First draw at the normal position
+	ply:SetupBones()
+	ply:DrawModel()
+
+	-- Second draw, raised and scaled. SetupBones forces the bone setup to
+	-- be rebuilt from the changed scale before this draw instead of keeping
+	-- the cache from the first one.
+	ply:SetPos( pos + Vector( 0, 0, 80 ) )
+	ply:SetModelScale( 0.5, 0 )
+
+	-- Restore after the frame so the hook does not permanently move or scale the player
+	hook.Add( "PostDrawOpaqueRenderables", "SetupBonesExampleCleanup", function()
+		ply:SetPos( pos )
+		ply:SetModelScale( 1, 0 )
+		hook.Remove( "PostDrawOpaqueRenderables", "SetupBonesExampleCleanup" )
+	end )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>The player is drawn twice: once at their normal position and once floating above, half size. The second copy keeps its own bone setup because of the SetupBones call between the draws.</output>
+</example>
+
```

## 1720. Entity:StartMotionController

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Entity%3AStartMotionController) | Revision: 514466

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

```diff
--- original/Entity:StartMotionController
+++ proposed/Entity:StartMotionController
@@ -1,17 +1,47 @@
 <function name="StartMotionController" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Starts a motion controller in the physics engine tied to this entity's <page>PhysObj</page>, which enables the use of <page>ENTITY:PhysicsSimulate</page>.
 
 The motion controller can later be destroyed via <page>Entity:StopMotionController</page>.
 
 Motion controllers are used internally to control other Entities' <page>PhysObj</page>ects, such as the Gravity Gun, +use pickup and the Physics Gun.
 
 This function should be called every time you recreate the Entity's <page>PhysObj</page>. Or alternatively you should call <page>Entity:AddToMotionController</page> on the new <page>PhysObj</page>.
 
 Also see <page>Entity:AddToMotionController</page> and <page>Entity:RemoveFromMotionController</page>.
 
 <note>Only works on a scripted <page>Entity</page> of anim type.</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Custom physics movement">
+	<description>Called in the <page>ENTITY:Initialize</page> hook of a scripted anim entity. The motion controller makes <page>ENTITY:PhysicsSimulate</page> run every tick, which here keeps the entity floating at its spawn height. The physics object must have motion enabled for the controller to move it.</description>
+	<code>
+function ENT:Initialize()
+	self:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+	self:PhysicsInit( SOLID_VPHYSICS )
+	self:SetMoveType( MOVETYPE_VPHYSICS )
+	self:SetSolid( SOLID_VPHYSICS )
+
+	local phys = self:GetPhysicsObject()
+	if ( IsValid( phys ) ) then
+		phys:Wake()
+		phys:EnableMotion( true )
+	end
+
+	self.hoverZ = self:GetPos().z
+
+	self:StartMotionController()
+end
+
+function ENT:PhysicsSimulate( phys, deltaTime )
+	phys:Wake()
+
+	-- Push upward whenever the crate drifts below its spawn height
+	local target = Vector( 0, 0, self.hoverZ - self:GetPos().z ) * 10
+
+	return target, Vector( 0, 0, 0 ), SIM_GLOBAL_ACCELERATION
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
```

 <function name="UseClientSideAnimation" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 <note>Does nothing on server.</note>
 
 Animations will be handled purely clientside instead of a fixed animtime, enabling interpolation. This does not affect layers and gestures.
+
+Call this on the client for each entity whose animations should be interpolated. The setting is per entity and per client, so every client that wants the effect must call it for that entity.

+	for _, npc in ipairs( ents.FindByClass( "npc_*" ) ) do

+	end

 	<description>
 Enables or disables trigger bounds.
 
 This will give the entity a "trigger box" that extends around its bounding box by boundSize units in X/Y and (boundSize / 2) in +Z (-Z remains the same).
 The trigger box is world aligned and will work regardless of the object's solidity and collision group.
 
 Valve use trigger boxes for all pickup items. Their bloat size is 24, a surprisingly large figure.
 
 <note>The trigger boxes can be made visible as a light blue box by using the **ent_bbox** console command while looking at the entity. Alternatively a classname or entity index can be used as the first argument.
 
 This requires **developer** to be set to **1**.</note>

 	</args>
 </function>

```diff
--- original/Entity:Visible
+++ proposed/Entity:Visible
@@ -1,23 +1,45 @@
 <function name="Visible" parent="Entity" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns whether the target/given entity is visible from the this entity.
 
 This is meant to be used only with NPCs.
 
 Differences from a simple trace include:
 * If target has `FL_NOTARGET`, returns `false`
 * If `ai_ignoreplayers` is turned on and target is a player, returns `false`
 * Reacts to `ai_LOS_mode`:
 * * If `1`, does a simple trace with `COLLISION_GROUP_NONE` and `MASK_BLOCKLOS`
 * * If not, does a trace with `MASK_BLOCKLOS_AND_NPCS` (- `CONTENTS_BLOCKLOS` is target is player) and a custom LOS filter (`CTraceFilterLOS`)
 * Returns `true` if hits a vehicle the target is driving
 	</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="target" type="Entity">Entity to check for visibility to.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">If the entities can see each other.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="NPC line of sight check">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Finds the nearest player to an NPC and reports whether the NPC can see them. The NPC must be a valid NPC entity for meaningful results.</description>
+	<code>
+local npc = ents.FindByClass( "npc_combine_s" )[ 1 ]
+if not IsValid( npc ) then return end
+
+local nearest
+for _, ply in ipairs( player.GetAll() ) do
+	if not nearest or npc:GetPos():DistToSqr( ply:GetPos() ) < npc:GetPos():DistToSqr( nearest:GetPos() ) then
+		nearest = ply
+	end
+end
+
+if nearest then
+	if npc:Visible( nearest ) then
+		print( npc, "can see", nearest )
+	else
+		print( npc, "cannot see", nearest )
+	end
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
```

+	<description>Translates a worldspace vector into a vector relative to the entity's coordinate system.
+

+ent:SetAngles( Angle( 0, 90, 0 ) )

+

+

FindTooltip is not supplied, so the exact source of tooltip text (e.g. SetTooltipText panel fields) is described generally rather than as a verified contract.

```diff
--- original/Global.ChangeTooltip
+++ proposed/Global.ChangeTooltip
@@ -1,9 +1,39 @@
 <function name="ChangeTooltip" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Automatically called by the engine when a panel is hovered over with the mouse</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="38-L64">lua/includes/util/tooltips.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="panel" type="Panel">Panel that has been hovered over</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<description>
+This function first removes any existing tooltip, then asks `FindTooltip` what should be shown for the given panel. If the panel has no tooltip text, no content panel, and no tooltip panel override, nothing is created and the previous tooltip stays removed.
+
+Otherwise it creates a new `DTooltip` (or the overriding panel class), sets either the text or the contents panel on it, and calls `DTooltip:OpenForPanel` to position and show it near the panel.
+
+You normally do not call this directly. The engine calls it for you when the mouse hovers a panel that had a tooltip assigned, such as through Panel.SetTooltipText.
+</description>
+
+<example name="Manually opening a tooltip">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a frame and a button with tooltip text, then calls ChangeTooltip manually to show the tooltip without waiting for a hover. Clicking the button closes the frame and, since the tooltip is parented to the frame's panel tree, it is removed with it.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 150 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:SetTitle( "Tooltip test" )
+
+local btn = vgui.Create( "DButton", frame )
+btn:Dock( FILL )
+btn:SetText( "Hover me, or click to close" )
+btn:SetTooltipText( "This tooltip was opened by ChangeTooltip" )
+
+-- Force the tooltip to open right now instead of waiting for a mouse hover
+ChangeTooltip( btn )
+
+function btn.DoClick()
+	frame:Remove()
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

 	<description>
 A hacky method used to fix some bugs regarding DoF. What this basically does it force all `C_BaseAnimating` entities to have the translucent <page text="rendergroup">Enums/RENDERGROUP</page>, even if they use opaque or two-pass models.
 
 This is specifically to do with <page>GM:NeedsDepthPass</page>

--- original/Global.DOF_Start
+++ proposed/Global.DOF_Start
@@ -1,9 +1,27 @@
 <function name="DOF_Start" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Cancels any existing DOF post-process effects.
 Begins the DOF post-process effect.
+
+The implementation first calls <page text="DOF_Kill">Global.DOF_Kill</page> to remove any previous effect, then spawns one `dof_node` scripted effect for each node index from 0 up to `NUM_DOF_NODES` (inclusive) using <page text="util.Effect">Global.util.Effect</page>, with the node index passed as the effect scale. Finally it enables the DOF render hack via <page text="DOFModeHack">Global.DOFModeHack</page>.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<file line="32-L46">lua/postprocess/dof.lua</file>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Start and stop the DOF effect">
+    <description>Runs on the client. Toggles the depth of field effect with a console command. Running the command again removes the effect and restores normal rendering.</description>
+    <code>
+concommand.Add( "toggle_dof", function( ply )
+
+	if ( DOF_SPON ) then
+		DOF_Kill()
+	else
+		DOF_Start()
+	end
+
+end )
+    </code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The effect constructs its node setup through the `dof_node` scripted effect, so the nodes are created as temporary clientside effects. Calling <page text="DOF_Kill">Global.DOF_Kill</page> removes them and disables the mode hack.</note>
```

```diff
--- original/Global.EffectData
+++ proposed/Global.EffectData
@@ -1,16 +1,53 @@
 <function name="EffectData" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns a <page>CEffectData</page> object to be used with <page>util.Effect</page>.
 
 <bug issue="2771">This does not create a unique object, but instead returns a shared reference. That means you cannot use two or more of these objects at once.
 
 As a result any values previously set (Origin, Magnitude, Scale etc) will carry over to all future calls of this function, and may unexpectedly affect effects created via <page>util.Effect</page>.
 </bug>
 
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
+	<note>Because of the shared reference bug, every field you do not set explicitly keeps whatever value the last effect left there. Set Origin, Scale, Magnitude, Radius and any other relevant fields yourself, even when you only need some of them.</note>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="CEffectData">The <page>CEffectData</page> object.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Creating a glass break effect">
+    <description>Runs on the server when a prop is destroyed. Gets the shared <page>CEffectData</page> object, sets all fields the effect needs, then broadcasts the effect to clients. Because the object is shared, every field is set explicitly so stale values from other effects cannot leak in.</description>
+    <code>
+local glass_props = {
+	[ "models/props_junk/glassbottle001a.mdl" ] = true,
+	[ "models/props_junk/garbage_glassbottle003a.mdl" ] = true,
+}
+
+hook.Add( "EntityRemoved", "ShatterGlassProps", function( ent )
+	if ( not glass_props[ ent:GetModel() ] ) then return end
+	
+	local ed = EffectData()
+	ed:SetOrigin( ent:GetPos() )
+	ed:SetScale( 1 )
+	ed:SetMagnitude( 1 )
+	ed:SetRadius( 50 )
+	
+	util.Effect( "GlassImpact", ed, true, true )
+end )
+    </code>
+    <description name="Resetting the shared object">If you call EffectData more than once in a row, fields from the first call persist into the second. Setting or zeroing the fields before every util.Effect call prevents this.</description>
+    <code name="Reset before reuse">
+local ed = EffectData()
+ed:SetOrigin( Vector( 100, 200, 0 ) )
+ed:SetMagnitude( 5 )
+
+-- Second use: Origin and Magnitude still hold the old values until they are set again.
+ed = EffectData()
+ed:SetOrigin( Entity( 1 ):GetPos() )
+ed:SetMagnitude( 1 )
+ed:SetScale( 1 )
+
+util.Effect( "GlassImpact", ed, true, true )
+    </code>
+</example>
+
```
