 <function name="EyeVector" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns the normal vector of the current render context as calculated by <page>GM:CalcView</page>, similar to <page>Global.EyeAngles</page>.
+
+The returned vector is a unit vector pointing in the direction the currently rendered scene is viewed from. It is derived from the view angles, so it normally matches <page>Global.EyeAngles</page>:Forward(). It can differ from the local player's aim direction when the view is modified, for example while riding in a vehicle with a free camera or when a hook alters the view.
 
 <bug issue="2516">This function is only reliable inside rendering hooks.</bug>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Vector">View direction of the currently rendered scene.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="View direction versus aim direction">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Prints the rendered view direction and compares it with the player's aim direction while the view is being rotated. The two vectors differ because the hook changes the view angles.</description>
+	<code>
+local spin = 0
+
+hook.Add( "CalcView", "EyeVectorExample", function( ply, pos, angles, fov )
+	spin = spin + FrameTime() * 45
+
+	local view = {}
+	view.origin = pos
+	view.angles = angles + Angle( 0, spin, 0 )
+	view.fov = fov
+
+	return view
+end )
+
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "EyeVectorExample", function()
+	local viewdir = EyeVector()
+	local aimdir = LocalPlayer():GetAimVector()
+
+	print( "View direction:", viewdir )
+	print( "Aim direction:", aimdir )
+	print( "Matching:", viewdir:Dot( aimdir ) > 0.999 )
+end )
+
+-- Remove the hooks when done testing
+hook.Remove( "CalcView", "EyeVectorExample" )
+hook.Remove( "HUDPaint", "EyeVectorExample" )
+	</code>
+	<output>The view direction rotates away from the aim direction while the hook spins the view, so the printed match check becomes false. Without view modification both vectors are equal.</output>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/Global.GetGlobal2Var
+++ proposed/Global.GetGlobal2Var
@@ -1,13 +1,29 @@
 <function name="GetGlobal2Var" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns a value that is shared between the server and all clients.
+
+The value must be set on the server with <page>Global.SetGlobal2Var</page> for it to exist. Values set on the client are not shared with anyone else. Global2 values are networked automatically, so a value set on the server becomes readable on all clients without extra code.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="index" type="string">The unique index to identify the global value with.</arg>
 		<arg name="default" type="any" default="nil">The value to return if the global value is not set.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="any">The global value, or the default if the global value is not set.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Reading a shared value">
+	<description>Run this on the server to set a value, then on any client to read it. The client prints the server set value once it has been networked.</description>
+	<code>
+-- Server
+SetGlobal2Var( "round_number", 3 )
+
+-- Client
+print( GetGlobal2Var( "round_number", 0 ) )
+	</code>
+	<output>3</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>Using a default argument avoids nil errors when the value has not been set yet, for example on a client that just joined.</note>

+local rt = GetRenderTargetEx( "myexample_rt", 256, 256, RT_SIZE_NO_CHANGE,

+	render.PopRenderTarget()
+

 <function name="HSLToColor" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<file line="76-L105">lua/includes/util/color.lua</file>
 	<description>
 Converts a color from [HSL color space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HSL_and_HSV) into RGB color space and returns a <page>Color</page>.
+
+The hue is wrapped with the modulo operation, so values outside 0-360 are accepted and wrap around. The returned color always has an alpha of 255. Each RGB component is floored and clamped to 0-255.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="hue" type="number">The hue in degrees from 0-360.</arg>

 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="HSL color wheel">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Prints the RGB values for a fully saturated red and a mid tone blue, and shows that hue values wrap around.</description>
+	<code>
+local red = HSLToColor( 0, 1, 0.5 )
+print( red.r, red.g, red.b ) -- 255 0 0
+
+local blue = HSLToColor( 240, 1, 0.5 )
+print( blue.r, blue.g, blue.b ) -- 0 0 255
+
+-- Hue wraps, so 360 is the same as 0
+local wrapped = HSLToColor( 360, 1, 0.5 )
+print( wrapped.r, wrapped.g, wrapped.b ) -- 255 0 0
+	</code>
+</example>

@@ -1,17 +1,33 @@
 <function name="HWBToColor" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<file line="107-L117">lua/includes/util/color.lua</file>
 	<description>
 Converts a color from [HWB color space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HWB_color_model) (Hue-Whiteness-Blackness) into RGB color space and returns a <page>Color</page>.
+
+In HWB, a whiteness and blackness of 0 gives the pure, fully saturated hue. Increasing whiteness mixes in white, increasing blackness mixes in black. A whiteness of 1 gives white and a blackness of 1 gives black, regardless of hue.
+
+Internally the function converts the HWB values to HSV saturation and value and calls <page>Global.HSVToColor</page>.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<added>2025.01.23</added>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="hue" type="number">The hue of the color in degrees from 0-360.</arg>
 		<arg name="whiteness" type="number">The whiteness of the color from 0-1.</arg>
 		<arg name="blackness" type="number">The blackness of the color from 0-1.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Color">The <page>Color</page> created from the HWB color space.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Pure hue and tinted variants">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Prints the pure hue for 120 degrees (green), then the same hue mixed with white and with black.</description>
+	<code>
+local pure = HWBToColor( 120, 0, 0 )
+local pale = HWBToColor( 120, 0.5, 0 )
+local dark = HWBToColor( 120, 0, 0.5 )
+
+print( pure ) -- 0 255 0
+print( pale ) -- 128 255 128
+print( dark ) -- 0 128 0
+	</code>
+</example>
```

 <function name="isentity" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
-	<description>Returns if the passed object is an <page>Entity</page>.</description>
+	<description>Returns if the passed object is an <page>Entity</page>.
+
+The check is done by inspecting the object's metatable. Objects whose metatable is based on the Entity metatable, such as <page>Player</page>, <page>Vehicle</page> and <page>NPC</page> objects, also return true. Non entity values, including <page>number</page>s, <page>string</page>s, tables and <page>Vector</page>s, return false.</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>

 	</rets>

+<example>
+	<description>Runs on the server. Prints whether several values are entities.</description>
+	<code>
+local ply = Entity( 1 )
+
+print( isentity( ply ) ) -- true, players are entities
+print( isentity( game.GetWorld() ) ) -- true, the world entity is an entity
+print( isentity( NULL ) ) -- true, NULL is an entity with no reference
+print( isentity( "ply" ) ) -- false, a string is not an entity
+print( isentity( Vector( 0, 0, 0 ) ) ) -- false, vectors are not entities
+print( isentity( nil ) ) -- false
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>Use <page>Global.IsValid</page> or <page>Global.IsValidEntity</page> instead when you need to know whether an entity variable is usable, not just whether it holds an entity. <page>Global.IsValid</page> also accepts non entity values and returns false for them.</note>
+

 <function name="IsUselessModel" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns whether or not a model is useless by checking that the file path is that of a proper model.
 
 If the string ".mdl" is not found in the model name, the function will return true.
 
 The function will also return true if any of the following strings are found in the given model name:
 * "_gesture"
 * "_anim"
 * "_gst"
 * "_pst"
 * "_shd"
 * "_ss"
 * "_posture"
 * "_anm"
 * "ghostanim"
 * "_paths"
 * "_shared"
 * "anim_"
 * "gestures_"
 * "shared_ragdoll_"
+
+The check is not case sensitive. The given model name is converted to lowercase before the substring search, so "MODEL.MDL" is treated the same as "model.mdl".
+
+This is a plain substring check only. It does not verify that the model file exists or is actually loadable.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="312-L334">lua/includes/util.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="modelName" type="string">The model name to be checked</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Whether or not the model is useless</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Filtering animation models">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Rejects model paths that are animation or gesture files before spawning a prop, and prints the result.</description>
+	<code>
+local models = {
+	"models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl",
+	"models/player/kleiner_anim.mdl"
+}
+
+for _, mdl in ipairs( models ) do
+	if ( IsUselessModel( mdl ) ) then
+		print( "Rejected: " .. mdl )
+	else
+		local prop = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+		if ( IsValid( prop ) ) then
+			prop:SetModel( mdl )
+			prop:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+			prop:Spawn()
+		end
+	end
+end
+	</code>
+	<output>Rejected: models/player/kleiner_anim.mdl</output>
+</example>
+
```

 Returns whether an object is valid or not. (Such as <page text="entities">Entity</page>, <page>Panel</page>s, custom <page>table</page> objects and more).
 
 Checks that an object is not <page>nil</page>, has an `IsValid` method and if this method returns `true`. If the object has no `IsValid` method, it will return `false`.
 
 <note>If you are sure that the object you are about to check is not `nil` and has the `IsValid` method, it would be faster to call it directly rather than using `IsValid`.</note>

 </function>

+

+

+end )
+	</code>

+	<description>Adds workshop related JavaScript functions to an HTML panel, used by the "Dupes" and "Saves" tabs in the spawnmenu.
+
+The functions are added to the JavaScript global object `gmod` on the panel. This registers the following functions, which the built in spawnmenu pages call:
+
+* `gmod.OpenWorkshopFile( id )` opens the workshop page for the given file ID with <page>Global.steamworks.ViewFile</page>.
+* `gmod.DeleteLocal( path )` deletes a file from the `MOD` search path with <page>Global.file.Delete</page>.
+* `gmod.FetchItems( namespace, cat, offset, perpage, extraTags, searchText, filter, sort )` calls `Fetch` on the global object named by `namespace` (for example a workshop list object) to load a page of workshop items.
+* `gmod.Vote( id, vote )` votes on a workshop item with <page>Global.steamworks.Vote</page>.
+* `gmod.SetFavorite( id, vote )` favorites a workshop item with <page>Global.steamworks.SetFavorite</page>.
+* `gmod.Publish( namespace, filePath, background )` calls `Publish` on the global object named by `namespace`.
+* `gmod.DownloadDupe( id )` and `gmod.ArmDupe( id )` download and arm a duplication from the workshop.
+* `gmod.SaveDupe()` runs the `dupe_save spawnmenu` console command.
+* `gmod.DownloadSave( id )` and `gmod.LoadSave( id )` download and load a saved game from the workshop.
+* `gmod.SaveSave()` runs the `gm_save spawnmenu` console command.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="19-L40">lua/includes/util/javascript_util.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="htmlPanel" type="Panel">Panel to add JavaScript functions to.</arg>

 </function>

+

+

 <function name="MainEyeAngles" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns the main view angles, as they were at the start of the latest main view render.
 
 This is a good alternative to <page>Global.EyeAngles</page> which is affected by other rendering operations, including <page>render.RenderView</page>.
+
+Because the returned angles describe the main view rather than the current rendering pass, they stay stable while drawing inside hooks such as <page>GM:HUDPaint</page> even if other view rendering has run in the same frame.
 	</description>
 	<added>2025.10.02</added>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Angle">The angles of the main view.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Comparing with EyeAngles inside a render hook">
+    <description>Runs on the client. Adds a hook that draws the pitch angle of the main view on screen, using <page>cam.Start3D2D</page> free drawing via <page>surface.DrawText</page>. The value from MainEyeAngles matches the player's actual view pitch, while <page>Global.EyeAngles</page> could differ if a <page>render.RenderView</page> pass has already run this frame.</description>
+    <code>
+-- Put this in a client Lua file, for example lua/autorun/client/maineyeangles_demo.lua
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "MainEyeAngles_compare", function()
+    local main = MainEyeAngles()
+    local eye = EyeAngles()
+
+    local text = "Main: " .. math.Round( main.pitch ) .. "  Eye: " .. math.Round( eye.pitch )
+    draw.SimpleText( text, "DermaDefault", 20, 20, color_white )
+end )
+
+-- Remove the hook when it is no longer needed:

+    </code>
+</example>

```diff
--- original/Global.OrderVectors
+++ proposed/Global.OrderVectors
@@ -1,13 +1,30 @@
 <function name="OrderVectors" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Modifies the given vectors so that values of `vector2` on each axis (X Y Z) are larger than those of `vector1` by switching them around. Also known as ordering vectors.
 
 This is useful to convert (or guarantee) 2 position vectors to a bounding box "mins" and "maxs" vectors.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="vector1" type="Vector">Vector 1. This will become a "mins" vector of the resulting bounding box.</arg>
 		<arg name="vector2" type="Vector">Vector 2. This will become a "maxs" vector of the resulting bounding box.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<note>The vectors are modified in place. The original values are not preserved, so clone them first if they are needed later.</note>
+
+<example name="Ordering two positions into a bounding box">
+	<description>Runs in any realm. Two vectors with unordered components are given to Global.OrderVectors, which rewrites them in place so `mins` holds the smaller value on each axis and `maxs` holds the larger value. The vectors are cloned first so the original corner positions stay intact.</description>
+	<code>
+local cornerA = Vector( 10, -5, 3 )
+local cornerB = Vector( -2, 7, -8 )
+
+-- Keep the original corners, since OrderVectors rewrites the vectors in place
+local mins, maxs = cornerA:Clone(), cornerB:Clone()
+OrderVectors( mins, maxs )
+
+print( mins ) -- prints -2 -5 -8
+print( maxs ) -- prints 10 7 3
+print( cornerA ) -- unchanged: 10 -5 3
+	</code>
+</example>
```

- Added a serverside example using the built in sparkler_main effect; confirm the effect name and that the eyes attachment exists on player models.

```diff
--- original/Global.ParticleEffectAttach
+++ proposed/Global.ParticleEffectAttach
@@ -1,17 +1,39 @@
 <function name="ParticleEffectAttach" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Creates a particle effect with specialized parameters. See also <page>Entity:CreateParticleEffect</page> and <page>Global.CreateParticleSystem</page>.
 
 <note>The particle effect must be precached **serverside** with <page>Global.PrecacheParticleSystem</page> and the file its from must be added via <page>game.AddParticles</page> before it can be used! This is due to the function using networked IDs for particle names, not directly networking particle system name.
 
 Clientside, you can use <page>Global.CreateParticleSystemNoEntity</page> (and similar) instead.</note>
+
+The behavior depends on the <page>Enums/PATTACH</page> value:
+
+* `PATTACH_ABSORIGIN` and `PATTACH_ABSORIGIN_FOLLOW` place the effect at the entity's origin. The `attachmentID` argument is ignored.
+* `PATTACH_POINT` and `PATTACH_POINT_FOLLOW` attach the effect to the attachment with the given `attachmentID`. Use <page>Entity:LookupAttachment</page> to find the ID by name. With `PATTACH_POINT_FOLLOW` the effect follows the attachment as it moves.
+* `PATTACH_CUSTOM_ORIGIN` places the effect at the entity's origin and lets you move it afterwards with <page>ParticleEffect</page> style control.
+
+The function returns nothing. The effect is removed automatically when the entity it is attached to is removed.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="particleName" type="string">The name of the particle effect.</arg>
 		<arg name="attachType" type="number">Attachment type using <page>Enums/PATTACH</page>.</arg>
 		<arg name="entity" type="Entity">The entity to be used in the way specified by the attachType.</arg>
 		<arg name="attachmentID" type="number">The id of the attachment to be used in the way specified by the attachType.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example>
+	<description>Runs on the server. Precaches and attaches the `sparkler_main` effect from the default particle file to the player's eyes attachment, so it follows their view. The file is already registered by the game, so <page>game.AddParticles</page> is not needed here.</description>
+	<code>
+-- Call this once, for example in a console command or on player spawn.
+PrecacheParticleSystem( "sparkler_main" )
+
+local ply = Entity( 1 ) -- replace with a valid player
+local attachID = ply:LookupAttachment( "eyes" )
+
+ParticleEffectAttach( "sparkler_main", PATTACH_POINT_FOLLOW, ply, attachID )
+	</code>
+	<output>A sparkler particle effect appears at the player's eyes and follows their view position.</output>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
--- original/Global.Path
+++ proposed/Global.Path
@@ -1,18 +1,33 @@
 <function name="Path" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Creates a path for the bot to follow using one of two types (`Follow` or `Chase`)
 
 `Follow` is a general purpose path. Best used for static or infrequently updated locations. The path will only be updated once <page>PathFollower:Update</page> is called. This needs to be done manually (typically inside the bots `BehaveThread` coroutine.
 
 `Chase` is a specifically optimized for chasing a moving entity. Paths of this type will use <page>PathFollower:Chase</page>
 
-
+The returned <page>PathFollower</page> is not connected to any bot by itself. You must call <page>PathFollower:Compute</page> to build a route to a goal, then call <page>PathFollower:Update</page> (or <page>PathFollower:Chase</page> for `"Chase"` paths) each tick to make the bot move along it.
 </description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<args> 
 		<arg name="type" type="string">The type of the path to create, must be `"Follow"` or `"Chase"`</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="PathFollower">The path</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Making a bot walk to a position">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Assumes a NextBot exists with a `BehaveThread` coroutine (for example a bot created with <page>NextBot</page> based code). The path is computed once toward a fixed goal and followed every update, which suits the `"Follow"` type for a static destination.</description>
+	<code>
+-- Inside the bot's BehaveThread coroutine
+local path = Path( "Follow" )
+path:Compute( self, self:GetPos() + Vector( 500, 0, 0 ) )
+
+while path:IsValid() do
+	-- Move the bot along the path, giving up after 5 seconds without progress
+	path:Update( self )
+	coroutine.wait( 0.25 )
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
--- original/Global.ProtectedCall
+++ proposed/Global.ProtectedCall
@@ -1,16 +1,36 @@
 <function name="ProtectedCall" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Runs a function without stopping the whole script on error.
 
 This function is similar to <page>Global.pcall</page> and <page>Global.xpcall</page> except the errors are still printed and sent to the error handler (i.e. sent to server console if clientside and <page>GM:OnLuaError</page> called).
+
+Unlike <page>Global.pcall</page>, the error message is not returned. Only a boolean success flag is returned, so use this when you want the error reported through the normal error pipeline rather than handled manually.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="func" type="function">Function to run</arg>
         <arg name="arguments" type="vararg">Arguments to call the function with.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Whether the function executed successfully or not</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Running a function that may error">
+	<description>Runs on the server. The first call succeeds and returns true. The second call raises an error inside the protected function, which is printed to the console, and ProtectedCall returns false instead of halting the script.</description>

```diff
--- original/Global.RealTime
+++ proposed/Global.RealTime
@@ -1,19 +1,43 @@
 <function name="RealTime" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns the uptime of the game/server in seconds (to at least **4** decimal places). This value updates itself once every time the realm thinks. For servers, this is the server tickrate. For clients, this is once per frame.
 
 <note>This is **not** synchronised or affected by the game.
 
 This will be affected by precision loss if the uptime is more than 30+(?) days, and effectively cease to be functional after 50+(?) days.
 
 Changing the map will **not** fix it like it does with <page>Global.CurTime</page>. A server restart is necessary.</note>
 
 You should use this function (or <page>Global.SysTime</page>) for timing real-world events such as user interaction, but not for timing game events such as animations.
 
 See also: <page>Global.CurTime</page>, <page>Global.SysTime</page>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">Uptime of the game/server.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Measuring real-world elapsed time">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Stores the real time when a player first spawns and prints how much real time has passed on their next spawn. Because the value comes from the server clock and not the game world, it keeps counting even while the game is paused or the timescale is changed.</description>
+	<code>
+local firstSpawn = {}
+
+hook.Add( "PlayerSpawn", "RealTimeExample", function( ply )
+	local now = RealTime()
+
+	if ( not firstSpawn[ ply:SteamID64() ] ) then
+		firstSpawn[ ply:SteamID64() ] = now
+		print( ply:Nick() .. " first seen at " .. now .. " seconds of server uptime." )
+	else
+		print( ply:Nick() .. " respawned after " .. math.Round( now - firstSpawn[ ply:SteamID64() ], 2 ) .. " real seconds." )
+	end
+end )
+
+-- Remove stored times when a player leaves to avoid the table growing forever
+hook.Add( "PlayerDisconnected", "RealTimeExampleCleanup", function( ply )
+	firstSpawn[ ply:SteamID64() ] = nil
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>PlayerName respawned after 12.34 real seconds.</output>
+</example>
```

@@ -1,11 +1,32 @@
 <function name="RegisterMetaTable" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Registers a given table as a metatable. It can then be accessed by other code/addons via <page>Global.FindMetaTable</page>.
+
+The registration happens once per name. Calling this function again with the same `metaName` does not replace the previously registered table, so addons that share a metatable name should agree on its contents or guard the call with <page>Global.FindMetaTable</page>.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<added>2024.06.04</added>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="metaName" type="string">The new metatable name. Cannot override existing types.</arg>
 		<arg name="metaTable" type="table">The new metatable table. It will be given a `MetaID` and `MetaName` fields.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Registering and using a custom metatable">
+	<description>Registers a metatable for a simple vector like type, then uses <page>Global.FindMetaTable</page> to attach methods that work on any table with that metatable. This can run on the server, the client, or the menu.</description>
+	<code>
+local meta = FindMetaTable( "MyVec" ) or {}
+
+function meta:GetLength()
+	return math.sqrt( self.x ^ 2 + self.y ^ 2 )
+end
+
+RegisterMetaTable( "MyVec", meta )
+
+local v = { x = 3, y = 4 }
+setmetatable( v, FindMetaTable( "MyVec" ) )
+
+print( v:GetLength() )
+	</code>
+	<output>5</output>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/Global.RenderSuperDoF
+++ proposed/Global.RenderSuperDoF
@@ -1,11 +1,47 @@
 <function name="RenderSuperDoF" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Renders the Super Depth of Field post-process effect</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<file line="281-L329">lua/postprocess/super_dof.lua</file>
 	<args>

 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<note>This function depends on internal state from `lua/postprocess/super_dof.lua`, the same state used by the Super DoF tool. It reads the globals `Status`, `Distance`, `BlurSize`, `Steps`, `Passes`, `FocusGrabber`, `matFSB` and `texFSB` from that file. If `Status` is not set to `"Preview"`, `"Render"` or `"ViewShot"`, no effect is drawn.</note>
+
+<description>
+Renders the Super Depth of Field post-process effect for the given view.
+
+The focus distance is computed as the distance from `viewOrigin` to the point `viewOrigin + viewAngles:Forward() * Distance`, where `Distance` is an internal global of the Super DoF post-process file, not a function argument.
+
+The internal `Status` global selects the render mode:
+
+* `"Preview"` draws a fast, low quality depth of field using `RenderDoF` with 2 steps and 2 passes.
+* `"Render"` draws a high quality result using the internal `Steps` and `Passes` globals, then sets `Status` to `"ViewShot"`.
+* `"ViewShot"` draws the previously rendered frame texture back over the screen as a fullscreen quad.
+
+If the internal `FocusGrabber` global is set, the function also traces from the cursor position, updates `Distance` and the Super DoF window, and spawns a `Sparks` effect at the hit position.
+</description>
+
+<warning>This function is meant for the Super DoF tool and its own render flow. Calling it outside that flow requires manually setting the internal globals described above, which can change without notice.</warning>
+
+<example name="Preview render">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Sets up the internal Super DoF state for a preview render, then calls the function every frame from the `RenderScreenspaceEffects` hook using the player's current view. The world appears blurred beyond 500 units from the view origin. Run the cleanup snippet once to stop the effect and remove the hook.</description>
+	<code>
+-- Set up the state normally managed by the Super DoF tool
+Status = "Preview"
+BlurSize = 4
+Distance = 500
+
+hook.Add( "RenderScreenspaceEffects", "SuperDoFPreview", function()
+	local view = render.GetViewSetup()
+	RenderSuperDoF( view.origin, view.angles, view.fov )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<code name="Cleanup">
+hook.Remove( "RenderScreenspaceEffects", "SuperDoFPreview" )
+Status = nil
+	</code>
+</example>
```

- Existing markup declared an alias of sql.SQLStr while the supplied source is the definition of sql.SQLStr itself; the alias relationship was preserved as written.
- Extended the description with behavior supported by the supplied source: tostring conversion, single quote doubling, null byte truncation, and quote wrapping based on noQuotes. Marked input as accepting non string values since the body calls tostring; no existing contract was changed.
- Added a note to the expanded description explaining that false and an omitted argument select quotes, matching the if ( bNoQuotes ) branch.

```diff
--- original/Global.SQLStr
+++ proposed/Global.SQLStr
@@ -1,16 +1,46 @@
 <function name="SQLStr" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Returns the input value in an escaped form so that it can safely be used inside of queries. The returned value is surrounded by quotes unless `noQuotes` is true. Alias of <page>sql.SQLStr</page>.
+
+The function replaces each single quote in the value with two single quotes, which is the SQLite escape sequence. It passes the value through <page>Global.tostring</page> first, so non string values such as numbers are accepted and converted.
+
+If the escaped value contains a null byte, everything from the null byte onward is removed before the value is returned.
+
+When `noQuotes` is `false` or omitted, the returned string is wrapped in single quotes so it can be inserted directly into a query as a string literal. Setting `noQuotes` to `true` returns the escaped value without quotes, which is useful when the value is already quoted in the query or used in a context where quotes are invalid. `false` selects no quotes the same way an omitted argument does; only `true` removes them.
 
 <warning>Do not use this function with external database engines such as `MySQL`. `MySQL` and `SQLite` use different escape sequences that are incompatible with each other! Escaping strings with inadequate functions is dangerous and will lead to SQL injection vulnerabilities.</warning>
 </description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="27-L27">lua/includes/util/sql.lua</file>
 	<args>
-		<arg name="input" type="string">String to be escaped</arg>
+		<arg name="input" type="string">String to be escaped. Any other value is converted to a string first.</arg>
 		<arg name="noQuotes" type="boolean" default="false">Set this as `true`, and the function will not wrap the input string in apostrophes.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="string">Escaped input</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Building a safe query">
+	<description>Runs on the server. A player supplied string is escaped and inserted into a query, then the stored row is read back to confirm the value was saved correctly.</description>
+	<code>
+-- Imagine this came from untrusted input
+local nickname = "O'Brien"
+
+-- The quote is doubled, so the value is safe to embed
+local escaped = SQLStr( nickname )
+print( escaped )
+
+sql.Query( "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS nicknames( name TEXT )" )
+sql.Query( "INSERT INTO nicknames( name ) VALUES( " .. escaped .. " )" )
+
+local rows = sql.Query( "SELECT name FROM nicknames WHERE name = " .. escaped )
+if ( istable( rows ) and rows[ 1 ] ) then
+	print( "Stored: " .. rows[ 1 ].name )
+end
+
+sql.Query( "DROP TABLE nicknames" )
+	</code>
+	<output>'O''Brien'
+Stored: O'Brien</output>
+</example>
+
```

+The returned value is computed as `math.cos( frequency * math.tau * CurTime() + offset ) * ( max - min ) * 0.5 + min`, so it oscillates smoothly between `min` and `max`. +		<arg name="min" type="number">Minimum value.</arg>
+		<arg name="max" type="number">Maximum value.</arg>
+		<arg name="offset" type="number">Offset variable that doesn't affect the rate of change, but causes the returned value to be offset by time.</arg>

 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Oscillating light brightness">
+	<description>Runs on the server. A point lamp's brightness pulses smoothly between 0.2 and 1 every 2 seconds. The lamp is removed after 10 seconds.</description>
+	<code>
+local lamp = ents.Create( "light_dynamic" )
+lamp:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 64 ) )
+lamp:SetKeyValue( "_light", "255 255 255" )
+lamp:Spawn()
+lamp:Activate()
+
+local timerName = "TimedCosLamp" .. lamp:EntIndex()
+
+timer.Create( timerName, 0, 0, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( lamp ) ) then
+		timer.Remove( timerName )
+		return
+	end
+
+	-- 0.5 frequency means one full pulse every 2 seconds
+	local brightness = TimedCos( 0.5, 0.2, 1, 0 )
+	lamp:SetKeyValue( "light", tostring( brightness ) )
+end )
+
+timer.Simple( 10, function()
+	if ( IsValid( lamp ) ) then lamp:Remove() end
+	timer.Remove( timerName )
+end )
+	</code>

It is designed to drive a <page text="DHTML">DHTML</page> panel: results are pushed to JavaScript on the panel through calls like `namespace.ReceiveIndex( json )`, `namespace.ReceiveFileInfo( wsid, json )`, and `namespace.ReceiveImage( wsid, path )`. +}

+
+-- Fetch the first 10 subscribed addons, sorted by most recently added

+end
+
+-- Give the function its own environment, inheriting from _G
+local env = setmetatable( { myCustomGlobal = "hello" }, { __index = _G } )
+setfenv( test, env )
+
+-- The environment table is the same one we assigned
+PrintTable( getfenv( test ) )
+
+-- Level 0 is the global environment

## 1901. Global.module

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.module) | Revision: 514883

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

```diff
--- original/Global.module
+++ proposed/Global.module
@@ -1,13 +1,35 @@
 <function name="module" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Creates a table with the specified module name and sets the function environment for said table.
 
 Any passed loaders are called with the table as an argument. An example of this is <page>package.seeall</page>.
+
+This behaves like the Lua 5.1 standard library function of the same name. Calling it inside a file makes that file act as a module. The new table is stored in the global environment under `name`, and code after the call runs with that table as its function environment, so assignments and functions written afterwards become members of the module table instead of globals.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="name" type="string">The name of the module. This will be used to access the module table in the runtime environment.</arg>
 		<arg name="loaders" type="vararg">Calls each function passed with the new table as an argument.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Defining a module">
+	<description>Runs on both realms. The file `mymod.lua` is loaded with <page>Global.include</page> from another file. Everything defined after the `module` call is stored in the module table and returned by `include`.</description>
+	<code>
+-- mymod.lua
+module( "mymod" )
+
+function greet( name )
+    print( "Hello, " .. name .. "!" )
+end
+
+-- some other file
+local mymod = include( "mymod.lua" )
+mymod.greet( "world" ) -- also accessible as the global mymod.greet
+	</code>
+	<output>Hello, world!</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>
+Because the module table becomes the function environment, creating global variables inside a module file after the `module` call is not possible. Use <page>package.seeall</page> as a loader if the module needs access to globals through its environment.
+</note>
```

```diff
--- original/Global.newproxy
+++ proposed/Global.newproxy
@@ -1,17 +1,48 @@
 <function name="newproxy" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 		<bug issue="5299">Fails under certain conditions when called in coroutines</bug>
 		Creates a new <page>userdata</page> object.
+		This is a standard Lua function, not specific to Garry's Mod. It is commonly used to create an empty object that can carry a metatable, which makes it useful for building objects with custom behavior or for detecting garbage collection through a <code>__gc</code> metamethod.
+		When called with no arguments, the new userdata has no metatable. When called with <code>true</code>, it gets its own empty metatable that can be modified with <page>Global.getmetatable</page> and <page>Global.setmetatable</page>. When called with an existing userdata created by this function, the new userdata shares that userdata's metatable.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="addMetatable" type="boolean" default="false">If true, the created <page>userdata</page> will be given its own metatable.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<args name="Userdata Copy">
 		<arg name="userData" type="userdata">Creates a new <page>userdata</page> with the same metatable the <page>userdata</page> passed in had. The <page>userdata</page> passed in **must be** a <page>userdata</page> that has a metatable that was created from this function.</arg>
 	</args> 
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="userdata">The newly created <page>userdata</page>.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example>
+	<description>Runs on the server. Creates a proxy with its own metatable, gives it an <code>__index</code> metamethod, and shows that a second proxy can share the same metatable. Both proxies then respond to field access like a table would.</description>
+	<code>
+local proxy = newproxy( true )
+
+local meta = getmetatable( proxy )
+meta.__index = {
+	health = 100,
+	name = "proxy object"
+}
+
+-- A second proxy sharing the same metatable
+local proxy2 = newproxy( proxy )
+
+print( proxy.health )
+print( proxy2.name )
+print( getmetatable( proxy ) == getmetatable( proxy2 ) )
+	</code>
+	<output>
+100
+proxy object
+true
+	</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>Calling <code>newproxy()</code> with no argument creates a userdata without a metatable, so <code>getmetatable</code> on it returns <code>nil</code> and it cannot be given one afterward with <page>Global.setmetatable</page>.</note>
+
+<note>The userdata created by this function stores no value by itself. Its usefulness comes entirely from the metatable attached to it.</note>
+
```

+local a = { 1, 2, 3 }
+local b = { 1, 2, 3 }
+
+local meta = {
+	__eq = function( x, y )
+		return #x == #y
+	end
+}
+
+print( a == b )        -- true, __eq compares the lengths
+print( rawequal( a, b ) ) -- false, different tables

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global.rawget) | Revision: 511334

- No Lua implementation was supplied for this page. The added explanation and example describe standard Lua 5.1 rawget behavior, which matches the existing description, but the native status remains unverified.
- The existing rets entry says only "The value". I expanded it to mention nil for missing keys, which is standard rawget behavior. Reviewer may want to confirm against source.
- The note links Global.rawset without supplied evidence that the page exists; adjust or remove the link if the target is wrong.

```diff
--- original/Global.rawget
+++ proposed/Global.rawget
@@ -1,12 +1,31 @@
 <function name="rawget" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
-	<description>Gets the value with the specified key from the table without calling the __index method.</description>
+	<description>Gets the value with the specified key from the table without calling the __index method.
+
+	A normal index such as `table[index]` first checks the table itself. If the key is not found, Lua calls the `__index` metamethod of the table's metatable. This function skips that lookup and only reads the table's own contents, so it returns nil for keys that exist only through `__index`.</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="table" type="table">Table to get the value from.</arg>
 		<arg name="index" type="any">The index to get the value from.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
-		<ret name="" type="any">The value.</ret>
+		<ret name="" type="any">The value stored directly in the table, or nil if the key is not present in the table itself.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Bypassing __index">
+	<description>Runs in any realm. A metatable provides a fallback value through `__index`. `rawget` reads only the table itself, so it returns nil for the key that exists only through the metamethod.</description>
+	<code>
+local t = setmetatable( {}, { __index = function( tbl, key )
+	return "fallback for " .. key
+end } )
+
+print( t.hello ) -- "fallback for hello", found through __index
+print( rawget( t, "hello" ) ) -- nil, the table itself has no "hello" key
+
+t.hello = "stored"
+print( rawget( t, "hello" ) ) -- "stored", now present in the table itself
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>This is the read counterpart of <page text="Global.rawset">Global.rawset</page>. Both are useful inside metamethods such as `__index` and `__newindex`, where a normal index or assignment would call the metamethod again and cause infinite recursion.</note>
+
```

```diff
--- original/Global.rawset
+++ proposed/Global.rawset
@@ -1,10 +1,26 @@
 <function name="rawset" parent="Global" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Sets the value with the specified key from the table without calling the __newindex method.</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="table" type="table">Table to get the value from.</arg>
 		<arg name="index" type="any">The index to get the value from.</arg>
 		<arg name="value" type="any">The value to set for the specified key.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Bypassing __newindex">
+	<description>Demonstrates that rawset writes to the table directly while a normal assignment goes through the __newindex metamethod. This code can be run anywhere, for example in the console with lua_openscript_cl.</description>
+	<code>
+local t = setmetatable( {}, { __newindex = function( self, k, v )
+	print( "__newindex called for key " .. tostring( k ) )
+	rawset( self, k, v )
+end } )
+
+t.health = 100 -- Triggers __newindex, which stores the value with rawset
+rawset( t, "armor", 50 ) -- Stores the value directly, __newindex is not called

+
+The name is resolved relative to the ``lua/`` folder. For example, ``require( "myaddon/init" )`` loads ``lua/myaddon/init.lua``. A module is only loaded once per session; later calls with the same name return the cached module instead of running its file again.

 <note>
 	Binary modules can't be installed as part of an addon and have to be put directly into ``garrysmod/lua/bin/`` to be detected.

 </note>
 
 	</description>

 	<args>
 		<arg name="name" type="string">The name of the module to be loaded.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>

+

+]] )
+

+		print( "Called greet with:", arguments[ 1 ], arguments[ 2 ] )

+end
+
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+-- Remove the panel when done:

## 1917. IGModAudioChannel:FFT

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/IGModAudioChannel%3AFFT) | Revision: 564453

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091621-kw297oiLw2kCOTejXy5c`. Duration: 5.09s. Attempt cost: 0.00063443.

- No source implementation was supplied, so the example relies only on the documented behavior: magnitudes from 0 to 1, bins starting at index 1, and the returned bin count. The frequency range comment in the example assumes a 44100 Hz sample rate, which is typical but not guaranteed for every stream.

```diff
--- original/IGModAudioChannel:FFT
+++ proposed/IGModAudioChannel:FFT
@@ -1,24 +1,60 @@
 <function name="FFT" parent="IGModAudioChannel" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Computes the [DFT (discrete Fourier transform)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_Fourier_transform) of the sound channel.
 
 The size parameter specifies the number of consecutive audio samples to use as the input to the DFT and is restricted to a power of two. A [Hann window](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hann_function) is applied to the input data.
 
 The computed DFT has the same number of frequency bins as the number of samples. Only half of this DFT is returned, since [the DFT magnitudes are symmetric for real input data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_Fourier_transform#The_real-input_DFT). The magnitudes of the DFT (values from 0 to 1) are used to fill the output table, starting at index 1.
 
 **Visualization protip:** For a size N DFT, bin k (1-indexed) corresponds to a frequency of (k - 1) / N * sampleRate.
 
 **Visualization protip:** Sound energy is proportional to the square of the magnitudes. Adding magnitudes together makes no sense physically, but adding energies does.
 
 **Visualization protip:** The human ear works on a logarithmic amplitude scale. You can convert to [decibels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decibel) by taking 20 * <page>math.log10</page> of frequency magnitudes, or 10 * <page>math.log10</page> of energy. The decibel values will range from -infinity to 0.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="tbl" type="table<number>">The table to output the DFT magnitudes (numbers between 0 and 1) into. Indices start from 1.</arg>
 		<arg name="size" type="number{FFT}">The number of samples to use. See <page>Enums/FFT</page></arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">The number of frequency bins that have been filled in the output table.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Measuring bass energy">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Loads a remote sound, then repeatedly measures the energy in the lowest frequency bins and prints it. The channel is stopped and the timer removed after 10 seconds.</description>
+	<code>
+sound.PlayFile( "http://example.com/song.ogg", "mono noplay", function( chan, id, errName )
+	if ( not IsValid( chan ) ) then
+		print( "Failed to load sound: " .. errName )
+		return
+	end
+
+	chan:Play()
+
+	local fft = {}
+
+	timer.Create( "MeasureBass", 0.5, 20, function()
+		if ( not IsValid( chan ) ) then return end
+
+		-- 512 samples gives 256 bins. With a 44100 Hz sample rate,
+		-- bin 1 covers roughly 0 to 86 Hz, so bins 1 to 4 are bass.
+		local bins = chan:FFT( fft, FFT_512 )
+
+		local energy = 0
+		for i = 1, math.min( 4, bins ) do
+			energy = energy + fft[ i ] * fft[ i ]
+		end
+
+		print( "Bass energy: " .. energy )
+	end )
+
+	-- Cleanup after 10 seconds
+	timer.Simple( 10, function()
+		timer.Remove( "MeasureBass" )
+		if ( IsValid( chan ) ) then chan:Stop() end
+	end )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

+

```diff
--- original/IGModAudioChannel:IsValid
+++ proposed/IGModAudioChannel:IsValid
@@ -1,8 +1,36 @@
 <function name="IsValid" parent="IGModAudioChannel" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Returns if the sound channel is valid or not.</description>
+	<description>A channel becomes invalid when it is stopped, when playback finishes without looping, or when the sound file fails to load. Always check validity before calling other <page text="IGModAudioChannel">IGModAudioChannel</page> methods on a stored channel, since using an invalid channel will error.</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Is the sound channel valid or not</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Checking a stored channel">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a looping sound channel, stores it, and checks its validity each second. The channel stays valid because it loops, so the message keeps printing until the timer is removed.</description>
+	<code>
+local channel
+
+sound.PlayFile( "sound/music/my_music.wav", "noplay loop", function( snd, id, err )
+	if ( IsValid( snd ) ) then
+		snd:Play()
+		channel = snd
+	end
+end )
+
+timer.Create( "CheckChannel", 1, 0, function()
+	if ( IsValid( channel ) ) then
+		print( "Channel is still playing" )
+	else
+		print( "Channel is gone" )
+	end
+end )
+
+-- Remove the timer when you no longer need it:
+-- timer.Remove( "CheckChannel" )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The callback of <page text="sound.PlayFile">Global.sound.PlayFile</page> passes an <page text="IGModAudioChannel">IGModAudioChannel</page>, which can be invalid if the file failed to load. Checking it with this function is the recommended way to detect that failure.</note>
+
```

--- original/IGModAudioChannel:Pause

 <function name="Pause" parent="IGModAudioChannel" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Pauses the stream. It can be started again using <page>IGModAudioChannel:Play</page></description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example>
+	<description>Plays a sound on the client, pauses it after two seconds, and resumes it after two more seconds. Run this code clientside, for example from the console with `lua_run_cl`.</description>
+	<code>
+local channel = sound.PlayFile( "sound/music/your_music_file.mp3", "noplay", function( snd, errorName, errorString )
+	if ( not IsValid( snd ) ) then
+		ErrorNoHalt( "Failed to play sound: " .. errorName .. " (" .. errorString .. ")\n" )
+		return
+	end
+
+	snd:Play()
+
+	timer.Simple( 2, function()
+		if ( IsValid( snd ) ) then
+			snd:Pause()
+		end
+	end )
+
+	timer.Simple( 4, function()
+		if ( IsValid( snd ) ) then
+			snd:Play()
+		end
+	end )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The channel keeps its playback position while paused. Calling <page>IGModAudioChannel:Play</page> resumes from that position instead of restarting the stream.</note>

## 1948. IGModAudioChannel:Set3DEnabled

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/IGModAudioChannel%3ASet3DEnabled) | Revision: 528191

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091609-lOJtRb97hkTQw2QKl9NC`. Duration: 12.16s. Attempt cost: 0.00067465.


```diff
--- original/IGModAudioChannel:Set3DEnabled
+++ proposed/IGModAudioChannel:Set3DEnabled
@@ -1,11 +1,41 @@
 <function name="Set3DEnabled" parent="IGModAudioChannel" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Sets the 3D mode of the channel. This will affect <page>IGModAudioChannel:Get3DEnabled</page> but not <page>IGModAudioChannel:Is3D</page>.
 
 This feature **requires** the channel to be initially created in 3D mode, i.e. <page>IGModAudioChannel:Is3D</page> should return true or this function will do nothing.
+
+When 3D mode is enabled, the channel's position set with <page>IGModAudioChannel:SetPos</page> is used for spatial audio, so the sound gets quieter and panned as the listener moves away from that position. When 3D mode is disabled, the channel plays at full volume regardless of position.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<added>2020.04.29</added>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="enable" type="boolean">true to enable, false to disable 3D.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Toggling 3D playback on a 3D channel">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a looping 3D channel at a fixed position, then disables 3D mode after 5 seconds so the sound plays at full volume everywhere. The channel is stopped and removed afterwards.</description>
+	<code>
+-- The "3d" flag is required, otherwise Set3DEnabled does nothing.
+sound.PlayFile( "sound/gmod/balloon_pop_cute.wav", "3d noplay", function( channel, errid, errname )
+	if ( not IsValid( channel ) ) then
+		print( "Failed to create channel: " .. errname )
+		return
+	end
+
+	channel:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 0 ) )
+	channel:Play()
+
+	print( "3D enabled: " .. tostring( channel:Get3DEnabled() ) )
+
+	-- After 5 seconds, disable 3D so the sound is heard at full volume everywhere.
+	timer.Simple( 5, function()
+		if ( not IsValid( channel ) ) then return end
+
+		channel:Set3DEnabled( false )
+		print( "3D enabled: " .. tostring( channel:Get3DEnabled() ) )
+
+		channel:Stop()
+	end )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

 <function name="GetInt" parent="IMaterial" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Returns the specified material value as a int, rounds the value if its a float, or nil if the value is not set.
 
 <note>Please note that certain material flags such as `$model` are stored in the `$flags` variable and cannot be directly retrieved with this function. See the full list here: <page>Material Flags</page></note>
 </description>

The `$flags` variable holds the combined bit flags of the material, so individual flags such as `$model` must be checked with <page>Global.bit.band</page> instead of being queried by name.</description>
+	<code>
+local mat = Material( "models/debug/debugwhite" )
+
+local flags = mat:GetInt( "$flags" )
+if flags then
+	print( "$flags is " .. flags )
+
+	if bit.band( flags, 32 ) != 0 then

+end
+	</code>
+</example>

```diff
--- original/IMaterial:GetVector
+++ proposed/IMaterial:GetVector
@@ -1,15 +1,41 @@
 <function name="GetVector" parent="IMaterial" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns the specified material vector, or nil if the value is not set.
+
+Material vectors are shader parameters stored as Vector values, such as the `$color` tint used by many standard shaders. The name must match the parameter exactly, including the leading `$`.
 
 See also <page>IMaterial:GetVectorLinear</page>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="materialVector" type="string">The name of the material vector.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Vector">The color vector</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Reading a material tint">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Prints the `$color` tint of the material applied to the local player's weapon, or a message when the parameter is not set.</description>
+	<code>
+local wep = LocalPlayer():GetActiveWeapon()
+if not IsValid( wep ) then return end
+
+local mat = wep:GetMaterials()[ 1 ]
+if not mat then return end
+
+local material = Material( mat )
+local color = material:GetVector( "$color" )
+
+if color then
+	print( "Tint: ", color )
+else
+	print( "This material has no $color parameter." )
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>Materials fetched with <page>Global.Material</page> are cached and shared. Changing a vector on such a material affects every entity using it.</note>
+
+<note>Not every material exposes every parameter. A parameter that is absent from the material returns nil rather than a zero vector.</note>
+
```

+
+-- Fade from opaque (1) to invisible (0) over one second
+for i = 0, 20 do

+		if not IsValid( mat ) then return end
+		mat:SetFloat( "$alpha", 1 - i / 20 )
+	end )
+end
+
+-- Restore the original value afterwards
+timer.Simple( 1.1, function()
+	if not IsValid( mat ) then return end
+	mat:SetFloat( "$alpha", 1 )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<warning>Materials created with <page>Global.Material</page> or fetched with <page>Entity:GetMaterial</page> can be shared between entities. Changing a float affects every entity using that material object.</warning>

 <function name="AutoMovement" parent="NPC" type="classfunc">
-	<description>Executes any movement the current sequence may have.</description>
+	<description>Executes any movement the current sequence may have.
+
+Some sequences contain built in movement, such as walking or attacking animations. By default the engine applies this movement automatically. When an NPC is driven manually, for example with <page>NPC:SetMovementActivity</page> disabled or custom AI, this function can be called to apply the sequence's movement manually. It moves the NPC forward along its current facing direction by the amount the current animation frame dictates.
+
+This function should be called every tick while the animated sequence plays, typically from the <page>GM:Think</page> hook or an NPC's <page>ENTITY:Think</page>.</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<added>2021.03.31</added>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="interval" type="number">This is a good place to use <page>Entity:GetAnimTimeInterval</page>.</arg>
 		<arg name="target" type="Entity" default="NULL"></arg>
 	</args>

 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example>
+	<description>Runs on the server. Spawns a manhack like NPC and forces it to play its attack sequence, applying the sequence's built in movement manually each tick. The NPC visibly lunges forward while the animation plays. The NPC is removed after five seconds.</description>
+	<code>
+local npc = ents.Create( "npc_manhack" )
+npc:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 64 ) )
+npc:Spawn()
+
+npc:SetSchedule( SCHED_SCRIPTED_RUN )
+
+local timerName = "AutoMovementExample_" .. npc:EntIndex()
+
+timer.Create( timerName, 0, 0, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( npc ) ) then
+		timer.Remove( timerName )
+		return
+	end
+
+	-- Apply the movement built into the current sequence
+	local moved = npc:AutoMovement( npc:GetAnimTimeInterval() )
+
+	if ( moved ) then
+		debugoverlay.Cross( npc:GetPos(), 8, 0.1, color_white, true )
+	end
+end )
+
+-- Cleanup
+timer.Simple( 5, function()
+	if ( IsValid( npc ) ) then npc:Remove() end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>

 <function name="GetMovementActivity" parent="NPC" type="classfunc">

+	<description>Returns the NPC's current movement activity.
+
+The movement activity is the animation state the NPC uses while walking, running, or otherwise moving around. It changes automatically as the NPC navigates, and can differ from the activity set with <page>NPC:SetMovementActivity</page> if the NPC has started moving.</description>

 <function name="GetTimeEnemyLastReacquired" parent="NPC" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Returns <page>Global.CurTime</page> based time since the enemy was reacquired, meaning it is currently in Line of Sight of the NPC.
+
+Each time the NPC sees the enemy again after losing sight, the timer resets. The returned value is an absolute <page>Global.CurTime</page> timestamp, not a duration. Subtract it from <page>Global.CurTime</page> to get how long the enemy has been continuously visible.
 	</description>
 	<added>2022.06.08</added>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="enemy" type="Entity" default="nil">The enemy to test. Defaults to currently active enemy (<page>NPC:GetEnemy</page>)</arg>

 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example>
+	<description>Runs on the server. A scripted NPC prints how long it has continuously seen its current enemy. The NPC must have an enemy for the value to be meaningful, so this checks <page>NPC:GetEnemy</page> first.</description>
+	<code>
+-- ents.Create and Spawn must be called on the server
+local npc = ents.Create( "npc_combine_s" )
+npc:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 0 ) )
+npc:Spawn()
+
+-- Give the NPC a moment to acquire a target
+local timerName = "CheckEnemyReacquired_" .. npc:EntIndex()
+
+timer.Create( timerName, 1, 10, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( npc ) ) then
+		timer.Remove( timerName )
+		return
+	end
+
+	local enemy = npc:GetEnemy()
+	if ( not IsValid( enemy ) ) then
+		print( "No enemy yet" )
+		return
+	end
+
+	local reacquired = npc:GetTimeEnemyLastReacquired()
+	print( "Enemy visible for " .. math.Round( CurTime() - reacquired, 1 ) .. " seconds" )
+end )
+
+-- Cleanup after the test
+hook.Add( "EntityRemoved", "CleanupReacquiredTest", function( ent )
+	if ( ent == npc ) then
+		timer.Remove( timerName )
+		hook.Remove( "EntityRemoved", "CleanupReacquiredTest" )
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>The printed value grows while the enemy stays in line of sight and drops back near zero each time the NPC loses and regains sight of it.</output>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
--- original/NPC:IsUnreachable
+++ proposed/NPC:IsUnreachable
@@ -1,17 +1,42 @@
 <function name="IsUnreachable" parent="NPC" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Returns true if the entity was remembered as unreachable. The memory is updated automatically from following engine tasks if they failed:
 * TASK_GET_CHASE_PATH_TO_ENEMY
 * TASK_GET_PATH_TO_ENEMY_LKP
 * TASK_GET_PATH_TO_INTERACTION_PARTNER
 * TASK_ANTLIONGUARD_GET_CHASE_PATH_ENEMY_TOLERANCE
 * SCHED_FAIL_ESTABLISH_LINE_OF_FIRE - Combine NPCs, also when failing to change their enemy
+
+The unreachable memory is cleared when the NPC successfully builds a path to the entity, so a return value of true means the last pathing attempt to that entity failed. This can be used to avoid repeatedly ordering an NPC to chase a target it cannot reach, for example a player standing on a high ledge.
 </description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="testEntity" type="Entity">The entity to test.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">If the entity is reachable or not.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Chase only reachable enemies">
+	<description>Runs on the server. A scripted NPC stops chasing its enemy while the enemy is remembered as unreachable and resumes once a path succeeds again.</description>
+	<code>
+local npc = ents.Create( "npc_combine_s" )
+npc:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 0 ) )
+npc:Spawn()
+
+-- Called every AI think, for example from a schedule or think hook
+local function UpdateChase( npc )
+	local enemy = npc:GetEnemy()
+
+	if ( not IsValid( enemy ) ) then return end
+
+	if ( npc:IsUnreachable( enemy ) ) then
+		-- The last pathing attempt to this enemy failed, hold position
+		npc:SetSchedule( SCHED_IDLE_STAND )
+	else
+		npc:SetSchedule( SCHED_CHASE_ENEMY )
+	end
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

+local targetPos
+

+	self:SetModel( "models/alyx.mdl" )
+	self:CapabilitiesAdd( CAP_MOVE_GROUND )
+
+	-- Remember a reachable point near the spawn position
+	targetPos = self:GetPos() + self:GetForward() * 200

+

+end

 <note>This will call either <page>NPC:TaskComplete</page> or <page>NPC:TaskFail</page> for the current schedule and task, forcing the current task to progress to next task or fail. </note>
+
+The position is snapped to the closest node in the navigation mesh, so the NPC does not path to the exact position given. The generated path is stored on the NPC and can be followed with movement tasks such as <page>NPC:TaskMovePath</page>.
 
 See also <page>NPC:NavSetRandomGoal</page>.</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<added>2022.06.08</added>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="pos" type="Vector">The position to calculate a path to.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret type="boolean">Whether path generation was successful or not.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Path an NPC to a position">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Requires a map with a generated navigation mesh. Spawns a Combine soldier, builds a path to a point 500 units ahead of it, and makes it walk along that path. The NPC is removed after 10 seconds.</description>
+	<code>
+local npc = ents.Create( "npc_combine_s" )
+npc:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 0 ) )
+npc:Spawn()
+
+local goalPos = npc:GetPos() + npc:GetForward() * 500
+
+if ( npc:NavSetGoalPos( goalPos ) ) then
+	print( "Path generated successfully" )
+
+	-- Make the NPC walk along the generated path
+	npc:SetSchedule( SCHED_FORCED_GO_RUN )
+else
+	print( "Path generation failed" )
+end
+
+-- Cleanup
+timer.Simple( 10, function()
+	if ( IsValid( npc ) ) then
+		npc:Remove()
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

+	<description>Sets the ideal activity the NPC currently wants to achieve. This is most useful for custom SNPCs.
+
+The NPC will not switch to the activity instantly. The engine transitions to the ideal activity when it can, so the animation may lag behind the call. Call this every time the NPC's state changes, for example in a scripted NPC's think function, to keep the desired activity up to date.
+
+See <page>Enums/ACT</page> for available activities.</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<added>2021.01.27</added>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="" type="number">The ideal activity to set. <page>Enums/ACT</page>.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Switching activities on a scripted NPC">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Assumes `ENT` is a scripted NPC (SENT) whose class file defines this function. The NPC plays its idle activity when calm and switches to walking when it starts moving. The activity is reasserted whenever the state changes.</description>
+	<code>
+function ENT:UpdateActivity()
+	if ( self:IsMoving() ) then
+		self:SetIdealActivity( ACT_WALK )
+	else
+		self:SetIdealActivity( ACT_IDLE )
+	end
+end
+
+-- Call this from ENT:Think or after movement state changes.
+-- The NPC then blends into the requested activity when the engine allows it.
+	</code>
+</example>
```

 To be able to use this, first set <page>NPC:SetIdealActivity</page> to `ACT_DO_NOT_DISTURB`, set this to any sequence with root motion data and call <page>Entity:SetSequence</page> on your desired sequence.  	</args>
 </function>

```diff
--- original/NPC:TaskComplete
+++ proposed/NPC:TaskComplete
@@ -1,9 +1,45 @@
 <function name="TaskComplete" parent="NPC" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Marks the current NPC task as completed.
 
 This is meant to be used alongside <page>NPC:TaskFail</page> to complete or fail custom Lua defined tasks. (<page>Schedule:AddTask</page>)
+
+Call this from within a Lua task function added with <page>Schedule:AddTask</page> once the task's goal is reached. The NPC then moves on to the next task in the schedule. If neither this nor <page>NPC:TaskFail</page> is called, the NPC stays on the current task.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Completing a custom Lua task">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Creates a citizen NPC, gives it a schedule with a custom Lua task, and completes the task from inside the task function so the NPC advances to the next task. The NPC is removed after 10 seconds.</description>
+	<code>
+local npc = ents.Create( "npc_citizen" )
+npc:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 0 ) )
+npc:Spawn()
+
+local schedule = ai_schedule.New( "ExampleSchedule" )
+
+-- A normal engine task
+schedule:AddTask( "FindEnemy" )
+
+-- A custom Lua task that completes itself after 3 seconds
+schedule:AddTask( function( npc )
+	if ( not npc.WaitStart ) then
+		npc.WaitStart = CurTime()
+	end
+
+	if ( CurTime() - npc.WaitStart &gt;= 3 ) then
+		npc.WaitStart = nil
+		npc:TaskComplete()
+	end
+end )
+
+npc:StartSchedule( schedule )
+
+-- Cleanup
+ timer.Simple( 10, function()
+	if ( IsValid( npc ) ) then
+		npc:Remove()
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

 <function name="GetRangeSquaredTo" parent="NextBot" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns squared distance to an entity or a position.
+
+The result is the distance without the square root applied. This is cheaper to compute and useful for range checks. Compare against a squared threshold instead of the actual distance. For example, to check whether something is within 300 units, compare against 300 * 300 = 90000.
 
 See also <page>NextBot:GetRangeTo</page>.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="to" type="Vector">The position to measure distance to. Can be an entity.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">The squared distance</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Checking attack range">
+	<description>
+Runs on the server. A scripted nextbot checks whether the nearest player is within 300 units before attacking. The threshold is squared once so the comparison matches the squared return value.
+	</description>
+	<code>
+local range = 300
+local rangeSq = range * range
+
+-- inside the bot's think or behavior code, where self is the nextbot entity
+local target = self:GetNearestPlayer()
+if not IsValid( target ) then return end
+
+if self:GetRangeSquaredTo( target ) <= rangeSq then
+	-- target is within 300 units, start the attack
+	self:StartAttack( target )
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
```

+* <page>number</page> tolerance - How close we must be to the goal before it can be considered complete. Defaults to `20`.
+* <page>boolean</page> draw - Draw the path. Only visible on listen servers and single player. Defaults to `false`.
+* <page>number</page> maxage - Maximum age of the path before it times out. No timeout when unset.

 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="string">Either `"failed"`, `"stuck"`, `"timeout"` or `"ok"` - depending on how the NPC got on</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>

+	local result = self:MoveToPos( target, {

## 2223. Panel:AnimationThinkInternal

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Panel%3AAnimationThinkInternal) | Revision: 560817

Source: [lua/includes/extensions/client/panel/animation.lua:20](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/9bacca4b786123ac1da54145e625b1db970dbf21/garrysmod/lua/includes/extensions/client/panel/animation.lua#L20-L59)

Matched committed Lua definitions; helper and caller context may be incomplete

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091628-2vcIcKCKiCTgUgddgpQ9`. Duration: 5.64s. Attempt cost: 0.00061913.


```diff
--- original/Panel:AnimationThinkInternal
+++ proposed/Panel:AnimationThinkInternal
@@ -1,10 +1,51 @@
 <function name="AnimationThinkInternal" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<file line="20-L59">lua/includes/extensions/client/panel/animation.lua</file>
 	<description>
 <internal></internal> Performs the per-frame operations required for panel animations.
 
 This is called every frame by <page>PANEL:AnimationThink</page>.
+
+For each animation stored in the panel's `m_AnimList` table it computes the current fraction of the animation from `SysTime()`, applies the animation's easing, calls the animation's `Think` callback with the eased fraction, and removes the animation from the list when it reaches the end. When an animation finishes, its `OnEnd` callback is called before it is removed.
+
+If the panel has a `Term` value set and `SysTime()` has passed it, the panel removes itself immediately instead of processing animations.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Manually driving an animation">
+    <description>Runs on the client. Creates a panel with a manually registered animation table matching the structure AnimationThinkInternal expects, then calls the function directly to advance it. The Think callback prints the eased fraction each call.</description>
+    <code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 200 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+frame.m_AnimList = frame.m_AnimList or {}
+frame.m_AnimList[ 1 ] = {
+	StartTime = SysTime(),
+	EndTime = SysTime() + 2,
+	Ease = 0.5,
+	Think = function( anim, pnl, frac )
+		print( "fraction", frac )
+		pnl:SetAlpha( 255 * frac )
+	end,
+	OnEnd = function( anim, pnl )
+		print( "animation finished" )
+	end
+}
+
+-- Normally called every frame by PANEL:AnimationThink.
+-- Called here once to advance the animation manually.
+frame:AnimationThinkInternal()
+
+-- Cleanup when done with the test panel
+timer.Simple( 3, function()
+	if ( IsValid( frame ) ) then frame:Remove() end
+end )
+    </code>
+    <output>The fraction value printed each call rises from 0 toward 1 over two seconds, the panel fades in, and "animation finished" prints when the fraction reaches 1.</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>The easing behavior depends on the animation's `Ease` value. A value of 0 leaves the fraction unchanged. Negative values produce an ease in out curve. Values between 0 and 1 produce an ease out curve. Values of 1 or greater use `Fraction ^ Ease` directly.</note>
+
+<warning>Do not call this function manually on panels that use the standard animation system. It is already driven every frame by <page>PANEL:AnimationThink</page>, and calling it again will advance animations faster than intended.</warning>
```

```diff
--- original/Panel:Distance
+++ proposed/Panel:Distance
@@ -1,12 +1,58 @@
 <function name="Distance" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<file line="422-L428">lua/includes/extensions/client/panel.lua</file>
-	<description>Returns the linear distance from the center of this panel object and another. **Both panels must have the same parent for this function to work properly.**</description>
+	<description>Returns the linear distance from the center of this panel object and another. **Both panels must have the same parent for this function to work properly.**
+
+The distance is measured between the center points. The center of the target panel is computed from its `x`, `y` position and its width and height. If the target panel is not valid, the function returns `0` instead of a distance.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>

+		<ret name="" type="number">The linear (straight-line) distance between the center of the two objects. Returns `0` if the target panel is invalid.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Finding the closest panel">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates three panels inside one parent frame and uses `Panel:Distance` to find which of them is closest to a marker panel. The result is printed to the console.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 400, 300 )
+frame:SetTitle( "Distance example" )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+local marker = frame:Add( "DPanel" )
+marker:SetPos( 200, 150 )
+marker:SetSize( 20, 20 )
+
+local panels = {}
+for i = 1, 3 do
+	local pnl = frame:Add( "DPanel" )
+	pnl:SetPos( math.random( 0, 350 ), math.random( 0, 250 ) )
+	pnl:SetSize( 40, 40 )
+	panels[ i ] = pnl
+end
+
+-- Find the panel whose center is closest to the marker's center.
+-- All panels share the same parent (frame), so the comparison is valid.
+local closest, closestDist
+for _, pnl in ipairs( panels ) do
+	local dist = marker:Distance( pnl )
+	if ( !closestDist or dist < closestDist ) then
+		closest = pnl
+		closestDist = dist
+	end
+end
+
+print( "Closest panel distance: " .. closestDist )
+
+-- Cleanup when the frame is closed.
+frame.OnRemove = function()
+	for _, pnl in ipairs( panels ) do
+		if ( IsValid( pnl ) ) then pnl:Remove() end
+	end
+end
+	</code>
+	<output>The distance in pixels between the marker and the closest panel, for example `Closest panel distance: 96.5`. The exact value depends on the random panel positions.</output>
+</example>
+
```

If the panel has a drag parent, the call is forwarded to that parent instead. If a drag is already in progress, it is stopped first.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="mouseCode" type="number">The code for the mouse button pressed, passed by, for example, <page>PANEL:OnMousePressed</page>. See the <page>Enums/MOUSE</page>.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>

+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 200 )

+

+panel:Dock( FILL )

+panel:DragMousePress( MOUSE_LEFT )

- The original description said the mouse button was depressed, but the source shows this function ends a drag (calls dragndrop.Drop). The description was expanded to match the implementation while keeping the original first sentence.
- The behavior list (drop menu check, DragClick forwarding on mismatched mouse code, false when not dragging, screen clicker and mouse capture handling) is derived directly from lua/includes/extensions/client/panel/dragdrop.lua lines 444-470.

```diff
--- original/Panel:DragMouseRelease
+++ proposed/Panel:DragMouseRelease
@@ -1,12 +1,55 @@
 <function name="DragMouseRelease" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<file line="440-L466">lua/includes/extensions/client/panel/dragdrop.lua</file>
-	<description>Called to inform the <page>dragndrop</page> that a mouse button has been depressed on a panel object.</description>
+	<description>Called to inform the <page>dragndrop</page> that a mouse button has been depressed on a panel object.
+
+Despite the name, this function ends a drag operation started with <page>Panel:DragMousePress</page>. Call it from <page>PANEL:OnMouseReleased</page> with the same mouse code that started the drag.
+
+Behavior:
+* If a drop menu is open, nothing happens.
+* If a drag is in progress with a different mouse button code, the call is forwarded to <page>Panel:DragClick</page> instead of dropping.
+* If no drag is in progress, the drag state is cleared and `false` is returned.
+* Otherwise the dragged object is dropped, the screen clicker is disabled if it was enabled, and mouse capture is released.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="mouseCode" type="number">The code for the mouse button pressed, passed by, for example, <page>PANEL:OnMouseReleased</page>. See the <page>Enums/MOUSE</page>.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">`true` if an object was being dragged, otherwise `false`.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Making a panel draggable">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a small panel that can be dragged with the left mouse button. The panel prints a message when the drag ends, and is removed after 10 seconds.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 200 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:SetTitle( "Drag source demo" )
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+local draggable = vgui.Create( "DPanel", frame )
+draggable:Dock( FILL )
+draggable:DockMargin( 5, 5, 5, 5 )
+
+function draggable:OnMousePressed( mouseCode )
+	self:MouseCapture( true )
+	self:DragMousePress( mouseCode )
+end
+
+function draggable:OnMouseReleased( mouseCode )
+	self:MouseCapture( false )
+
+	-- Returns true only if a drag was actually in progress and has now ended
+	local wasDragging = self:DragMouseRelease( mouseCode )
+
+	if ( wasDragging ) then
+		print( "Drag finished with mouse code " .. mouseCode )
+	end
+end
+
+-- Cleanup for the demo panel
+timer.Simple( 10, function()
+	if ( IsValid( frame ) ) then frame:Remove() end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

+	surface.DrawRect( x, y, w, h )

```diff
--- original/Panel:FocusPrevious
+++ proposed/Panel:FocusPrevious
@@ -1,5 +1,37 @@
 <function name="FocusPrevious" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
-	<description>Focuses the previous panel in the focus queue.</description>
+	<description>Focuses the previous panel in the focus queue.
+
+The focus queue is the order in which panels were added to the focus chain, typically via <page text="Panel:MakePopup">Panel:MakePopup</page> or keyboard input focus. This moves keyboard focus one panel backward, which is useful for tab style navigation between text entries.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Navigating between text entries">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a frame with two text entries. Pressing the bound key moves focus to the previous entry in the focus queue, so the caret jumps back to the first entry.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 120 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:SetTitle( "Focus test" )
+
+local first = vgui.Create( "DTextEntry", frame )
+first:Dock( TOP )
+first:DockMargin( 5, 5, 5, 0 )
+
+local second = vgui.Create( "DTextEntry", frame )
+second:Dock( TOP )
+second:DockMargin( 5, 5, 5, 5 )
+
+frame:MakePopup()
+second:RequestFocus()
+
+-- Press the key bound to +menu (default Q) to move focus back one panel
+hook.Add( "Think", "FocusPreviousExample", function()
+	if input.IsKeyDown( KEY_Q ) then
+		frame:FocusPrevious()
+		hook.Remove( "Think", "FocusPreviousExample" )
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The panel calling this method should be part of the focus chain, usually a popup frame created with <page text="Panel:MakePopup">Panel:MakePopup</page>. Calling it on a panel with no focus queue has no visible effect.</note>
```

- Added explanation of the summation behavior and the non descendant case, both directly visible in the supplied implementation at lua/includes/extensions/client/panel.lua lines 442 to 458. The loop stops when pnl has no parent, so a panel that is not a descendant yields the sum of its own and its ancestors' positions rather than an error or nil. The example output is the deterministic result of the default DFrame title bar height (25) plus the inner panel's docked position within middle; if a reviewer considers the exact numbers too environment dependent, the output tag can be removed while keeping the print.

```diff

 <function name="GetChildPosition" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<file line="442-L458">lua/includes/extensions/client/panel.lua</file>
-	<description>Gets a child object's position relative to this panel object. The number of levels is not relevant; the child may have many parents between itself and the object on which the method is called.</description>
+	<description>Gets a child object's position relative to this panel object. The number of levels is not relevant; the child may have many parents between itself and the object on which the method is called.
+
+The position is calculated by summing the `x` and `y` fields of the child panel and each of its parents until this panel is reached. If the given panel is not a descendant of this panel, the loop stops when the panel has no parent, and the returned position is the sum of the panel's own position and all of its ancestors' positions.</description>

 </function>
