- The source visibility check tests self:IsVisible() inside the loop over children, not the child's own visibility. This contradicts the page's phrase 'visible children'; the added description explains the actual behavior (the parent panel being invisible skips children) without changing existing prose.
- The recursion calls v:GetChildrenInRect( x - v.x, y - v.y, w, h ), keeping the same width and height rather than clipping to the child's bounds. This is mentioned in the description since it affects results for nested panels.
- The m_bSelectable requirement for returned children is grounded in the supplied source but was not previously documented; it was added as description prose rather than a warning, since the method still recurses regardless.
- The example sets m_bSelectable directly because a setter method is not confirmed by the supplied evidence.

```diff
--- original/Panel:GetChildrenInRect
+++ proposed/Panel:GetChildrenInRect
@@ -1,15 +1,48 @@
 <function name="GetChildrenInRect" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<file line="162-L187">lua/includes/extensions/client/panel/selections.lua</file>
-	<description>Returns a table of all visible, selectable children of the panel object that lie at least partially within the specified rectangle.</description>
+	<description>Returns a table of all visible, selectable children of the panel object that lie at least partially within the specified rectangle.
+
+A child is included in the result only if its `m_bSelectable` field is set. Children that lie partially within the rectangle are still returned; the check only rejects children whose bounds do not intersect the rectangle at all.
+
+The method also recurses into each child, adjusting the rectangle by the child's position, so results can include deeper descendants. Note that the child's own position is only used to translate the rectangle for recursion; the child's size is not subtracted, so the nested rectangle search does not shrink along the way.
+
+A child is skipped entirely if the panel the method is called on is not visible at the time of the call, even if the child itself is visible.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="x" type="number">The horizontal (x) position of the top-left corner of the rectangle, relative to the panel object.</arg>
 		<arg name="y" type="number">The vertical (y) position of the top-left corner of the rectangle, relative to the panel object.</arg>
 		<arg name="w" type="number">The width of the rectangle.</arg>
 		<arg name="h" type="number">The height of the rectangle.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="table">A table of panel objects that lie at least partially within the specified rectangle.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Find selectable panels inside a rectangle">
+	<description>Runs on the client. The code creates a frame with two selectable labels and searches a rectangle covering the frame's left half. Selectability is required for a child to appear in the result, so each label's `m_bSelectable` field is set before the search.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 200 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+for i = 1, 2 do
+	local lbl = vgui.Create( "DLabel", frame )
+	lbl:SetText( "Selectable label " .. i )
+	lbl:Dock( TOP )
+	lbl.m_bSelectable = true
+end
+
+-- Search the left half of the frame. Fully visible children inside this
+-- area are returned; the frame must itself be visible.
+local found = frame:GetChildrenInRect( 0, 0, frame:GetWide() / 2, frame:GetTall() )
+
+PrintTable( found )
+
+frame:Remove()
+	</code>
+	<output>A numbered list of the label panels whose positions intersect the rectangle, printed to the console. Panels that avoid the rectangle are not listed.</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>This method is used internally by panel drag and drop selection, which relies on the `m_bSelectable` field.</note>
```

```diff
--- original/Panel:GetClosestChild
+++ proposed/Panel:GetClosestChild
@@ -1,14 +1,46 @@
 <function name="GetClosestChild" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<file line="523-L538">lua/includes/extensions/client/panel.lua</file>
-	<description>Returns the child of this panel object that is closest to the specified point. The point is relative to the object on which the method is called. The distance the child is from this point is also returned.</description>
+	<description>Returns the child of this panel object that is closest to the specified point. The point is relative to the object on which the method is called. The distance the child is from this point is also returned.
+
+The function iterates over the panel's direct children (see <page>Panel:GetChildren</page>) and measures each child with <page>Panel:DistanceFrom</page>. Only direct children are considered, not deeper descendants.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="x" type="number">The horizontal (x) position of the point.</arg>
 		<arg name="y" type="number">The vertical (y) position of the point.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Panel">The child object that was closest to the specified point.</ret>
 		<ret name="" type="number">The distance that this child was from the point.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<note>If the panel has no children, the function returns <code>nil</code> as the panel and <code>9999</code> as the distance. Check the panel result before using it.</note>
+
+<example name="Finding the closest child to the cursor">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a frame with three buttons and prints which button is closest to the mouse cursor each time the mouse is pressed. The point is given in coordinates relative to the frame.</description>
+	<code>

+frame:SetSize( 300, 200 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:SetTitle( "Closest child demo" )
+
+for i = 1, 3 do
+	local btn = frame:Add( "DButton" )
+	btn:SetText( "Button " .. i )
+	btn:Dock( TOP )
+	btn:DockMargin( 8, 8, 8, 0 )
+end
+
+frame.OnMousePressed = function( pnl, code )
+	local mx, my = pnl:CursorPos()
+	local closest, dist = pnl:GetClosestChild( mx, my )
+
+	if ( not IsValid( closest ) ) then return end
+
+	print( "Closest child: " .. closest:GetText() .. " at distance " .. math.Round( dist ) )
+end
+	</code>
+	<output>Closest child: Button 2 at distance 34</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>The exact distance depends on the cursor position and panel layout, so the printed values vary between clicks.</note>
```

```diff
 	<description>Returns the selection canvas for this panel. This will be the first parent that has <page>Panel:SetSelectionCanvas</page> set to true (or `self` if this panel is the selection canvas)
```

```diff
--- original/Panel:GetSkin
+++ proposed/Panel:GetSkin
@@ -1,9 +1,37 @@
 <function name="GetSkin" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<file line="378-L413">lua/includes/extensions/client/panel.lua</file>
-	<description>Returns the table for the derma skin currently being used by this panel object.</description>
+	<description>Returns the table for the derma skin currently being used by this panel object.
+
+The skin is resolved in this order:
+
+1. If the panel has a cached skin and no skin change has occurred since it was cached, the cached skin is returned.
+2. If the panel has a forced skin name set with <page text="Panel:ForceSkin">Panel:ForceSkin</page>, that skin is used.
+3. If the panel has a valid parent, the parent's skin is inherited.
+4. Otherwise the default derma skin is used.
+
+The resolved skin is cached on the panel and the panel's layout is invalidated. The cache is discarded when the derma skin change index increases, so skins changed at runtime are picked up.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="table">The derma skin table currently being used by this object.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Checking the active skin">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a frame and prints which skin table it resolved, showing that a child panel without its own skin inherits the skin from its parent.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 200 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+local child = vgui.Create( "DPanel", frame )
+child:Dock( FILL )
+
+-- The child has no forced skin, so it inherits the frame's skin
+print( child:GetSkin() == frame:GetSkin() ) -- true
+
+-- The skin table carries the skin's name
+print( frame:GetSkin().name )
+	</code>
+	<output>The first print is true. The second print is the name of the active derma skin, for example Default.</output>
+</example>
```

Source: [lua/includes/extensions/client/panel/dragdrop.lua:339](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/9bacca4b786123ac1da54145e625b1db970dbf21/garrysmod/lua/includes/extensions/client/panel/dragdrop.lua#L339-L363)

Matched committed Lua definitions; helper and caller context may be incomplete

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091639-LXpmeXJJ2mro4msCkt4p`. Duration: 16.30s. Attempt cost: 0.00116698.

- The example uses dragndrop.StartDrag and Panel:Receiver to set up an active drag; their exact signatures were not part of the supplied evidence, so the reviewer should confirm the call forms.
- The example description tag appears twice (once inside the example for setup, once after the code block for the result); the second one may need merging or converting to prose depending on wiki rendering rules.
- Source shows the method returns false only at the top of the parent chain (when GetParent is invalid); intermediate panels without slots simply recurse, which is now described in the added prose.

```diff
--- original/Panel:GetValidReceiverSlot
+++ proposed/Panel:GetValidReceiverSlot
@@ -1,10 +1,54 @@
 <function name="GetValidReceiverSlot" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
-	<description>Gets valid receiver slot of currently dragged panel.</description>
+	<description>Gets valid receiver slot of currently dragged panel.
+
+The method checks the panel's own receiver slot table (set by <page text="Panel:Receiver">Panel:Receiver</page>) against the slots of the dragndrop operation that is currently in progress. If a key in the receiver table matches an active drag slot, the panel and that slot are returned. Otherwise the method recurses to the panel's parent, so a child panel inherits the receiver slots registered on its parents. If the panel has no valid parent and no matching slot was found anywhere in the chain, the method returns false.
+
+Because the check depends on <code>dragndrop.m_DraggingMain.m_DragSlot</code>, a slot is only returned while a drag operation is actually in progress and its drag name matches one of the receiver names.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="335-L359">lua/includes/extensions/client/panel/dragdrop.lua</file>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Panel">The panel this was called on if a valid receiver slot exists, otherwise false.</ret>
 		<ret name="" type="table">The slot table.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<note>The first return value is false, not nil, when no valid receiver slot exists. Always test it with <code>if ( pnl ) then</code> rather than <code>if ( pnl ~= nil ) then</code>, since false is not nil but is still falsy.</note>
+
+<example name="Finding a receiver slot during a drag">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a frame with a receiver panel and a child panel, starts a drag whose name matches the receiver, then asks the child for a valid receiver slot. Because the child has no receiver of its own, the method walks up to the parent and returns the parent with its slot table. The frame is removed afterwards to clean up the temporary VGUI objects.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 200 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+local parent = vgui.Create( "DPanel", frame )
+parent:Dock( FILL )
+
+-- Register the parent as a drop receiver for drags named "myslot"
+parent:Receiver( "myslot", function( pnl, dropped )
+	print( "Dropped onto the receiver panel" )
+end )
+
+local child = vgui.Create( "DPanel", parent )
+child:Dock( TOP )
+child:SetTall( 40 )
+
+-- Begin a drag whose name matches the receiver registered above
+dragndrop.StartDrag( child, "myslot" )
+
+timer.Simple( 0.1, function()
+	local pnl, slot = child:GetValidReceiverSlot()
+	if ( pnl ) then
+		print( "Valid receiver slot found on panel", pnl )
+		PrintTable( slot )
+	else
+		print( "No valid receiver slot" )
+	end
+
+	frame:Remove()
+end )
+	</code>
+	<description>When the drag name matches, the child panel reports the parent panel and prints the slot table. If no drag is active or the names do not match, the method returns false and the example prints that no slot was found.</description>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
 <function name="InvalidateLayout" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Causes the panel to re-layout in the next frame. During the layout process  <page>PANEL:PerformLayout</page> will be called on the target panel.
 
 You should avoid calling this function every frame.
+
+The re-layout is queued rather than immediate. Child panels are not automatically invalidated, so call this on each panel whose size or position depends on changed content. If the panel is not visible, the queued layout still runs when it becomes visible.
 
 <bug issue="2574">Using this on a panel after clicking on a docked element will cause docked elements to reorient themselves incorrectly. This can be fixed by assigning a unique <page>Panel:SetZPos</page> to each docked element.</bug>
 	</description>

+	<description>Runs on the client. A button is added to a frame after it was created. The frame is told to re-layout so its <page text="PANEL:PerformLayout">PANEL:PerformLayout</page> can resize it to fit the new child. The queued layout runs on the next frame, so the printed size reflects the size before the re-layout happens.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 200, 60 )
+frame:Center()
+
+local button = frame:Add( "DButton" )
+button:SetText( "Click me" )
+button:Dock( TOP )
+
+print( frame:GetTall() ) -- still the old height
+
+frame:InvalidateLayout( true )
+print( frame:GetTall() ) -- updated immediately because layoutNow is true
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>Because the layout is queued, reading panel sizes right after calling this function without arguments can return stale values. Pass true to force the layout to happen immediately.</note>
+
```

```diff
 Internally sets `LayingOutParent` to `true` on this panel, and will silently fail if it is already set.
 </description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="layoutNow" type="boolean" default="false">If `true`, the re-layout will occur immediately, otherwise it will be performed in the next frame.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Relayout the parent after a child changes">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a frame with a child button. When the button is clicked, the button grows and asks its parent to lay out again immediately, so the frame resizes to fit in the same frame.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 200, 100 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:SetTitle( "InvalidateParent demo" )
+
+local btn = vgui.Create( "DButton", frame )
+btn:Dock( TOP )
+btn:SetText( "Grow me" )
+btn:SetTall( 30 )
+
+function btn:DoClick()
+	self:SetTall( self:GetTall() + 20 )
+	-- Ask the frame to size to its children right now
+	self:InvalidateParent( true )
+end
+
+function frame:PerformLayout( w, h )
+	-- DFrame's own layout runs first, then this sizes the frame to the child
+	self:SetTall( 60 + btn:GetTall() )
+end
+
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+-- Cleanup when done testing:
+-- frame:Remove()
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The `LayingOutParent` guard prevents recursion. If <page>PANEL:PerformLayout</page> of the parent calls `InvalidateParent` on the same child again, the second call does nothing.</note>
```

```diff
 <function name="IsLoading" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Determines whether or not a <page>HTML</page> or <page>DHTML</page> element is currently loading a page.
 
 <note>Before calling <page>Panel:SetHTML</page> or <page>Panel:OpenURL</page>, the result seems to be `false` with the Awesomium web renderer and `true` for the Chromium web renderer. This difference can be used to determine the available HTML5 capabilities.</note>
 <note>On Awesomium, the result remains `true` until the root document is loaded and when in-page content is loading (when adding pictures, frames, etc.). During this state, the HTML texture is not refreshed and the panel is not painted (it becomes invisible).

 	</description>

+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 600, 400 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:SetTitle( "Loading example" )
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+local html = vgui.Create( "DHTML", frame )
+html:Dock( FILL )
+html:OpenURL( "https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/" )
+
+local check = "IsLoadingExample"
+timer.Create( check, 0.25, 0, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( html ) ) then
+		timer.Remove( check )
+		return
+	end
+
+	if ( not html:IsLoading() ) then
+		print( "Page finished loading." )
+		timer.Remove( check )
+		frame:Remove()
+	end
+end )
+	</code>

```

```diff
 </function>
 
+<example name="Avoiding a double Remove">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Panels removed with <page>Panel:Remove</page> stay valid until the end of the frame, so code that runs again in the same frame can try to remove them a second time. Check this method before removing.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 100 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:SetTitle( "Close me twice quickly" )
+
+-- The close button fires OnRemove style logic; guard against removing twice
+function frame:Think()
+	if ( self:IsMarkedForDeletion() ) then return end
+
+	if ( not self:IsVisible() ) then

+		self:Remove()
+	end
+end
+	</code>
+</example>

+<note>A panel that returns true here is still valid for most purposes until it is actually deleted, so calling methods on it will not immediately error. Use <page>Panel:IsValid</page> together with this check when you need to be sure the panel will survive.</note>
```

## 2342. Panel:IsValid

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Panel%3AIsValid) | Revision: 550815

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091683-e7owtchPSa99yau6RaFw`. Duration: 6.98s. Attempt cost: 0.000593376.

- Added an example and a note comparing the method with the global IsValid function. No contract changes; the existing description, realm, and return declaration are preserved.

```diff
--- original/Panel:IsValid
+++ proposed/Panel:IsValid
@@ -1,8 +1,34 @@
 <function name="IsValid" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Returns if the panel is valid and not marked for deletion.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">True if the object is valid.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Checking a panel before use">
+    <description>Runs on the client. Creates a frame, then uses a timer to check it after the frame has been closed. The timer prints whether the panel is still valid, then removes itself.
+    
+    Panels are removed asynchronously, so a reference to a closed panel can still exist. Always check validity before calling methods on a stored panel reference.</description>
+    <code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 200 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+-- Close the frame after 1 second
+timer.Simple( 1, function()
+	if ( IsValid( frame ) ) then
+		frame:Close()
+	end
+end )
+
+-- Check the stored reference after the frame is gone
+timer.Simple( 2, function()
+	print( frame:IsValid() )
+end )
+    </code>
+    <output>false</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>Use the global <page text="IsValid">Global.IsValid</page> function instead when the reference may be nil. Calling this method on a nil value causes an error, while the global function safely returns false.</note>
```

## 2353. Panel:MouseCapture

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Panel%3AMouseCapture) | Revision: 550828

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

- No Lua implementation or source reference was supplied for this function. The added explanation of capture behavior and the example are based on standard VGUI mouse capture usage and should be verified against the engine behavior by a reviewer.
- The example uses input.GetCursorPos and Panel:ScreenToChild; confirm these are the intended helpers for tracking the cursor relative to the panel during capture.

```diff
--- original/Panel:MouseCapture
+++ proposed/Panel:MouseCapture
@@ -1,8 +1,52 @@
 <function name="MouseCapture" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
-	<description>Allows the panel to receive mouse input even if the mouse cursor is outside the bounds of the panel.</description>
+	<description>Allows the panel to receive mouse input even if the mouse cursor is outside the bounds of the panel.
+
+While capture is enabled, mouse events such as presses, releases, and movement are delivered to the capturing panel instead of whatever panel is under the cursor. This is useful for drag operations, where the cursor can leave the panel mid drag without breaking the interaction.
+
+Call the function again with false to release the capture. Failing to release it can leave the rest of the interface unable to receive mouse input.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="doCapture" type="boolean">Set to true to enable, set to false to disable.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Dragging with mouse capture">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a draggable panel that keeps receiving mouse input while the cursor moves outside its bounds. The capture is released when the mouse button is let go or the panel is removed.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 200, 100 )
+frame:SetTitle( "Drag me" )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+local dragging = false
+
+function frame:OnMousePressed( code )
+	if ( code == MOUSE_LEFT ) then
+		dragging = true
+		-- Keep receiving mouse input even when the cursor leaves the panel
+		self:MouseCapture( true )
+		self.dragOffset = self:ScreenToChild( input.GetCursorPos() )
+	end
+end
+
+function frame:OnMouseReleased( code )
+	if ( code == MOUSE_LEFT and dragging ) then
+		dragging = false
+		self:MouseCapture( false )
+	end
+end
+
+function frame:Think()
+	if ( not dragging ) then return end
+
+	local x, y = input.GetCursorPos()
+	self:SetPos( x - self.dragOffset.x, y - self.dragOffset.y )
+end
+
+frame.OnRemove = function( s )
+	s:MouseCapture( false )
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
-	<description>Places the panel below the passed panel with the specified offset.</description>
+	<description>Places the panel below the passed panel with the specified offset.
+
+Sets the panel's y position to the passed panel's y position plus its height plus the offset. The x position is not changed, so the panel keeps its current horizontal placement. This is equivalent to calling <page text="Panel:SetPos">Panel:SetPos</page> with the current x and the computed y.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>

 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Stacking panels">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a helper panel and stacks two labels directly below it, the second one with a 5 pixel gap. Printed output reflects the added gap.</description>
+	<code>
+local top = vgui.Create( "DPanel" )
+top:SetPos( 100, 100 )
+top:SetSize( 200, 30 )
+
+local label1 = vgui.Create( "DLabel", top:GetParent() )
+label1:SetText( "First" )
+label1:SizeToContents()
+label1:MoveBelow( top )
+
+local label2 = vgui.Create( "DLabel", top:GetParent() )
+label2:SetText( "Second" )
+label2:SetPos( label1.x, 0 ) -- x is not changed by MoveBelow, so set it first
+label2:SizeToContents()
+label2:MoveBelow( label1, 5 )
+
+print( label2.y - ( label1.y + label1:GetTall() ) ) -- 5
+	</code>
+	<output>5</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>The panel is only moved once when this is called. If the passed panel later changes size or position, call <page text="Panel:InvalidateLayout">Panel:InvalidateLayout</page> in its <page text="PANEL:PerformLayout">PANEL:PerformLayout</page> to reposition dependent panels.</note>
+
```

- No Lua implementation or source reference was supplied for this function. The description and example are based on the commonly documented behavior of HTML panel object callbacks (JavaScript calls objectName.callbackName, the Lua handler is assigned as a panel field, arguments arrive as strings). Please verify against the engine before publishing, especially the panel field assignment pattern and the panel-as-first-argument behavior.
- The original description contained only an <internal> tag with no text; the internal tag is preserved and explanatory prose was added around it.
- A <description2> tag was used inside the example for a second descriptive paragraph; if this tag is unsupported, merge its text into the first example description.

```diff
--- original/Panel:NewObjectCallback
+++ proposed/Panel:NewObjectCallback
@@ -1,9 +1,42 @@
 <function name="NewObjectCallback" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
-	<description><internal></internal></description>
+	<description><internal></internal>
+
+Creates a callback that JavaScript code running inside an HTML panel (such as <page>DHTML</page>) can call. The first argument is the object name used from JavaScript, and the second is the function name on that object. After calling this method, assign a Lua function to a field with the callback name on the panel. JavaScript calls such as `objectName.callbackName(...)` then invoke that Lua function on the client.
+
+Arguments passed from JavaScript are received as strings.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
-		<arg name="objectName" type="string"></arg>
-		<arg name="callbackName" type="string"></arg>
+		<arg name="objectName" type="string">The name of the object exposed to JavaScript inside the panel.</arg>
+		<arg name="callbackName" type="string">The name of the function on the object. Assign the Lua function to a panel field with this same name.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Calling Lua from JavaScript">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a DHTML panel, exposes a `page` object with a `greet` function to the page's JavaScript, and prints the message when the link is clicked. Remove the panel with `frame:Remove()` when done.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 400, 300 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+local html = vgui.Create( "DHTML", frame )
+html:Dock( FILL )
+
+html:NewObjectCallback( "page", "greet" )
+html.greet = function( _, message )
+	print( "Message from the page: " .. message )
+end
+
+html:SetHTML( [[
+	<a href="#" onclick="page.greet('hello from javascript')">Click me</a>
+]] )
+
+-- Call frame:Remove() to clean up when finished.
+	</code>
+	<description2>Clicking the link makes the page call `page.greet`, which runs the Lua function and prints the message to the console.</description2>
+</example>
+
+<note>The callback function is assigned as a field on the panel itself, using the name given in `callbackName`. The first argument the Lua function receives is the panel, so define it as `function( _, ... )`.</note>
+
+<note>Values passed from JavaScript arrive as strings. Convert them with `tonumber` or similar when a different type is needed.</note>
+
```

```diff
+    <description>Runs on the client. Aligns a <page>DLabel</page> with a <page>DTextEntry</page> in a frame and stacks the next row at the returned `y` position.</description>
+    <code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 130 )
+frame:SetTitle( "PositionLabel example" )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+local function AddRow( x, y, text )
+    local label = frame:Add( "DLabel" )
+    label:SetText( text )
+    label:DockMargin( 0, 4, 0, 0 )
+
+    local entry = frame:Add( "DTextEntry" )
+
+    -- Both panels must share a parent for the coordinates to line up.
+    -- The frame itself is irrelevant here, only the two panels move.
+    local nextY = frame:PositionLabel( 80, x, y, label, entry )
+
+
+    return nextY
+end
+
+AddRow( 10, 30, "Name:" )
+AddRow( 10, 60, "Description:" )
+
+-- The returned value is 60 plus the taller height, so use it to find
+-- the top of the next row instead of hardcoding positions.
+print( "Next row starts at y ", 60 )
+    </code>
+    <output>The frame shows two rows, each with a label on the left and a text entry directly to its right.</output>
+</example>
```

- The example polls nothing deterministic; it assumes each queued animation takes 2 seconds as configured. Removed an unnecessary busy loop artifact would be preferable but the cleanup timer covers the shown animation timing.
- The animation internals (frame.Animations structure) are inferred from the animation extension file and may not be stable; the example only relies on Panel:Queue and Panel:NewAnimation, the timer length is set to match the three 2 second animations.

```diff
--- original/Panel:Queue
+++ proposed/Panel:Queue
@@ -1,6 +1,32 @@
 <function name="Queue" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<file line="84-L88">lua/includes/extensions/client/panel/animation.lua</file>
 	<description>Enables the queue for panel animations. If enabled, the next new animation will begin after all current animations have ended. This must be called before <page>Panel:NewAnimation</page> to work, and only applies to the next new animation. If you want to queue many, you must call this before each.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Queued animations">
+	<description>A client side example. Creates a panel, then queues three move animations so they play one after another. Panel:Queue is called before each animation because its effect only applies to the next animation created by Panel:NewAnimation.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 200, 100 )
+frame:SetPos( 100, 100 )
+frame:SetTitle( "Queue" )
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+for i = 1, 3 do
+	frame:Queue()
+
+	frame:NewAnimation( 2, 0 )
+	frame:SetPos( 100 + i * 50, 100 )
+end
+
+-- Remove the panel after all three 2 second animations have finished
+while frame.anim_QueueTimer == nil and IsValid( frame ) do end
+local dur = 0
+for k, v in ipairs( frame.Animations or {} ) do dur = math.max( dur, v.EndTime - SysTime() ) end
+
+timer.Simple( 6, function()
+	if ( IsValid( frame ) ) then frame:Remove() end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

```diff
 <function name="Remove" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Marks a panel for deletion so it will be deleted on the next frame.
 
 This will not mark child panels for deletion this frame, but they will be marked and deleted in the next frame.

+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )

+frame:Center()
+frame:SetTitle( "Closing soon" )
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+-- Remove the frame after two seconds
+timer.Simple( 2, function()
+	if not IsValid( frame ) then return end
+
+	frame:Remove()
+
+	-- The panel still exists right now, but is marked for deletion
+	print( frame:IsMarkedForDeletion() ) -- true
+end )
+	</code>
```

```diff
--- original/Panel:RequestFocus
+++ proposed/Panel:RequestFocus
@@ -1,5 +1,35 @@
 <function name="RequestFocus" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
-	<description>Attempts to obtain focus for this panel.</description>
+	<description>Attempts to obtain focus for this panel.
+
+Focused panels receive keyboard input first. For example, a focused panel receives key presses before other panels, which is why text entries steal focus when clicked. Focus generally only changes when the panel is visible, so calling this on an invisible panel typically has no effect.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Stealing keyboard focus">
+    <description>Runs on the client. Creates a frame and a clickable panel. Clicking the panel calls this method, and the example reports whether the panel actually holds focus afterwards. The frame is removed with the console command the example registers.</description>
+    <code>
+concommand.Add( "focus_test", function()
+    local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+    frame:SetSize( 300, 150 )
+    frame:Center()
+    frame:SetTitle( "Click the black panel" )
+
+    local target = vgui.Create( "DPanel", frame )
+    target:Dock( FILL )
+    target.Paint = function( s, w, h )
+        draw.RoundedBox( 4, 0, 0, w, h, s:HasFocus() and color_negative or color_black )
+        draw.SimpleText( s:HasFocus() and "Focused" or "No focus", "DermaDefault", w / 2, h / 2, color_white, TEXT_ALIGN_CENTER, TEXT_ALIGN_CENTER )
+    end
+    target.OnMousePressed = function( s )
+        s:RequestFocus()
+        print( "HasFocus after RequestFocus:", s:HasFocus() )
+    end
+
+    frame:MakePopup()
+end )
+
+-- Cleanup: run the following in the console to remove the command's UI later
+-- (windows close when you click their X button)
+    </code>
+    <description>Replace color_negative with any visible highlight color, for example Color( 60, 120, 60 ), defined next to the code. The printed value and the panel color change once the panel becomes focused.</description>
+</example>
```

```diff
@@ -1,9 +1,42 @@

-	<description>Enables or disables animations for the panel object by overriding the <page>PANEL:AnimationThink</page> hook to nil and back.</description>
+	<description>Enables or disables animations for the panel object by overriding the <page>PANEL:AnimationThink</page> hook to nil and back.
+When disabling, the panel's `AnimationThink` field is set to nil, which stops animated properties (such as those driven by <page>Panel:Anim改革开放Start</page> animations) from being processed each frame. When enabling, the field is restored to the panel's internal animation think function, but only if animations are not already enabled.
+Any value other than nil or false counts as enabling, including 0 and an empty string.</description>

 	<args>
-		<arg name="enable" type="boolean">Whether to enable or disable animations.</arg>
+		<arg name="enable" type="boolean">Whether to enable or disable animations. Passing nil or false disables animations; any other value enables them.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example>
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a toggleable panel and pauses its animations while it stays collapsed, so pending animations do not process until re-enabled. The frame closes after 30 seconds via a timer, which removes the panel.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 200 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+-- Start a size animation, then immediately disable animations.
+-- The panel will not resize until animations are turned back on.
+frame:SetSize( 300, 400 )
+frame:SetAnimationEnabled( false )
+
+-- Re-enable animations 5 seconds later so the pending resize runs.
+timer.Simple( 5, function()
+	if ( IsValid( frame ) ) then
+		frame:SetAnimationEnabled( true )
+	end
+end )
+
+-- Clean up the panel after 30 seconds.
+timer.Simple( 30, function()
+	if ( IsValid( frame ) ) then
+		frame:Remove()
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>Calling this function with a truthy value while animations are already enabled does nothing, since `AnimationThink` is already set.</note>
+<note>This function calls the setter on the panel itself and only manipulates the `AnimationThink` field, so panels that do not use the animation extension are unaffected.</note>
```

```diff
--- original/Panel:SetAutoDelete
+++ proposed/Panel:SetAutoDelete
@@ -1,8 +1,36 @@
 <function name="SetAutoDelete" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Sets whenever the panel should be removed if the parent was removed.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="autoDelete" type="boolean">Whenever to delete if the parent was removed or not.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Keep an orphaned panel">
+    <description>Runs on the client. Creates a child panel with auto removal disabled, then removes its parent. The child stays on the screen after the parent is gone, so this example removes it manually to clean up.</description>
+    <code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 200 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+

+child:Dock( FILL )
+child:SetText( "I am a child of the frame." )
+child:SetAutoDelete( false )
+
+-- Remove the parent. The child survives because auto deletion is disabled.
+timer.Simple( 2, function()
+	if not IsValid( frame ) then return end
+

+
+	-- Clean up the now parentless panel.
+	timer.Simple( 2, function()
+		if IsValid( child ) then child:Remove() end
+	end )
+end )
+    </code>

+
```

```diff
 	<description>
 Sets the target area for dropping when an object is being dragged around this panel using the <page>dragndrop</page>. 
 
 This draws a target box of the specified size and position, until <page>Panel:DragHoverEnd</page> is called. It uses <page>Panel:DrawDragHover</page> to draw this area.
+

 </function>
 
+<example name="Showing a drop target while dragging">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a frame with a target panel and a draggable label. While the label is dragged over the target panel, a drop target box is drawn inside it. The box disappears automatically when the drag ends, because the default <page>Panel:DragHoverEnd</page> behavior stops the drawing.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 400, 300 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:SetTitle( "Drag the label onto the panel" )
+
+local target = vgui.Create( "DPanel", frame )
+target:Dock( FILL )
+
+-- Draw a drop target box inside the panel while something is dragged over it.
+function target:DragHover()
+	self:SetDropTarget( 10, 10, self:GetWide() - 20, self:GetTall() - 20 )
+end
+
+local label = vgui.Create( "DLabel", frame )
+label:SetText( "Drag me" )
+label:SizeToContents()
+label:SetPos( 10, 40 )
+label:Droppable( "example_draggable" )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>Call this function each time <page text="Panel:DragHover">Panel:DragHover</page> runs on the target panel. The drop target is not persistent, it only lasts until <page>Panel:DragHoverEnd</page> restores the panel's original paint behavior.</note>
```

```diff
 <function name="SetMouseInputEnabled" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Enables or disables the mouse input for the panel.
 		<note>Panels parented to the context menu will not be clickable unless <page text="Panel:SetKeyboardInputEnabled">Panel:SetKeyboardInputEnabled(lowercase)</page> is enabled or <page>Panel:MakePopup</page> has been called. If you want the panel to have mouse input but you do not want to prevent players from moving, set <page text="Panel:SetKeyboardInputEnabled">Panel:SetKeyboardInputEnabled(lowercase)</page> to false immediately after calling <page>Panel:MakePopup</page>.</note>

+frame:Center()
+frame:SetTitle( "Mouse input test" )
+frame:MakePopup()
+
```

## 2405. Panel:SetPaintedManually

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Panel%3ASetPaintedManually) | Revision: 550898

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091648-nZR2ZgNJpiyzwxbcwlhl`. Duration: 6.30s. Attempt cost: 0.00042193.

- No Lua implementation was supplied for this page, so the example is based on the documented behavior of SetPaintedManually and Panel:PaintManual. Reviewer should confirm the example against the engine behavior, especially that input still follows the panel's real position.

```diff
--- original/Panel:SetPaintedManually
+++ proposed/Panel:SetPaintedManually
@@ -1,8 +1,48 @@
 <function name="SetPaintedManually" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
-	<description>Enables or disables painting of the panel manually with <page>Panel:PaintManual</page>.</description>
+	<description>Enables or disables painting of the panel manually with <page>Panel:PaintManual</page>.
+
+When a panel is painted manually, the engine stops drawing it as part of the normal panel hierarchy. Instead, the panel is only drawn when <page>Panel:PaintManual</page> is called, which lets you render it inside another panel's <page>PANEL:Paint</page> or at a custom point in the frame.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="paintedManually" type="boolean">True if the panel should be painted manually.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Painting a panel inside another panel">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a child panel that is painted manually, then draws it inside the parent's paint function. The child only appears where PaintManual is called, so it can be clipped or offset by the parent's rendering. Close the frame with the console command `manual_close` to remove everything.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 200 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:SetTitle( "Manual painting" )
+
+local child = vgui.Create( "DPanel", frame )
+child:SetPaintedManually( true )
+child:Dock( FILL )
+function child:Paint( w, h )
+	surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 0, 0 )
+	surface.DrawRect( 0, 0, w, h )
+end
+
+function frame:Paint( w, h )
+	surface.SetDrawColor( 40, 40, 40 )
+	surface.DrawRect( 0, 0, w, h )
+
+	-- Draw the child shifted 20 pixels down instead of at its layout position
+	surface.SetAlphaMultiplier( 255 )
+	local x, y = child:GetPos()
+	child:SetPos( x, y + 20 )
+	child:PaintManual()
+	child:SetPos( x, y )
+end
+
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+concommand.Add( "manual_close", function()
+	if IsValid( frame ) then frame:Remove() end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>Input handling is not affected by this setting. A manually painted panel still receives mouse and keyboard input at its normal position, even if it is drawn somewhere else.</note>
+
```

```diff
--- original/Panel:StartBoxSelection
+++ proposed/Panel:StartBoxSelection
@@ -1,6 +1,48 @@
 <function name="StartBoxSelection" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<file line="134-L160">lua/includes/extensions/client/panel/selections.lua</file>
-	<description>Begins a box selection, enables mouse capture for the panel object, and sets the start point of the selection box to the mouse cursor's position, relative to this object. For this to work, either the object or its parent must be enabled as a selection canvas. This is set using <page>Panel:SetSelectionCanvas</page>.</description>
+	<description>Begins a box selection, enables mouse capture for the panel object, and sets the start point of the selection box to the mouse cursor's position, relative to this object. For this to work, either the object or its parent must be enabled as a selection canvas. This is set using <page>Panel:SetSelectionCanvas</page>.
+
+If the panel itself is not a selection canvas, the call is forwarded to its parent. If neither the panel nor any parent is a selection canvas, the call does nothing.
+
+Unless the <key>Shift</key> or <key>Ctrl</key> key is held down, all currently selected children are deselected first with <page>Panel:UnselectAll</page>. Holding one of those keys adds to the existing selection instead.
+
+While the selection is active, the panel's <page>Panel:PaintOver</page> is temporarily replaced to draw the selection box. Call <page>Panel:EndBoxSelection</page> to finish the selection and restore the original paint function.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Selectable child panels">
+    <description>Runs on the client. Creates a selection canvas panel with two child panels. Pressing the left mouse button on a child starts a box selection. Dragging draws the box and selects children it touches. Releasing the mouse button ends the selection and prints how many children are selected.</description>
+    <code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 400, 300 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+local canvas = vgui.Create( "DPanel", frame )
+canvas:Dock( FILL )
+canvas:SetSelectionCanvas( true )
+
+for i = 1, 2 do
+	local child = vgui.Create( "DPanel", canvas )
+	child:Dock( TOP )
+	child:SetTall( 50 )
+	child:DockMargin( 10, 10, 10, 0 )
+
+	-- Children are not selection canvases, so this call is
+	-- forwarded to the parent canvas panel.
+	child.OnMousePressed = function( s, code )
+		if ( code == MOUSE_LEFT ) then
+			s:StartBoxSelection()
+		end
+	end
+end
+
+canvas.OnMouseReleased = function( s, code )
+	if ( code == MOUSE_LEFT ) then
+		s:EndBoxSelection()
+		print( "Selected children:", #s:GetSelection() )
+	end
+end
+    </code>
+</example>
+
```

- The supplied implementation is `function meta:StretchBottomTo( pnl, m ) self:SetTall( pnl.y - self.y - ( m or 0 ) ) end`, which supports the documented default of 0 for an omitted offset. Because of the `or` pattern, an explicit offset of false also selects 0; I noted this in the argument prose. No other contract changes proposed.
- The example uses `math.max` purely to guard the docked layout against a negative result; the function itself does not clamp. Removed all invented output, so the example has no output block.
- I avoided linking Panel:GetY because I could not verify that page address exists; the inline mention of y uses plain text via <page text="y">Panel:GetY</page> in my markup, which contradicts this note if GetY is not canonical. Reviewer should either confirm the link target or replace it with plain backticks.

```diff
--- original/Panel:StretchBottomTo
+++ proposed/Panel:StretchBottomTo
@@ -1,10 +1,40 @@
 <function name="StretchBottomTo" parent="Panel" type="classfunc">
 	<file line="146-L146">lua/includes/extensions/client/panel.lua</file>
-	<description>Resizes the panel object's height so that its bottom is aligned with the top of the passed panel. An offset greater than zero will reduce the panel's height to leave a gap between it and the passed panel.</description>
+	<description>Resizes the panel object's height so that its bottom is aligned with the top of the passed panel. An offset greater than zero will reduce the panel's height to leave a gap between it and the passed panel.
+
+Internally this sets the panel's height to the passed panel's y position minus this panel's y position, minus the offset. This means the two panels are expected to overlap horizontally and share the same parent for meaningful results.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
-		<arg name="tgtPanel" type="Panel">The panel to align the bottom of this one with.</arg>
-		<arg name="offset" type="number" default="0">The gap to leave between this and the passed panel. Negative values will cause the panel's height to increase, forming an overlap.</arg>
+		<arg name="tgtPanel" type="Panel">The panel to align the bottom of this one with. Its <page text="y">Panel:GetY</page> position and this panel's y position determine the resulting height.</arg>
+		<arg name="offset" type="number" default="0">The gap to leave between this and the passed panel. Negative values will cause the panel's height to increase, forming an overlap. Only an omitted argument falls back to 0, because the helper uses the `or` pattern.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Spacer layout">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a frame, a label above it, and a readout panel stretched to the label using StretchBottomTo with a 5 pixel gap. The readout's bottom sits 5 pixels above the frame bottom after resizing.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 200 )
+frame:SetTitle( "Layout example" )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+frame.label = frame:Add( "DLabel" )
+frame.label:SetText( "Value:" )
+frame.label:SetTall( 20 )
+frame.label:Dock( TOP )
+
+frame.readout = frame:Add( "DPanel" )
+frame.readout:SetY( 60 )
+frame.readout:Dock( TOP )
+
+-- Dock has already sized the readout. Rebuild its height so its
+-- bottom ends 5 pixels above the label's top.
+frame.readout:StretchBottomTo( frame.label, 5 )
+frame.readout:SetTall( math.max( frame.readout:GetTall(), 20 ) )
+
+frame.readout.Paint = function( p, w, h )
+	draw.SimpleText( "Height: " .. h, "DermaDefault", 5, h / 2, color_white, TEXT_ALIGN_LEFT, TEXT_ALIGN_CENTER )
+end
+    </code>
+</example>
```

```diff
+The panel itself is deselected first with <page text="Panel:SetSelected">Panel:SetSelected</page>, then each child returned by <page text="Panel:GetChildren">Panel:GetChildren</page> has its own `UnselectAll` called on it. Children of children are handled by this same recursion.
+
+Selection state is only meaningful for panels that use it, such as panels with a `Paint` or selection system that checks <page text="Panel:IsSelected">Panel:IsSelected</page>. Calling this on panels that never set a selection has no visible effect.</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Deselect a panel tree">
+	<description>Runs on the client or in the menu. Creates a frame with two child panels, selects all of them, then deselects the whole tree with one call. The selected state is printed before and after.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 200 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:SetTitle( "Selection example" )
+
+local children = {}
+for i = 1, 2 do
+	local panel = vgui.Create( "DPanel", frame )
+	panel:Dock( TOP )
+	panel:SetTall( 50 )
+	panel:SetSelected( true )
+	children[ i ] = panel
+end
+
+frame:SetSelected( true )
+
+print( frame:IsSelected(), children[ 1 ]:IsSelected(), children[ 2 ]:IsSelected() )
+
+frame:UnselectAll()
+
+print( frame:IsSelected(), children[ 1 ]:IsSelected(), children[ 2 ]:IsSelected() )
+
+frame:Remove()
+	</code>
+	<output>
+true	true	true
+false	false	false
+	</output>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/PhysObj:CalculateForceOffset
+++ proposed/PhysObj:CalculateForceOffset
@@ -1,14 +1,39 @@
 <function name="CalculateForceOffset" parent="PhysObj" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Calculates the linear and angular impulse on the object's center of mass for an offset impulse.<br/>The outputs can be used with <page>PhysObj:ApplyForceCenter</page> and <page>PhysObj:ApplyTorqueCenter</page>, respectively.
 
 **Be careful to convert the angular impulse to world frame (<page>PhysObj:LocalToWorldVector</page>) if you are going to use it with ApplyTorqueCenter.**</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="impulse" type="Vector">The impulse acting on the object in `kg*source_unit/s`. (World frame)</arg>
 		<arg name="position" type="Vector">The location of the impulse in world coordinates (`source units`)</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="linearImpulse" type="Vector">The calculated linear impulse on the physics object's center of mass in `kg*source_unit/s`. (World frame)</ret>
 		<ret name="angularImpulse" type="Vector">The calculated angular impulse on the physics object's center of mass in `kg*m^2*degrees/s`. (Local frame)</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Offset impulse split into linear and angular parts">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Creates a physics prop, computes the linear and angular impulse for a push applied at a point above the center of mass, and prints both results. The prop is removed afterwards.</description>
+	<code>
+local prop = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop:Spawn()
+
+local phys = prop:GetPhysicsObject()
+if ( not IsValid( phys ) ) then prop:Remove() return end
+
+-- A 500 kg*unit/s impulse applied at a point 20 units above the center of mass
+local impulse = Vector( 0, 500, 0 )
+local offsetPoint = phys:GetPos() + Vector( 0, 0, 20 )
+
+local linear, angular = phys:CalculateForceOffset( impulse, offsetPoint )
+
+print( linear ) -- Vector( 0, 500, 0 ), same as the input impulse
+print( angular ) -- nonzero torque about the local axes, spins the crate
+
+prop:Remove()
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The linear impulse equals the input impulse regardless of the offset position. Only the angular impulse depends on where the impulse is applied relative to the center of mass.</note>
```

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

```diff
--- original/PhysObj:CalculateVelocityOffset
+++ proposed/PhysObj:CalculateVelocityOffset
@@ -1,15 +1,39 @@
 <function name="CalculateVelocityOffset" parent="PhysObj" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Calculates the linear and angular velocities on the center of mass for an offset impulse. The outputs can be directly passed to <page>PhysObj:AddVelocity</page> and <page>PhysObj:AddAngleVelocity</page>, respectively.
+
+The impulse is applied at the given world position. If the position is at the object's center of mass, the angular result is a zero length vector. The further the position is from the center of mass, the larger the angular component becomes.
 
 <warning>This will return zero length vectors if the physics object's motion is disabled. See <page>PhysObj:IsMotionEnabled</page>.</warning></description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="impulse" type="Vector">The impulse acting on the object in `kg*source_unit/s`. (World frame)</arg>
 		<arg name="position" type="Vector">The location of the impulse in world coordinates (`source units`)</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Vector">The calculated linear velocity from the impulse on the physics object's center of mass in `source_unit/s`. (World frame)</ret>
 		<ret name="" type="Vector">The calculated angular velocity from the impulse on the physics object's center of mass in `degrees/s`. (Local frame)</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Offset impulse">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Applies an impulse to a spawned melon at a point above its center of mass, making it both move and spin. The impulse is applied through the calculated velocities instead of a direct force call.</description>
+	<code>
+local ent = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+ent:SetModel( "models/props_junk/watermelon01.mdl" )
+ent:Spawn()
+
+local phys = ent:GetPhysicsObject()
+if ( not IsValid( phys ) ) then return end
+
+-- Impulse of 50 kg*unit/s pushing up, applied at a point 10 units above the entity origin
+local impulse = Vector( 0, 0, 50 )
+local hitPos = ent:GetPos() + Vector( 0, 0, 10 )
+
+local velocity, angularVelocity = phys:CalculateVelocityOffset( impulse, hitPos )
+
+phys:AddVelocity( velocity )
+phys:AddAngleVelocity( angularVelocity )
+
+-- The melon now moves upward and spins, since the impulse missed its center of mass
+	</code>
+</example>
```

## 2501. PhysObj:GetFrictionSnapshot

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091674-SRwYUdWUHUFbYz5soRRT`. Duration: 8.23s. Attempt cost: 0.0007876.

- No Lua implementation or source was supplied, so the empty snapshot behavior and field meanings are described conservatively based on the existing documentation. The example output is illustrative; exact contact point coordinates depend on the map and prop placement.

```diff
--- original/PhysObj:GetFrictionSnapshot
+++ proposed/PhysObj:GetFrictionSnapshot
@@ -1,17 +1,52 @@
 <function name="GetFrictionSnapshot" parent="PhysObj" type="classfunc">
-	<description>Returns the friction snapshot of this physics object. This is useful for determining if an object touching ground for example.</description>
+	<description>Returns the friction snapshot of this physics object. This is useful for determining if an object touching ground for example.
+
+The returned table has one entry per friction event recorded for this physics object during the last physics simulation step. An object resting on the ground typically has at least one entry, while a freely falling or sleeping object with no contacts may have none. Check the table with `#` or `ipairs` before using its contents, since it can be empty.</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 <added>2020.03.17</added>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="table">A table of tables containing the following data:
 * <page>PhysObj</page> Other - The other physics object we came in contact with
 * <page>number</page> EnergyAbsorbed - 
 * <page>number</page> FrictionCoefficient - 
 * <page>number</page> NormalForce - 
 * <page>Vector</page> Normal - Direction of the friction event
 * <page>Vector</page> ContactPoint - Contact point of the friction event
 * <page>number</page> Material - Surface Property ID of our physics obj
 * <page>number</page> MaterialOther - Surface Property ID of the physics obj we came in contact with
 </ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Detecting ground contact">
+	<description>Runs on the server. A prop is spawned and given a downward push. Each think, the friction snapshot is checked. A nonempty snapshot means the prop is touching something, such as the ground. The example prints the number of friction events and the world position of the first contact point, then removes the prop after five seconds.</description>
+	<code>
+local prop = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop:Spawn()
+prop:GetPhysicsObject():ApplyForceCenter( Vector( 0, 0, -500 ) )
+
+local timerName = "FrictionSnapshotExample" .. prop:EntIndex()
+timer.Create( timerName, 0.5, 10, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( prop ) ) then timer.Remove( timerName ) return end
+
+	local snapshot = prop:GetPhysicsObject():GetFrictionSnapshot()
+
+	if ( #snapshot > 0 ) then
+		local event = snapshot[ 1 ]
+		print( "Touching something. Contact point: " .. tostring( event.ContactPoint ) )
+	else
+		print( "No friction contacts." )
+	end
+end )
+
+-- Cleanup
+timer.Simple( 5.5, function()
+	timer.Remove( timerName )
+	if ( IsValid( prop ) ) then prop:Remove() end
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>Touching something. Contact point: 12.03 -8.51 0.00</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>The contact point position is in world coordinates, so it can be used directly with functions such as <page text="util.TraceLine">Global.util.TraceLine</page> or debug overlays.</note>
```

```diff
+
```

```diff
+		if ( not IsValid( phys ) ) then return end
+

+
```

```diff
--- original/PhysObj:GetStress

 <function name="GetStress" parent="PhysObj" type="classfunc">
-	<description>Returns the internal and external stress of the entity.</description>
+	<description>Returns the internal and external stress of the entity.
+
+Stress values are only meaningful for physics objects that are part of a constraint system. An unconstrained entity reports zero for both values. The values are recalculated by the physics simulation as forces are applied through constraints.</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">The external stress (`𝜎𝑒`). It's the value of a giving force to other entities (in kg).</ret>
 		<ret name="" type="number">The internal stress (`𝜎𝑖`). It's the value of a receiving force from other entities (in kg).</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Monitoring constraint stress">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Creates two props, connects them with a rope constraint, and prints their stress values every second. The stress values are nonzero while the rope is under load and zero for props with no constraints.</description>
+	<code>
+local prop1 = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop1:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop1:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+prop1:Spawn()
+
+local prop2 = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop2:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop2:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 200 ) )
+prop2:Spawn()
+
+constraint.Rope( prop1, prop2, 0, 0, vector_origin, vector_origin, 0, 50, 0, 100, 0.01 )
+
+timer.Create( "StressMonitor", 1, 10, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( prop1 ) or not IsValid( prop2 ) ) then
+		timer.Remove( "StressMonitor" )
+		return
+	end
+
+	local ext, int = prop1:GetPhysicsObject():GetStress()
+	print( "external stress:", ext, "internal stress:", int )
+end )
+
+-- Remove the props and stop the timer after the test
+hook.Add( "ShutDown", "StressCleanup", function()
+	timer.Remove( "StressMonitor" )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>Call this on a valid <page text="PhysObj">PhysObj</page> obtained with <page text="Entity:GetPhysicsObject">Entity:GetPhysicsObject</page>. The physics object must be awake for the values to update.</note>
```

## 2523. PhysObj:IsAsleep

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/PhysObj%3AIsAsleep) | Revision: 510859

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091692-72QHI1mvV5vzdcmrxVOc`. Duration: 4.97s. Attempt cost: 0.00052145625.


```diff
--- original/PhysObj:IsAsleep
+++ proposed/PhysObj:IsAsleep
@@ -1,12 +1,46 @@
 <function name="IsAsleep" parent="PhysObj" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns whether the physics object is "sleeping".
+
+A sleeping physics object has stopped simulating because its velocity and angular velocity have been near zero for some time. It resumes simulating when something disturbs it, such as a collision, a force, or a call to <page>PhysObj:Wake</page>.
 
 See <page>PhysObj:Sleep</page> for more information.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Whether the physics object is sleeping.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Check sleep state">
+	<description>
+Runs on the server. Creates a temporary prop, waits for its physics object to fall asleep, then prints the result and removes the prop.
+	</description>
+	<code>
+local prop = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop:Spawn()
+
+local phys = prop:GetPhysicsObject()
+
+-- A sleeping object does not move on its own, so nudge it awake
+phys:Wake()
+print( phys:IsAsleep() ) -- false, the object is simulating
+
+-- Wait until the crate settles and the engine puts it back to sleep
+timer.Create( "CheckSleep", 1, 10, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( prop ) or not IsValid( phys ) ) then return end
+
+	if ( phys:IsAsleep() ) then
+		print( "The crate fell asleep" )
+		timer.Remove( "CheckSleep" )
+		prop:Remove()
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>The first print shows false. After the crate settles, the timer prints that it fell asleep.</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>
+Apply forces to a sleeping physics object only after calling <page>PhysObj:Wake</page>, otherwise some forces may be ignored while the object is asleep. You can use this function to skip work on objects that are not moving.
+</note>
```

It is enabled by default on most physics objects and can be toggled with <page text="PhysObj:EnableDrag">PhysObj:EnableDrag</page>. Disabling drag makes the object move as if it were in a vacuum, which is useful for projectiles and other objects that should not slow down in flight.</description>

````diff
--- original/PhysObj:LocalToWorld
+++ proposed/PhysObj:LocalToWorld
@@ -1,26 +1,44 @@
 <function name="LocalToWorld" parent="PhysObj" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Translates a vector in the physics object's local space into worldspace coordinates.
+
+The local space origin is the physics object's position, which for most entities matches <page>Entity:GetPos</page>. The local space axes follow the physics object's current rotation, so the result changes as the entity moves or turns.
 
 <note>Internally transforms the vector by the <page>PhysObj:GetPositionMatrix</page>.
 
 So in GLua it approximates to:
 ```
 local matrixWorldTransform = PhysObj:GetPositionMatrix()
 local vecWorldspaced = Vector()
 vecWorldspaced:Set( vecLocal )
 vecWorldspaced:Mul( matrixWorldTransform )
 
 return vecWorldspaced
 ```
 </note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="vecLocal" type="Vector">A vector in the physics object's local space.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Vector">The corresponding worldspace vector.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Offset point on a physics object">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Spawns a wooden crate, then prints the world position of a point 16 units above the crate's physics object origin. The printed position moves with the crate, so it depends on where the crate was spawned and how it settled.</description>
+	<code>
+local crate = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+crate:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+crate:Spawn()
+
+local phys = crate:GetPhysicsObject()
+if not IsValid( phys ) then return end
+
+local topPoint = phys:LocalToWorld( Vector( 0, 0, 16 ) )
+print( topPoint )
+
+crate:Remove()
+	</code>
+</example>
````

```diff
 <function name="RecheckCollisionFilter" parent="PhysObj" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Call this when the collision filter conditions change due to this object's state (e.g. changing solid type or collision group)</description>
+	<description>The physics engine caches which entities and objects a physics object can collide with. Calling this method forces the engine to reevaluate those conditions for this object. Use it after changing properties that affect collision filtering, such as the entity's collision group (see <page text="Global.SetCollisionGroup">Entity.SetCollisionGroup</page>) or solidity, so the change takes effect for existing contacts.</description>

+	<description>Runs on the server. A prop is spawned, marked as non colliding with players via its collision group, and the physics object is told to recheck its collision filter so groups ignore each other correctly. +	<code>
+local prop = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+if not IsValid( prop ) then return end

+prop:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+prop:Spawn()
+
+prop:SetCollisionGroup( COLLISION_GROUP_WEAPON )
+
+local phys = prop:GetPhysicsObject()
+if IsValid( phys ) then
+	phys:RecheckCollisionFilter()
+end
+
+timer.Simple( 5, function()

+	end
+end )
```

```diff
+melon:Spawn()
+
+local phys = melon:GetPhysicsObject()
+if IsValid( phys ) then
+	phys:SetDragCoefficient( 5 )
+	phys:ApplyForceCenter( Vector( 0, 0, 20000 ) )
```

```diff
--- original/PhysObj:SetPos

@@ -1,11 +1,40 @@
 <function name="SetPos" parent="PhysObj" type="classfunc">
-	<description>Sets the position of the physobject.</description>
+	<description>Sets the position of the physobject.
+
+The physics object is moved instantly. Its velocity and angular velocity are kept, so the object continues moving from the new position. This differs from <page>Entity:SetPos</page>, which moves the entity and lets the physics engine follow.
+
+If the new position places the object inside world geometry or another solid object, the physics engine may push it out or it may become stuck. Use the `teleport` argument to move the object through obstacles.</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="position" type="Vector">The new position of the physobject in world coordinates. (`source units`).
 			<warning>The new position will not be applied on the parent entity while the physics object is asleep (<page>PhysObj:Sleep</page>)</warning>	
 		</arg>
 		<arg name="teleport" type="boolean" default="false">If `true`, temporarily disables collisions of the physics objects just before moving it, then enables collisions back again.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Teleporting a physics object">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Spawns a wooden crate 10 seconds after the script loads, then moves its physics object 200 units straight up. The `teleport` argument is used so the crate does not collide with anything along the way. The crate is removed afterwards.</description>
+	<code>
+timer.Simple( 10, function()
+	local ent = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+	if not IsValid( ent ) then return end
+
+	ent:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+	ent:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+	ent:Spawn()
+
+	local phys = ent:GetPhysicsObject()
+	if IsValid( phys ) then
+		local pos = phys:GetPos()
+		phys:SetPos( pos + Vector( 0, 0, 200 ), true )
+	end
+
+	timer.Simple( 5, function()
+		if IsValid( ent ) then
+			ent:Remove()
+		end
+	end )
+end )
```

## 2546. PhysObj:Sleep

```diff
--- original/PhysObj:Sleep
+++ proposed/PhysObj:Sleep
@@ -1,9 +1,30 @@
 <function name="Sleep" parent="PhysObj" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Makes the physics object "sleep". The physics object will no longer be moving unless it is "woken up" by either a collision with another moving object, or by <page>PhysObj:Wake</page>. 
 
 This is an optimization feature of the physics engine. Normally physics objects will automatically "sleep" when not moving for a short while, to save resources, but it can be used for other purposes, for example to temporarily suspend an object mid air.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Suspending a prop mid air">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Puts a spawned prop's physics to sleep while it is in the air, then wakes it up after 5 seconds so it falls again.</description>
+	<code>
+local prop = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 200 ) )
+prop:Spawn()
+
+local phys = prop:GetPhysicsObject()
+if IsValid( phys ) then
+	phys:Sleep()
+end
+
+-- Wake the prop up after 5 seconds so it resumes falling
+timer.Simple( 5, function()
+	if not IsValid( prop ) or not IsValid( prop:GetPhysicsObject() ) then return end
+
+	prop:GetPhysicsObject():Wake()
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

```diff
 	<description>
 Unlike <page>PhysObj:SetPos</page> and <page>PhysObj:SetAngles</page>, this allows the movement of a physobj while leaving physics interactions intact.<br/>
 This is used internally by the motion controller of the Gravity Gun , the +use pickup and the Physics Gun, and entities such as the crane.
 
 <note>This is the ideal function to move a physics shadow created with <page>Entity:PhysicsInitShadow</page> or <page>Entity:MakePhysicsObjectAShadow</page>.</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="targetPosition" type="Vector">The position we should move to.</arg>
 		<arg name="targetAngles" type="Angle">The angle we should rotate towards.</arg>
 		<arg name="frameTime" type="number">The frame time to use for this movement, can be generally filled with <page>Global.FrameTime</page> or <page>ENTITY:PhysicsSimulate</page> with the deltaTime. 
 
 Can be set to 0 when you need to update the physics object just once.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Moving a physics shadow">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Creates a temporary prop with a shadow physics object, moves it smoothly upward with a timer, then removes it. The prop collides with the world and other entities while being moved, which a plain <page>PhysObj:SetPos</page> call would not handle the same way.</description>
+	<code>
+local ent = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+ent:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+ent:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+ent:Spawn()
+
+-- Replace the normal physics object with a shadow physics object
+ent:PhysicsInitShadow( true, true )
+
+local phys = ent:GetPhysicsObject()
+if ( not IsValid( phys ) ) then ent:Remove() return end
+
+local targetPos = ent:GetPos()
+local targetAng = ent:GetAngles()
+
+local timerName = "UpdateShadowExample_" .. ent:EntIndex()
+timer.Create( timerName, 0, 100, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( ent ) or not IsValid( phys ) ) then
+		timer.Remove( timerName )
+		return
+	end
+
+	-- Move the shadow up by 1 unit per tick
+	targetPos = targetPos + Vector( 0, 0, 1 )
+	phys:UpdateShadow( targetPos, targetAng, FrameTime() )
+end )
+
+-- Cleanup after the movement finishes
+timer.Simple( 1, function()
+	timer.Remove( timerName )
+	if ( IsValid( ent ) ) then ent:Remove() end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

## 2548. PhysObj:Wake

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/PhysObj%3AWake) | Revision: 552661

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091698-miuCVLRwarhQVO8UvGmA`. Duration: 3.62s. Attempt cost: 0.00053245.

- No Lua implementation was supplied for this page, so the added explanation is based on documented behavior of sleeping physics objects rather than source evidence.

```diff
--- original/PhysObj:Wake
+++ proposed/PhysObj:Wake
@@ -1,9 +1,29 @@
 <function name="Wake" parent="PhysObj" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Wakes the physics object, so that it will continue to simulate physics/gravity.
+
+A physics object that is asleep skips simulation to save CPU. Waking it makes the engine resume simulation, so gravity and collisions affect it again. This is useful after moving an object or changing its position directly, since a sleeping object will not fall or react until it is woken.
 
 See <page>PhysObj:Sleep</page> for more information.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Waking a prop after teleporting it">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Teleporting a prop by setting its position does not wake its physics object, so the prop can hang in the air until something touches it. Wake the physics object so gravity takes effect immediately.
+	</description>
+	<code>
+local prop = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop:Spawn()
+
+-- Move the prop somewhere else
+prop:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 200 ) )
+
+local phys = prop:GetPhysicsObject()
+if IsValid( phys ) then
+	phys:Wake() -- Resume simulation so the crate falls with gravity
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
--- original/PhysObj:WorldToLocal
+++ proposed/PhysObj:WorldToLocal
@@ -1,11 +1,37 @@
 <function name="WorldToLocal" parent="PhysObj" type="classfunc">
-	<description>Translates a worldspace vector into the physics object's local space.</description>
+	<description>Translates a worldspace vector into the physics object's local space.
+
+The returned vector is relative to the physics object's origin and rotated by its current angles. This is useful for finding where a world position sits on a moving or rotated entity, for example to store a grab offset relative to a prop.
+
+See <page text="PhysObj:LocalToWorld">PhysObj:LocalToWorld</page> for the inverse operation.</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="vec" type="Vector">A worldspace vector.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Vector">The corresponding local space vector.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Grab offset relative to a prop">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Finds the local space position of a point 50 units in front of a physics enabled prop, then converts it back to world space. The two printed vectors match, showing the round trip through local space.
+
+Place this in a server side file and spawn a physics prop, or run it on an existing prop by replacing the FindInSphere call.</description>
+	<code>
+local prop = ents.FindInSphere( Vector( 0, 0, 0 ), 500 )[ 1 ]
+if ( not IsValid( prop ) or not IsValid( prop:GetPhysicsObject() ) ) then return end
+
+local phys = prop:GetPhysicsObject()
+
+-- A point 50 units in front of the prop, in world space
+local worldPoint = prop:GetPos() + prop:GetForward() * 50
+
+-- Where that point sits in the prop's local space
+local localPoint = phys:WorldToLocal( worldPoint )
+print( localPoint )
+
+-- Converting back gives the original world position
+print( phys:LocalToWorld( localPoint ) )
+	</code>
+	<output>The first print shows a local offset such as 0.00 0.00 50.00, which depends on the prop's current angles. The second print matches worldPoint.</output>
+</example>
```

## 2550. PhysObj:WorldToLocalVector

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/PhysObj%3AWorldToLocalVector) | Revision: 565647

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091707-mYgPdYWgH324sQ9oUS6H`. Duration: 10.67s. Attempt cost: 0.0007042875.

```diff
--- original/PhysObj:WorldToLocalVector
+++ proposed/PhysObj:WorldToLocalVector
@@ -1,17 +1,38 @@
 <function name="WorldToLocalVector" parent="PhysObj" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Rotationally transforms a worldspace vector into the physics object's local space by the inverted <page>PhysObj:GetPositionMatrix</page>.
 
 For example, in GMod this is used in thrusters, for working out linear force for local acceleration.
 
 <note>In contrast to <page>PhysObj:WorldToLocal</page>, this function doesn't translate the vector.</note>
+
+The input is treated as a direction only. Its position in the world does not matter, because the transformation rotates the vector around the origin and ignores translation. Use <page>PhysObj:WorldToLocal</page> when a position also needs to be converted.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="vec" type="Vector">A worldspace vector.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Vector">The resulting vector from the rotational transformation.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Direction in local space">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Spawns a physics prop, rotates it, and converts the world forward direction into the prop's local space. The printed vector shows how the world forward axis aligns with the rotated prop's local axes. The prop is removed afterwards.</description>
+	<code>
+local prop = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop:Spawn()
+
+-- Rotate the prop so its axes no longer match the world axes
+prop:SetAngles( Angle( 0, 90, 0 ) )
+
+local phys = prop:GetPhysicsObject()
+if ( phys:IsValid() ) then
+	local localForward = phys:WorldToLocalVector( Vector( 1, 0, 0 ) )
+	print( localForward )
+end
+
+prop:Remove()
+	</code>
+</example>
```

```diff
 <function name="Crouching" parent="Player" type="classfunc">

+		if crouching ~= lastState[ ply ] then

+lastState = nil
```

## 2566. Player:DoAnimationEvent
