- No Lua implementation was supplied, so argument defaults and exact native behavior could not be verified from source. The example relies only on the documented contract: Player:DoAnimationEvent calls GM:DoAnimationEvent with PLAYERANIMEVENT_CUSTOM_GESTURE and the given data.
- The example uses AddVCDSequenceToGestureSlot inside the hook because that is the standard gesture handling path in the base gamemode; this usage should be confirmed against the gamemode's own DoAnimationEvent handler during review.

```diff
--- original/Player:DoAnimationEvent
+++ proposed/Player:DoAnimationEvent
@@ -1,12 +1,47 @@
 <function name="DoAnimationEvent" parent="Player" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Sends a third person animation event to the player.
 
 Calls <page>GM:DoAnimationEvent</page> with <page text="PLAYERANIMEVENT_CUSTOM_GESTURE">Enums/PLAYERANIMEVENT</page> as the event, data as the given data.
+
+The gesture hook receives the player as its first argument. A gamemode or addon can react to the event by playing a gesture on the player, for example with <page>Entity:AddGesture</page> or <page text="Player:AnimRestartGesture">Player:AnimRestartGesture</page>.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
-		<arg name="data" type="number">The data to send.</arg>
+		<arg name="data" type="number">The data to send. This value is passed through to the <page>GM:DoAnimationEvent</page> hook, so its meaning depends on how the gamemode interprets it. A common choice is a sequence ID or activity ID.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Triggering a custom gesture event">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Sends a custom gesture event carrying a sequence ID, and listens for it with the <page>GM:DoAnimationEvent</page> hook. Add this to a Lua file in `lua/autorun/` and run `trigger_gesture` in the server console while a player is present. The player plays the gesture.</description>
+	<code>
+if ( SERVER ) then
+	-- Respond to the event sent by Player:DoAnimationEvent
+	-- and play the gesture on the player.
+	hook.Add( "DoAnimationEvent", "CustomGestureExample", function( ply, event, data )
+		if ( event == PLAYERANIMEVENT_CUSTOM_GESTURE and data == 1 ) then
+			-- Pick a sequence that exists on the player's model.
+			local seq = ply:LookupSequence( "gesture_blowkiss" )
+			if ( seq > 0 ) then
+				ply:AddVCDSequenceToGestureSlot( GESTURE_SLOT_CUSTOM, seq, 0, true )
+			end
+		end
+	end )
+
+	concommand.Add( "trigger_gesture", function( ply )
+		local target = ply
+		if ( not IsValid( target ) ) then
+			-- Console fallback: use the first player.
+			for _, p in ipairs( player.GetAll() ) do
+				target = p
+				break
+			end
+		end
+
+		if ( IsValid( target ) ) then
+			target:DoAnimationEvent( 1 )
+		end
+	end )
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/Player:GetObserverTarget
+++ proposed/Player:GetObserverTarget
@@ -1,12 +1,42 @@
 <function name="GetObserverTarget" parent="Player" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns the entity the player is currently observing.
 
 Set using <page>Player:SpectateEntity</page>.
+
+The target is only meaningful while the player is in a spectating mode, such as after <page>Player:Spectate</page>. A player who is alive and not spectating has no target, so the function returns <page text="NULL">Global_Variables</page> in that case.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Entity">The entity the player is currently spectating, or <page text="NULL">Global_Variables</page> if the player has no target.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example>
+	<description>Runs on the server. Forces a player to spectate another player, then prints the observed entity to the console. The spectate mode is reset after five seconds so the player returns to normal.</description>
+	<code>
+local observer = player.GetByID( 1 )
+local target = player.GetByID( 2 )
+
+if ( not IsValid( observer ) or not IsValid( target ) ) then return end
+
+observer:Spectate( OBSERVE_MODE_CHASE )
+observer:SpectateEntity( target )
+observer:StripWeapons()
+
+print( observer:GetObserverTarget() )
+
+-- Return the player to normal after five seconds.
+timer.Simple( 5, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( observer ) ) then return end
+
+	observer:UnSpectate()
+	observer:Spawn()
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>Player [2][Bot01]</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>
+The returned entity can be any entity, not just players. It can also become invalid while spectating, so check it with <page>Global.IsValid</page> before use.
+</note>
```

```diff
--- original/Player:IsFullyAuthenticated
+++ proposed/Player:IsFullyAuthenticated
@@ -1,14 +1,41 @@
 <function name="IsFullyAuthenticated" parent="Player" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Returns whether the player identity was confirmed by the Steam network.
+
+Authentication happens shortly after a player connects. A player can be in the server and fully spawned before this returns true, so do not treat a false result as proof of an invalid identity. Poll this function or use <page>GM:NetworkIDValidated</page> to react when authentication completes.
 
 See also <page>GM:NetworkIDValidated</page>.
 </description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Whether the player has been fully authenticated or not.
 
 This will always be true for singleplayer and the listen server host.
 This will always be false for bots.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Waiting for authentication">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Prints the authentication state of a joining player and announces once the Steam network confirms the identity. Bots never authenticate, so they are skipped.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "PlayerInitialSpawn", "AuthStatusExample", function( ply )
+	if ply:IsBot() then return end
+
+	print( ply:Nick() .. " authenticated: " .. tostring( ply:IsFullyAuthenticated() ) )
+
+	-- Poll until the Steam network confirms the identity.
+	local token = "AuthStatusExample_" .. ply:SteamID64()
+	timer.Create( token, 1, 30, function()
+		if not IsValid( ply ) then
+			timer.Remove( token )
+			return
+		end
+
+		if ply:IsFullyAuthenticated() then
+			timer.Remove( token )
+			print( ply:Nick() .. " is now fully authenticated." )
+		end
+	end )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>On join the first print usually reports false, and after a short delay a second print reports that the player is fully authenticated.</output>
+</example>
```

## 2631. Player:IsSprinting

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Player%3AIsSprinting) | Revision: 528903

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091677-H5n1PU6O68nVFW5N9ASj`. Duration: 4.44s. Attempt cost: 0.0005270125.

- No source implementation was supplied for this function; the example is grounded only in the documented description, not verified against code.
- The added note rephrases the documented wall/Standing still caveat rather than introducing new behavior claims.
- Output shown is illustrative; the printed player name depends on who is sprinting.

```diff
--- original/Player:IsSprinting
+++ proposed/Player:IsSprinting
@@ -1,10 +1,40 @@
 <function name="IsSprinting" parent="Player" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Returns whether the player is currently sprinting or not, specifically if they are holding their sprint key and are allowed to sprint.
 
 This will not check if the player is currently sprinting into a wall. (i.e. holding their sprint key but not moving)</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Is the player sprinting or not</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Detect sprinting">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Checks every half second whether a player is sprinting and prints a message whenever the state changes. Use `killtimer` in the console to remove the timer.</description>
+	<code>
+local wasSprinting = false
+
+timer.Create( "CheckSprint", 0.5, 0, function()
+	local ply = Entity( 1 ) -- the first player, usually the host
+	if not IsValid( ply ) then return end
+
+	local isSprinting = ply:IsSprinting()
+	if isSprinting ~= wasSprinting then
+		if isSprinting then
+			print( ply:Nick() .. " started sprinting" )
+		else
+			print( ply:Nick() .. " stopped sprinting" )
+		end
+
+		wasSprinting = isSprinting
+	end
+end )
+
+-- cleanup: run this when the check is no longer needed
+concommand.Add( "killtimer", function()
+	timer.Remove( "CheckSprint" )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>Player1 started sprinting</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>The returned value only reflects the player's held sprint key and permission to sprint. A player holding the sprint key while standing still still returns true.</note>
```

- Added explanation that the returned angle is relative to the player's parent and matches Entity:EyeAngles when unparented. This follows from the function name and the documented difference from Entity:EyeAngles; no Lua implementation was supplied, so the wording stays general.
- Added a server Think hook example using GetVehicle and LocalEyeAngles, with a commented cleanup line. No output block because values depend on player view.

```diff
--- original/Player:LocalEyeAngles
+++ proposed/Player:LocalEyeAngles
@@ -1,14 +1,34 @@
 <function name="LocalEyeAngles" parent="Player" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns the direction a player is looking as a entity/local-oriented angle.
 
 Unlike <page>Entity:EyeAngles</page>, this function does not include angles of the Player's <page>Entity:GetParent</page>.
+
+The returned angle is relative to the player's parent. For a player with no parent, the result is the same as <page>Entity:EyeAngles</page>. This is useful for converting a player's view direction into the local space of a vehicle or other parented entity, for example with <page>Angle:RotateAroundAxis</page> or by comparing it against the parent's angles.
 
 <bug>Does not work correctly clientside for non local players when in a vehicle. (validate: when parented in general?)</bug>
 	</description>
 	<added>2021.06.09</added>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Angle">The local eye angles.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Detecting where a driver is looking">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Prints the local eye angles of every player driving a vehicle. A pitch near 0 means the driver looks straight ahead relative to the vehicle, while a large pitch means they look up or down inside it.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "Think", "LocalEyeAnglesExample", function()
+	for _, ply in ipairs( player.GetAll() ) do
+		local vehicle = ply:GetVehicle()
+		if not IsValid( vehicle ) then continue end
+
+		local localAng = ply:LocalEyeAngles()
+		print( ply:Nick() .. " looks " .. math.Round( localAng.p ) .. " degrees up or down in their vehicle" )
+	end
+end )
+
+-- Remove the hook when it is no longer needed:
+-- hook.Remove( "Think", "LocalEyeAnglesExample" )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

Source: [gamemodes/base/gamemode/obj_player_extend.lua:57](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/9bacca4b786123ac1da54145e625b1db970dbf21/garrysmod/gamemodes/base/gamemode/obj_player_extend.lua#L57-L94)

Matched committed Lua definitions; helper and caller context may be incomplete

- Added explanation of the two branches (targeted entity unfreeze versus double press unfreeze all) and the 0.25 second window, all grounded in the supplied source.
- The double press timer is only set on the miss path (tab.LastPhysUnfreeze = CurTime() after the trace check), which the note describes.
- Example uses Entity(1) as the player; adjust if the reviewer prefers a different way to obtain a player.

```diff
--- original/Player:PhysgunUnfreeze
+++ proposed/Player:PhysgunUnfreeze
@@ -1,11 +1,34 @@
 <function name="PhysgunUnfreeze" parent="Player" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Unfreezes the props player is looking at. This is essentially the same as pressing reload with the physics gun, including double press for unfreeze all.
 
-For freezing props, use <page>PhysObj:EnableMotion</page>.</description>
+For freezing props, use <page>PhysObj:EnableMotion</page>.
+
+The behavior depends on what the player is looking at:
+
+* If the eye trace hits a valid non world entity, every physics object of that entity and of all entities constrained to it is unfrozen. The return value is the number of physics objects that were actually unfrozen.
+* If the eye trace hits nothing (or the world), the call only records the time of this attempt and returns 0. Calling this method again within 0.25 seconds of such an attempt counts as a double press and unfreezes every frozen physics object the player is responsible for, returning that count instead.
+
+Only objects frozen by this player are counted and unfrozen. Objects frozen by other players or by the server are left alone.</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<file line="53-L96">gamemodes/base/gamemode/obj_player_extend.lua</file>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">Number of props unfrozen.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Unfreeze everything a player froze">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Simulates the double press behavior by calling the method twice in quick succession while the player looks at empty space, which unfreezes all props the player froze. Prints how many physics objects were released.</description>
+	<code>
+local ply = Entity( 1 ) -- first player on the server
+
+-- First call hits nothing and only starts the double press timer
+ply:PhysgunUnfreeze()
+
+-- Second call within 0.25 seconds unfreezes everything this player froze
+local count = ply:PhysgunUnfreeze()
+
+print( "Unfroze " .. count .. " physics objects" )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The double press timer is stored per player in the player's table as `LastPhysUnfreeze` and is only updated when the eye trace misses. A successful unfreeze of a targeted entity does not start the timer.</note>
```

```diff
 <function name="SetFOV" parent="Player" type="classfunc">
 	<description>Set a player's FOV (Field Of View) over a certain amount of time.
 
-This is meant to be called on the server or shared (for prediction), it will have no effect if called clientside only. You may want to use <page>GM:CalcView</page> for that instead.</description>
+This is meant to be called on the server or shared (for prediction), it will have no effect if called clientside only. You may want to use <page>GM:CalcView</page> for that instead.
+
+The zoom state is global per player, not per requester. While the FOV is nonzero, only the entity stored as the requester may change it again. Passing 0 as `fov` clears the zoom and returns the player to their default FOV, after which any entity may set a new FOV.</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="fov" type="number">the angle of perception (FOV). Set to 0 to return to default user FOV. ( Which is ranging from 75 to 100, depending on user settings )</arg>
 		<arg name="time" type="number" default="0">the time it takes to transition to the FOV expressed in a floating point.</arg>
 		<arg name="requester" type="Entity" default="self" added="2020.03.17">The requester or "owner" of the zoom event. Only this entity will be able to change the player's FOV until it is set back to 0.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<note>Call this function on both server and client (shared) if the FOV change should be predicted smoothly, for example from a weapon's primary attack. A server only call still works but may appear less smooth during prediction.</note>
+
+<example name="Zooming with a scoped weapon">
+	<description>Runs on the server. A swep-like zoom: pressing the attack key zooms the player in over 0.3 seconds, and a timer returns them to their default FOV after 3 seconds. The player is the requester, so only this code path can change their FOV until it is reset to 0.</description>
+	<code>
+-- Example runs in a server context, e.g. from a SWEP's PrimaryAttack
+function SWEP:PrimaryAttack()
+	local ply = self:GetOwner()
+
+	if not ply:GetNWBool( "Scoped" ) then
+		ply:SetFOV( 30, 0.3, ply ) -- zoom in over 0.3 seconds
+		ply:SetNWBool( "Scoped", true )
+
+		timer.Create( "SWEPZoomReset" .. ply:SteamID64(), 3, 1, function()
+			if not IsValid( ply ) then return end
+
+			ply:SetFOV( 0, 0.3, ply ) -- 0 returns to the user's default FOV
+			if IsValid( ply ) then ply:SetNWBool( "Scoped", false ) end
+		end )
+	end
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
+
+		The hull is axis aligned, so the mins and maxs are relative to the player's position and do not rotate with the player's view angles. The mins should normally have a z value of `0` so the hull starts at the player's feet position.
 
 		See also: <page>Player:GetHull</page>, <page>Player:SetHullDuck</page>, <page>Player:GetHullDuck</page>
 
 		<note>
 			This value is **not** replicated automatically to clients and must be manually called in both the Server and Client <page text="Realms">States</page>.
+		</note>
+
+		<note>
+			The default standing hull is `Vector( -16, -16, 0 )` to `Vector( 16, 16, 72 )`. Store the values from <page>Player:GetHull</page> before changing the hull if you need to restore the original size later.
 		</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="mins" type="Vector">
 			The hull mins, the lowest corner of the Player's bounding box.
 		</arg>
 		<arg name="maxs" type="Vector">
 			The hull maxs, the highest corner of the Player's bounding box, opposite of the mins.
 		</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Shrinking the player hull">
+	<description>
+		Runs on both the server and client. Gives every player a smaller hull so they fit through narrow gaps. The hull is set in the same way in both realms because it is not replicated automatically.
+
+		Put the server part in a serverside file and the client part in a clientside file, or use a single shared file with realm checks.
+	</description>
+	<code>
+local MINS = Vector( -12, -12, 0 )
+local MAXS = Vector( 12, 12, 36 )
+
+if SERVER then
+	hook.Add( "PlayerSpawn", "SmallHull", function( ply )
+		if not IsValid( ply ) then return end
+
+		-- Store the original hull once so it can be restored later
+		if not ply.SmallHullOriginal then
+			ply.SmallHullOriginal = ply:GetHull()
+		end
+
+		ply:SetHull( MINS, MAXS )
+	end )
+end
+
+if CLIENT then
+	hook.Add( "InitPostEntity", "SmallHull", function()
+		for _, ply in ipairs( player.GetAll() ) do
+			if IsValid( ply ) then
+				ply:SetHull( MINS, MAXS )
+			end
+		end
+	end )
+end
+	</code>
+	<description>
+		Players use a 24 by 36 unit hull for movement and hull traces. To undo the change, call `ply:SetHull( ply.SmallHullOriginal.mins, ply.SmallHullOriginal.maxs )` on both realms, or remove the hooks and call `ply:SetHull( Vector( -16, -16, 0 ), Vector( 16, 16, 72 ) )`.
+	</description>
+</example>
```

```diff
+This only changes how the player is rendered. It does not change the player's actual angles, aim direction, or movement. Because the value is reset after <page>GM:UpdateAnimation</page>, it must be set again every frame, for example from a hook that runs during rendering or animation updates.</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="ang" type="Angle">The new render angles to set</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Rendering a player facing a fixed direction">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Forces every player to be rendered facing straight up while a console variable is enabled, without changing where they actually aim. The angles are set every frame because the game resets them after <page>GM:UpdateAnimation</page>.</description>
+	<code>
+local convar = CreateClientConVar( "renderangles_up", "0", true, false, "Render all players facing up." )
+
+hook.Add( "Think", "RenderAnglesUpExample", function()
+	if ( not convar:GetBool() ) then return end
+
+	for _, ply in ipairs( player.GetAll() ) do
+		if ( not IsValid( ply ) ) then continue end
+
+		ply:SetRenderAngles( angle_up )
+	end
+end )
+
+-- Remove the hook and reset the convar when you are done with the example.
+-- hook.Remove( "Think", "RenderAnglesUpExample" )
+-- convar:SetBool( false )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note><page>Global.angle_up</page> is a shared constant pointing straight up. Do not modify it; pass a copy such as <code>angle_up * 1</code> if you need to change the angles before setting them.</note>
+
+<note>The reset happens right after <page>GM:UpdateAnimation</page>, so setting the angles from that hook or later in the frame gives a stable result. Setting them once, for example on spawn, has no lasting effect.</note>
+
```

```diff
 <function name="Spectate" parent="Player" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Starts spectate mode for given player. This will also affect the players movetype in some cases.
 
 <page>Player:UnSpectate</page> should be used to remove the player from spectate mode, or call this with `OBS_MODE_NONE`.
 
 <bug>The player must be respawned, otherwise they will be able to walk through doors and become invincible. This will be fixed in a future update.</bug>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>

+	<description>Runs on the server. Makes the calling player spectate the player they are looking at in third person chase mode. Call `Player:Respawn` on the spectating player afterwards so they cannot walk through doors or become invincible, as described in the bug note above.</description>
+	<code>
+local ply = Entity( 1 ) -- example player
+
+-- Find a player to spectate, here the first other player on the server
+local target
+for _, other in ipairs( player.GetAll() ) do
+	if ( other ~= ply ) then
+		target = other
+		break
+	end
+end
+
+if ( not IsValid( target ) ) then return end
+
+ply:Spectate( OBS_MODE_CHASE )
+ply:SpectateEntity( target )

+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>Use <page>Player:SpectateEntity</page> to choose which entity the spectating player follows, and <page>Player:StripWeapons</page> beforehand if you want to remove their weapons while they spectate.</note>
```

```diff
 <function name="SwitchToDefaultWeapon" parent="Player" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Attempts to switch the player weapon to the one specified in the "cl_defaultweapon" convar, if the player does not own the specified weapon nothing will happen.
+
+The "cl_defaultweapon" convar is a client side user convar, so each player can set their own default weapon with it. The value is read with <page>Player:GetInfo</page> and the weapon is selected with <page>Player:SelectWeapon</page> only if the player currently carries it.
 
 If you want to switch to a specific weapon, use: <page>Player:SetActiveWeapon</page>

 </function>

+	<description>Runs on the server. Gives each player their default weapon when they spawn, then switches to it if they own it. Players can change the weapon by setting the "cl_defaultweapon" convar, for example with `cl_defaultweapon weapon_pistol` in their console.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "PlayerSpawn", "SwitchToDefaultWeaponExample", function( ply )
+	-- Give the player a weapon so they actually own something to switch to.
+	-- Without this, nothing happens unless the weapon is already carried.
+	ply:Give( "weapon_crowbar" )
+
+	-- Switches to whatever "cl_defaultweapon" is set to,
+	-- but only if the player owns that weapon.
+	ply:SwitchToDefaultWeapon()
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The convar value is only checked at the moment this function runs. If the player sets "cl_defaultweapon" to a weapon they pick up later, call this function again after the pickup to switch to it.</note>
```

```diff
 		<arg name="damageFlags" type="number">Bitflag specifying the damage type, see <page>Enums/DMG</page>.</arg>
```

```diff
+	<description>Returns the angle of the ProjectedTexture, which were previously set by <page>ProjectedTexture:SetAngles</page>

+hook.Add( "Think", "UpdateLight", function()

+end )
+

+	print( light:GetAngles() )
+end )
+	</code>
```

````diff
 <function name="IsValid" parent="ProjectedTexture" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns true if the projected texture is valid (i.e. has not been removed), false otherwise.
 
 Instead of calling this directly it's a good idea to call <page>Global.IsValid</page> in case the variable is nil.
 
 
 ```
 IsValid( ptexture )
 ```
 
 
 This not only checks whether the projected texture is valid - but also checks whether it's nil.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<rets>

 	</rets>

+<example name="Checking a projected texture before use">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a projected texture, removes it, then shows the difference between calling this method directly and using the global IsValid function on a nil variable.</description>
+	<code>
+local ptexture = ProjectedTexture()
+
+ptexture:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+ptexture:SetAngles( Angle( 90, 0, 0 ) )
+ptexture:Update()
+
+print( ptexture:IsValid() ) -- true, the texture exists
+
+ptexture:Remove()
+
+print( ptexture:IsValid() ) -- false, the texture was removed
+
+-- The variable itself still holds the (now removed) texture object,
+-- so the global function returns the same result here.
+print( IsValid( ptexture ) ) -- false
+
+-- With a nil variable, calling the method directly would error,
+-- while the global function safely returns false.
+ptexture = nil
+print( IsValid( ptexture ) ) -- false
+	</code>
+</example>
````

```diff
--- original/ProjectedTexture:SetConstantAttenuation
+++ proposed/ProjectedTexture:SetConstantAttenuation
@@ -1,14 +1,43 @@
 <function name="SetConstantAttenuation" parent="ProjectedTexture" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets the constant attenuation of the projected texture.
+
+Attenuation controls how the light dims with distance. It is calculated as `1 / ( constant + linear * distance + quadratic * distance² )`. The constant term is a fixed divisor that applies at all distances, so a higher value makes the light dimmer everywhere, including close to its origin.
 
 See also <page>ProjectedTexture:SetLinearAttenuation</page> and <page>ProjectedTexture:SetQuadraticAttenuation</page>.
 
 You must call <page>ProjectedTexture:Update</page> after using this function for it to take effect.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<args>
-		<arg name="constAtten" type="number"></arg>
+		<arg name="constAtten" type="number">The constant attenuation value. Higher values make the light dimmer.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Adjusting light falloff">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a projected texture attached to the local player's view position and lowers its constant attenuation so the light stays brighter at a distance. The texture is removed when the player disconnects or the script is reloaded.</description>
+	<code>
+local light = ProjectedTexture()
+
+light:SetPos( Entity( 1 ):GetPos() + Vector( 0, 0, 64 ) )
+light:SetAngles( Angle( 90, 0, 0 ) )
+light:SetTexture( "effects/flashlight001" )
+light:SetFarZ( 500 )
+
+-- Lower constant attenuation so the light stays bright further away
+light:SetConstantAttenuation( 0 )
+light:SetLinearAttenuation( 100 )
+light:SetQuadraticAttenuation( 0 )
+
+light:Update()
+
+-- Remove the projected texture on reload or disconnect
+hook.Add( "OnEntityCreated", "RemoveProjectedTextureExample", function()
+	if not IsValid( light ) then return end
+
+	light:Remove()
+	hook.Remove( "OnEntityCreated", "RemoveProjectedTextureExample" )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
--- original/ProjectedTexture:SetNoCull
+++ proposed/ProjectedTexture:SetNoCull
@@ -1,13 +1,39 @@
 <function name="SetNoCull" parent="ProjectedTexture" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Allows disabling of projected texture view-frustum culling for cases where said culling creates unwanted side effects. Disabling culling will have a negative effect on performance.
 
 Culling makes projected textures off screen to stop rendering/updating.
 	</description>
 	<added>2024.10.09</added>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="enable" type="boolean">`false` to enable culling (default), `true` to disable.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Disabling culling on a projected texture">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a projected texture and disables its view-frustum culling, so it keeps rendering and updating even when it leaves the screen. The texture is removed after 10 seconds.</description>
+	<code>
+local proj = ProjectedTexture()
+
+proj:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 64 ) )
+proj:SetAngles( Angle( 90, 0, 0 ) )
+proj:SetTexture( "effects/flashlight001" )
+proj:SetEnableShadows( true )
+
+-- Keep the texture rendering even when it is outside the view frustum
+proj:SetNoCull( true )
+
+proj:Update()
+
+timer.Simple( 10, function()
+	if ( IsValid( proj ) ) then
+		proj:Remove()
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>Projected textures are culled by default. Call this with `true` only when culling causes visible problems, such as a texture popping off when its origin leaves the screen while its projected light should still be visible.</note>
+
+<note>Disabling culling makes the projected texture render and update regardless of whether it is on screen, which costs performance. Re-enable culling with `SetNoCull( false )` when it is no longer needed.</note>
```

Matched committed Lua definitions; helper and caller context may be incomplete

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091687-KCdmQzvyTBpJhlaDD8zI`. Duration: 7.92s. Attempt cost: 0.00067988.

- The example populates propsel.Controls manually because no population method for PropSelect was supplied in the evidence; if a documented method such as an AddModel or SetModelTable function exists, the example should use it instead.
- The source matches on either icon.Model or icon.Value; the description now reflects this. The existing arg name mdl and ret declaration were preserved.

```diff
--- original/PropSelect:FindModelByValue
+++ proposed/PropSelect:FindModelByValue
@@ -1,13 +1,54 @@
 <function name="FindModelByValue" parent="PropSelect" type="panelfunc">
 	<description>
 Find a <page>SpawnIcon</page> panel based on the input model path.
+
+The function loops through the panel's `Controls` table and returns the first icon whose `Model` or `Value` field equals the given value. This means it can match either a model path string or whatever value an icon was assigned.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<added>2024.09.02</added>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="mdl" type="string">The model to find within this <page>PropSelect</page>.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="SpawnIcon">The found spawnicon, or `nil`.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Finding an icon by model path">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a <page>PropSelect</page>, fills its `Controls` table with <page>SpawnIcon</page> panels, and looks one up by model path. The found icon is highlighted by printing its model.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 400, 300 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+local propsel = vgui.Create( "PropSelect", frame )
+propsel:Dock( FILL )
+
+-- Populate the panel's Controls table with spawn icons
+local models = {
+	"models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl",
+	"models/props_junk/popcan01a.mdl"
+}
+
+for _, mdl in ipairs( models ) do
+	local icon = vgui.Create( "SpawnIcon", propsel )
+	icon:SetModel( mdl )
+	icon.Model = mdl
+	icon.Value = mdl
+	icon:Dock( LEFT )
+
+	table.insert( propsel.Controls, icon )
+end
+
+-- Look up one of the icons by its model path
+local icon = propsel:FindModelByValue( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+
+if ( icon ) then
+	print( "Found icon for model: " .. icon.Model )
+else
+	print( "No icon found for that model" )
+end
+	</code>
+	<output>Found icon for model: models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl</output>
+</example>
```

- No Lua implementation was supplied. The hook name, arguments, and boolean return are preserved exactly as documented; native status remains unverified.
- The example's pattern of calling the stored panel method to preserve default behavior for unhandled keys is a common DPanel override technique, not behavior evidenced by a supplied implementation.

```diff
--- original/TextEntry:OnKeyCodeTyped
+++ proposed/TextEntry:OnKeyCodeTyped
@@ -1,15 +1,39 @@
 <function name="OnKeyCodeTyped" parent="TextEntry" type="panelhook">
 	<description>
 Called from engine whenever a valid character is typed while the text entry is focused.
 
 Used internally for functionality of <page>DTextEntry</page>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
-		<arg name="keyCode" type="number">They key code of the key pressed, see <page>Enums/KEY</page>.</arg>
+		<arg name="keyCode" type="number">The key code of the key pressed, see <page>Enums/KEY</page>.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Whether you've handled the key press. Returning true prevents the default text entry behavior from occurring.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Blocking the enter key">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a <page>DTextEntry</page> and overrides its OnKeyCodeTyped method so pressing the enter key prints the current text instead of submitting it. Other keys fall through to the default behavior by returning the result of the panel's original implementation.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 100 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:MakePopup()
+
+local entry = vgui.Create( "DTextEntry", frame )
+entry:Dock( FILL )
+
+-- Store the original implementation so non handled keys still work normally
+local baseOnKeyCodeTyped = entry.OnKeyCodeTyped
+
+function entry:OnKeyCodeTyped( keyCode )
+	if ( keyCode == KEY_ENTER ) then
+		print( "Enter pressed, text is: " .. self:GetText() )
+		return true -- Block the default enter behavior
+	end
+
+	return baseOnKeyCodeTyped( self, keyCode )
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
```

## 2807. VMatrix:GetInverse

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/VMatrix%3AGetInverse) | Revision: 512171

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091806-Z6Gelg2KyEYx8zpVWCJo`. Duration: 8.74s. Attempt cost: 0.00055505.


```diff
--- original/VMatrix:GetInverse
+++ proposed/VMatrix:GetInverse
@@ -1,14 +1,39 @@
 <function name="GetInverse" parent="VMatrix" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns an inverted matrix without modifying the original matrix.
 
 Inverting the matrix will fail if its [determinant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinant) is 0 or close to 0. (ie. its "scale" in any direction is 0.)
 
 See also <page>VMatrix:GetInverseTR</page>.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="VMatrix">The inverted matrix if possible, nil otherwise</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Undoing a transform">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Builds a matrix that scales and translates a vector, then uses its inverse to map the transformed vector back to the original. Prints the recovered vector.</description>
+	<code>
+local m = Matrix()
+m:Scale( Vector( 2, 2, 2 ) )
+m:Translate( Vector( 10, 0, 0 ) )
+
+local transformed = m * Vector( 1, 2, 3 )
+
+local inverse = m:GetInverse()
+if ( inverse ) then
+	local recovered = inverse * transformed
+
+	print( recovered )
+else
+	print( "Matrix is not invertible" )
+end
+	</code>
+	<output>1.000000 2.000000 3.000000</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>The multiplication operator applies the matrix to a <page>Vector</page>. Multiplying the inverse by the result of the original multiplication recovers the input vector.</note>
+
+<note>Because the original matrix is not modified, you can call this repeatedly on the same matrix without side effects.</note>
+
```

```diff
--- original/VMatrix:GetInverseTR
+++ proposed/VMatrix:GetInverseTR
@@ -1,14 +1,35 @@
 <function name="GetInverseTR" parent="VMatrix" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns an inverted matrix without modifying the original matrix. This function will not fail, but only works correctly on matrices that contain only translation and/or rotation.
 
 Using this function on a matrix with modified scale may return an incorrect inverted matrix.
 
 To get the inverse of a matrix that contains other modifications, see <page>VMatrix:GetInverse</page>.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="VMatrix">The inverted matrix.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Transforming a world position back to local space">
+	<description>Runs shared. Builds a matrix from a rotation and a translation, inverts it, and uses the inverse to convert a world position back into the matrix's local space. The printed result is the local offset of the world position relative to the matrix.</description>
+	<code>
+local matrix = Matrix()
+matrix:SetAngles( Angle( 0, 90, 0 ) ) -- rotated 90 degrees around the up axis
+matrix:SetTranslation( Vector( 100, 0, 0 ) )
+
+local inverse = matrix:GetInverseTR()
+
+-- A world position 50 units in front of the matrix origin
+local worldPos = matrix * Vector( 0, 50, 0 )
+
+-- The inverse matrix converts the world position back to local space
+local localPos = inverse * worldPos
+print( localPos ) -- should be close to 0, 50, 0
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>
```

## 2839. Vector:Cross

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector%3ACross) | Revision: 552453

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091696-iaVNY4UVe6qTZkCELxBa`. Duration: 6.53s. Attempt cost: 0.00041583.


```diff
--- original/Vector:Cross
+++ proposed/Vector:Cross
@@ -1,17 +1,34 @@
 <function name="Cross" parent="Vector" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Calculates the cross product of this vector and the passed one.
 
 The cross product of two vectors is a 3-dimensional vector with a direction perpendicular (at right angles) to both of them (according to the [right-hand rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right-hand_rule)), and magnitude equal to the area of parallelogram they span. This is defined as the product of the magnitudes, the sine of the angle between them, and unit (normal) vector `n` defined by the right-hand rule:
 :**a** &times; **b** = &#124;**a**&#124; &#124;**b**&#124; sin(&theta;) **n&#770;**
 where **a** and **b** are vectors, and **n&#770;** is a unit vector (magnitude of 1) perpendicular to both.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="otherVector" type="Vector">Vector to calculate the cross product with.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Vector">The cross product of the two vectors.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<note>Because the magnitude includes the sine of the angle between the vectors, the result is a zero vector when the two vectors are parallel or one of them is zero. Normalize the result with <page text="Vector:GetNormalized">Vector:GetNormalized</page> when a unit normal is needed.</note>
+
+<example name="Surface normal of a triangle">
+	<description>Computes a unit normal vector facing away from the front face of a triangle defined by three points. Runs in any realm. Prints the normal and the triangle area, which equals half the magnitude of the cross product.</description>
+	<code>
+local a = Vector( 0, 0, 0 )
+local b = Vector( 10, 0, 0 )
+local c = Vector( 0, 10, 0 )
+
+local normal = ( b - a ):Cross( c - a ):GetNormalized()
+local area = ( b - a ):Cross( c - a ):Length() / 2
+
+print( normal ) -- 0 0 1, straight up for this triangle
+print( area ) -- 50
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
 Returns the squared length of the vectors x and y value, x&sup2; + y&sup2;.
 
 This is faster than <page>Vector:Length2D</page> as calculating the square root is an expensive process.
+

Call <page>Vector:Length2D</page> or <page>math.sqrt</page> on the result when you need the actual distance.

+

+for _, ent in ipairs( ents.FindByClass( "info_player_start" ) ) do

+
+	if ( not closestDist or dist < closestDist ) then
```

## 2848. Vector:LengthSqr

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Vector%3ALengthSqr) | Revision: 549246

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091707-apmvxZxGchqolwP1W8up`. Duration: 8.39s. Attempt cost: 0.000247868.

- Original page had no sources; LengthSqr behavior is standard and native status remains unverified, so no source tags were added.
- Example uses Vector:DistanceToSqr, which is the two vector form of the same squared length calculation; its page should be verified to exist at that address.

```diff
--- original/Vector:LengthSqr
+++ proposed/Vector:LengthSqr
@@ -1,12 +1,41 @@
 <function name="LengthSqr" parent="Vector" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns the squared length of the vector, x&sup2; + y&sup2; + z&sup2;.
 
 This is faster than <page>Vector:Length</page> as calculating the square root is an expensive process.
+
+Because the result is squared, it cannot be compared directly with distances expressed in units. Use it when comparing lengths against each other, or when the actual distance is not needed. For example, comparing two squared lengths gives the same result as comparing their lengths, since squaring preserves order for nonnegative values.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">Squared length of the vector</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Finding the closest entity">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Finds which of the map's spawn points is closest to a player without calling <page>Vector:Length</page> or <page>Vector:Distance</page>, avoiding square root calculations entirely.</description>
+	<code>
+local playerPos = Entity( 1 ):GetPos()
+
+local closest, closestDistSqr
+for _, spawnPoint in ipairs( ents.FindByClass( "info_player_start" ) ) do
+	local distSqr = spawnPoint:GetPos():DistanceToSqr( playerPos )
+
+	if not closest or distSqr &lt; closestDistSqr then
+		closest = spawnPoint
+		closestDistSqr = distSqr
+	end
+end
+
+if closest then
+	print( "Closest spawn point is at", closest:GetPos() )
+end
+	</code>
+	<description>
+The squared distance between two vectors can also be computed as `( a - b ):LengthSqr()`. <page>Vector:DistanceToSqr</page> does the same in one call.
+	</description>
+</example>
+
+<note>
+To check whether a point is within a radius, compare the squared length against the squared radius. For example, `pos:LengthSqr() &lt; 100 * 100` is true when `pos` is closer than 100 units to the origin.
+</note>
```

```diff
--- original/Vehicle:SetSteering
+++ proposed/Vehicle:SetSteering
@@ -1,12 +1,44 @@
 <function name="SetSteering" parent="Vehicle" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets the steering of the vehicle.
 <validate>The correct range, 0 to 1 or -1 to 1</validate>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="front" type="number">Angle of the front wheels (-1 to 1)</arg>
 		<arg name="rear" type="number">Angle of the rear wheels (-1 to 1)</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Steering a vehicle from code">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Steers a spawned jeep to the left for one second, then releases the steering. The value is applied every tick because the game resets steering when no input is given.</description>
+	<code>
+local veh = ents.Create( "prop_vehicle_jeep" )
+veh:SetModel( "models/buggy.mdl" )
+veh:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+veh:Spawn()
+
+local timerName = "SteerTest" .. veh:EntIndex()
+
+timer.Create( timerName, 0, 0, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( veh ) ) then
+		timer.Remove( timerName )
+		return
+	end
+
+	-- Steer left. Use 0 to release the steering.
+	veh:SetSteering( -1, 0 )
+end )
+
+-- Stop steering after one second and clean up.
+timer.Simple( 1, function()
+	timer.Remove( timerName )
+
+	if ( IsValid( veh ) ) then
+		veh:SetSteering( 0, 0 )
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The steering value is not held between calls. Call this function repeatedly, for example in a timer or the <page text="Think">Global.Think</page> hook, to keep the wheels turned.</note>
```

```diff
+	if ( self.Owner:IsValid() and CurTime() < ( self.NextReloadAnim or 0 ) ) then return end

+
+	-- Play the viewmodel reload activity
+	self:SendWeaponAnim( ACT_VM_RELOAD )

+	-- Reset to the idle activity after the animation finishes

+	end )
+end
```

```diff
--- original/Weapon:SetNextPrimaryFire
+++ proposed/Weapon:SetNextPrimaryFire
@@ -1,13 +1,36 @@
 <function name="SetNextPrimaryFire" parent="Weapon" type="classfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets when the weapon can fire again. Time should be based on <page>Global.CurTime</page>.
+
+This is usually called inside <page>WEAPON:PrimaryAttack</page> to enforce a fire rate. Until the given time is reached, the engine blocks further primary attacks for the weapon's owner. Passing a time in the past or equal to <page>Global.CurTime</page> allows firing again immediately.
 
 <note>The standard HL2 Pistol (`weapon_pistol`) bypasses this function due to an [internal implementation](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/master/src/game/server/hl2/weapon_pistol.cpp#L313-L317).</note>
 <bug issue="3786">This will fire extra bullets if the time is set to less than <page>Global.CurTime</page>.</bug>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="time" type="number">Time when player should be able to use primary fire again</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Enforcing a fire rate">
+	<description>Inside a scripted weapon's <page>WEAPON:PrimaryAttack</page> hook. Runs on the server in normal play. The weapon fires one bullet, then waits 0.3 seconds before it can fire again.</description>
+	<code>
+function SWEP:PrimaryAttack()
+	self:SetNextPrimaryFire( CurTime() + 0.3 )
+
+	local owner = self:GetOwner()
+	if not IsValid( owner ) then return end
+
+	local bullet = {}
+	bullet.Num = 1
+	bullet.Src = owner:GetShootPos()
+	bullet.Dir = owner:GetAimVector()
+	bullet.Spread = Vector( 0.01, 0.01, 0 )
+	bullet.Damage = 10
+
+	owner:FireBullets( bullet )
+	self:EmitSound( "Weapon_Pistol.Single" )
+end
```

```diff
+	<description>Returns the arithmetically shifted value.

+Performs a right shift that preserves the sign of the number. Instead of filling the vacated high bits with zeros like a logical shift, the sign bit is copied into them. This means negative values stay negative and positive values stay positive after the shift. Dividing a value by 2 once per shifted bit is a common way to think about the result, with the result rounded toward negative infinity for negative values.

+print( bit.arshift( 16, 2 ) )
+print( bit.arshift( -16, 2 ) )
+print( bit.rshift( -16, 2 ) )
+	</code>
```

```diff
--- original/bit.rshift
+++ proposed/bit.rshift
@@ -1,15 +1,29 @@
 <function name="rshift" parent="bit" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 		Returns the right shifted value.
+		Each shift by one bit moves every bit one position to the right. The lowest bit is discarded and a zero bit is added on the left, so for nonnegative values this is the same as dividing by 2 to the power of shiftCount and dropping the remainder.
 		<note>The returned value will be clamped to a signed 32-bit integer, even on 64-bit builds.</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="value" type="number">The value to be manipulated.</arg>
 		<arg name="shiftCount" type="number">Amounts of bits to shift right by.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">The shifted value.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Extracting a byte from a packed number">
+	<description>Runs shared. Right shifts can be used to read parts of a packed 32-bit value. This splits a packed color value into its red, green, and blue components.</description>
+	<code>
+local packed = bit.bor( bit.lshift( 255, 16 ), bit.lshift( 128, 8 ), 64 )
+
+local r = bit.band( bit.rshift( packed, 16 ), 255 )
+local g = bit.band( bit.rshift( packed, 8 ), 255 )
+local b = bit.band( packed, 255 )
+
+print( r, g, b )
+	</code>
+	<output>255	128	64</output>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/cam.End2D
+++ proposed/cam.End2D
@@ -1,7 +1,30 @@
 <function name="End2D" parent="cam" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Switches the renderer back to the previous drawing mode from a 2D context.
+
+This must be called after every successful <page>cam.Start2D</page> call. It restores the rendering state that was active before the 2D context was entered, so subsequent rendering (such as 3D rendering or the game view) is not drawn with 2D settings.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Drawing 2D text">
+	<description>Runs on the client inside the <page>GM:HUDPaint</page> hook. Draws a message in the middle of the screen inside a 2D rendering context, then ends it.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "My2DDrawing", function()
+	if ( not cam.Start2D() ) then return end
+
+	draw.SimpleText( "Hello!", "DermaDefault", ScrW() / 2, ScrH() / 2, color_white, TEXT_ALIGN_CENTER, TEXT_ALIGN_CENTER )
+
+	cam.End2D()
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>
+<page>cam.Start2D</page> returns false when a 2D context is already active. In that case <page>cam.End2D</page> must not be called, since there is no matching context to end. The example above checks the return value and returns early to keep the calls balanced.
+</note>
+
+<warning>
+Calling <page>cam.End2D</page> without a matching successful <page>cam.Start2D</page> call can cause rendering errors or unexpected behavior. Always end every 2D context you start.
+</warning>
+
```

```diff
-	<description>Sets up a new 3d context using orthographic projection.</description>
+	<description>Sets up a new 3d context using orthographic projection.
+
+
+In an orthographic projection objects do not shrink with distance, so the view has no perspective. The four offsets define the visible plane in world units relative to the current view origin. The call must be paired with <page>cam.EndOrthoView</page> to restore the previous projection.</description>

 </function>

+	<description>Runs on the client inside <page>HUDPaint</page>. It renders the world with an orthographic projection centered on the local player, then restores the normal projection. The offsets are chosen so the visible area is 512 by 512 world units around the player.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "OrthoViewExample", function()
+	local ply = LocalPlayer()
+	if ( not IsValid( ply ) ) then return end
+
+	local half = 256
+
+	cam.StartOrthoView( -half, -half, half, half )
+		render.SetBlend( 0.5 )
+		cam.Start3D()
+			render.SetViewSetup( {
+				origin = ply:GetPos() + Vector( 0, 0, 512 ),
+				angles = Angle( 90, 0, 0 ),
+				x = 0,
+				y = 0,
+				w = ScrW(),
+				h = ScrH()
+			} )
+			render.RenderView( {
+				origin = ply:GetPos() + Vector( 0, 0, 512 ),
+				angles = Angle( 90, 0, 0 ),
+				x = 0,
+				y = 0,
+				w = ScrW(),
+				h = ScrH()
+			} )
+		cam.End3D()
+		render.SetBlend( 1 )
+	cam.EndOrthoView()
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The view is centered on the current render origin, so the offsets act like a rectangle around that point rather than absolute world coordinates.</note>
+
```

```diff
 	<description>
 <internal></internal>
 Stores the constraint entity in the constrained entity's `Constraints` table.
 
 This will make the `constrt` entity be removed if any of the other entities `ent1`, `ent2`, `ent3` or `ent4` are removed by any means.

+
```

```diff
+	box1, box2,
+	0, 0,
+	Vector( 0, 0, 10 ), Vector( 0, 0, 10 ),
+	1000, -- stiffness
+	100, -- damping
+	50, -- relative damping
+	"cable/cable2", -- rope material
+	2, -- rope width
+	false, -- push and pull, not stretch only
+	Color( 255, 0, 0 ) -- red rope
+)
+
+if ( IsValid( constraintEnt ) ) then
+	print( "Created spring:", constraintEnt )
+end
+
```

## 3030. coroutine.resume

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/coroutine.resume) | Revision: 529430

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091718-ODOBfbySLvvYz0fVSbpI`. Duration: 17.77s. Attempt cost: 0.000523497.

- No Lua implementation was supplied, so no default values could be verified or added; the existing contract is preserved unchanged.
- Added explanation of first resume versus later resume argument routing and the success/error return shape, which follows standard Lua coroutine semantics; confirm against the native implementation if available.

```diff
--- original/coroutine.resume
+++ proposed/coroutine.resume
@@ -1,13 +1,41 @@
 <function name="resume" parent="coroutine" type="libraryfunc">
-	<description>Resumes the given coroutine and passes the given vararg to either the function arguments or the <page>coroutine.yield</page> that is inside that function and returns whatever yield is called with the next time or by the final return in the function.</description>
+	<description>Resumes the given coroutine and passes the given vararg to either the function arguments or the <page>coroutine.yield</page> that is inside that function and returns whatever yield is called with the next time or by the final return in the function.
+
+The first resume passes the vararg to the coroutine function itself as arguments. Any later resume passes the vararg to the <page>coroutine.yield</page> call the coroutine is currently suspended at. The coroutine runs until it yields again, returns, or raises an error.
+
+The first returned value reports success. If it is false, the second value is the error message. If it is true, the remaining values are the arguments the coroutine passed to <page>coroutine.yield</page>, or the coroutine function's return values if it finished.</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="coroutine" type="thread">Coroutine to resume.</arg>
 		<arg name="args" type="vararg">Arguments to be returned by <page>coroutine.yield</page>.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">If the executed thread code had no errors occur within it.</ret>
 		<ret name="" type="vararg">If an error occurred, this will be a string containing the error message. Otherwise, this will be arguments that were yielded.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Stepping through a coroutine">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Creates a coroutine that yields twice, then resumes it step by step. The first resume supplies the function arguments, later resumes supply the values returned by coroutine.yield.</description>
+	<code>
+local co = coroutine.create( function( name )
+	local greeting = coroutine.yield( "started " .. name )
+	coroutine.yield( "received " .. greeting )
+	return "done"
+end )
+
+print( coroutine.resume( co, "task" ) ) -- true, "started task"
+print( coroutine.resume( co, "hello" ) ) -- true, "received hello"
+print( coroutine.resume( co ) ) -- true, "done"
+print( coroutine.resume( co ) ) -- false, "cannot resume dead coroutine"
+	</code>
+	<output>
+true	started task
+true	received hello
+true	done
+false	cannot resume dead coroutine
+	</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>Resuming a coroutine that has finished or raised an error returns false and an error message instead of raising an error itself. Check the first return value before using the rest.</note>
+
```

```diff
 Repeatedly yields the coroutine for the given duration before continuing.
```

```diff
 Enters an interactive mode with the user, running each string that the user enters. ## 3044. debug.sethook
```

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/debug.sethook) | Revision: 565896

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091736-Lmo9FnXqgmn4WhFdZLrR`. Duration: 44.00s. Attempt cost: 0.000907.

- No Lua implementation was supplied, so the example count output is an approximation based on typical LuaJIT behavior and is labeled as such on the page.
- The event string values ("call", "return", "line", "count") and the single hook per thread behavior come from the Lua reference linked in the existing description, not from supplied source code.

```diff
--- original/debug.sethook
+++ proposed/debug.sethook
@@ -1,20 +1,57 @@
 <function name="sethook" parent="debug" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 <deprecated></deprecated>
 
 Sets the given function as a Lua hook. This is completely different to gamemode hooks. The thread argument can be completely omitted and calling this function with no arguments will remove the current hook. This is used by default for infinite loop detection. More information on hooks can be found at http://www.lua.org/pil/23.2.html and https://www.gammon.com.au/scripts/doc.php?lua=debug.sethook
 
 Hooks are not always ran when code that has been compiled by LuaJIT's JIT compiler is being executed, this is due to Intermediate Representation internally storing constantly running bytecode for performance reasons. 	
-</description>
+
+Only one hook can be active at a time per thread. Setting a new hook replaces the previous one, and calling this function with no arguments removes the current hook.
+
+The hook function receives one argument: the event that triggered it as a full string. The possible values are `"call"`, `"return"`, `"line"`, and `"count"`. The `"count"` event only occurs when a count is set and the instruction count is reached.
+
+When the mask contains `l`, the count argument controls how many instructions pass between line events. With a count of `0` the hook runs on every instruction, which is very slow. A higher count such as `100` is usually enough for progress checks like infinite loop detection.
+
+Inside the hook, <page text="debug.getinfo">Global.debug</page> can be used to find out where the event happened.
+	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="thread" type="thread">Thread to set the hook on. This argument can be omitted.</arg>
 		<arg name="hook" type="function">Function for the hook to call. First argument in this function will be the mask event that called the hook as a full string (not as 'c' but instead as 'call').</arg>
 		<arg name="mask" type="string">The hook's mask. Can be one or more of the following events: 
 * c - Triggers the hook on each function call made from Lua.
 * r - Triggers the hook on each function return made from Lua.
 * l - Triggers the hook on each line compiled of code.</arg>
 		<arg name="count" type="number">How often to call the hook (in instructions). 0 for every instruction. Can be omitted.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Counting instructions with a line hook">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Installs a line hook that counts how many instructions run inside a loop, then removes the hook. The count is printed to the console. The exact number varies with the Lua build, so treat it as an approximation.</description>
+	<code>
+local instructions = 0
+
+debug.sethook( function( event )
+	instructions = instructions + 1
+end, "l", 1 )
+
+-- Work measured by the hook.
+local total = 0
+for i = 1, 1000 do
+	total = total + i
+end
+
+-- Remove the hook so it stops counting.
+debug.sethook()
+
+print( "Roughly " .. instructions .. " instructions ran. Sum was " .. total )
+	</code>
+	<output>Roughly 3000 instructions ran. Sum was 500500</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>The count in the output is approximate. The LuaJIT note above means some instructions may not trigger the hook at all.</note>
+
+<note>Use a larger count such as `100` for infinite loop detection. A count of `0` calls the hook on every instruction and will slow down the whole script.</note>
+
+<warning>Errors raised inside the hook function are not handled like normal errors and can break the state the hook runs in. Keep the hook function small and avoid calling code that can fail.</warning>
+
```

```diff
 <deprecated></deprecated>
 
-Sets the object's metatable. Unlike <page>Global.setmetatable</page>, this function works regardless of whether the first object passed is a valid table or not; this function even works on primitive datatypes such as numbers, functions, and even nil.</description>
+Sets the object's metatable. Unlike <page>Global.setmetatable</page>, this function works regardless of whether the first object passed is a valid table or not; this function even works on primitive datatypes such as numbers, functions, and even nil.
+
+Metatables set this way apply globally to every value of that primitive type. For example, setting a metatable on a number changes the behavior of all numbers, not just the one passed in. Passing nil as the metatable removes it and restores default behavior.

 		<arg name="metatable" type="table">The metatable to set for the object.
 If this argument is nil, then the object's metatable is removed.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">true if the object's metatable was set successfully.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Adding methods to numbers">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Sets a metatable on all numbers so they gain a `square` method, uses it, then removes the metatable to restore default behavior.</description>
+	<code>
+debug.setmetatable( 0, {
+	__index = {
+		square = function( self )
+			return self * self
+		end
+	}
+} )
+
+print( 5:square() )
+
+-- Remove the metatable so other code is not affected
+debug.setmetatable( 0, nil )
+	</code>
+	<output>25</output>
+</example>
+
+<warning>Metatables set on primitive types affect every value of that type in the entire Lua state, including code from other addons. Always remove such metatables when you are done with them, and avoid using them in released code unless you have a specific reason.</warning>
+
```

Each valid panel then has its <page text="PANEL:OnStartDragging">PANEL:OnStartDragging</page> hook called, the watched panel becomes the main dragged panel, and mouse input is captured so the drag can be tracked.

```diff
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
```

```diff
 <function name="Think" parent="dragndrop" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 <internal></internal>
 Handles all the drag'n'drop processes. Calls <page>dragndrop.UpdateReceiver</page> and <page>dragndrop.HoverThink</page>.
+
+Each call does the following:
+* Returns early if a drop menu is open.
+* If a panel is being watched for a drag (see <page>dragndrop.StartDragging</page>), starts the actual drag once the mouse moves more than 20 pixels (measured as the sum of absolute X and Y movement) from where the watch began.

If you build a custom input loop that bypasses the usual panel input processing, you can call it from a Think hook so watched panels still start dragging and drop receivers still update. This example prints whether a drag is in progress each tick while the hook is active.</description>
+    <code>
+local function DragThink()
+	dragndrop.Think()
+
+	-- Observable effect: reports the current drag state each tick.
+	print( "dragging:", dragndrop.m_Dragging != nil )
+end
+
+hook.Add( "Think", "MyDragndropThink", DragThink )
+

+    </code>
+</example>
+

+
```

```diff
 <function name="GetMethod" parent="drive" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 <internal></internal>
 Returns ( or creates if inexistent ) a driving method.
+
+The returned table stores the driven entity in its `Entity` field, the player in its `Player` field, and the driving mode network ID in its `ModeID` field. Its metatable indexes the method type registered for the current driving mode, so mode specific functions can be called on it.
+
+Returns nothing if the player is not driving an entity, the driven entity is invalid, the driving mode is unset ( `0` ), the mode ID has no registered network string, or no method type exists for that mode. A previously created method is reused as long as the player is still driving the same entity in the same mode.
 	</description>

 </function>

+	<code>
+hook.Add( "Tick", "DriveMethodExample", function()
+	local ply = Entity( 1 )
+	if ( !IsValid( ply ) ) then return end
+
+	local method = drive.GetMethod( ply )
+	if ( !method ) then return end
```

```diff
--- original/duplicator.Copy
+++ proposed/duplicator.Copy
@@ -1,20 +1,65 @@
 <function name="Copy" parent="duplicator" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Copies the entity, and all of its constraints and entities, then returns them in a table.</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<file line="615-L645">lua/includes/modules/duplicator.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="ent" type="Entity">The entity to duplicate. The function will automatically copy all constrained entities.</arg>
 		<arg name="tableToAdd" type="table" default="{}">A preexisting table to add entities and constraints in from.
 Uses the same table format as the table returned from this function.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="table">A table containing duplication info which includes the following members:
 * <page>table</page> Entities
 * <page>table</page> Constraints
 * <page>Vector</page> Mins
 * <page>Vector</page> Maxs
 
 The values of Mins & Maxs from the table are returned from <page>duplicator.WorkoutSize</page>.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<note>Only the `Entities` and `Constraints` fields of `tableToAdd` are read. If `tableToAdd` is `nil`, a fresh table is used. If either field is missing, an empty table is used for it. Passing an existing result table here lets you merge several copies into one duplication table, for example when copying multiple props at once.</note>
+
+<example name="Copy a prop and its constraints">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Finds the prop the player is looking at, copies it together with everything constrained to it, and prints how many entities and constraints were captured.</description>
+	<code>
+local ply = Entity( 1 )
+local trace = ply:GetEyeTrace()
+
+if ( not IsValid( trace.Entity ) or not trace.Entity:GetClass() == "prop_physics" ) then return end
+
+local dupe = duplicator.Copy( trace.Entity )
+
+print( "Copied " .. table.Count( dupe.Entities ) .. " entities" )
+print( "Copied " .. table.Count( dupe.Constraints ) .. " constraints" )
+print( "Bounds: " .. tostring( dupe.Mins ) .. " to " .. tostring( dupe.Maxs ) )
+	</code>
+	<output>Copied 2 entities
+Copied 1 constraints
+Bounds: -24.000000 -24.000000 -24.000000 to 24.000000 24.000000 24.000000</output>
+</example>
+
+<example name="Merge two copies into one table">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Copies two props into a single duplication table by passing the first result as `tableToAdd` for the second copy. The returned table then contains both props and any constraints between them.</description>
+	<code>
+local prop1 = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop1:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop1:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+prop1:Spawn()
+
+local prop2 = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+prop2:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+prop2:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 150 ) )
+prop2:Spawn()
+
+local combined = duplicator.Copy( prop1 )
+combined = duplicator.Copy( prop2, combined )
+
+print( table.Count( combined.Entities ) ) -- 2, both props are in one table
+
+-- Cleanup
+prop1:Remove()
+prop2:Remove()
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
 <function name="FigureOutRequiredAddons" parent="duplicator" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Checks the given duplication table and tries to figure out any addons that might be required to correctly spawn the duplication. Currently this is limited to models and material overrides saved in the duplication.
+
+The function iterates over every entity table in `dupe.Entities` (accessed with <pageGlobal>pairs</page>). For each addon returned by <page>engine.GetAddons</page>, an addon workshop ID is collected when:
+
+* the entity has a `Model` and the model file exists in that addon's mounted files, or
+* the entity has an `_DuplicatedMaterial` key and `materials/<material>.vmt` exists in that addon.
+
+The result is stored on the duplication table itself as `dupe.RequiredAddons`, a sequential table of workshop ID numbers (values from the addons' `wsid` field) with no guaranteed order. Duplicate IDs collapse into one entry.
+
+<note>The search only covers addons currently mounted by the game (as reported by <page>engine.GetAddons</page>). Addons that are required but not mounted cannot be detected.</note>
 </description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<added>2021.07.23</added>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="dupe" type="table">The duplication table to process, for example from <page>duplicator.Copy</page>.
 
-The provided table will have `RequiredAddons` key added.
-</arg>
+The provided table will have `RequiredAddons` key added. An existing `RequiredAddons` value is overwritten.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Finding required addons for a duplication">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Copies an entity with <page>duplicator.Copy</page>, runs the check on the resulting duplication table, and prints the detected required addon workshop IDs. If the model or material override comes from a currently mounted workshop addon, its workshop ID appears in the list; otherwise the list is empty.</description>
+	<code>
+local ent = entity.GetByIndex( 1 ) -- replace with a valid entity you want to copy
+if ( not IsValid( ent ) ) then return end
+
+local dupe = duplicator.Copy( ent )
+
+-- Give the entity a material override to check as well (optional)
+dupe.Entities[ 1 ]._DuplicatedMaterial = "models/debug/debugwhite"
+
+duplicator.FigureOutRequiredAddons( dupe )
+
+PrintTable( dupe.RequiredAddons )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The function reads `ent.Model` and `ent._DuplicatedMaterial` on each entity table, which are the keys the duplicator saves for entity models and material overrides. Custom duplication tables need those keys for anything to be detected.</note>
+
+
```

```diff
 <function name="GenericDuplicatorFunction" parent="duplicator" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 "Generic function for duplicating stuff" 
 
 
 This is called when <page>duplicator.CreateEntityFromTable</page> can't find an entity factory to build with. It calls <page>duplicator.DoGeneric</page> and <page>duplicator.DoGenericPhysics</page> to apply standard duplicator stored things such as the model and position.

+The function performs several checks before creating anything:
+

+* If `ents.Create` fails for the class, `nil` is returned.

+			frozen = false

+}
```

```diff
--- original/duplicator.StoreEntityModifier
+++ proposed/duplicator.StoreEntityModifier
@@ -1,11 +1,35 @@
 <function name="StoreEntityModifier" parent="duplicator" type="libraryfunc">
-	<description>Stores an entity modifier into an entity for saving.</description>
+	<description>Stores an entity modifier into an entity for saving.
+
+The data is merged into any existing modifier data of the same name and stored on the entity in the `Entity.EntityMods` table. When the entity is saved with the duplicator, the stored data is written into the save. On duplication, the function registered with <page>duplicator.RegisterEntityModifier</page> under the same name receives the data and can reapply it to the new entity.
+
+Calling this function with the same name more than once merges the new table into the stored one with <page>table.Merge</page>, so existing keys are overwritten and new keys are added. Nothing is returned and invalid entities are silently ignored.</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<file line="510-L522">lua/includes/modules/duplicator.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="entity" type="Entity">The entity to store modifier in.</arg>
 		<arg name="name" type="string">Unique modifier name as defined in <page>duplicator.RegisterEntityModifier</page>.</arg>
 		<arg name="data" type="table">Modifier data.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Storing and restoring a modifier">
+    <description>Runs on the server. Registers an entity modifier that stores a custom color on an entity and reapplies it after duplication, then stores the data on a provided entity. The registered apply function only runs when a copy is created, so the entity keeps the stored data in its `Entity.EntityMods` table for saving in the meantime.</description>
+    <code>
+duplicator.RegisterEntityModifier( "custom_color", function( ply, ent, data )
+	if ( not IsValid( ent ) ) then return end
+
+	ent.CustomColor = data.color
+end )
+
+-- Store modifier data on an entity from a provided reference.
+-- ent is the server Entity the value should be saved with.
+duplicator.StoreEntityModifier( ent, "custom_color", { color = Color( 255, 0, 0 ) } )
+
+-- Later duplication calls the registered function with the same table,
+-- setting CustomColor on the newly created copy.
+    </code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The modifier data only reaches duplicated entities. It is not applied to the original entity; if the effect should be visible immediately, apply it to the entity yourself after calling this function.</note>
+
```

## 3124. duplicator.WorkoutSize

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/duplicator.WorkoutSize) | Revision: 565964

Source: [lua/includes/modules/duplicator.lua:573](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/9bacca4b786123ac1da54145e625b1db970dbf21/garrysmod/lua/includes/modules/duplicator.lua#L573-L613)

Matched committed Lua definitions; helper and caller context may be incomplete

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091795-0c3FXZQpuTs7JPc2eHcy`. Duration: 10.62s. Attempt cost: 0.0009148.

- Source starts the bounds at Vector( -1, -1, -1 ) and Vector( 1, 1, 1 ), so the returned box is never smaller than 2 units per axis; documented in the description.
- Entries missing Mins, Maxs, Pos or Angle are silently skipped via continue; documented in the description and argument prose.
- File line range in the existing markup (569-L609) differs slightly from the supplied source range (573-613); left unchanged.

```diff
--- original/duplicator.WorkoutSize
+++ proposed/duplicator.WorkoutSize
@@ -1,15 +1,51 @@
 <function name="WorkoutSize" parent="duplicator" type="libraryfunc">
-	<description>Works out the AABB size of the duplication.</description>
+	<description>Works out the AABB size of the duplication.
+
+Each entry in the table is a duplication datum. Entries are skipped unless they contain the fields `Mins`, `Maxs`, `Pos` and `Angle`. The local bounds of each entry are rotated by its `Angle` and offset by its `Pos` with <page text="LocalToWorld">Global.LocalToWorld</page>, and the returned vectors are the combined world space bounds of all entries.
+
+The result is never smaller than a 2 by 2 by 2 unit box centered on the origin, because the calculation starts from `Vector( -1, -1, -1 )` and `Vector( 1, 1, 1 )`.</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<file line="569-L609">lua/includes/modules/duplicator.lua</file>
 	<args>
-		<arg name="Ents" type="table">A table of entity duplication datums.</arg>
+		<arg name="Ents" type="table">A table of entity duplication datums. Each datum needs `Mins`, `Maxs`, `Pos` and `Angle` fields to be counted.</arg>
 	</args>
 
 
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="Mins" type="Vector">AABB mins vector.</ret>
 		<ret name="Maxs" type="Vector">AABB maxs vector.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Measuring a duplication">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Builds two duplication datums from an existing prop's bounds and prints the combined world space size of the duplication. The datums are offset so the second copy sits 100 units to the right of the first.</description>
+	<code>
+local prop = Entity( 1 ) -- replace with a valid prop entity
+
+if ( !IsValid( prop ) ) then return end
+
+local mins, maxs = prop:OBBMins(), prop:OBBMaxs()
+
+local Ents = {
+	{
+		Pos = prop:GetPos(),
+		Angle = prop:GetAngles(),
+		Mins = mins,
+		Maxs = maxs
+	},
+	{
+		Pos = prop:GetPos() + Vector( 100, 0, 0 ),
+		Angle = prop:GetAngles(),
+		Mins = mins,
+		Maxs = maxs
+	}
+}
+
+local dmins, dmaxs = duplicator.WorkoutSize( Ents )
+
+print( "Duplication bounds:", dmins, dmaxs )
+print( "Size:", dmaxs - dmins )
+	</code>
+	<output>The first print shows the combined world space mins and maxs vectors. The second shows the total size, which is at least 2 units wide on every axis even for a tiny prop, and wider on the x axis because of the 100 unit offset.</output>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
--- original/engine.IsPlayingDemo
+++ proposed/engine.IsPlayingDemo
@@ -1,12 +1,39 @@
 <function name="IsPlayingDemo" parent="engine" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns true if we're currently playing a demo.
 
 You will notice that there's no server-side version of this. That's because there is no server when playing a demo. Demos are both recorded and played back purely clientside.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Whether the game is currently playing a demo or not.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Demo playback indicator">
+	<description>Runs clientside. Prints a message once when demo playback starts and once when it stops. Demos can be played back from the main menu or in game, so this works in both realms where the function is available.</description>
+	<code>
+local wasPlaying = false
+
+hook.Add( "Think", "DemoPlaybackCheck", function()
+	local playing = engine.IsPlayingDemo()
+
+	if playing ~= wasPlaying then
+		if playing then
+			print( "Demo playback started." )
+		else
+			print( "Demo playback stopped." )
+		end
+
+		wasPlaying = playing
+	end
+end )
+
+-- Remove the hook when it is no longer needed:
+-- hook.Remove( "Think", "DemoPlaybackCheck" )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>
+Because demo playback is purely clientside, any serverside logic recorded in the demo is not reexecuted. Addons that rely on serverside state will not behave the same during playback.
+</note>
```

```diff
--- original/engine.LightStyle
+++ proposed/engine.LightStyle
@@ -1,13 +1,27 @@
 <function name="LightStyle" parent="engine" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 This is a direct binding to the function `engine->LightStyle`. This function allows you to change the default light style of the map - so you can make lighting lighter or darker. You’ll need to call <page>render.RedownloadAllLightmaps</page> clientside to refresh the lightmaps to this new color.
+
+The pattern is a string of brightness characters. The engine samples through the pattern over time, so a single character such as `m` sets a constant brightness, while a longer string such as `abcxyz` cycles through those brightness levels and produces a flicker. Characters beyond `z` are accepted and produce brightness above the normal maximum.
 
 <bug issue="3626">Calling this function with arguments 0 and "a" will cause dynamic lights such as those produced by the Light tool to stop working.</bug>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="lightstyle" type="number">The lightstyle to edit. 0 to 63. If you want to edit map lighting, you want to set this to 0.</arg>
 		<arg name="pattern" type="string">The pattern to change the lightstyle to. `a` is the darkest, `z` is the brightest. You can use stuff like "abcxyz" to make flashing patterns. The normal brightness for a map is `m`. Values over `z` are allowed, `~` for instance.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Brighten the map lighting">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Sets lightstyle 0 to a constant brightness above the map default, then tells all clients to redownload their lightmaps so the change becomes visible.</description>
+	<code>
+-- Set lightstyle 0 to a constant brightness brighter than the default "m"
+engine.LightStyle( 0, "z" )
+
+-- Clients must refresh their lightmaps to see the change
+for _, ply in ipairs( player.GetAll() ) do
+	ply:SendLua( "render.RedownloadAllLightmaps()" )
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
```

```diff
 Similar to **#**<page>ents.GetAll</page>() but with better performance since the entity table doesn't have to be generated.
```
