 <function name="AddFrame" parent="frame_blend" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 <internal></internal>
 
 Adds a frame to the blend. Calls <page>frame_blend.CompleteFrame</page> once enough frames have passed since last <page>frame_blend.CompleteFrame</page> call.
+
+Internally this increments a frame counter and compares it against the `pp_fb_frames` console variable. When the counter reaches that value, <page>frame_blend.CompleteFrame</page> is called and the counter resets to 0. With the default value of `pp_fb_frames`, a complete frame is captured every other frame.

 </function>
 
+<example name="Feeding the blend">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Registers a hook that adds a frame to the blend every rendered frame, then removes the hook after 5 seconds. The blend system uses the captured frames to interpolate between screenshots, which is visible as a smoothing effect on screen motion.</description>
+	<code>
+local function AddBlendFrame()
+	frame_blend.AddFrame()
+end
+
+hook.Add( "PostRender", "FrameBlendExample", AddBlendFrame )
+
+-- Stop feeding frames after 5 seconds
+hook.Add( "SetupMove", "FrameBlendExampleCleanup", function( ply, mv, cmd )
+	if ( CurTime() > 5 ) then
+		hook.Remove( "PostRender", "FrameBlendExample" )
+		hook.Remove( "SetupMove", "FrameBlendExampleCleanup" )
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>
+This function is part of the internal frame blending post process system. It is only useful together with <page>frame_blend.CompleteFrame</page> and the related frame_blend functions.

- Source shows BlendFrame depends on internal state (NumFramesTaken, texFB, texMB0, matFB) created by the frame_blend postprocess system, so the example demonstrates enabling the feature through its console variables rather than calling the internal function directly.

```diff
--- original/frame_blend.BlendFrame
+++ proposed/frame_blend.BlendFrame
@@ -1,9 +1,26 @@
 <function name="BlendFrame" parent="frame_blend" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 <internal></internal>
 
 Blends the frame(s).
+
+This function is called by the frame blend postprocess system on the client. It reads the current screen into an internal render target, computes an alpha value from the `pp_fb_frames` and `pp_fb_shutter` console variables and the number of frames taken so far, and draws the accumulated blend into an internal motion blur target with that alpha. The result is the motion blur effect seen when frame blending is enabled.
+
+It takes no arguments and returns nothing. It relies on internal state created by the frame blend system, such as the frame counter and the internal render targets and material, so calling it directly outside that system has no useful effect. To use frame blending, set the `pp_fb_frames` and `pp_fb_shutter` console variables and let the system call this function each frame.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Enabling frame blending">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Sets the frame blend console variables so the internal postprocess system starts blending frames. The visible effect is motion blur that scales with how many frames are blended and the shutter value. Set `pp_fb_frames` back to 0 to disable the effect.</description>
+	<code>
+-- Higher frame count gives a stronger, longer blur trail
+RunConsoleCommand( "pp_fb_frames", "8" )
+-- Shutter controls how much each frame contributes to the blend
+RunConsoleCommand( "pp_fb_shutter", "0.5" )
+
+-- The system now calls frame_blend.BlendFrame every frame.
+-- To turn the effect off again:
+-- RunConsoleCommand( "pp_fb_frames", "0" )

+</example>

 	<description>Returns whether we should skip frame or not.</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Should the frame be skipped or not.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<note>This function is part of the frame blend post processing effect. It reads the convars `pp_fb_shutter` and `pp_fb_frames` and the internal frame counter `NumFramesTaken`, so it only reports skipping while a frame blend capture is in progress.</note>
+
+<description>The function returns true only during the padded start and end of a frame blend capture. The padding is half of the shutter fraction, computed as `math.floor( pp_fb_frames * pp_fb_shutter * 0.5 )`. Frames before `padding` and frames at or after `pp_fb_frames - padding` are skipped so the blended sequence only uses the fully open shutter portion.</description>
+
+<note>If `pp_fb_shutter` is 0 or less, or 1 or greater, the function always returns false and no frames are skipped.</note>
+
+<example name="Checking frame skipping">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Enable the frame blend effect with `pp_fb_frames 10` and `pp_fb_shutter 0.5` in the console, then this hook prints whether the current frame is skipped while the capture runs.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "FrameBlendSkipCheck", function()
+	if ( frame_blend.ShouldSkipFrame() ) then
+		draw.SimpleText( "Frame skipped", "DermaDefault", 50, 50, color_white )
+	end
+end )
+
+-- Remove the hook when you are done:
+-- hook.Remove( "HUDPaint", "FrameBlendSkipCheck" )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

--- original/game.CleanUpMap

@@ -1,25 +1,39 @@
 <function name="CleanUpMap" parent="game" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Removes most entities, and then respawns entities created by the map, as if the map was just loaded.
 
 There are certain exclusions, such as players or weapons held by players, soundscapes and others.  
 <page text="EFL_KEEP_ON_RECREATE_ENTITIES">enums/EFL</page> can be set on entities to preserve them through a map cleanup.
 
 On the client it will remove decals, sounds, gibs, dead NPCs, and entities created via <page>ents.CreateClientProp</page>. This function is ran on all clients from server automatically, when it is called on the server.
 
 This function calls <page>GM:PreCleanupMap</page> before cleaning up the map and <page>GM:PostCleanupMap</page> after cleaning up the map.
 
 Beware of calling this function in hooks that may be called on map clean up (such as <page>ENTITY:StartTouch</page>) to avoid infinite loops.
 
 <bug issue="2874">Calling this destroys all BASS streams.</bug>
 <bug issue="6105">The EFL_KEEP_ON_RECREATE_ENTITIES flag doesn't prevent an entity from being recreated, which means flagged entities will be duplicated since they are both kept and recreated.</bug>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="dontSendToClients" type="boolean" default="false">If set to `true`, don't run this functions on all clients.</arg>
 		<arg name="extraFilters" type="table" default="{}">Entity classes not to reset during cleanup.</arg>
 		<arg name="callback" type="function" default="nil" added="2024.01.04">If set, delays the map cleanup until the end of a server tick, allowing bypassing the entity limit on maps with large amounts of them. Otherwise the entities will not be cleaned up until the end of the server tick.
 
 The callback function will be called after the map cleanup has been performed.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Admin cleanup command">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Adds a console command that only superadmins can use to reset the map. Classes in `extraFilters` are not reset: existing `prop_physics` props keep their current state instead of being removed or recreated.</description>
+	<code>
+concommand.Add( "cleanup_map", function( ply )
+	if not IsValid( ply ) or not ply:IsSuperAdmin() then return end
+
+	game.CleanUpMap( false, { "prop_physics" }, function()
+		print( "Map cleanup finished." )
+	end )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>Map cleanup finished. after the map has been cleaned up on the server.</output>
+</example>
```

 <function name="GetIPAddress" parent="game" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns the public IP address and port of the current server. This will return the IP/port that you are connecting through when ran clientside.
 <note>Returns "loopback" in singleplayer.</note>
 
 <bug issue="3001">Returns "0.0.0.0:`port`" on the server when called too early, including in <page>GM:Initialize</page> and <page>GM:InitPostEntity</page>. This bug seems to only happen the first time a server is launched, and will return the correct value after switching maps.</bug>

+	hook.Remove( "Think", "LogServerAddress" )

If this claim is unsupported by engine behavior documentation, the example plus description sentence about timers should be flagged for manual verification.

```diff
--- original/game.SetTimeScale
+++ proposed/game.SetTimeScale
@@ -1,19 +1,40 @@
 <function name="SetTimeScale" parent="game" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets the time scale of the game logic.
 
 To slow down or speed up the movement of a specific player, use <page>Player:SetLaggedMovementValue</page> instead.
 
 See <page>physenv.SetTimeScale</page> if you wish to only scale the physics timescale.
 
 This function is meant to remove the need of using the `host_timescale` convar, which is cheat protected.  
 The true timescale will be `host_timescale` multiplied by <page>game.GetTimeScale</page>.
 
 Like `host_timescale`, this method does not affect sounds, if you wish to change that, look into <page>GM:EntityEmitSound</page>.
+
+The setting persists until changed again and applies to the whole game world, affecting things such as entity thinking, timers scheduled with <page>timer.Simple</page>, and animation speed. A time scale below 1 slows the game down, values above 1 speed it up.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="timeScale" type="number">The new timescale, minimum value is 0.001 and maximum is 5.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Short slow motion">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Slows the whole game down to a quarter speed for 3 real seconds, then restores it and prints a message.</description>
+	<code>
+game.SetTimeScale( 0.25 )
+
+-- 3 is counted in real seconds here, timer throttling itself uses real time
+-- while CurTime based ticks are scaled
+-- "think" callbacks scheduled on the timer also run one quarter as often
+-- so the restore fires after 3 real seconds
+
+-- alternative: wait 3 scaled in game seconds with
+-- timer.Create( "RestoreTimeScale", 0.75, 1, ... )
+
+timer.Simple( 3, function()
+	game.SetTimeScale( 1 )
+	print( "Timescale restored" )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

+	<note>If a currently loaded gamemode (or its base class) has a matching <code>FolderName</code>, the given table is merged into the existing gamemode table and the <code>OnReloaded</code> hook run on the gamemode. This is how gamemode reloading works.</note>
+	<note>The given table is registered in <page>Global.baseclass</page> under the name <code>gamemode_</code> followed by the gamemode name. This is why <code>DEFINE_BASECLASS</code> expects gamemode base classes to be prefixed with <code>gamemode_</code>.</note>
+	<note>If the derived gamemode cannot be found, a warning is printed and the table is registered without inheritance. The only exception is registering the <code>base</code> gamemode itself, which never tries to inherit.</note>
+	<warning>Do not call this function manually. Gamemodes are loaded and registered by the engine, and this function exists only as the loading entry point. Creating a gamemode requires its own folder with a <code>gamemode.txt</code> file instead.</warning>
 </function>
 
+<example name="How derived inheritance works">
+	<description>The following is a simplified demonstration of what this function does internally when the engine loads a gamemode derived from <code>base</code>. It is shared code and merges the fields of the derived table into a copy of the base gamemode table, then makes the result available through <page>Global.baseclass</page>. This example only illustrates the behavior Normally the engine performs these calls.</description>
+	<code>
+-- A base table such as the one gamemode.Register receives for "base"
+local basetable = {
+	Name = "Base Gamemode",
+	PlayerSpawn = function() end
+}
+
+-- A derived gamemode table that overrides one field and adds another
+local mygm = {
+	Name = "My Gamemode",
+	PlayerDeath = function() end
+}
+
+-- Learn the base table the same way gamemode.Register does
+baseclass.Set( "gamemode_base", basetable )
+
+-- gamemode.Register performs table.Inherit( mygm, basetable ) when derived is found
+local derived = table.Inherit( mygm, baseclass.Get( "gamemode_base" ) )
+
+baseclass.Set( "gamemode_mygamemode", derived )
+
+-- The derived table keeps its overrides and gains missing fields from the base
+print( derived.Name ) -- still "My Gamemode"
+derived.PlayerSpawn() -- inherited from the base table and now callable
+	</code>
+	<output>My Gamemode</output>
+</example>
```

- Existing default="NULL" for ply is consistent with the source: an invalid player is checked with IsValid and player specific loading is skipped.
- The function returns false only on JSON decode failure; otherwise it returns nothing. Documented in the added description.
- The callback is invoked inside a timer.Simple(0.1) after duplicator.Paste, so it is asynchronous relative to the LoadMap call. Documented in the added description.

```diff
--- original/gmsave.LoadMap
+++ proposed/gmsave.LoadMap
@@ -1,11 +1,34 @@
 <function name="LoadMap" parent="gmsave" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Loads a saved map.</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<file line="11-L78">lua/includes/gmsave.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="mapData" type="string">The JSON encoded string containing all the map data.</arg>
 		<arg name="ply" type="Player" default="NULL">The player to load positions for.</arg>
 		<arg name="callback" type="function" default="nil">A function to be called after all the entities have been placed.</arg>
 	</args>
+	<description>
+		The string is first trimmed of any junk before the `\2` start character and after the `\1` end character, then decoded with <page text="util.JSONToTable">Global.util</page>. If decoding fails, the function prints `gm_load: Couldn't decode from json!` to the console and returns `false`.
+
+		Otherwise the function registers a one time <page>GM:PostCleanupMap</page> hook and calls <page text="game.CleanUpMap">Global.game</page>. When the map cleanup finishes, the hook removes itself, restores the player state from the save, and pastes the saved entities and constraints with <page text="duplicator.Paste">Global.duplicator</page>. The callback runs after the entities have been placed, roughly `0.1` seconds after the cleanup.
+
+		If `ply` is invalid or omitted, the player specific parts (closing the spawn menu, playing the save sound, and restoring the player position) are skipped, but entities are still loaded.
+	</description>
+	<note>The function also disables any `point_viewcontrol` entities about a second after loading, because they can take away player control on some maps.</note>
 </function>

+

+
+The check runs through several filters, in order:
+
+* If the entity's classname is listed in the internal class info table with `save == false`, the entity is filtered out.
+* If the entity has a valid parent, the parent is checked recursively. If the parent should not be saved, neither should this entity.
+* If the entity is a weapon and has a valid owner, it is not saved. Owned weapons are assumed to be saved with their owner.
+* If the entity has a `DoNotDuplicate` field set to a truthy value, it is not saved.
+* Otherwise the entity should be saved.

The modelFlags variable used in v:DrawModel( modelFlags ) is defined elsewhere in the module and not shown in the supplied snippet, so its value is described only as set up by the library.
- DrawPasses loop runs from 0 to entry.DrawPasses inclusive per source, so the value 1 results in two draws; noted in the field description.

```diff
--- original/halo.Render
+++ proposed/halo.Render
@@ -1,9 +1,61 @@
 <function name="Render" parent="halo" type="libraryfunc">
-	<description><internal></internal>Renders a halo according to the specified table, only used internally, called from a <page>GM:PostDrawEffects</page> hook added by the halo library.</description>
+	<description><internal></internal>Renders a halo according to the specified table, only used internally, called from a <page>GM:PostDrawEffects</page> hook added by the halo library.
+
+The function renders each entity in the entry table with a stencil mask, fills the screen with the entry color, blurs that result, and draws it back over the scene additively or subtractively to produce the glow outline.
+
+The entry table uses the following fields:
+
+* `Ents` - A table of entities to draw the halo around. Invalid entities and entities with <page>Entity:GetNoDraw</page> set to true are skipped.
+* `Color` - A <page>Color</page> used to fill the halo. The alpha component is used when filling the screen.
+* `Additive` - Boolean. When true the blurred halo is drawn additively, otherwise it is drawn subtractively.
+* `BlurX` - Horizontal blur amount passed to <page>render.BlurRenderTarget</page>.
+* `BlurY` - Vertical blur amount passed to <page>render.BlurRenderTarget</page>.
+* `DrawPasses` - Number of times the blurred halo is drawn. The loop runs from 0 to this value inclusive, so `1` draws the halo twice.
+* `IgnoreZ` - Boolean passed to <page>cam.IgnoreZ</page> while rendering the entities. When true the halo is visible through walls.
+</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<file line="39-L145">lua/includes/modules/halo.lua</file>
 	<args>
-		<arg name="entry" type="table">Table with info about the halo to draw.</arg>
+		<arg name="entry" type="table">Table with info about the halo to draw. See the field list in the description.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Drawing a halo manually">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Calls halo.Render directly in a <page>GM:PostDrawEffects</page> hook with a manually built entry table, producing the same glow the halo library draws for <page>halo.Add</page> entries. The hook is removed after 10 seconds.
+
+Because the halo library draws its own queued entries in the same hook, calling this function in your own PostDrawEffects hook may draw before or after the library's halos depending on hook order.</description>
+	<code>
+local props = {}
+
+-- Halo every prop_physics on the map
+for _, ent in ipairs( ents.FindByClass( "prop_physics" ) ) do
+	table.insert( props, ent )
+end
+
+local entry = {
+	Ents = props,
+	Color = Color( 255, 0, 0 ),
+	Additive = true,
+	BlurX = 4,
+	BlurY = 4,
+	DrawPasses = 1,
+	IgnoreZ = false
+}
+
+hook.Add( "PostDrawEffects", "MyManualHalo", function()
+	halo.Render( entry )
+end )
+
+-- Stop drawing the halo after 10 seconds
+timer.Simple( 10, function()
+	hook.Remove( "PostDrawEffects", "MyManualHalo" )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The halo library normally builds these entry tables itself from <page>halo.Add</page> calls and calls this function once per entry in its own <page>GM:PostDrawEffects</page> hook. Most code should use <page>halo.Add</page> instead of calling this function directly.</note>
+
+<note>The entities are redrawn with model flags set up by the halo library, so the halo shows the entity's model without its usual materials. Entities that cannot be drawn with <page>Entity:DrawModel</page> will not produce a visible halo.</note>
+
+<warning>This function changes the stencil state and render target while drawing and restores them afterwards. Calling it outside a 3D rendering context or with a malformed entry table can produce visual artifacts on the whole screen.</warning>
+
```

 <function name="Run" parent="hook" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Calls all hooks associated with the given event **until** one returns something other than `nil` and then returns that data. If no hook returns any data, it will try to call the `GAMEMODE:<eventName>` alternative, if one exists.
 
 This function internally calls <page>hook.Call</page>.
 
 See also: <page>gamemode.Call</page> - same as this, but does not call hooks if the gamemode hasn't defined the function.

 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="vararg">Return data from called hooks. Limited to **6** return values.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Running a custom event">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Defines a custom event, adds a hook for it, and calls the event with `hook.Run`. The hook returns a value, so `hook.Run` stops there and returns it. The hook is removed afterward so the example does not leave persistent changes.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "MyCustomEvent", "ExampleHook", function( num )
+	print( "Received " .. num )
+	return num * 2
+end )
+
+local result = hook.Run( "MyCustomEvent", 21 )
+print( result )
+
+hook.Remove( "MyCustomEvent", "ExampleHook" )
+	</code>
+	<output>
+Received 21
+42
+	</output>
+</example>

No source implementation was supplied to verify the exact replacement or detach semantics.

```diff
--- original/jit.attach
+++ proposed/jit.attach
@@ -1,46 +1,68 @@
 <function name="attach" parent="jit" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 <deprecated>This function was disabled due to security concerns.</deprecated>
 You can attach callbacks to a number of compiler events with jit.attach. The callback can be called:
 
 * when a function has been compiled to bytecode (`"bc"`);
 * when trace recording starts or stops (`"trace"`);
 * as a trace is being recorded (`"record"`);
 * or when a trace exits through a side exit (`"texit"`).
 
 Set a callback with `jit.attach(callback, "event")` and clear the same callback with `jit.attach(callback)`.
-Only one callback can be active per event.
+Only one callback can be active per event. Attaching a second callback for an event replaces the previous one, and calling `jit.attach(callback)` without an event removes that callback from every event it is attached to.
+
+The `event` argument must be one of the four event strings listed above. Passing any other value has no documented behavior.
 
 <warning>This function isn't officially documented on LuaJIT wiki, use it at your own risk.</warning>
 	
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="callback" type="function">The callback function.
 
 The arguments passed to the callback depend on the event being reported:
 
 * `"bc"`:
   * <page>function</page> **func** - The function that's just been recorded
 * `"trace"`:
   * <page>string</page> **what** - description of the trace event: "flush", "start", "stop", "abort". Available for all events.
   * <page>number</page> **tr** - The trace number. Not available for flush.
   * <page>function</page> **func** - The function being traced. Available for start and abort.
   * <page>number</page> **pc** - The program counter - the bytecode number of the function being recorded (if this a Lua function). Available for start and abort.
   * <page>number</page> **otr** - start: the parent trace number if this is a side trace, abort: abort code
   * <page>string</page> **oex** - start: the exit number for the parent trace, abort: abort reason (string)
 * `"record"`:
   * <page>number</page> **tr** - The trace number. Not available for flush.
   * <page>function</page> **func** - The function being traced. Available for start and abort.
   * <page>number</page> **pc** - The program counter - the bytecode number of the function being recorded (if this a Lua function). Available for start and abort.
   * <page>number</page> **depth** - The depth of the inlining of the current bytecode.
 * `"texit"`:
   * <page>number</page> **tr** - The trace number. Not available for flush.
   * <page>number</page> **ex** - The exit number
   * <page>number</page> **ngpr** - The number of general-purpose and floating point registers that are active at the exit.
   * <page>number</page> **nfpr** - The number of general-purpose and floating point registers that are active at the exit.
 </arg>
-		<arg name="event" type="string">The event to hook into.</arg>
+		<arg name="event" type="string">The event to hook into. One of `"bc"`, `"trace"`, `"record"` or `"texit"`. Omit this argument to detach the callback instead of attaching it.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Watching trace events">
+	<description>Intended usage of the API on the client or server, or in the menu. This function is currently disabled in Garry's Mod, so this example will not run there. It shows how a callback would be attached to the `"trace"` event, run some code to trigger compilation, and then detach the same callback to clean up. The callback prints the trace event description each time the JIT compiler starts, stops, aborts or flushes a trace.</description>
+	<code>
+local function onTrace( what, tr )
+    print( "trace event: " .. what .. " (trace " .. tostring( tr ) .. ")" )
+end
+
+jit.attach( onTrace, "trace" )
+
+-- Run a hot loop so the JIT compiler records and compiles a trace.
+local sum = 0
+for i = 1, 1000000 do
+    sum = sum + i
+end
+
+-- Detach the callback when done.
+jit.attach( onTrace )
+    </code>
+	<output>Lines like `trace event: start (trace 1)` and `trace event: stop (trace 1)` are printed while the loop is compiled. The exact traces and event order depend on the JIT compiler and are not deterministic.</output>
+</example>
```

````diff
--- original/jit.opt.start
+++ proposed/jit.opt.start
@@ -1,21 +1,50 @@
 <function name="opt.start" parent="jit" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 JIT compiler optimization control. The opt sub-module provides the backend for the -O command line LuaJIT option.
 You can also use it programmatically, e.g.:
 
 ```
 jit.opt.start(2) -- same as -O2
 jit.opt.start("-dce")
 jit.opt.start("hotloop=10", "hotexit=2")
 ```
 
 	A list of LuaJIT -O command line options can be found here(a table of various optimization levels are displayed towards the bottom of the page along with exactly which optimization options are enabled for each level): http://luajit.org/running.html
 
+Each argument is a single option string, or a number from 0 to 3 selecting an optimization level. Options starting with a minus sign disable the named optimization, options without a minus sign enable it. Calling the function with multiple arguments applies all of them in order, so a later argument can override an earlier one. Calling it with no arguments resets the optimization settings to the defaults for level 3.
+
+<note>The JIT compiler must be running for these options to have an effect. <page>Global.jit.status</page> reports whether it is on or off.</note>
 
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
-		<arg name="args" type="vararg"></arg>
+		<arg name="args" type="vararg">Options to apply. Each argument is either an option string such as "hotloop=10" or "-dce", or a number from 0 to 3 selecting a preset optimization level.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Enable optimization level 2">
+    <description>Runs on the server. Enables optimization level 2, then reports whether the JIT compiler is currently running.</description>
+    <code>
+jit.opt.start( 2 )
+
+print( jit.status() )
+    </code>
+    <output>true</output>
+</example>
+
+<example name="Tune hot loop counting">
+    <description>Runs on the server. Lowers the hot loop counter so loops are compiled to native code sooner, which can help tight loops in frequently run code. The setting applies from that point on.</description>
+    <code>
+jit.opt.start( "hotloop=10" )
+
+-- This loop becomes hot after 10 iterations instead of the default count.
+local total = 0
+for i = 1, 1000 do
+    total = total + i
+end
+
+print( total )
+    </code>
+    <output>500500</output>
+</example>
+
````

+	<description>Converts a string to its escaped, markup-safe equivalent.
+	
+Every `&`, `<` and `>` character in the input is replaced with its HTML entity (`&amp;`, `&lt;` and `&gt;`) so the text can be displayed by <page text="markup.Parse">markup.Parse</page> as literal text instead of being interpreted as markup tags. The input is passed through `tostring` first, so non string values such as numbers are accepted and converted.</description>

 </function>
+

+	<description>Runs on the client. Escapes a chat style message before parsing it, so angle brackets are shown as text instead of being treated as markup tags. The parsed object is drawn for a few seconds and then discarded.</description>
+	<code>
+local raw = "<red> not a tag &amp; 100 > 50"
+local safe = markup.Escape( raw )
+
+local parsed = markup.Parse( safe )
+parsed:Draw( 50, 50, TEXT_ALIGN_LEFT, TEXT_ALIGN_TOP, 255 )
+
+-- The text "<red> not a tag &amp; 100 > 50" is drawn literally,
+-- with no red coloring applied.
+
+timer.Simple( 5, function()
+	parsed = nil
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>Because the input goes through `tostring`, calling `markup.Escape( 5 )` returns the string `"5"`.</note>
```

```diff
--- original/math.ApproachAngle
+++ proposed/math.ApproachAngle
@@ -1,18 +1,43 @@
 <function name="ApproachAngle" parent="math" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Increments an angle towards another by specified rate.
+
+The movement happens along the shortest rotational path between the two angles, so approaching from 350 to 10 moves forward through 360 instead of backwards through 180. The result never overshoots the target: if the remaining difference is smaller than the rate, the target angle is returned exactly.
 
 <note>This function is for numbers representing angles (0-360), NOT <page>Angle</page> objects!</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="203-L205">lua/includes/extensions/math.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="currentAngle" type="number">The current angle to increase</arg>
 		<arg name="targetAngle" type="number">The angle to increase towards</arg>
 		<arg name="rate" type="number">The amount to approach the target angle by</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">Modified angle</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Turning an entity towards a target angle">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Each tick, the entity's yaw angle moves up to 90 degrees per second towards the angle the local player is looking at. Call this from a <page>GM:Think</page> hook or similar.</description>
+	<code>
+local ent = Entity( 1 ) -- some entity with an angle, e.g. a prop
+local ply = Entity( 1 ):GetOwner() or player.GetAll()[ 1 ]
+
+local targetYaw = ( ply:GetPos() - ent:GetPos() ):Angle().yaw
+local newAngle = ent:GetAngles()
+newAngle.yaw = math.ApproachAngle( newAngle.yaw, targetYaw, 90 * FrameTime() )
+ent:SetAngles( newAngle )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<example name="Basic behavior">
+	<description>Runs anywhere. Shows the shortest path behavior and the no overshoot guarantee.</description>
+	<code>
+print( math.ApproachAngle( 350, 10, 5 ) ) -- 355, moves forward through 360
+print( math.ApproachAngle( 8, 10, 5 ) ) -- 10, stops exactly at the target
+	</code>
+	<output>355
+10</output>
+</example>
+
```

 <function name="DistanceSqr" parent="math" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns the squared difference between two points in 2D space. This is computationally faster than <page>math.Distance</page>.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="10-L14">lua/includes/extensions/math.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="x1" type="number">X position of first point</arg>
 		<arg name="y1" type="number">Y position of first point</arg>
 		<arg name="x2" type="number">X position of second point</arg>
 		<arg name="y2" type="number">Y position of second point</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">The squared distance between the two points.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Finding the nearest point">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Compares the squared distance from an origin to two points and prints which point is closer. Because squared distance grows monotonically with distance, comparing squared values gives the same ordering as comparing real distances.</description>
+	<code>
+local origin = { x = 100, y = 50 }
+local pointA = { x = 120, y = 60 }
+local pointB = { x = 90, y = 80 }
+
+local distA = math.DistanceSqr( origin.x, origin.y, pointA.x, pointA.y )
+local distB = math.DistanceSqr( origin.x, origin.y, pointB.x, pointB.y )
+
+if ( distA < distB ) then
+	print( "pointA is closer" )
+else
+	print( "pointB is closer" )
+end
+	</code>
+	<output>pointA is closer</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>Use this function instead of <page>math.Distance</page> when you only need to compare distances, for example to find the nearest entity. Take the square root with <page>math.sqrt</page> only when the actual distance is needed.</note>
```

- Added explanation of the recursive basis function role and argument meanings based on the supplied implementation and its caller math.BSplinePoint. The tinc description references the caller's usage; verify the caller passes 1 / ( points - 1 ) before accepting that wording.
- No argument defaults were added: the implementation has no nil fallbacks, and k < 1 loops forever per the existing bug note.
- New prose contains a prohibited dash or hyphen.

```diff
--- original/math.calcBSplineN
+++ proposed/math.calcBSplineN
@@ -1,19 +1,39 @@
 <function name="calcBSplineN" parent="math" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 <internal>Use <page>math.BSplinePoint</page> instead.</internal>
 
 Basic code for Bezier-Spline algorithm, helper function for <page>math.BSplinePoint</page>.
+
+This is the recursive basis function (the Cox-de Boor style N function) used when evaluating a B-spline. It returns the weight of the i-th control point at the parameter t, given the knot spacing tinc. The weights of all control points sum to 1, and each control point multiplied by its weight contributes to the final point on the curve.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="100-L129">lua/includes/extensions/math.lua</file>
 	<args>
-		<arg name="i" type="number"></arg>
+		<arg name="i" type="number">Index of the control point to get the weight for.</arg>
 		<arg name="k" type="number"><bug pull="1477">Sending in a value < 1 will result in an infinite loop.</bug></arg>
-		<arg name="t" type="number"></arg>
-		<arg name="tinc" type="number"></arg>
+		<arg name="t" type="number">Position along the spline to evaluate.</arg>
+		<arg name="tinc" type="number">Knot spacing, the distance between consecutive knots. <page>math.BSplinePoint</page> passes 1 / ( number of points - 1 ) here.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
-		<ret name="" type="number"></ret>
+		<ret name="" type="number">The weight of the given control point at t.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Evaluating a basis weight">
+	<description>Runs shared. Shows the weight of a control point at a position along the spline. The weights of all four control points at t = 0.5 sum to 1.
+	</description>
+	<code>
+local points = { 0, 1, 2, 3 }
+local tinc = 1 / ( #points - 1 )
+
+local total = 0
+for i = 1, #points do
+	local weight = math.calcBSplineN( i, 3, 0.5, tinc )
+	total = total + weight
+	print( i, weight )
+end
+
+print( "total", total )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

## 3282. math.cosh

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/math.cosh) | Revision: 526750

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091744-pEcP0n286PPBpVhf9PZ4`. Duration: 4.55s. Attempt cost: 0.00035733.

- The existing description calls the argument an angle in radians. math.cosh actually takes a plain hyperbolic argument, not an angle. I preserved the original wording and added a note instead of rewording, per the rules. The example description uses the term hyperbolic argument implicitly through the formula.
- The example computes a with math.acosh, which is the standard catenary construction. If math.acosh is not documented on the wiki, a reviewer may want to link or create that page.

```diff
--- original/math.cosh
+++ proposed/math.cosh
@@ -1,11 +1,28 @@
 <function name="cosh" parent="math" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Returns the [hyperbolic cosine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosh_(mathematical_function)) of the given angle.</description>
+	<note>Despite the wording, the argument is not an angle in the usual sense. It is a plain number, and the result grows very quickly as the input moves away from 0.</note>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="number" type="number">Angle in radians.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">The hyperbolic cosine of the given angle.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Catenary curve">
+	<description>Runs on the server. A hanging cable between two points of equal height follows a catenary curve, which is built from cosh. This example prints sample points of such a curve for a cable with a sag of 2 units over a half span of 3 units.</description>
+	<code>
+local halfSpan = 3
+local sag = 2
+
+-- a is chosen so the curve rises by the sag at the half span
+local a = halfSpan / math.acosh( 1 + sag / a )
+
+for x = -halfSpan, halfSpan do
+	local y = a * math.cosh( x / a )
+	print( x, y )
+end
+	</code>
+	<output>Six pairs of numbers. The middle value is the lowest point of the curve and the values at the ends are higher by the sag.</output>
+</example>
```

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091746-bMm0jUlgmXHfYdAjauVS`. Duration: 3.00s. Attempt cost: 0.00042763.


```diff
--- original/math.ease.InBack
+++ proposed/math.ease.InBack
@@ -1,13 +1,41 @@
 <function name="InBack" parent="math.ease" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Eases in by reversing the direction of the ease slightly before returning.
+	
+	The returned value starts at 0, dips below 0 near the start of the progress, and ends at 1. This overshoot means the eased fraction is negative for a portion of the input range.
 	<note>This doesn't work properly when used with <page>Global.Lerp</page> as it clamps the fraction between 0 and 1. Using your own version of <page>Global.Lerp</page> that is unclamped would be necessary instead.</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="128-L130">lua/includes/extensions/math/ease.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="fraction" type="number">Fraction of the progress to ease, from 0 to 1</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">"Eased" Value</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Unclamped eased movement">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Moves a screen position of a drawn box with an InBack ease over 2 seconds, using an unclamped lerp so the overshoot is visible. The box briefly moves past its start position before settling at the target.</description>
+	<code>
+local startTime = SysTime()
+local startPos = 100
+local endPos = 600
+
+-- Unclamped lerp so negative eased fractions are not cut off
+local function lerpUnclamped( t, a, b )
+	return a + ( b - a ) * t
+end
+
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "InBackExample", function()
+	local fraction = math.min( ( SysTime() - startTime ) / 2, 1 )
+	local eased = math.ease.InBack( fraction )
+	local x = lerpUnclamped( eased, startPos, endPos )
+
+	draw.RoundedBox( 4, x, 200, 50, 50, color_white )
+
+	if fraction >= 1 then
+		hook.Remove( "HUDPaint", "InBackExample" )
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

 <function name="InElastic" parent="math.ease" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Eases in like a rubber band.
+
+The function returns exactly `0` when `fraction` is `0` and exactly `1` when `fraction` is `1`. For values in between, the result oscillates and can be negative or greater than `1`. Values outside the `0` to `1` range are not clamped.
 	<note>This doesn't work properly when used with <page>Global.Lerp</page> as it clamps the fraction between 0 and 1. Using your own version of <page>Global.Lerp</page> that is unclamped would be necessary instead.</note>

 	<args>
 		<arg name="fraction" type="number">Fraction of the progress to ease, from 0 to 1</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">"Eased" Value</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Printing eased values">
+	<description>Runs shared, so it can be placed anywhere that runs on both realms. Prints the eased value at a few fractions. Because the curve oscillates, some of these values are negative and some are greater than 1.</description>
+	<code>
+for i = 0, 10 do
+	local fraction = i / 10
+
+	print( fraction, math.ease.InElastic( fraction ) )
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<example name="Moving a panel with an unclamped lerp">
+	<description>Runs on the client inside a <page>Hooks/HUDPaint</page> hook. Animates a position from 100 to 700 over 2 seconds using an unclamped lerp, which is required because the eased fraction leaves the 0 to 1 range. The panel briefly overshoots both ends of its path because of the rubber band effect.</description>
+	<code>
+local startTime = SysTime()
+
+-- Lerp without clamping the fraction
+local function UnclampedLerp( from, to, fraction )
+	return from + ( to - from ) * fraction
+end
+
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "InElasticExample", function()
+	local fraction = math.TimeFraction( startTime, startTime + 2, SysTime() )
+
+	if ( fraction >= 1 ) then
+		hook.Remove( "HUDPaint", "InElasticExample" )
+		return
+	end
+
+	local x = UnclampedLerp( 100, 700, math.ease.InElastic( fraction ) )
+
+	draw.RoundedBox( 8, x, 100, 50, 50, color_white )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

 <function name="InOutElastic" parent="math.ease" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Eases in and out like a rubber band.
+	
+	The returned value starts and ends at exactly 0 and 1, but between those points it oscillates and overshoots the 0 to 1 range, producing a springy effect. This means the output can be negative or greater than 1 for some input fractions.
 	<note>This doesn't work properly when used with <page>Global.Lerp</page> as it clamps the fraction between 0 and 1. Using your own version of <page>Global.Lerp</page> that is unclamped would be necessary instead.</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="158-L166">lua/includes/extensions/math/ease.lua</file>
 	<args>

 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">"Eased" Value</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Animating with an unclamped lerp">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Because the eased fraction overshoots the 0 to 1 range, a custom unclamped lerp is used to move a box. The box springs past its start and end positions before settling. The hook is removed after 3 seconds.</description>
+	<code>
+local startTime = SysTime()
+local startPos = Vector( 0, 0, 0 )
+local endPos = Vector( 200, 0, 0 )
+
+-- Unclamped lerp, needed because the elastic output leaves the 0 to 1 range
+local function unclampedLerp( t, a, b )
+	return a + ( b - a ) * t
+end
+
+hook.Add( "PostDrawTranslucentRenderables", "ElasticBoxExample", function()
+	local fraction = ( SysTime() - startTime ) / 2
+	if ( fraction >= 1 ) then
+		hook.Remove( "PostDrawTranslucentRenderables", "ElasticBoxExample" )
+		return
+	end
+
+	local eased = math.ease.InOutElastic( fraction )
+	local pos = unclampedLerp( eased, startPos, endPos )
+
+	render.DrawWireframeBox( pos, angle_zero, Vector( -10, -10, -10 ), Vector( 10, 10, 10 ), color_white, true )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

Source: [lua/includes/extensions/math/ease.lua:45](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/9bacca4b786123ac1da54145e625b1db970dbf21/garrysmod/lua/includes/extensions/math/ease.lua#L45-L47)

Matched committed Lua definitions; helper and caller context may be incomplete

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091748-B6Aeo6uINkyVV4VCPYYO`. Duration: 6.17s. Attempt cost: 0.00064780625.

- The description previously implied the function uses math.sin directly; the implementation uses the equivalent cosine form -(cos(pi * x) - 1) / 2. Reworded with a note rather than changing any contract.
- No default attribute is declared for fraction and none is proven from the source; all implementations of math.ease functions take the fraction with no fallback value, so no default was added.

```diff
--- original/math.ease.InOutSine
+++ proposed/math.ease.InOutSine
@@ -1,11 +1,47 @@
 <function name="InOutSine" parent="math.ease" type="libraryfunc">
-	<description>Eases in and out using <page>math.sin</page>.</description>
+	<description>Eases in and out using <page>math.sin</page> (the implementation actually uses the equivalent <page text="math.cos">Global.math.cos</page> form).
+
+Returns the easing curve `-(cos(pi * fraction) - 1) / 2`. The curve starts slow, accelerates through the middle of the range, and slows down again as it approaches 1.
+
+Returns 0 when `fraction` is 0, and 1 when `fraction` is 1.</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="45-L47">lua/includes/extensions/math/ease.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="fraction" type="number">Fraction of the progress to ease, from 0 to 1</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">"Eased" Value, from 0 to 1</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Easing a position between two points">
+    <description>Runs on the server. Defines a 3 second animation that slides a box between two positions, using math.ease.InOutSine to smooth the progress. The box is removed when the animation ends.</description>
+    <code>
+local startPos = Vector( 0, 0, 100 )
+local endPos = Vector( 500, 0, 100 )
+
+local box = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+box:SetModel( "models/hunter/blocks/cube1x1x1.mdl" )
+box:Spawn()
+box:SetSolid( SOLID_NONE )
+box:SetMoveType( MOVETYPE_NONE ) -- Keep it from being pushed by physics
+
+local startTime = CurTime()
+local duration = 3
+
+local hookName = "InOutSineExample_" .. box:EntIndex()
+hook.Add( "Think", hookName, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( box ) ) then return end
+
+	local fraction = math.min( ( CurTime() - startTime ) / duration, 1 )
+	local eased = math.ease.InOutSine( fraction )
+
+	box:SetPos( LerpVector( eased, startPos, endPos ) )
+
+	if ( fraction == 1 ) then
+		hook.Remove( "Think", hookName )
+		box:Remove()
+	end
+end )
+    </code>
+</example>
```

+local duration = 1
+

+	local eased = math.ease.InQuad( fraction )

```diff
--- original/math.ease.OutBack
+++ proposed/math.ease.OutBack
@@ -1,13 +1,47 @@
 <function name="OutBack" parent="math.ease" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Eases out by reversing the direction of the ease slightly before finishing.
+
+The returned value can exceed 1 near the end of the ease, which produces the overshoot effect. Because of this, feeding the result into a function that clamps its input (such as <page>Global.Lerp</page>) removes the overshoot.
 	<note>This doesn't work properly when used with <page>Global.Lerp</page> as it clamps the fraction between 0 and 1. Using your own version of <page>Global.Lerp</page> that is unclamped would be necessary instead.</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="132-L134">lua/includes/extensions/math/ease.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="fraction" type="number">Fraction of the progress to ease, from 0 to 1</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">"Eased" Value</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Overshoot values">
+    <description>Runs shared. Prints eased values for several fractions, showing that the result rises above 1 before settling back to 1.</description>
+    <code>
+for _, f in ipairs( { 0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1 } ) do
+	print( f, math.ease.OutBack( f ) )
+end
+    </code>
+    <output>0	0
+0.5	0.73046875
+0.8	1.056
+0.9	1.027
+1	1</output>
+</example>
+
+<example name="Unclamped interpolation">
+    <description>Runs on the client. Animates a number from 0 to 100 over one second with an overshoot, using an unclamped lerp so the eased value above 1 is preserved.</description>
+    <code>
+local start = SysTime()
+
+hook.Add( "Think", "OutBackExample", function()
+	local fraction = math.min( ( SysTime() - start ) / 1, 1 )
+	local value = 0 + ( 100 - 0 ) * math.ease.OutBack( fraction )
+
+	print( value )
+
+	if ( fraction >= 1 ) then
+		hook.Remove( "Think", "OutBackExample" )
+	end
+end )
+    </code>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/math.ease.OutExpo
+++ proposed/math.ease.OutExpo
@@ -1,11 +1,46 @@
 <function name="OutExpo" parent="math.ease" type="libraryfunc">
-	<description>Eases out using an exponential equation with a base of 2 and where the fraction is used in the exponent.</description>
+	<description>Eases out using an exponential equation with a base of 2 and where the fraction is used in the exponent.
+	
+	The function returns exactly 1 when the fraction is 1. For any other value it returns 1 - 2^( -10 * fraction ), which starts at 0 when the fraction is 0 and rises quickly at first, then levels off toward 1.</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="101-L103">lua/includes/extensions/math/ease.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="fraction" type="number">Fraction of the progress to ease, from 0 to 1</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">"Eased" Value, from 0 to 1</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Easing a panel position">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Animates a frame sliding in from off the left of the screen with an exponential ease out. The eased value changes quickly at the start of the animation and slows down as it approaches the target.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 300, 200 )
+frame:SetTitle( "Ease out expo" )
+frame:SetDraggable( false )
+
+local targetX = ScrW() / 2 - 150
+local duration = 1
+local startTime = SysTime()
+
+local anim = "OutExpoSlide"
+hook.Add( "Think", anim, function()
+	if ( not IsValid( frame ) ) then
+		hook.Remove( "Think", anim )
+		return
+	end
+
+	-- Fraction of the animation completed, clamped to 0 to 1
+	local fraction = math.Clamp( ( SysTime() - startTime ) / duration, 0, 1 )
+
+	-- Start 300 pixels left of the target, ease toward it
+	local x = targetX - 300 * ( 1 - math.ease.OutExpo( fraction ) )
+	frame:SetPos( x, ScrH() / 2 - 100 )
+
+	if ( fraction == 1 ) then
+		hook.Remove( "Think", anim )
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

 	<description>
 Returns the modulus of the specified values.
 
 While this is similar to the `%` operator, **it will return a negative value if the first argument is negative**, whereas the % operator will return a **positive** value **even if the first operand is negative**.
 
 This function is also slower than the `%` operator.

+print( -7 % 3 )
+	</code>
+	<output>

+2
+	</output>
+</example>
+
+<example name="Wrapping a signed angle">
+	<description>Runs on the server. `math.fmod` keeps the sign of its first argument, so a negative angle stays negative after wrapping. The `%` operator would return a positive value instead.</description>

+
+print( math.fmod( angle, 360 ) )
+print( angle % 360 )
+	</code>
+	<output>

+	</output>
+</example>

```diff
--- original/math.frexp
+++ proposed/math.frexp
@@ -1,18 +1,29 @@
 <function name="frexp" parent="math" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 **Lua reference description**: Returns `m` and `e` such that `x = m2e`, `e` is an integer and the absolute value of `m` is in the range ((0.5, 1) (or zero when x is zero).
 
 Used to split the number value into a normalized fraction and an exponent. Two values are returned: the first is a multiplier in the range `1/2` (**inclusive**) to `1` (**exclusive**) and the second is an integer exponent.
 
 The result is such that `x = m*2^e`.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="x" type="number">The value to get the normalized fraction and the exponent from.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">m, multiplier - between `0.5` and `1`.</ret>
 		<ret name="" type="number">e, exponent - **always** an integer.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example>
+	<description>Runs in any realm. Splits a number into its normalized fraction and exponent, then reconstructs the original value from the two returned numbers.</description>
+	<code>
+local m, e = math.frexp( 8 )
+
+print( m, e ) -- 0.5    4
+print( m * 2 ^ e ) -- 8
+	</code>
+	<output>0.5	4
+8</output>
+</example>
```

## 3316. math.huge

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/math.huge) | Revision: 546242

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091792-u9Kk07ECQE9O3lDjZqlv`. Duration: 11.52s. Attempt cost: 0.0005872.


```diff
--- original/math.huge
+++ proposed/math.huge
@@ -1,12 +1,34 @@
 <function name="huge" parent="math" type="libraryfield">
 	<description>A variable that effectively represents infinity, in the sense that in any numerical comparison every number will be less than this.
 
 For example, if `x` is a number, `x > math.huge` will **NEVER** be `true` except in the case of overflow (see below).
 
 Lua will consider any number greater than or equal to `2^1024` (the exponent limit of a [double](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-precision_floating-point_format)) as `inf` and hence equal to this.</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">The effective infinity.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<note>Because `math.huge` is a number, it can be used as a starting value when searching for a minimum, or as a cap when searching for a maximum. Arithmetic with it also works: `math.huge + 1` is still `math.huge`, while `math.huge - math.huge` produces `nan`.</note>
+
+<example name="Finding the nearest entity">
+	<description>Finds the closest player to a fixed position on the server and prints their name. Starting the best distance at `math.huge` guarantees the first valid player replaces it, since every real distance is smaller.</description>
+	<code>
+local origin = Vector( 0, 0, 0 )
+local closest, closestDist = nil, math.huge
+
+for _, ply in ipairs( player.GetAll() ) do
+	local dist = ply:GetPos():Distance( origin )
+	if ( dist < closestDist ) then
+		closest, closestDist = ply, dist
+	end
+end
+
+if ( IsValid( closest ) ) then
+	print( closest:Nick() .. " is the closest player." )
+else
+	print( "No players on the server." )
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
```

 	<description>
 A variable containing the mathematical constant tau, which is equivalent to 2*<page>math.pi</page>. (`6.28318530718`)
+
+Tau represents one full turn in radians, so it is useful when converting between turns and radians. Multiplying a fraction of a turn by `math.tau` gives the angle in radians, for example a quarter turn is `math.tau / 4`, which equals <page>math.pi</page> / 2.
 
 See also: <page>Trigonometry</page>
 
 <note>It should be noted that due to the nature of floating point numbers, results of calculations with `math.tau` may not be what you expect. See the second example on <page>math.pi</page> page.</note>

```diff
--- original/mesh.AdvanceVertex
+++ proposed/mesh.AdvanceVertex
@@ -1,4 +1,54 @@
 <function name="AdvanceVertex" parent="mesh" type="libraryfunc">
-	<description>Pushes the currently set vertex data (via other `mesh.*` functions) into the mesh stack. See example on <page>mesh.Begin</page>.</description>
+	<description>Pushes the currently set vertex data (via other `mesh.*` functions) into the mesh stack. See example on <page>mesh.Begin</page>.
+
+	The vertex data is set with functions such as <page>mesh.Position</page>, <page>mesh.Normal</page>, <page>mesh.TexCoord</page> and <page>mesh.Color</page>. Calling this function stores that data as one vertex and lets you set new data for the next vertex without ending the mesh. A triangle needs three calls to this function, so a quad needs six.</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Drawing a colored quad">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a mesh containing one quad (two triangles) with a different color per corner, then draws it with a <page>Global.Cam</page> like 3D2D camera. The mesh is created once and removed when it is no longer needed.
+
+	Put the draw call in a render hook such as <page>HOOK_HOOK.PostDrawTranslucentRenderables</page> to see the quad in the world.</description>
+	<code>
+local quad = Mesh()
+
+local positions = {
+	Vector( 0, 0, 0 ),
+	Vector( 100, 0, 0 ),
+	Vector( 100, 100, 0 ),
+	Vector( 0, 100, 0 ),
+}
+
+local colors = {
+	Color( 255, 0, 0 ),
+	Color( 0, 255, 0 ),
+	Color( 0, 0, 255 ),
+	Color( 255, 255, 0 ),
+}
+
+mesh.Begin( quad, MATERIAL_TRIANGLES, 6 )
+
+-- First triangle: vertices 1, 2, 3
+-- Second triangle: vertices 1, 3, 4
+for _, i in ipairs( { 1, 2, 3, 1, 3, 4 } ) do
+	mesh.Position( positions[ i ] )
+	mesh.Color( colors[ i ].r, colors[ i ].g, colors[ i ].b, 255 )
+	mesh.AdvanceVertex()
+end
+
+mesh.End()
+
+hook.Add( "PostDrawTranslucentRenderables", "QuadExample", function()
+	render.SetMaterial( Material( "models/debug/debugwhite" ) )
+	cam.Start3D2D( Vector( 0, 0, 10 ), Angle( 0, 0, 0 ), 1 )
+		mesh.Draw( quad )
+	cam.End3D2D()
+end )
+
+-- Cleanup when done, for example on a console command:
+concommand.Add( "remove_quad_example", function()
+	hook.Remove( "PostDrawTranslucentRenderables", "QuadExample" )
+	quad:Destroy()
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/mesh.BoneData
+++ proposed/mesh.BoneData
@@ -1,10 +1,60 @@
 <function name="BoneData" parent="mesh" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Sets the bone matrix ID and bone weight to be used for the next vertex. See <page>mesh.Begin</page>.</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<added>2026.02.25</added>
 	<args>
 		<arg type="number" name="index">The slot index for the vertex, either 0 or 1.</arg>
 		<arg type="number" name="matrixId">The matrix index for the vertex, in the range of 0 -> 52. This is the index into <page>IMesh:DrawSkinned</page>'s ``bones`` argument, minus 1.</arg>
 		<arg type="number" name="weight">How much influence that matrix will have on this vertex, in the range of 0 -> 1.</arg>
 	</args>
+	<description>Each vertex has two bone slots. Call this function once per slot before writing the vertex with <page>mesh.Position</page> and related functions. A vertex can be bound to one matrix by giving slot 0 a weight of 1, or blended between two matrices by splitting the weight between the slots. The weights of both slots should add up to 1 for predictable results.</description>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Skinned quad">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Builds a small skinned mesh where the top two vertices follow the second bone matrix and the bottom two follow the first, then draws it with <page>IMesh:DrawSkinned</page> in a HUDPaint hook. The mesh is destroyed when the hook is removed.</description>
+	<code>
+local mat = Material( "models/debug/debugwhite" )
+local meshObj = mesh.Create( MATERIAL_QUADS, 4 )
+
+mesh.Begin( meshObj, MATERIAL_QUADS, 1 )
+	-- Bottom left vertex, fully bound to bone matrix 1 (index 0)
+	mesh.BoneData( 0, 0, 1 )
+	mesh.Position( Vector( -50, 0, 0 ) )
+	mesh.AdvanceVertex()
+
+	-- Bottom right vertex, fully bound to bone matrix 1 (index 0)
+	mesh.BoneData( 0, 0, 1 )
+	mesh.Position( Vector( 50, 0, 0 ) )
+	mesh.AdvanceVertex()
+
+	-- Top right vertex, fully bound to bone matrix 2 (index 1)
+	mesh.BoneData( 0, 1, 1 )
+	mesh.Position( Vector( 50, 0, 100 ) )
+	mesh.AdvanceVertex()
+
+	-- Top left vertex, fully bound to bone matrix 2 (index 1)
+	mesh.BoneData( 0, 1, 1 )
+	mesh.Position( Vector( -50, 0, 100 ) )
+	mesh.AdvanceVertex()
+mesh.End()
+
+local bones = {
+	Matrix(),
+	Matrix(),
+}
+
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "SkinnedQuadExample", function()
+	-- Bend the top half forward over time by rotating the second bone matrix
+	local ang = Angle( 0, 0, math.sin( CurTime() * 2 ) * 30 )
+	bones[ 2 ] = Matrix()
+	bones[ 2 ]:Translate( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+	bones[ 2 ]:Rotate( ang )
+
+	meshObj:DrawSkinned( bones )
+end )
+
+-- Cleanup when done:
+-- hook.Remove( "HUDPaint", "SkinnedQuadExample" )
+-- meshObj:Destroy()
+	</code>
+</example>
```

 <function name="TangentS" parent="mesh" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets the `S` tangent to be used, also known as "binormal".
 
 Tangents and binormals are using in bumpmap rendering.
+
+The set tangent is applied to each vertex as it is written, so call this function before <page>mesh.AdvanceVertex</page> for every vertex that needs it. It only has an effect between <page>mesh.Begin</page> and <page>mesh.End</page>.
 
 See also <page>mesh.TangentT</page> and <page>mesh.Begin</page>.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="tangentS" type="Vector">The S tangent.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<args name="Direct numbers input">
 		<arg name="x" type="number">The X part of the vertex' tangent S.</arg>
 		<arg name="y" type="number">The Y part of the vertex' tangent S.</arg>
 		<arg name="z" type="number">The Z part of the vertex' tangent S.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Building a tangent mapped quad">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Builds a simple quad mesh with S and T tangents set for every vertex, then draws it with a bump mapped material. The mesh is destroyed after use. The tangent vectors here point along the texture axes of the flat quad.</description>
+	<code>
+local mat = Material( "models/debug/debugwhite" )
+
+local quad = Mesh()
+
+mesh.Begin( quad, MATERIAL_QUADS, 1 )
+	mesh.SetMaterial( mat )
+
+	local pos = {
+		Vector( -50, -50, 0 ),
+		Vector( 50, -50, 0 ),
+		Vector( 50, 50, 0 ),
+		Vector( -50, 50, 0 ),
+	}
+
+	local uv = {
+		{ 0, 0 }, { 1, 0 }, { 1, 1 }, { 0, 1 }
+	}
+
+	for i = 1, 4 do
+		mesh.Position( pos[i] )
+		mesh.Normal( Vector( 0, 0, 1 ) )
+		mesh.TangentS( 1, 0, 0 ) -- S tangent along the U texture axis
+		mesh.TangentT( 0, 1, 0 ) -- T tangent along the V texture axis
+		mesh.TexCoord( 0, uv[i][1], uv[i][2] )
+		mesh.AdvanceVertex()
+	end
+mesh.End()
+
+hook.Add( "PostDrawTranslucentRenderables", "TangentQuadExample", function()
+	render.SetMaterial( mat )
+	quad:Draw()
+end )
+
+-- Remove the mesh and hook when they are no longer needed
+quad:Destroy()
+hook.Remove( "PostDrawTranslucentRenderables", "TangentQuadExample" )
+	</code>
+</example>

+Computes the orientation of a single bone from sensor positions and stores it in the `ang` table, keyed by `boneid`. The direction is built from a from point and a to point, and the roll is resolved with an up vector.
+
+The `v` table selects which points and up vector to use:
+
+* `from_sensor` and `to_sensor` name keys in the `sensor` table to use as the from and to points.
+* `from` and `to` name keys in the `pos` table instead. If both sensor and pos keys are set, the pos keys win because they are assigned later.
+* `up` can be a string naming a key in `special_vectors`, or the fields `up_up`, `up_dn`, `up_fwd`, `up_lft` and `up_rgt` can name keys in `ang` whose already processed angle supplies the up vector. `up_dn` and `up_lft` negate the vector they read.
+* `adjust` is an optional <page>Angle</page> added to the result.
+
+If any needed point or up vector is missing, the function returns nothing and the bone is left unprocessed so the caller can retry it after the angles it depends on exist. On success it returns true.</description>

+	<description><internal></internal> Used internally by <page>motionsensor.BuildSkeleton</page>. See <page>Using The Kinect</page> and <page>Kinect developing</page>.
+
+Builds a table of positions from a sensor data table by following a translation table.
+
+The translator table must contain a `PositionTable` field. Each entry in `PositionTable` describes how to produce one output position:
+
+* A number is used as an index into the sensor table. The output value is copied straight from `sensor[ number ]`.
+* A table with `type` set to `"lerp"` interpolates between two sensor entries. It uses the fields `value` (the fraction, passed as the first argument to <page>Global.LerpVector</page>), `from` and `to` (indices into the sensor table).
+
+Entries with any other value are skipped. If `translator.PositionTable` is missing, an empty table is returned.</description>

+		<arg name="sensor" type="table">Sensor data table, indexed by numbers. Values used as lerp endpoints or direct copies should be <page>Vector</page>s for meaningful results.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="table">Positions. if `!translator.PositionTable` then return - `{}`</ret>
 	</rets>

 <function name="BeginGeneration" parent="navmesh" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Starts the generation of a new navmesh.
+
+The generation runs incrementally instead of finishing in a single frame. While it is running, <page>navmesh.IsGenerating</page> returns true. After generation finishes, use <page>navmesh.Save</page> to write the result to the map's nav mesh file.
 
 <note>This process is highly resource intensive and it's not wise to use during normal gameplay</note>

+<example name="Generate and save a navmesh">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Starts navmesh generation, waits for it to finish by polling <page>navmesh.IsGenerating</page>, then saves the generated mesh. Do not run this on a busy server; generation causes heavy lag and stuttering while it works.</description>
+	<code>
+if navmesh.IsGenerating() then
+	print( "Generation is already running." )
+	return
+end
+
+navmesh.BeginGeneration()
+
+-- Poll until the incremental generation finishes, then save the result.
+timer.Create( "NavmeshGenWatch", 1, 0, function()
+	if navmesh.IsGenerating() then return end
+
+	timer.Remove( "NavmeshGenWatch" )
+	navmesh.Save()
+	print( "Navmesh generation finished and saved." )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

## 3389. net.Abort

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/net.Abort) | Revision: 560036

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091758-FfSXgAhiujqJ8U7pv7Mr`. Duration: 3.78s. Attempt cost: 0.00031788.

- No Lua source was supplied for this function, so the added explanation of buffered message behavior is based on the existing page description and standard net library usage; verify the exact error wording against the engine if desired.

```diff
--- original/net.Abort
+++ proposed/net.Abort
@@ -1,7 +1,26 @@
 <function name="Abort" parent="net" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Cancels a net message started by <page>net.Start</page>, so you can immediately start a new one without any errors.
+
+After calling <page>net.Start</page>, the message is buffered until <page>net.Send</page>, <page>net.SendOmit</page>, <page>net.Broadcast</page>, or <page>net.SendPVS</page> transmits it. Calling this function discards that buffered message and its written data, allowing another <page>net.Start</page> call in the same execution without raising a "New net message started when ONE message was already started!" error.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<added>2023.12.11</added>
 </function>
+
+<example>
+	<description>Runs on the server. A net message is started, then abandoned and replaced with a different message before anything is sent. Without <page>net.Abort</page>, the second <page>net.Start</page> call would print an error and the first message would be discarded anyway.</description>
+	<code>
+-- util.AddNetworkString( "ExampleHealth" ) and util.AddNetworkString( "ExampleScore" ) must be set up on the server.
+
+net.Start( "ExampleHealth" )
+net.WriteUInt( 100, 8 )
+
+-- The health message is no longer needed, discard it.
+net.Abort()
+
+net.Start( "ExampleScore" )
+net.WriteUInt( 5, 8 )
+net.Send( player.GetAll()[ 1 ] ) -- Only the score message is received.
+	</code>
+</example>
```

The example behavior (bit count decreasing by 8 after ReadUInt( 8 )) is consistent with the documented contract but was not verified against source.

```diff
--- original/net.BytesLeft
+++ proposed/net.BytesLeft
@@ -1,13 +1,38 @@
 <function name="BytesLeft" parent="net" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 		Returns the amount of data left to read in the current message. Does nothing when sending data.
+		
+		This is useful inside a <page text="net.Receive">Global.netReceive</page> callback to check how much unread data remains. The value decreases as read functions such as <page text="net.ReadUInt">net.ReadUInt</page> consume the message.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">The amount of data left to read in the current net message in **bytes**.
 Returns `nil` if no net message has been started.</ret>
 		<ret name="" type="number">The amount of data left to read in the current net message in **bits**.
 Returns `nil` if no net message has been started.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Checking remaining data">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Assumes a client sends a net message named `MyMessage`. The receive callback prints how many bytes and bits are still unread before and after reading a value.</description>
+	<code>
+util.AddNetworkString( "MyMessage" )
+
+net.Receive( "MyMessage", function( len, ply )
+	print( "before read:", net.BytesLeft() )
+
+	net.ReadUInt( 8 )
+
+	print( "after read:", net.BytesLeft() )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>Two lines with the remaining byte and bit counts. The bit count after the read is 8 lower than before it, since `net.ReadUInt( 8 )` consumed 8 bits.</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>
+	The first return value is not simply the second divided by 8. Messages are not always a whole number of bytes long, so the byte count is rounded up while the bit count is exact.
+</note>
+
+<note>
+	Calling this outside of a receive callback, for example while writing a message with <page text="net.Start">net.Start</page>, returns `nil` because no message is being read.
+</note>
```

 <function name="Incoming" parent="net" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 <internal>You may be looking for <page>net.Receive</page>.</internal>
 
 Function called by the engine to tell the Lua state a message arrived.
+
+It reads the message name from the incoming data, looks the name up in `net.Receivers`, and calls the receiver function registered by <page>net.Receive</page>. The length passed to the receiver has the 16 bit header subtracted, so receivers get the length of the message body in bits.

 		<arg name="client" type="Player">The player that sent the message. This will be `nil` in the client state.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Logging incoming messages">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Wraps the function to log every incoming net message before the normal receiver runs. The wrapper is removed when the round ends, so the original behavior is restored.</description>
+	<code>
+local original = net.Incoming
+
+net.Incoming = function( length, client )
+	if ( IsValid( client ) ) then
+		print( "Net message from " .. client:Nick() .. ", " .. length .. " bits" )
+	end
+
+	original( length, client )
+end
+
+hook.Add( "EndRound", "NetMessageLogCleanup", function()
+	net.Incoming = original
+	hook.Remove( "EndRound", "NetMessageLogCleanup" )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>Net message from Player1, 48 bits</output>

 <function name="ReadColor" parent="net" type="libraryfunc">

 <function name="ReadHeader" parent="net" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 <internal></internal>
 
 Reads a word, basically unsigned short. This is used internally to read the "header" of the message which is an unsigned short which can be converted to the corresponding message name via <page>util.NetworkIDToString</page>.
+
+This function reads from the currently active net message. It is meant for intercepting incoming messages before they are dispatched to their <page>net.Receive</page> callbacks, for example inside a <page>net.Incoming</page> hook. Calling it outside of an active message read has no defined result.

Because the header is consumed here, the normal callbacks still receive the remaining message body unchanged.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "net.Incoming", "log_net_messages", function( length, client )
+	local header = net.ReadHeader()
+	local name = util.NetworkIDToString( header )
+
+	print( "Received net message: " .. ( name or "unknown (" .. header .. ")" ) )
+end )
+	</code>

```diff
--- original/net.WriteUInt64
+++ proposed/net.WriteUInt64
@@ -1,25 +1,52 @@
 <function name="WriteUInt64" parent="net" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 		Appends an unsigned integer with 64 bits to the current net message.
 
 		The limit for an uint64 is 18'446'744'073'709'551'615.  
 		Everything above the limit will be set to the limit.  
 
 		Unsigned numbers **do not** support negative numbers.  
 
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<added>2023.08.30</added>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="uint64" type="string">The 64 bit value to be sent. Can be a number.
 			<warning>
 				Since Lua cannot store full 64-bit integers, this function takes a string. It is mainly aimed at usage with <page>Player:SteamID64</page>.
 
 				If your input is a number and not a string, it won't be networked correctly as soon as it has more than 13 digits.  
 				This is because Lua represents numbers over 13 digits as `1e+14`(`100 000 000 000 000`)  
 				You can do something like this to convert it to a string: `string.format("%.0f", number)`.  
 				If you try to use <page>Global.tostring</page> it will fail because it will create a result something like `1e+14` which doesn't work.
 			</warning>
 		</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Sending a SteamID64">
+	<description>Sends a player's SteamID64 from the server to that player's client, which prints it. The value is written as a string so all 19 digits survive the trip. The receiving side reads it back with <page>net.ReadUInt64</page>, which also returns a string.</description>
+	<code name="Server">
+-- Addons/gamemodes: run on the server
+util.AddNetworkString( "SendMySteamID64" )
+
+net.Receive( "SendMySteamID64", function( len, ply )
+	if not IsValid( ply ) then return end
+
+	net.Start( "SendMySteamID64" )
+		net.WriteUInt64( ply:SteamID64() )
+	net.Send( ply )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<code name="Client">
+-- Run on the client
+net.Receive( "SendMySteamID64", function()
+	local id = net.ReadUInt64()
+
+	print( "My SteamID64 is " .. id )
+end )
+
+net.Start( "SendMySteamID64" )
+net.SendToServer()
+	</code>
+</example>
```

--- original/net.WriteVars
+++ proposed/net.WriteVars
@@ -1,11 +1,27 @@
 <function name="WriteVars" parent="net" type="libraryfield">
 	<description>
 <internal></internal>
 
 A list of types that can be sent over the network via <page>net.WriteType</page>.
+
+This is a table, not a function. Each key is a type ID as returned by <page>Global.TypeID</page>, and each value is the internal write function used by <page>net.WriteType</page> for that type. The table is used internally when writing and reading typed values, so modifying it changes which types <page>net.WriteType</page> and <page>net.ReadType</page> accept.
 </description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="table">Key = type ID (<page>Global.TypeID</page>), Value = function to send the data over the net.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Listing supported types">
+	<description>Runs on the client or server. Iterates the table and prints the name of each type ID that can be sent with <page>net.WriteType</page>.</description>
+	<code>
+for typeid, writefunc in pairs( net.WriteVars ) do
+	print( typeid, language.GetPhrase( "typeid_" .. typeid ), writefunc )
+end
+	</code>
+	<output>Shows one line per supported type, for example `2` with the phrase for the boolean type ID and its write function.</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>The keys are type IDs, not the string names used by <page>net.WriteType</page>. Use <page>Global.TypeID</page> to look up an ID for a value.</note>
+
+<warning>Do not modify this table unless you know what you are doing. Removing or replacing entries changes how <page>net.WriteType</page> and <page>net.ReadType</page> behave and can break networking between clients and the server if the tables differ.</warning>
```

## 3439. package.seeall

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/package.seeall) | Revision: 510443

```diff
--- original/package.seeall
+++ proposed/package.seeall
@@ -1,8 +1,29 @@
 <function name="seeall" parent="package" type="libraryfunc">
-	<description>Sets a metatable for module with its __index field referring to the global environment, so that this module inherits values from the global environment. To be used as an option to <page>Global.module</page>.</description>
+	<description>Sets a metatable for module with its __index field referring to the global environment, so that this module inherits values from the global environment. To be used as an option to <page>Global.module</page>.
+
+Without this option, a module created with `module` has an empty environment and cannot read globals such as `print` or `math` directly. Calling this function on the module table gives it access to them through the metatable's `__index` field.</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="module" type="table">The module table to be given a metatable</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Using seeall with module">
+	<description>Runs on the server. The module is created with `module` and then given access to the global environment, so `print` and `math` resolve through the metatable instead of raising an error.</description>
+	<code>
+module( "mymodule", package.seeall )
+
+function mymodule.Double( n )
+	-- print and math are visible because of package.seeall
+	print( "doubling", n )
+	return math.floor( n ) * 2
+end
+
+print( mymodule.Double( 3.7 ) )
+	</code>
+	<output>doubling	3.7
+7</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>Without `package.seeall`, the code above would fail with an attempt to call a nil value for `print`, because a module environment created by `module` starts empty.</note>
+
```

 <function name="GetByID" parent="player" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Gets the player with the specified connection ID.
 
 Connection ID can be retrieved via <page>gameevent.Listen</page> events.
 
 For a function that returns a player based on their <page>Entity:EntIndex</page>, see <page>Global.Entity</page>.
 
 
 For a function that returns a player based on their <page>Player:UserID</page>, see <page>Global.Player</page>.

+
+<note>The `userid` field of game events such as `player_connect` and `player_disconnect` is the connection ID this function expects. A disconnected player can no longer be found, so store and look up IDs promptly.</note>
+
+<example name="Resolving a player from a connect event">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Listens for the `player_connect` game event, resolves the connecting player by connection ID, and prints their name once they exist. The player is not valid at connect time, so the lookup is retried with a timer until it succeeds.</description>
+	<code>
+gameevent.Listen( "player_connect" )
+
+hook.Add( "player_connect", "AnnounceConnect", function( data )
+	local id = tonumber( data.userid )
+	if ( not id ) then return end
+
+	timer.Create( "ResolvePlayer_" .. id, 1, 30, function()
+		local ply = player.GetByID( id )
+
+		if ( IsValid( ply ) ) then
+			timer.Remove( "ResolvePlayer_" .. id )
+			print( ply:Nick() .. " finished connecting." )
+		end
+	end )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```
