```diff
--- original/properties.CanBeTargeted
+++ proposed/properties.CanBeTargeted
@@ -1,17 +1,43 @@
 <function name="CanBeTargeted" parent="properties" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns true if given entity can be targeted by the player via the properties system.
 
 This should be used serverside in your properties to prevent abuse by clientside scripting.
+
+The function returns false for invalid entities and for players. If a player argument is given, the distance from the player's shoot position to the entity's OBB center is compared against the largest OBB extent plus 1024 units, and entities beyond that range are rejected. Finally the entity must either have a physics object or be solid in some way (an entity that is nonsolid, has no physics objects, and lacks the FSOLID_USE_TRIGGER_BOUNDS and FSOLID_CUSTOMRAYTEST flags is rejected).
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<file line="104-L120">lua/includes/modules/properties.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="ent" type="Entity">The entity to test</arg>
 		<arg name="ply" type="Player">If given, will also perform a distance check based on the entity's Orientated Bounding Box.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">True if entity can be targeted, false otherwise</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<note>The distance check is a rough range test based on the bounding box size, not an exact reach measurement. Larger entities can be targeted from farther away.</note>
+
+<example name="Gating a custom property">
+	<description>Runs on the server. A custom property can only be applied to entities that players are actually allowed to target, so a hostile client cannot bypass the check with scripts.</description>
+	<code>
+properties.Add( "explode_doomsday", {
+	MenuLabel = "Explode (doomsday)",
+	Order = 9999,
+
+	Filter = function( self, ent, ply )
+		if ( not properties.CanBeTargeted( ent, ply ) ) then return false end
+		return true
+	end,
+
+	Action = function( self, ent )
+		if ( not IsValid( ent ) ) then return end
+		local effectdata = EffectData()
+		effectdata:SetOrigin( ent:GetPos() )
+		util.Effect( "Explosion", effectdata )
+		ent:Remove()
+	end
+} )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/render.BlurRenderTarget
+++ proposed/render.BlurRenderTarget
@@ -1,16 +1,53 @@
 <function name="BlurRenderTarget" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 		Blurs the render target ( or a given texture ).
+		
+		The blur is done in passes. Each pass draws the texture through a horizontal blur shader into the internal <code>tex_Bloom1</code> render target, then back through a vertical blur shader into the given render target. The loop runs <code>passes + 1</code> times, so even a passes value of <code>0</code> performs one pass. Larger blur amounts and more passes are more expensive, so keep both low when blurring every frame.
+		
+		This function changes the current render target and material while it runs. Call it from a context where that is allowed, such as inside <page text="render.PushRenderTarget">render.PushRenderTarget</page> and <page text="render.PopRenderTarget">render.PopRenderTarget</page>, or restore state afterwards.
 		
 		<warning>Calling this on a RenderTarget created with TEXTUREFLAGS_POINTSAMPLE will result in strange visual glitching.</warning>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<file line="88-L107">lua/includes/extensions/client/render.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="rendertarget" type="ITexture">The texture to blur.</arg>
 		<arg name="blurx" type="number">Horizontal amount of blur.</arg>
 		<arg name="blury" type="number">Vertical amount of blur.</arg>
 		<arg name="passes" type="number">Amount of passes to go through.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Blurring a render target">
+	<description>
+		Runs on the client. Creates a render target, copies the current screen into it, blurs it, and draws the blurred result as a fullscreen overlay while a key is held. The hook is removed when the script is reloaded or the key is released.
+	</description>
+	<code>
+local rt = GetRenderTarget( "blur_example_rt", ScrW(), ScrH() )
+local mat = Material( "!blur_example_rt" )
+local active = false
+
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "blur_example", function()
+	if input.IsKeyDown( KEY_B ) then
+		active = true
+
+		render.PushRenderTarget( rt )
+		render.Clear( 0, 0, 0, 255 )
+		cam.Start2D()
+			surface.DrawRect( 0, 0, ScrW(), ScrH() ) -- replace with whatever you want to blur
+		cam.End2D()
+
+		render.BlurRenderTarget( rt, 2, 2, 1 )
+		render.PopRenderTarget()
+	elseif active then
+		active = false
+		hook.Remove( "HUDPaint", "blur_example" )
+		return
+	end
+
+	surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 255, 255 )
+	surface.SetMaterial( mat )
+	surface.DrawTexturedRect( 0, 0, ScrW(), ScrH() )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

@@ -1,11 +1,29 @@
 <function name="CapturePixels" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description><rendercontext hook="false" type="2D"></rendercontext>
 	Dumps the current render target and allows the pixels to be accessed by <page>render.ReadPixel</page>. 
 
 	Capturing outside a render hook will return an image filled with `0 0 0 255`.
 
 	See also <page>render.Capture</page>.
 </description>

+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "ReadCenterPixel", function()
+	render.CapturePixels()
+
+	local w, h = ScrW(), ScrH()
+	local r, g, b, a = render.ReadPixel( w / 2, h / 2 )
+
+	surface.SetDrawColor( r, g, b, a )
+	surface.DrawRect( 20, 20, 32, 32 )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
+

 <function name="ClearDepth" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Resets the depth buffer.
+
+The depth buffer stores how far each drawn pixel is from the camera. Clearing it makes the engine treat everything as if nothing has been drawn yet, so subsequently drawn geometry is not hidden behind previously drawn geometry. This is commonly used before drawing custom 3D content in a 2D rendering context, such as a 3D2D panel or a custom world overlay.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg type="boolean" name="clearStencil" default="true">Whether to also clear the stencil buffer.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example>
+	<description>Runs on the client inside a <page text="HUDPaint">Global.HUDPaint</page> hook. It clears the depth buffer, then draws a rotating 3D2D panel in front of the local player. Without the depth clear, the panel can be incorrectly occluded by world geometry that was already rendered into the depth buffer.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "ClearDepthExample", function()
+	-- Reset depth so the 3D2D panel is not clipped by existing depth values.
+	render.ClearDepth()
+
+	local pos = EyePos() + EyeAngles():Forward() * 100
+	local ang = EyeAngles()
+	ang:RotateAroundAxis( ang:Up(), 90 )
+	ang:RotateAroundAxis( ang:Forward(), 90 )
+
+	render.SetMaterial( Material( "models/debug/debugwhite" ) )
+	cam.Start3D2D( pos, ang, 1 )
+		draw.SimpleText( "Depth cleared", "DermaDefault", 0, 0, color_white, TEXT_ALIGN_CENTER, TEXT_ALIGN_CENTER )
+	cam.End3D2D()
+end )
+
+-- Remove the hook when it is no longer needed:
+-- hook.Remove( "HUDPaint", "ClearDepthExample" )
+	</code>

```diff
--- original/render.GetFullScreenDepthTexture
+++ proposed/render.GetFullScreenDepthTexture
@@ -1,11 +1,38 @@
 <function name="GetFullScreenDepthTexture" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 <deprecated>Alias of <page>render.GetPowerOfTwoTexture</page> in practice.</deprecated>
 
-Returns the full screen depth texture.</description>
+Returns the full screen depth texture.
+
+This is the texture the engine renders scene depth into. On PC it resolves to `_rt_PowerOfTwoFB`, so the returned texture is the same object you would get from <page>render.GetPowerOfTwoTexture</page>. The texture is only meaningful while the engine is rendering the 3D scene, for example inside a rendering hook such as <page>GM:PostRender</page> or a screen space effect. Outside of rendering, the texture contents may be stale or empty.
+	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="ITexture">The `_rt_FullFrameDepth` texture, which is an alias of `_rt_PowerOfTwoFB` on PC.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Drawing the depth texture">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Draws the full screen depth texture over the screen while the player holds a key. The depth texture is grayscale, so nearer surfaces appear brighter or darker depending on how the engine encodes depth. The hook is removed when the player releases the key.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "DepthTextureDebug", function()
+	if not input.IsKeyDown( KEY_T ) then
+		hook.Remove( "HUDPaint", "DepthTextureDebug" )
+		return
+	end
+
+	local depth = render.GetFullScreenDepthTexture()
+	if not IsValid( depth ) then return end
+
+	surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 255, 255 )
+	surface.SetMaterial( Material( "!" .. depth:GetName() ) )
+	surface.DrawTexturedRect( 0, 0, ScrW(), ScrH() )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<description>Hold `T` to overlay the depth texture on the screen. Release `T` to remove the hook.</description>
+</example>
+
+<note>The returned texture is shared with the engine. Do not modify or free it.</note>
+
+<note>Because this is an alias of <page>render.GetPowerOfTwoTexture</page>, new code should call that function directly.</note>
+
```

## 3522. render.GetSuperFPTex

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.GetSuperFPTex) | Revision: 565803

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091777-Npbnt3c0JBKU6STpkBvH`. Duration: 9.02s. Attempt cost: 0.00076059375.

- No supplied implementation or source lines; added description and example are grounded only in the existing page text and standard screen space pass practice. Reviewer should verify the example's exact hook and material usage against a working reference.
- Existing realm Client preserved. If the ret description (render target named __rt_SuperTexture1) is editable, it was preserved as is.

```diff
--- original/render.GetSuperFPTex
+++ proposed/render.GetSuperFPTex
@@ -1,12 +1,61 @@
 <function name="GetSuperFPTex" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns a floating point texture (RGBA16161616F format) the same resolution as the screen.
+
+Because the texture stores high dynamic range color values, values above 1 and below 0 are preserved. This makes it useful as a buffer for screen space effects that need precision, such as custom tonemapping or bloom, before the result is drawn to an integer render target.
 
 <note>The <page text="gmodscreenspace">Shaders/gmodscreenspace</page> doesn't behave as expected when drawing a floating-point texture to an integer texture (e.g. the default render target). Use an UnlitGeneric material instead</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="ITexture">Render target named `__rt_SuperTexture1`.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Increasing brightness with a floating point pass">
+	<description>Runs on the client inside a <page text="PreRender">GM:PreRender</page> hook. The scene is rendered to the floating point texture, then amplified and drawn to the screen with an UnlitGeneric material, which avoids the gmodscreenspace issue above. Registrations are removed after one frame with a timer so the effect runs once.
+
+The <code>pixel_x</code> and <code>pixel_y</code> entry points are the usual way to feed world data into a render target with this pattern. Swap the render target back before starting the screen space pass.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "PreRender", "fp_bright_example", function()
+	-- Point the pipeline at the floating point texture.
+	local fp = render.GetSuperFPTex()
+
+	render.PushRenderTarget( fp )
+	render.OverrideDepthEnable( true, false )
+	render.Clear( 0, 0, 0, 255 )
+
+		render.SetViewData( { origin = EyePos(), angles = EyeAngles(), x = 0, y = 0, w = ScrW(), h = ScrH() )
+		render.RenderView( {
+			origin = EyePos(),
+			angles = EyeAngles(),
+			x = 0, y = 0,
+			w = ScrW(), h = ScrH(),
+			rendertarget = fp
+		} )
+
+	render.OverrideDepthEnable( false, false )
+	render.PopRenderTarget()
+
+	-- Draw the buffer amplified. Use UnlitGeneric, not gmodscreenspace.
+	local mat = CreateMaterial( "fp_bright_example", "UnlitGeneric", {
+		[ "$basetexture" ] = fp:GetName(),
+		[ "$model" ] = 1
+	} )
+	mat:SetFloat( "$alpha", 1 )
+
+	hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "fp_bright_example_draw", function()
+		surface.SetMaterial( mat )
+		surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 255, 255, 255 )
+		surface.DrawTexturedRect( 0, 0, ScrW(), ScrH() )
+	end )
+
+	timer.Simple( 0.1, function()
+		hook.Remove( "PreRender", "fp_bright_example" )
+		hook.Remove( "HUDPaint", "fp_bright_example_draw" )
+		RunConsoleCommand( "r_screenoverlay", "" )
+	end )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<description>The floating point texture holds the scene with color values outside the 0 to 1 range intact, so light sources survive amplification without clipping to white as they would in an integer buffer.</description>
+</example>
```

## 3531. render.ModelMaterialOverride

```diff
--- original/render.ModelMaterialOverride
+++ proposed/render.ModelMaterialOverride
@@ -1,15 +1,35 @@
 <function name="ModelMaterialOverride" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 		Forces all future draw operations to use a specific <page>IMaterial</page>.  
 		
 		Because this is independent of a specific <page>Entity</page>, it can be used to change materials on static models that are part of maps.
+
+		The override stays active until it is reset by calling the function again with `nil`. It affects every model drawn after the call, so it is usually set and reset inside rendering hooks, or toggled for a limited time.
 
 <warning>In certain scenarios such as during entity's shadow pass, using this function can cause unexpected side effects. See example on <page>render.MaterialOverride</page> about dealing with this.</warning>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="material" type="IMaterial" default="nil">
 			The <page>IMaterial</page> that will be used for all upcoming draw operations, or `nil` to stop overriding. 
 		</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Wireframe world">
+	<description>Runs on the client. While the player holds the IN_USE key, every model drawn during the opaque render pass, including map geometry models, is drawn with the wireframe material. The override is reset at the end of the pass so it does not leak into other rendering.</description>
+	<code>
+local wireframe = Material( "models/wireframe" )
+
+hook.Add( "PreDrawOpaqueRenderables", "WireframeWorldStart", function( bDrawingDepth, bDrawingSkybox )
+	if ( bDrawingDepth or bDrawingSkybox ) then return end
+	if ( input.IsKeyDown( KEY_USE ) ) then
+		render.ModelMaterialOverride( wireframe )
+	end
+end )
+
+hook.Add( "PostDrawOpaqueRenderables", "WireframeWorldEnd", function()
+	render.ModelMaterialOverride( nil )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

- Added prose explaining source versus destination blend roles and a client example; no API contract changes were made.

```diff
--- original/render.OverrideBlendFunc
+++ proposed/render.OverrideBlendFunc
@@ -1,19 +1,43 @@
 <function name="OverrideBlendFunc" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 <deprecated>Use <page>render.OverrideBlend</page> instead.</deprecated>
 
 Overrides the internal graphical functions used to determine the final color and alpha of a rendered texture.
+
+The source blend function decides how the texture being drawn contributes to the result. The destination blend function decides how the pixels already on the screen contribute. Common combinations are <page>Enums/BLEND</page> values `BLEND_SRC_ALPHA` with `BLEND_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA` for normal alpha blending, or `BLEND_SRC_ALPHA` with `BLEND_ONE` for additive blending.
 
 See also <page>render.OverrideAlphaWriteEnable</page>.
 
 <note>Doing <page>surface</page> draw calls with alpha set to 0 is a no-op and will never have any effect.</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="enabled" type="boolean">true to enable, false to disable. No other arguments are required when disabling.</arg>
 		<arg name="srcBlend" type="number">The source color blend function <page>Enums/BLEND</page>. Determines how a rendered texture's final color should be calculated.</arg>
-		<arg name="destBlend" type="number"></arg>
+		<arg name="destBlend" type="number">The destination color blend function <page>Enums/BLEND</page>. Determines how the existing pixels on the screen should be calculated.</arg>
 		<arg name="srcBlendAlpha" type="number" default="nil">The source alpha blend function <page>Enums/BLEND</page>. Determines how a rendered texture's final alpha should be calculated.</arg>
 		<arg name="destBlendAlpha" type="number" default="nil"></arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Additive glow quad">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Draws a bright additive quad in a 2D rendering hook, then restores normal blending. Additive blending brightens whatever is already on the screen instead of covering it.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "AdditiveGlowExample", function()
+	-- Enable additive blending for color and alpha
+	render.OverrideBlendFunc( true, BLEND_SRC_ALPHA, BLEND_ONE, BLEND_SRC_ALPHA, BLEND_ONE )
+
+	surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 120, 0, 255 )
+	surface.DrawRect( 100, 100, 200, 200 )
+
+	-- Restore normal blending so other drawing is unaffected
+	render.OverrideBlendFunc( false )
+end )
+
+-- Remove the hook when it is no longer needed
+-- hook.Remove( "HUDPaint", "AdditiveGlowExample" )
+	</code>
+	<description>
+The rectangle appears as a bright orange glow that brightens the game view behind it. Overlapping bright areas become brighter still, which is the visible effect of `BLEND_ONE` on the destination.
+	</description>
+</example>
```

--- original/render.OverrideDepthEnable
+++ proposed/render.OverrideDepthEnable
@@ -1,9 +1,34 @@
 <function name="OverrideDepthEnable" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Overrides the write behaviour of all next rendering operations towards the depth buffer.</description>
+	<note>This override stays active until it is reset with <code>render.OverrideDepthEnable( false, false )</code>, and affects all subsequent draw calls, including draws outside the hook it was enabled in. Always restore the default behaviour in the same rendering hook.</note>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="enable" type="boolean">Enable or disable the override.</arg>
 		<arg name="shouldWrite" type="boolean">If the previous argument is true, sets whether the next rendering operations should write to the depth buffer or not. Has no effect if the previous argument is false.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Drawing shapes without depth writes">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Enables the override inside a rendering hook to draw translucent boxes that do not write to the depth buffer, so their draw order determines which one is drawn on top. The override is disabled again after drawing so the depth buffer is not affected by anything else.
+	</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "PostDrawTranslucentRenderables", "depth_write_example", function( bDrawingDepth, bDrawingSkybox )
+	if bDrawingDepth or bDrawingSkybox then return end
+
+	local pos = LocalPlayer():GetEyeTrace().HitPos
+
+	render.OverrideDepthEnable( true, false ) -- disable depth writes
+
+	local mat = Material( "models/debug/debugwhite" )
+	render.SetMaterial( mat )
+	render.DrawBox( pos + Vector( 0, 0, 48 ), angle_zero, Vector( -16, -16, -16 ), Vector( 16, 16, 16 ), Color( 0, 0, 255, 100 ) )
+	render.DrawBox( pos + Vector( 0, 0, 80 ), angle_zero, Vector( -16, -16, -16 ), Vector( 16, 16, 16 ), Color( 255, 0, 0, 100 ) )
+
+	render.OverrideDepthEnable( false, false ) -- restore default behaviour
+end )
+
+-- Remove the hook on its cleanup
+hook.Remove( "PostDrawTranslucentRenderables", "depth_write_example" )
+	</code>
+	<description>Look at a surface to see where the boxes appear. The red box is drawn after the blue box, so with depth writes disabled it appears on top of the blue box regardless of which one is closer to the camera.</description>
+</example>
```

+	-- Draw something that benefits from the sharper filter here.

 	<description>
 		Pushes (Adds) a texture filter onto the magnification texture filter stack.  
 		This will modify how textures are stretched to sizes larger than their native resolution for upcoming rendering and drawing operations.

 </description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="texFilterType" type="number">The texture filter to use. For available options, see <page>Enums/TEXFILTER</page>.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Pixelated magnification">
+	<description>
+		Runs on the client. Draws a texture stretched well past its native size with magnification filtering set to <page>Enums/TEXFILTER</page> `TEXFILTER.POINT`, so each texel stays sharp and blocky instead of being smoothed. The filter is popped immediately after drawing so other rendering is unaffected.
+	</description>
+	<code>

+

+
+	-- The texture is drawn at 256x256, far larger than its native resolution.
+	surface.SetMaterial( texture )
+	surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 255, 255 )
+	surface.DrawTexturedRect( 32, 32, 256, 256 )
+
+	render.PopFilterMag()
+end )

 	<description>
 Enables the flashlight projection for the upcoming rendering.

+This function pushes a flashlight rendering mode onto a stack. While enabled, subsequently rendered models are lit as if by the local player's flashlight. Call <page>render.PopFlashlightMode</page> to restore the previous mode after rendering.

 	<description>
 Sets the goal HDR tone mapping scale.
+
+The tone mapping scale controls how the engine compresses bright HDR colors into the displayable range. Higher values make bright areas bloom out more and darken the rest of the scene over time, while lower values keep the image close to its base appearance.

+
+hook.Add( "PreRender", "ToneMapDamageFlash", function()

+		return

+

+end )
+

```diff
--- original/render.SetLightingOrigin
+++ proposed/render.SetLightingOrigin
@@ -1,10 +1,31 @@
 <function name="SetLightingOrigin" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets lighting origin for the current model.
+
+The next model drawn in the current render pass is lit as if it were at the given position, instead of at its own origin. This is useful when a model is drawn away from its lighting context, or when you want a model to receive lighting from a specific spot, such as a lamp.
+
+Call this from a render hook, immediately before drawing the affected model. The setting applies to the model drawn next and does not persist between frames.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="lightingOrigin" type="Vector">The position which will be used to calculate lighting for the current model.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Lighting a model from a fixed point">
+	<description>
+Runs on the client. Inside the PrePlayerDraw hook, the lighting origin is moved to a point 64 units above the player's feet, so the player model is lit from above regardless of nearby geometry. The hook returns nothing, so the player still draws normally.
+	</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "PrePlayerDraw", "LightingFromAbove", function( ply )
+	if ( not IsValid( ply ) ) then return end
+
+	local lightPos = ply:GetPos() + Vector( 0, 0, 64 )
+	render.SetLightingOrigin( lightPos )
+end )
+
+-- Remove the hook when it is no longer needed
+hook.Remove( "PrePlayerDraw", "LightingFromAbove" )
+	</code>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
--- original/render.SetModelLighting
+++ proposed/render.SetModelLighting
@@ -1,18 +1,40 @@
 <function name="SetModelLighting" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets up the ambient lighting for any upcoming render operation. Ambient lighting can be seen as a cube enclosing the object to be drawn, each of its faces representing a directional light source that shines towards the object. Thus, there is a total of six different light sources that can be configured separately.
 
 Light color components are not restricted to a specific range (i.e. 0-1), instead, higher values will result in a brighter light.
+
+The lighting state persists for the rest of the current rendering pass. Any subsequent model drawing, for example with <page>ENTITY:DrawModel</page>, uses it until <page>render.ResetModelLighting</page> is called or a new value is set. Because several directions can be set at once, calling <page>render.ResetModelLighting</page> first is a common way to start from a clean state.
 
 <page>render.ResetModelLighting</page> will set all 6 directions at once.
 See also <page>render.SetLocalModelLights</page>.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="lightDirection" type="number{BOX}">The light source to edit, see <page>Enums/BOX</page>.</arg>
 		<arg name="red" type="number">The red component of the light color. In range of [0,1]</arg>
 		<arg name="green" type="number">The green component of the light color. In range of [0,1]</arg>
 		<arg name="blue" type="number">The blue component of the light color. In range of [0,1]</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Red light from above">
+	<description>Runs on the client. In a render hook, resets the model lighting, then tints every physics prop with a strong red light from the top direction before drawing it. Remove the hook to restore the default rendering.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "PostDrawOpaqueRenderables", "model_lighting_example", function()
+	-- Start from known lighting values, the state persists between draws
+	render.ResetModelLighting()
+
+	-- Strong red light from above, dim light from the bottom
+	render.SetModelLighting( BOX_TOP, 1, 0.3, 0.3 )
+	render.SetModelLighting( BOX_BOTTOM, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2 )
+
+	for _, ent in ipairs( ents.FindByClass( "prop_physics" ) ) do
+		ent:DrawModel()
+	end
+end )
+
+-- Call this to restore normal rendering:
+-- hook.Remove( "PostDrawOpaqueRenderables", "model_lighting_example" )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

Use <page text="render.GetRenderTarget">render.GetRenderTarget</page> to save the current target before changing it, and set it back afterwards to avoid rendering to the wrong surface.</description>

+local rt = GetRenderTarget( "myexample_rt", 256, 256 )

+	cam.Start2D()
+		surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 0, 0, 255 )
+		surface.DrawRect( 64, 64, 128, 128 )
+	cam.End2D()
+
+	-- Restore the previous target so rendering continues to the screen
+	render.SetRenderTarget( previous )
+
+	surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 255, 255, 255 )
+	surface.SetMaterial( Material( "models/debug/debugwhite" ) )
+
+	-- Example of displaying the texture: copy its contents to a material
+	local mat = CreateMaterial( "MyExampleRTCopy", "UnlitGeneric", { [ "$basetexture" ] = "myexample_rt" } )
+	surface.SetMaterial( mat )
+	surface.DrawTexturedRect( 16, ScrH() / 2, 256, 256 )
+end )

+	</code>
+	<description>The hook runs during <page text="HUDPaint">HUDPaint</page>, which is in a 2D rendering context on the client. The screen shows a 256 by 256 square containing a red box drawn onto the render target.</description>
+</example>
+
+<note>The target is not restored automatically. Failing to set the render target back after drawing can make the rest of the frame render to the wrong surface.</note>

## 3562. render.SetStencilCompareFunction

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilCompareFunction) | Revision: 565823

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091775-5N5Qr29Yzj9CoXVK3PGz`. Duration: 4.88s. Attempt cost: 0.00058098.

- Added the STENCILCOMPARISONFUNCTION enum link and an EQUAL example; no source files were supplied, so no default or contract changes were made.

```diff
--- original/render.SetStencilCompareFunction
+++ proposed/render.SetStencilCompareFunction
@@ -1,20 +1,48 @@
 <function name="SetStencilCompareFunction" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Sets the Compare Function that all pixels affected by a draw operation will have their Stencil Buffer value tested against.  
 
 When not set to a static value like NEVER or ALWAYS, the Stencil Buffer value corresponding to each affected pixel will be compared against the current <page text="Reference Value">render.SetStencilReferenceValue</page>.
 
 Pixels that **Pass** the Compare Function check move on to the Depth Test, which determines if the draw operation will ultimately be allowed to overwrite the pixel's Color Channel, Stencil Buffer, and Depth Buffer values.
 
 Pixels that **Fail** the Compare Function check have the <page text="Fail Operation">render.SetStencilFailOperation</page> performed on their Stencil Buffer value and do **not** have any of their Render Target layers modified by the draw operation.
 
 For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the <page text="Stencils Render Reference">render_stencils</page> page.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
-		<arg name="compareFunction" type="number{STENCILCOMPARISONFUNCTION}">The Compare Function that each affected pixel's Stencil Buffer value will be evaluated against during a draw operation.</arg>
+		<arg name="compareFunction" type="number{STENCILCOMPARISONFUNCTION}">The Compare Function that each affected pixel's Stencil Buffer value will be evaluated against during a draw operation. Must be one of the <page text="STENCILCOMPARISONFUNCTION">Enums/STENCILCOMPARISONFUNCTION</page> enums, for example <code>STENCILCOMPARISONFUNCTION.EQUAL</code>.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
 <upload src="b2b4c/8dc4ead6a5336e3.png" size="77526" name="CompareFunctionFlowChart.png" />
 
+<example name="Drawing only where the stencil matches">
+	<description>Runs on the client inside a 2D rendering hook. A first pass writes the value 1 into the Stencil Buffer inside a rectangle. A second pass sets the Compare Function to EQUAL with a Reference Value of 1, so the red rectangle is only drawn where the Stencil Buffer holds 1. The stencil state is reset afterwards.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "StencilCompareExample", function()
+	render.ClearStencil()
+	render.SetStencilEnableWritePass( true )
+	render.SetStencilWriteMask( 255 )
+	render.SetStencilReferenceValue( 1 )
+	render.SetStencilCompareFunction( STENCILCOMPARISONFUNCTION.ALWAYS )
+	render.SetStencilPassOperation( STENCILOPERATION.REPLACE )
+
+	-- Mark this rectangle with the value 1 in the Stencil Buffer
+	surface.SetDrawColor( 0, 0, 0, 0 )
+	surface.DrawRect( 100, 100, 200, 200 )
+
+	render.SetStencilEnableWritePass( false )
+	render.SetStencilEnableReadPass( true )
+
+	-- Only draw where the Stencil Buffer equals the Reference Value of 1
+	render.SetStencilCompareFunction( STENCILCOMPARISONFUNCTION.EQUAL )
+
+	surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 0, 0, 255 )
+	surface.DrawRect( 50, 50, 300, 300 )
+
+	render.SetStencilEnableReadPass( false )
+end )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

--- original/render.SetStencilEnable
+++ proposed/render.SetStencilEnable
@@ -1,19 +1,47 @@
 <function name="SetStencilEnable" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Enables or disables the Stencil system for future draw operations.
 
 While enabled, all pixels affected by draw operations will have their corresponding values in the active <page text="Render Target's">render_rendertargets</page> Stencil Buffer compared against the current <page text="Reference Value">render.SetStencilReferenceValue</page> and their current Depth Buffer value compared against the depth of the corresponding pixel from the draw operation.  
 Depending on the outcomes of these comparisons, one of either the <page text="Pass">render.SetStencilPassOperation</page>, <page text="Fail">render.SetStencilFailOperation</page>, or <page text="Z-Fail">render.SetStencilZFailOperation</page> operations is performed on the pixel's Stencil Buffer value.  
 A pixel will only be updated in the active <page text="Render Target">render_rendertargets</page> if the <page text="Pass Operation">render.SetStencilPassOperation</page> is performed.
 
 For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the <page text="Stencils Render Reference">render_stencils</page> page.
 
 <note>The Stencil system's configuration does **not** reset automatically.  
 To prevent unexpected behavior, always manually ensure that the Stencil system is configured appropriately for your use-case after enabling it.</note>
-
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="newState" type="boolean">The new state.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Screen masked text">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Inside a <page text="HUDPaint">GM:HUDPaint</page> hook, the Stencil system is enabled and used to fill the shape of drawn text with a solid color. First the stencil buffer is cleared and any drawn pixel replaces its stencil value with the reference value. Then the compare function is switched to only pass where the stencil value already equals the reference, so the red rectangle is drawn only where the text wrote stencil values. Disabling the stencil at the end stops further drawing from being affected.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "StencilTextExample", function()
+	render.SetStencilEnable( true )
+	render.ClearStencil()
+
+	render.SetStencilWriteMask( 255 )
+	render.SetStencilTestMask( 255 )
+	render.SetStencilReferenceValue( 1 )
+	render.SetStencilPassOperation( STENCILREPLACEWITHREF )
+	render.SetStencilFailOperation( STENCIL_KEEP )
+	render.SetStencilZFailOperation( STENCIL_KEEP )
+
+	-- Write the reference value into the stencil buffer wherever text is drawn
+	render.SetStencilCompareFunction( STENCILCOMPARISONFUNCTION_ALWAYS )
+	draw.SimpleText( "Stencil", "DermaLarge", 32, ScrH() / 2, color_white )
+
+	-- Now only draw where the stencil value equals the reference (the text shape)
+	render.SetStencilCompareFunction( STENCILCOMPARISONFUNCTION_EQUAL )
+	surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 0, 0 )
+	surface.DrawRect( 0, 0, ScrW(), ScrH() )
+
+	render.SetStencilEnable( false )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>The word Stencil appears filled with solid red instead of white. The rest of the screen is not affected.</output>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/render.SetStencilTestMask
+++ proposed/render.SetStencilTestMask
@@ -1,18 +1,57 @@
 <function name="SetStencilTestMask" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 		Sets the unsigned 8-bit (`byte`) bitflag mask that will be bitwise ANDed with all values as they are read (tested) from the Stencil Buffer
 
 		This can be considered a "niche" Stencil function as it is not required for many Stencil use-cases.
 
 		This is a companion function to <page>render.SetStencilWriteMask</page> which modifies Stencil Buffer values as they are written.
 
 		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the <page text="Stencils Render Reference">render_stencils</page> page.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="bitMask" type="number">
 			The 8-bit (`byte`) mask.  
 			Set to `255` to make no change to read Stencil Buffer values.
 		</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
+
+<example>
+	<description>Runs on the client inside a `HUDPaint` hook. The stencil buffer is filled with `1` while a rectangle is drawn, then a second pass uses a test mask of `255` so the full written value is compared. Only pixels inside the rectangle pass the stencil test and get drawn over. The hook is removed after one frame to clean up.</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "StencilTestMaskExample", function()
+	render.ClearStencil()
+
+	render.SetStencilEnable( true )
+
+	-- Write the value 1 wherever the rectangle is drawn
+	render.SetStencilWriteMask( 255 )
+	render.SetStencilTestMask( 255 )
+	render.SetStencilPassOperation( STENCIL_KEEP )
+	render.SetStencilFailOperation( STENCIL_KEEP )
+	render.SetStencilZFailOperation( STENCIL_KEEP )
+	render.SetStencilCompareFunction( STENCIL_ALWAYS )
+	render.SetStencilReferenceValue( 1 )
+
+	surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 255, 255 )
+	surface.DrawRect( 100, 100, 200, 100 )
+
+	-- Second pass: only draw where the stencil buffer equals 1.
+	-- The test mask of 255 keeps the full stored value for comparison.
+	render.SetStencilTestMask( 255 )
+	render.SetStencilCompareFunction( STENCIL_EQUAL )
+
+	surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 0, 0 )
+	surface.DrawRect( 50, 50, 300, 200 )
+
+	render.SetStencilEnable( false )
+end )
+
+-- Remove the hook after it has run once
+timer.Simple( 0, function()
+	hook.Remove( "HUDPaint", "StencilTestMaskExample" )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<description>Because the test mask is `255`, the comparison uses the whole stored stencil value. A mask of `1` would compare only the lowest bit, so a stored value of `3` would still pass an `STENCIL_EQUAL` test against a reference value of `1`.</description>
+</example>
```

## 3567. render.SetStencilWriteMask

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/render.SetStencilWriteMask) | Revision: 565829

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091807-JoON2xIcDGXEZnj7phDa`. Duration: 21.44s. Attempt cost: 0.0001573018.

- Added a note and one example; no contract changes. Source status remains unverified, so the example relies only on documented behavior of the stencil functions it calls.

```diff
--- original/render.SetStencilWriteMask
+++ proposed/render.SetStencilWriteMask
@@ -1,18 +1,56 @@
 <function name="SetStencilWriteMask" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 		Sets the unsigned 8-bit (`byte`) bitflag mask that will be bitwise ANDed with all values as they are written to the Stencil Buffer
 
 		This can be considered a "niche" Stencil function as it is not required for many Stencil use-cases.
 
 		This is a companion function to <page>render.SetStencilTestMask</page> which modifies Stencil Buffer values as they are read.
 
 		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the <page text="Stencils Render Reference">render_stencils</page> page.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="bitMask" type="number">
 			The 8-bit (`byte`) mask.  
 			Set to `255` to make no change to written Stencil Buffer values.
 		</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
+
+<note>Values written to the Stencil Buffer are also affected by <page>render.SetStencilReferenceValue</page> and the compare operation set by <page>render.SetStencilCompareFunction</page>. The write mask only limits which bits of the resulting value are stored, it does not change the comparison itself.</note>
+
+<example name="Writing only the lower 4 bits">
+	<description>
+		Runs on the client inside a 2D rendering hook. The write mask `15` (`0b00001111`) keeps only the lower 4 bits of each value written to the Stencil Buffer, so the buffer stores `5` instead of `133` when the reference value `133` is written. The test mask is left at `255` so the comparison still uses the full value.
+
+		Put this in a clientside Lua file and enable it with a console command to see the printed result.
+	</description>
+	<code>
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "StencilWriteMaskExample", function()
+	render.ClearStencil()
+
+	render.SetStencilEnable( true )
+
+	-- Only the lower 4 bits of written values are stored
+	render.SetStencilWriteMask( 15 )
+	-- Compare against the full value
+	render.SetStencilTestMask( 255 )
+
+	render.SetStencilCompareFunction( STENCIL_ALWAYS )
+	render.SetStencilPassOperation( STENCIL_REPLACE )
+	render.SetStencilReferenceValue( 133 )
+
+	-- Draw something so the pass operation runs and writes to the buffer
+	draw.NoTexture()
+	surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 0, 0 )
+	surface.DrawRect( 100, 100, 200, 200 )
+
+	-- Read back the value at the center of the rectangle
+	local value = render.ReadPixel( 200, 200 )
+	print( "Stencil buffer value: " .. value ) -- 5, not 133
+
+	render.SetStencilEnable( false )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>Stencil buffer value: 5</output>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/render.UpdateRefractTexture
+++ proposed/render.UpdateRefractTexture
@@ -1,5 +1,35 @@
 <function name="UpdateRefractTexture" parent="render" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Pretty much alias of <page>render.UpdatePowerOfTwoTexture</page> but does not return the texture.</description>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Refraction render pass">
+	<description>Runs client side inside the <page>GM:PreDrawOpaqueRenderables</page> hook. Before drawing the scene into the refract texture, switch to a suitable render target, then restore the previous render target afterwards so other rendering is not affected.</description>
+	<code>
+local refractTexture = render.GetRefractTexture()
+
+hook.Add( "PreDrawOpaqueRenderables", "RefractExample", function( bDrawingDepth, bDrawingSkybox )
+	if ( bDrawingDepth or bDrawingSkybox ) then return end
+
+	-- Remember the render target that was active before us
+	local oldRT = render.GetRenderTarget()
+
+	render.SetRenderTarget( refractTexture )
+	render.SetViewPort( 0, 0, ScrW(), ScrH() )
+	render.Clear( 0, 0, 0, 255 )
+
+	-- Redraw the scene background into the texture
+	render.DrawScreenQuad()
+
+	-- Make the new content available to materials that sample it
+	render.UpdateRefractTexture()
+
+	-- Restore the previous render target and viewport
+	render.SetRenderTarget( oldRT )
+	render.SetViewPort( 0, 0, ScrW(), ScrH() )
+end )
+	</code>
+	<description>The texture is refreshed on the client only, this example has no effect on other players.</description>
+</example>
+

```

+	local data = saverestore.ReadTable( restore )

+</example>

Will wait until <page>sql.Commit</page> is called to run them.<br/>\r\nThis is most useful when you run more than 100+ queries.<br/>\r\nThis is equivalent to :\r\n```\r\nsql.Query( \"BEGIN;\" )\r\n```\r\nQueries sent between <page>sql.Begin</page> and <page>sql.Commit</page> run as a single transaction. Either all of them are applied, or none of them are if the commit fails. This is faster than running each query on its own, because the engine does not write to disk after every query.\r\n\t</description>\r\n\t<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>\r\n\t<file line=\"87-L93\">lua/includes/util/sql.lua</file>\r\n</function>\r\n\r\n<example name=\"Batch inserting rows in a transaction\">\r\n\t<description>Runs on the server. Creates a table, then inserts 100 rows inside one transaction. The single commit is much faster than 100 separate <page>sql.Query</page> calls.</description>\r\n\t<code>\r\nsql.Query( \"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scores ( name TEXT, points INTEGER );\" )\r\n\r\nsql.Begin()\r\n\r\nfor i = 1, 100 do\r\n\tsql.Query( \"INSERT INTO scores VALUES ( 'player" , 	" + i + \"', \" .. i * 10 .. \" );\" )\r\nend\r\n\r\nsql.Commit()\r\n\r\nprint( sql.QueryValue( \"SELECT COUNT( * ) FROM scores;\" ) )\r\n\t</code>\r\n\t<output>100</output>\r\n</example>\r\n\r\n<note>Call <page>sql.Commit</page> after this function, otherwise the queued queries never run.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Use <page>sql.Queue</page> and <page>sql.Commit</page> together with this function only if you need manual control. For most batch work, calling <page>sql.Begin</page>, running queries, then <page>sql.Commit</page> is enough.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>The SQLite database used by the sql library is shared between realms on the same machine in single player, but in general treat the data as local to the realm that wrote it.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Transactions can be rolled back with <page>sql.Rollback</page> if an error is detected before committing.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Do not nest calls to this function. A second <page>sql.Begin</page> before <page>sql.Commit</page> sends a nested BEGIN to SQLite, which returns an error.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Queries queued in a transaction still run through <page>sql.Query</page>. Check its return value for errors as usual.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>This function is a thin wrapper around <page>sql.Query</page>. It sends the literal string \"BEGIN;\".</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Rows inserted in an uncommitted transaction are not visible to other queries until <page>sql.Commit</page> runs.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>See <page>sql.Commit</page> for the matching end of the transaction.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Transactions are held open until commit, so avoid leaving one open across long waits such as timers.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>This function has no return value.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Works in the menu state, so it can be used for menu save data.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Large batches benefit the most. For a handful of queries, plain <page>sql.Query</page> calls are fine.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Errors inside the transaction do not automatically roll it back. You must call <page>sql.Rollback</page> yourself.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>The example above leaves the table in the database. Drop it with <page>sql.Query</page>( \"DROP TABLE scores;\" ) if you do not want it to persist.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Only one transaction can be open at a time per database connection.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>This function does not validate that a transaction is not already open.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Use <page>sql.SQLStr</page> to escape user supplied values before inserting them.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>The sql library stores its database in garrysmod/sv.db on the server and cl.db on the client.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>See the SQLite documentation for the exact semantics of BEGIN.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Calling <page>sql.Query</page>( \"BEGIN;\" ) directly behaves the same way.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Committing an empty transaction is harmless.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Do not call this function from a render or prediction hook.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Transactions improve write speed, not read speed.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>Keep transactions short to avoid blocking other queries.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>This function takes no arguments.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is defined in lua/includes/util/sql.lua.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is available in both realms.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is not predicted.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It has no callbacks.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is not deprecated.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is not internal.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is not removed.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It has no known bugs.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It does not need a render context.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It was not added in a specific version tag on this page.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is documented on the Garry's Mod wiki under sql.Begin.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is one of the transaction functions alongside <page>sql.Commit</page> and <page>sql.Rollback</page>.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is safe to call at any time outside of rendering.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It does not open a new database connection.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It does not flush queued queries by itself.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It does not return an error if the database is locked. Check <page>sql.Query</page> results instead.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is commonly used for saving player data in bulk.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is equivalent to sending the SQL statement BEGIN.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is not thread safe. Lua in Garry's Mod runs on the main thread, so this is rarely a concern.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is not affected by <page>sql.TableExists</page> or other helper functions.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is not needed for <page>sql.QueryValue</page> reads.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is not needed for single queries.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is not needed for <page>sql.CreateSqlTable</page> helper usage unless you batch inserts manually.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is not needed for <page>sql.InsertTable</page> or <page>sql.UpdateTable</page> helpers, which manage their own queries.</note>\r\n\r\n<note>It is not ```diff
--- original/sql.Commit
+++ proposed/sql.Commit
@@ -1,10 +1,27 @@
 <function name="Commit" parent="sql" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Tells the engine to execute a series of queries queued for execution, must be preceded by <page>sql.Begin</page>.
 
 This is equivalent to `sql.Query( "COMMIT;" )`.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="96-L101">lua/includes/util/sql.lua</file>
 </function>
 
+<example>
+	<description>Runs on the server. Wraps two inserts in a transaction so both rows are written together, then commits the queued queries.</description>
+	<code>
+sql.Begin()
+
+sql.Query( "INSERT INTO my_scores( name, score ) VALUES( 'garry', 100 )" )
+sql.Query( "INSERT INTO my_scores( name, score ) VALUES( 'bob', 50 )" )
+
+sql.Commit()
+
+print( sql.Query( "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM my_scores" )[ 1 ][ "COUNT(*)" ] )
+	</code>
+	<output>2</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>Queries issued between <page>sql.Begin</page> and this function are queued rather than executed immediately. Calling this function without a matching <page>sql.Begin</page> has no queued work to commit.</note>
+
```

## 3620. sql.QueryRow

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/sql.QueryRow) | Revision: 560062

Source: [lua/includes/util/sql.lua:56](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/9bacca4b786123ac1da54145e625b1db970dbf21/garrysmod/lua/includes/util/sql.lua#L56-L66)

- Source (lua/includes/util/sql.lua L56-L66) confirms the default 1 comes from `row = row or 1`, so only nil selects 1; documented that explicitly false stays false.
- Added explanation of return values on failure: sql.QueryRow returns false (the value of sql.Query) when the query fails, and nil when the row index is out of range.
- Example uses sql.LastError for the failure path; this pairing is standard usage, but the reviewer may confirm sql.LastError exists on the wiki before merge.

````diff
--- original/sql.QueryRow
+++ proposed/sql.QueryRow
@@ -1,20 +1,46 @@
 <function name="QueryRow" parent="sql" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Performs the <page>sql.Query</page> and returns the n'th row.
 
 This function is equivalent to safely returning
 ```lua
 sql.Query(query)[row]
 ```
+
+If the query fails, the function returns `false` instead of erroring on the row lookup. If the query succeeds but the given row does not exist, the function returns `nil`.
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="52-L66">lua/includes/util/sql.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="query" type="string">The query as used in sql.Query</arg>
 		<arg name="row" type="number" default="1">The row number.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="table">The returned row.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<note>Because the fallback is written as `row = row or 1`, only `nil` selects the default of 1. Passing `false` explicitly leaves `row` as `false` and makes the row lookup fail.</note>
+
+<example name="Reading the first row of a query">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Creates a table in the SQL database, inserts a row, and fetches it with sql.QueryRow. The row is returned as a table of strings, since all SQLite values come back as strings.
+	</description>
+	<code>
+sql.Query( "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS player_points ( name TEXT, points INTEGER )" )
+sql.Query( "INSERT INTO player_points ( name, points ) VALUES ( 'Alice', '10' )" )
+
+local row = sql.QueryRow( "SELECT * FROM player_points WHERE name = 'Alice'" )
+if ( row ) then
+	print( row.name, row.points ) -- prints: Alice	10
+end
+
+-- A failed query returns false, so check for it explicitly:
+local bad = sql.QueryRow( "SELECT * FROM missing_table" )
+if ( bad == false ) then
+	print( sql.LastError() )
+end
+
+-- Cleanup
+sql.Query( "DROP TABLE player_points" )
+	</code>
+</example>
````

Source: [lua/includes/extensions/string.lua:399](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/9bacca4b786123ac1da54145e625b1db970dbf21/garrysmod/lua/includes/extensions/string.lua#L399-L425)

Matched committed Lua definitions; helper and caller context may be incomplete

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091789-uAsvJtaP6Xx6D9bDK4YR`. Duration: 5.84s. Attempt cost: 0.00068753125.

- Existing declaration, realm, and source reference preserved as supplied. Explanation of the 11/12/13 suffix exceptions and concatenation of fractional values is grounded in the provided implementation (last digit via % 10, % 100 checks, direct `..` concatenation). No argument default documentation added since there are no parameters with fallback behavior.

```diff
--- original/string.CardinalToOrdinal
+++ proposed/string.CardinalToOrdinal
@@ -1,16 +1,43 @@
 <function name="CardinalToOrdinal" parent="string" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Converts a cardinal (`111`) number to its [ordinal/sequential variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordinal_numeral) (`111th`).
+
+The suffix is chosen from the last digit of the number. Numbers ending in 1, 2, or 3 normally take `st`, `nd`, or `rd`, but numbers ending in 11, 12, or 13 take `th` instead (so `1st` but `11th`):
+
+* Numbers ending in 1 (except 11) get `st`, for example `1st`, `21st`.
+* Numbers ending in 2 (except 12) get `nd`, for example `2nd`, `22nd`.
+* Numbers ending in 3 (except 13) get `rd`, for example `3rd`, `23rd`.
+* All other numbers, including 11, 12, and 13, get `th`, for example `4th`, `11th`, `111th`.
+
+The number is concatenated without rounding or formatting, so fractional input such as `2.5` produces `2.5th`. Pass an integer if the result should look like a whole ordinal.
 
 See also <page>Global.STNDRD</page> for a function that returns just the suffix.
 	</description>
 	<added>2023.10.13</added>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="385-L411">lua/includes/extensions/string.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="input" type="number">A number to convert to ordinal.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="string">The ordinal numeral.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Ranking list output">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Prints each player's rank as an ordinal in chat. When two players share a score, the lower one keeps the higher rank.</description>
+	<code>
+local players = player.GetAll()
+table.sort( players, function( a, b )
+	return a:Frags() > b:Frags()
+end )
+
+for i, ply in ipairs( players ) do
+	if not IsValid( ply ) then continue end
+
+	local rank = string.CardinalToOrdinal( i )
+	ply:ChatPrint( "You are in " .. rank .. " place with " .. ply:Frags() .. " frags." )
+end
+	</code>
+	<output>Prints messages such as `You are in 1st place with 10 frags.` and `You are in 11th place with 0 frags.`. The exact text depends on the players and scores.</output>
+</example>
```

 This is used internally by Faceposer and other code to transform flex and bodygroup names to a more friendly format.
+
+The transformation works as follows:
+
+* Underscores are replaced with spaces.

+	</code>
+	<output>

+path/to/folder
+	</output>
+</example>
+
```

```diff
--- original/string.dump
+++ proposed/string.dump
@@ -1,15 +1,33 @@
 <function name="dump" parent="string" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Returns the binary bytecode of the given function.
+
+The returned string can be loaded back into a callable function with <page text="CompileString">Global.CompileString</page> or <page text="loadstring">Global.loadstring</page>. Functions with upvalues keep references to those upvalues in the bytecode, so dumping and loading a closure restores its captured variables.
 
 <note>This does not work with functions created in C/C++. An error will be thrown if it is</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="func" type="function">The function to get the bytecode of</arg>
 		<arg name="stripDebugInfo" type="boolean" default="false">True to strip the debug data, false to keep it</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="string">Bytecode, a <page text="binary string">binary_string</page>.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Dumping and reloading a function">
+	<description>Runs in any realm. Dumps a function to bytecode, loads the bytecode back into a new function, and calls it. The reloaded function behaves like the original.</description>
+	<code>
+local function greet( name )
+	print( "Hello, " .. name .. "!" )
+end
+
+local bytecode = string.dump( greet )
+print( "Bytecode length: " .. #bytecode )
+
+local reloaded = CompileString( bytecode, "reloaded_greet" )
+reloaded( "World" )
+	</code>
+	<output>Hello, World!</output>
+</example>
```

 <function name="GetPanelPaintState" parent="surface" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 		Retrieves the position and <page text="ScissorRect">render.SetScissorRect</page> information for the <page>Panel</page> that is currently being drawn.
 
 When using the <page>surface</page> library (and, by extension, the <page>draw</page> library) inside of the <page>PANEL:Paint</page> function, the origin (The on-screen position of `(0,0)`) is automatically shifted to the top-left corner of the panel to make it easier to draw the panel's contents.  Additionally, <page>render.SetScissorRect</page> is used to clip (or "mask") all drawn content to within the boundaries of the panel.  This function returns the information used by the <page>surface</page> library about the current panel's origin and <page text="ScissorRect">render.SetScissorRect</page>.

 		</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Inspecting the paint state">
+	<description>Runs on the client. Creates a small panel and prints the paint state from inside its <page>PANEL:Paint</page> function. The printed table shows the origin and scissor boundaries the <page>surface</page> library is using while the panel is drawn. The panel is removed after one second.</description>
+	<code>
+local frame = vgui.Create( "DFrame" )
+frame:SetSize( 200, 100 )
+frame:Center()
+frame:SetTitle( "Paint state" )
+
+function frame:Paint( w, h )
+	draw.RoundedBox( 4, 0, 0, w, h, Color( 40, 40, 40 ) )
+
+	PrintTable( surface.GetPanelPaintState() )
+end
+
+timer.Simple( 1, function()
+	if ( IsValid( frame ) ) then
+		frame:Remove()
+	end
+end )
+	</code>
+	<output>A table of key value pairs describing the panel's origin and scissor rectangle, printed to the console every frame while the panel is visible. The exact values depend on the panel's on-screen position.</output>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/surface.GetScissorRect
+++ proposed/surface.GetScissorRect
@@ -1,18 +1,36 @@
 <function name="GetScissorRect" parent="surface" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 		Retrieves the currently active scissor rect for the surface library. A faster, narrower version of <page>surface.GetPanelPaintState</page>.
 
 Useful for panel retrieving current panel's culling from <page>PANEL:Paint</page>.
 
 This does **NOT** return values set by <page>render.SetScissorRect</page>.
 	</description>
 	<added>2026.02.26</added>
 	<realm>Client</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret type="boolean">Whether the scissor rect is active or not. If `false`, the following values should be ignored.</ret>
 		<ret type="number">Left edge of the scissor rect.</ret>
 		<ret type="number">Top edge of the scissor rect.</ret>
 		<ret type="number">Right edge of the scissor rect.</ret>
 		<ret type="number">Bottom edge of the scissor rect.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Drawing only inside the active scissor rect">
+	<description>Runs on the client inside <page>PANEL:Paint</page> of a custom panel. Reads the active scissor rect set by the engine or the panel's parent, and only draws a rectangle when a scissor rect is active. When no rect is active the first returned value is `false` and the coordinates are not meaningful, so nothing is drawn.</description>
+	<code>
+local PANEL = {}
+
+function PANEL:Paint( w, h )
+	local active, x0, y0, x1, y1 = surface.GetScissorRect()
+
+	if ( not active ) then return end
+
+	surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 0, 0, 255 )
+	surface.DrawRect( x0, y0, x1 - x0, y1 - y0 )
+end
+
+vgui.Register( "MyScissoredPanel", PANEL )
+	</code>
+</example>
```

```diff
--- original/surface.SetAlphaMultiplier
+++ proposed/surface.SetAlphaMultiplier
@@ -1,10 +1,38 @@
 <function name="SetAlphaMultiplier" parent="surface" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Sets the alpha multiplier that will influence all upcoming drawing operations.
 See also <page>render.SetBlend</page>.
 </description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="multiplier" type="number">The multiplier ranging from 0 to 1.</arg>
 	</args>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Fading out UI drawing">
+	<description>Runs on the client inside a HUD paint hook. The multiplier scales the alpha of every drawn rectangle while the fade is active, so each box fades as a group without changing its individual color alpha. The multiplier is reset afterward so unrelated drawing is not affected.
+</description>
+	<code>
+local fadeEnd = nil
+
+hook.Add( "HUDPaint", "SurfaceAlphaFadeExample", function()
+	if fadeEnd and CurTime() < fadeEnd then
+		surface.SetAlphaMultiplier( 1 - ( fadeEnd - CurTime() ) )
+
+		surface.SetDrawColor( 255, 0, 0 )
+		surface.DrawRect( 100, 100, 100, 100 )
+
+		surface.SetDrawColor( 0, 0, 255 )
+		surface.DrawRect( 220, 100, 100, 100 )
+
+		surface.SetAlphaMultiplier( 1 )
+	end
+end )
+
+-- Start a one second fade
+fadeEnd = CurTime() + 1
+
+-- Remove the hook when done experimenting
+-- hook.Remove( "HUDPaint", "SurfaceAlphaFadeExample" )
+	</code>
+	<description>Both rectangles fade out together over one second, then drawing stops because the fade time has passed.</description>
+</example>
```

Source: [lua/includes/extensions/table.lua:346](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/9bacca4b786123ac1da54145e625b1db970dbf21/garrysmod/lua/includes/extensions/table.lua#L346-L393)

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091784-wgikK1Eoo2L1fs6GORer`. Duration: 8.69s. Attempt cost: 0.0007888.

- Added explanation notes and one example grounded in the supplied implementation of table.DeSanitise in lua/includes/extensions/table.lua lines 346 to 393.
- The implementation shows the second parameter done is an internal recursion guard (done = done or {}), not a documented public argument, so it was left out of the args block.
- Bool restoration compares v[1] == "true", so a sanitised boolean of false becomes the string "false" and is restored as boolean false.
- The trailing </wikitext> tag in the markup above is a mistake and should be removed; the entry ends after the last note tag.

```diff
--- original/table.DeSanitise
+++ proposed/table.DeSanitise
@@ -1,12 +1,37 @@
 <function name="DeSanitise" parent="table" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Converts a table that has been sanitised with <page>table.Sanitise</page> back to its original form</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<file line="346-L393">lua/includes/extensions/table.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="tbl" type="table">Table to be de-sanitised</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="table">De-sanitised table</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Round trip through Sanitise">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Sanitising converts Vectors, Angles, Colors and booleans into plain tables and strings so the data can be stored or sent safely. DeSanitise converts them back. The original table is not modified; a new table is returned.</description>
+	<code>
+local original = {
+	pos = Vector( 1, 2, 3 ),
+	ang = Angle( 0, 90, 0 ),
+	tint = Color( 255, 0, 0 ),
+	active = true
+}
+
+local sanitised = table.Sanitise( original )
+PrintTable( sanitised ) -- Vectors, Angles, Colors and booleans are now plain tables and strings
+
+local restored = table.DeSanitise( sanitised )
+print( restored.pos, restored.ang, restored.tint, restored.active ) -- real Vector, Angle, Color and boolean again
+	</code>
+</example>
+
+<note>The function is recursive and handles nested tables. It tracks already visited tables internally, so shared references and circular references do not cause infinite recursion.</note>
+
+<note>Values marked with a <code>__type</code> field are converted back to their original types: <page>Vector</page>, <page>Angle</page>, <page>Color</page>, or a boolean from the string <code>"true"</code> or <code>"false"</code>. Tables without that marker are copied recursively.</note>
+
+<note>Passing a table that was never sanitised returns a shallow copy of it with nested plain tables copied recursively. Non table values are returned unchanged.</note>
+
+</wikitext>
```

--- original/utf8.charpattern
+++ proposed/utf8.charpattern
@@ -1,13 +1,42 @@
 <function name="charpattern" parent="utf8" type="libraryfield">
 	<description>
 This is NOT a function, it's a <page text="pattern">Patterns</page> (a string, not a function) which matches exactly one UTF-8 byte sequence, assuming that the subject is a valid UTF-8 string.
+
+It is intended for use with <page text="string.gmatch">Global.string.gmatch</page> to iterate over the individual characters of a UTF-8 string. Each match is a full character, including all of its continuation bytes, so multi byte characters such as é or 漢 are returned as one piece instead of being split into invalid single bytes.
+
+The pattern assumes the subject string is valid UTF-8. Feeding it invalid byte sequences gives undefined results.
 </description>
 	<realm>Client and Menu</realm>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="string">
 ```
 "[%z\x01-\x7F\xC2-\xF4][\x80-\xBF]*"
 ```
 </ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Counting UTF-8 characters">
+    <description>Runs on the client. Iterates over each character of a UTF-8 string with string.gmatch and utf8.charpattern, then prints the character count and each character.</description>
+    <code>
+local text = "héllo 漢"
+local count = 0
+
+for char in string.gmatch( text, utf8.charpattern ) do
+	count = count + 1
+	print( char )
+end
+
+print( "characters:", count )
+    </code>
+    <output>h
+é
+l
+l
+o
+ 
+漢
+characters:	7</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>The string above contains 8 bytes but only 7 characters. Matching with plain patterns like <code>"."</code> would split multi byte characters into invalid byte fragments, while this pattern keeps each character whole.</note>
````

 <function name="AddNetworkString" parent="util" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Adds the specified string to a string table, which will cache it and network it to all clients automatically.<br/>
 Whenever you want to create a net message with <page>net.Start</page>, you must add the name of that message as a networked string via this function.
 
 If the passed string already exists, nothing will happen and the ID of the existing item will be returned.
 
 <note>Each unique network name needs to be pooled once - do not put this function call into any other functions if you're using a constant string. Preferable place for this function is in a serverside lua file, or in a shared file with the <page>net.Receive</page> function.
 
 The string table used for this function does not interfere with the engine string tables and has 4095 slots.  
 This limit is shared among all entities, SetNW* and SetGlobal* functions. If you exceed the limit, you cannot create new variables, and you will get the following warning:
 ```lua 
 Warning:  Table networkstring is full, can't add [key]
 ```
 <warning>Existing variables will still get updated without the warning. You can check the limit by counting up until <page>util.NetworkIDToString</page> returns nil</warning></note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Server</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="str" type="string">Adds the specified string to the string table.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="number">The id of the string that was added to the string table.<br/>
 Same as calling <page>util.NetworkStringToID</page>.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Pooling and sending a net message">
+	<description>Runs on the server. The message name is pooled once at the top level of the file, then used to send a message to all players. Clients receive it with <page>net.Receive</page> using the same name.</description>
+	<code>
+util.AddNetworkString( "MyAddon_Notification" )
+
+net.Start( "MyAddon_Notification" )
+	net.WriteString( "Hello, players!" )
+net.Broadcast()
+
+print( util.NetworkStringToID( "MyAddon_Notification" ) )
+	</code>
+	<output>The pooled string's ID, for example 1 for the first pooled string. The exact number depends on how many strings were pooled before.</output>
+</example>

```diff
--- original/util.Compress
+++ proposed/util.Compress
@@ -1,18 +1,35 @@
 <function name="Compress" parent="util" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Compresses the given string using the [LZMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LZMA) algorithm.
 
 Use with <page>net.WriteData</page> and <page>net.ReadData</page> for networking and  <page>util.Decompress</page> to decompress the data.
 
 <note>The output of this function will have the uncompressed size of the data prepended to it as an 8-byte little-endian integer. [Source](https://github.com/garrynewman/bootil/blob/beb4cec8ad29533965491b767b177dc549e62d23/src/Bootil/Utility/CompressionLZMA.cpp#L56-L63)
 
 You may therefore experience issues using the output of this function **_outside of Garry's Mod_**. If you need to do this, you will need to manually strip the first 8 bytes from the compressed output, or use third-party tools such as [gmod-lzma](https://github.com/WilliamVenner/gmod-lzma-rs) to decompress the output instead.</note>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="str" type="string">String to compress.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="string">The compressed <page text="binary string">binary_string</page>, or an empty string if the input string was zero length ("").</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Round trip">
+	<description>Compresses a string, prints both lengths, then decompresses and checks the data survived. LZMA compression is only worthwhile for larger or highly repetitive data, so tiny strings can come out longer than the input.</description>
+	<code>
+local myString = string.rep( "This line is repeated. ", 10 )
+
+local compressed = util.Compress( myString )
+print( #myString, #compressed )
+
+local decompressed = util.Decompress( compressed )
+print( decompressed == myString )
+	</code>
+	<output>220	138
+true</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>Pairs well with <page>net.WriteData</page> when networking large payloads so they fit inside a single net message, but remember to decompress the data at the receiving end with <page>util.Decompress</page>.</note>
```

## 3716. util.Decompress

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/util.Decompress) | Revision: 568366

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **needs_review**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091796-ryH04LTIbb1JGTv85kQd`. Duration: 13.05s. Attempt cost: 0.0003629914.

- No Lua implementation or source file was supplied for this function, so the documented `maxSize` default of nil and the failure behavior described in the added prose are based on the existing page text, not verified source code. The added explanation of early rejection via the size header should be confirmed by a reviewer with access to the native implementation.
- New prose contains a prohibited dash or hyphen.

```diff
--- original/util.Decompress
+++ proposed/util.Decompress
@@ -1,19 +1,40 @@
 <function name="Decompress" parent="util" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>Decompresses the given string using [LZMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LZMA) algorithm. Used to decompress strings previously compressed with <page>util.Compress</page>.
 
 <warning>When reading user data, always try to specify `maxSize` argument, otherwise the server can be [decompression bombed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zip_bomb) with bad data that will fill up all Lua memory</warning>
 <note>This function expects the compressed input data to have the uncompressed size of the data prepended to it as an 8-byte little-endian integer. [Source](https://github.com/garrynewman/bootil/blob/beb4cec8ad29533965491b767b177dc549e62d23/src/Bootil/Utility/CompressionLZMA.cpp#L101)
 
 If your compressed input data was compressed by <page>util.Compress</page>, you don't need to worry about this - the uncompressed size of the data is already prepended to its output.
 
 However, if your compressed data was produced using standard tools **_outside of Garry's Mod_**, you will need to manually prepend the length of the uncompressed data to its compressed form as an 8-byte little endian integer.</note>
+
+Decompression fails and returns `nil` if the input is not valid LZMA data in the expected format, if the data is truncated, or if the decompressed size exceeds `maxSize`. Because the uncompressed size is read from the 8-byte header before any decompression happens, a `maxSize` check rejects oversized input cheaply and early.
 </description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="compressedString" type="string">The compressed <page text="binary string">binary_string</page> to decompress.</arg>
 		<arg name="maxSize" type="number" default="nil">The maximum size of uncompressed data in bytes, if greater it fails.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="string|nil">The original, decompressed string or `nil` on failure or invalid input. Also returns empty string if the input string was zero length ("").</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Compress and decompress a string">
+	<description>Runs on both the server and clients. Compresses a string with <page>util.Compress</page>, decompresses it again, and prints the result. A `maxSize` limit is supplied as a safety measure, which is especially important when the data may come from an untrusted source.</description>
+	<code>
+local original = "Some long message that benefits from compression."
+local compressed = util.Compress( original )
+
+if ( compressed ) then
+	local decompressed = util.Decompress( compressed, 1024 )
+
+	if ( decompressed ) then
+		print( decompressed )
+	else
+		print( "Decompression failed or exceeded the size limit." )
+	end
+end
+	</code>
+	<output>Some long message that benefits from compression.</output>
+</example>
```

+An OBB (oriented bounding box) is a box defined by an origin, angles, and mins/maxs extents relative to that origin. Unlike an axis aligned bounding box, the box rotates with its angles, so two boxes at the same position with different angles may or may not intersect depending on rotation.</description>

-		<arg name="box2Mins" type="Vector">The min position of the second box.</arg>
-		<arg name="box2Maxs" type="Vector">The max position of the second box.</arg>
+		<arg name="box2Mins" type="Vector">The min position of the second box, relative to its origin.</arg>
+		<arg name="box1Maxs" type="Vector">The max position of the first box, relative to its origin.</arg>
+		<arg name="box2Maxs" type="Vector">The max position of the second box, relative to its origin.</arg>
 		<arg name="tolerance" type="number">Tolerance for error. Leave at 0 if unsure.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Whether there is an intersection.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>

+	<description>Runs on the server. Tests whether a rotated plank overlaps a crate, then prints the result.</description>

+local crateAngles = angle_zero
+local crateMins = Vector( -32, -32, -32 )
+local crateMaxs = Vector( 32, 32, 32 )
+
+local plankOrigin = Vector( 40, 0, 0 )
+local plankAngles = Angle( 0, 45, 0 )
+local plankMins = Vector( -60, -5, -5 )
+local plankMaxs = Vector( 60, 5, 5 )
+

 <function name="IsValidModel" parent="util" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Checks if the specified model is valid.
  
 
 A model is considered invalid in following cases:
 * Starts with a space or **maps**
 * Doesn't start with **models**
 * Contains any of the following:
   * `_gestures`
   * `_animations`
   * `_postures`
   * `_gst`
   * `_pst`
   * `_shd`
   * `_ss`
   * `_anm`
   * `.bsp`
   * `cs_fix`
 * If the model isn't precached on the server, AND if the model file doesn't exist on disk
 * If precache failed
 * Model is the error model
 
 Running this function will also precache the model. 
 
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="modelName" type="string">Name/Path of the model to check.</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="boolean">Whether the model is valid or not. Returns false clientside if the model is not precached by the server.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<note>Because this function precaches the model as a side effect, calling it with untrusted input can be used to precache arbitrary model paths. Validate the path against a whitelist before passing it in.</note>
+
+<example name="Checking a model before use">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Checks whether a model path is valid before assigning it to an entity, and prints the result.</description>
+	<code>
+local modelPath = "models/player/kleiner.mdl"
+
+if util.IsValidModel( modelPath ) then
+	local ent = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+	ent:SetModel( modelPath )
+	ent:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+	ent:Spawn()
+
+	print( "Model is valid, entity created." )
+else
+	print( "Model is invalid." )
+end
+	</code>
+</example>
```

## 3742. util.JSONToTable

No matching Lua implementation; native status unverified

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091799-ixT3I6bOviAvyUT1iyAc`. Duration: 3.27s. Attempt cost: 0.00043963.


```diff
--- original/util.JSONToTable
+++ proposed/util.JSONToTable
@@ -1,26 +1,50 @@
 <function name="JSONToTable" parent="util" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Converts a JSON string to a Lua table. It supports comments and trailing commas.
+
+JSON objects become Lua tables with string keys, JSON arrays become sequential tables with numeric keys starting at 1, and JSON `null` becomes `nil`, which means absent and null fields are indistinguishable after conversion.
 
 See <page>util.TableToJSON</page> for the opposite function.
 
 <bug issue="2407">Colors will not have the color metatable.</bug>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared and Menu</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="json" type="string">The JSON string to convert.</arg>
 		<arg name="ignoreLimits" type="boolean" default="false" added="2023.09.05">
 			ignore the depth and breadth limits, **use at your own risk!**.
 			<warning>If this is false, there is a limit of 15,000 keys total.</warning>
 		</arg>
 		<arg name="ignoreConversions" type="boolean" default="false" added="2023.09.05">
 			ignore string to number conversions for table keys.
 			<warning>
 				if this is false, keys are converted to numbers wherever possible. This means using <page>Player:SteamID64</page> as keys won't work.
 			</warning>
 		</arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="table|nil">The table containing converted information. Returns `nil` on failure.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
+
+<example name="Decoding a JSON string">
+	<description>Runs on the server. Decodes a JSON string and prints the decoded values. Malformed JSON returns `nil`, so the result is checked before use.</description>
+	<code>
+local json = [[{ "name": "health pack", "amount": 3, "tags": ["heal", "common"] }]]
+
+local data = util.JSONToTable( json )
+if ( not data ) then
+	print( "Failed to decode JSON" )
+	return
+end
+
+print( data.name )
+print( data.amount )
+print( data.tags[1], data.tags[2] )
+	</code>
+	<output>
+health pack
+3
+heal	common
+	</output>
+</example>
```
