- Existing default attribute for bone (0) is confirmed by the source: `bone = bone or 0` in lua/includes/extensions/util.lua. Note that explicit false also selects 0 under this fallback, while 0 itself is truthy and unchanged; documented in a note.
- Example output is approximate and derived from the rotation math, not from execution.

```diff
--- original/util.LocalToWorld
+++ proposed/util.LocalToWorld
@@ -1,24 +1,45 @@
 <function name="LocalToWorld" parent="util" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 A convenience function around LocalToWorld-related functions.
 
+Converts a vector from the entity's local space to world space. If the physics object matching the `bone` argument is valid, the conversion uses that physics object's position and angles. Otherwise the entity's own position and angles are used. This makes the function useful for ragdolls and other multi bone entities, where individual physics objects can move independently of the entity origin.
+
 <note>If <page>Entity:EntIndex</page> returns `0`, the function will return the passed `lpos`.</note>
+<note>The `bone` argument defaults to `0` through a `bone = bone or 0` fallback. Because `0` is truthy in Lua, passing `0` explicitly behaves the same as omitting the argument.</note>
 </description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<file line="76-L95">lua/includes/extensions/util.lua</file>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="ent" type="Entity">The entity to take.</arg>
 		<arg name="lpos" type="Vector">A local space vector.</arg>
 		<arg name="bone" type="number" default="0">
 Actually to be treated as the number corresponding to a specific <page>PhysObj</page> of the entity.
 
 If that specific physics object is valid, then <page>PhysObj:LocalToWorld</page> is used.
 
 Otherwise, <page>Entity:LocalToWorld</page>.
 </arg>
 	</args>
 	<rets>
 		<ret name="" type="Vector">The corresponding worldspace vector.</ret>
 	</rets>
 </function>
 
+<example name="Tracking a point on a prop">
+    <description>Runs on the server. Spawns a wooden crate, rotates it, and prints the world position of a point 10 units in front of, 10 units above, and 10 units to the right of the crate's origin. The crate is removed afterwards.</description>
+    <code>
+local crate = ents.Create( "prop_physics" )
+crate:SetModel( "models/props_junk/wood_crate001a.mdl" )
+crate:SetPos( Vector( 0, 0, 100 ) )
+crate:SetAngles( Angle( 0, 90, 0 ) )
+crate:Spawn()
+
+local lpos = Vector( 10, 10, 10 )
+local wpos = util.LocalToWorld( crate, lpos )
+
+print( wpos )
+
+crate:Remove()
+    </code>
+    <output>Because the crate is yawed 90 degrees, the local X offset appears along the world Y axis. The printed vector is roughly ( -10, 10, 110 ), shifted by the crate's position and orientation.</output>
+</example>
```

```diff
-	<description>Returns the networked string associated with the given ID from the string table.</description>
+	<description>Returns the networked string associated with the given ID from the string table.
+
+Strings are added to the string table with <page>Global.util.AddNetworkString</page>. The table is shared between the server and all clients, so the same ID maps to the same string on both realms. This is mostly useful for debugging network messages, since network names are transmitted as these IDs.</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>
 	<args>
 		<arg name="stringTableID" type="number">ID to get the associated string from.</arg>

+	<code>
+util.AddNetworkString( "MyCustomMessage" )
+
+-- Find the ID by looping the string table with util.NetworkIDToString's counterpart
+for id = 0, 512 do
+	local name = util.NetworkIDToString( id )
+	if name == "MyCustomMessage" then
+		print( "MyCustomMessage has ID " .. id )
+		-- Prints the name again from the ID

+		break
+	end
+end
+	</code>

+MyCustomMessage</output>
+</example>
+
+<note>The exact ID for a given string is not fixed. It depends on the order strings are added, so never hardcode IDs. Always look them up or send them over the network when needed.</note>
```

## 3783. weapons.Register

[Wiki page](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/weapons.Register) | Revision: 568346

Source: [lua/includes/modules/weapons.lua:46](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/9bacca4b786123ac1da54145e625b1db970dbf21/garrysmod/lua/includes/modules/weapons.lua#L46-L109)

Matched committed Lua definitions; helper and caller context may be incomplete

Status: **ready**. Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`. Request: `gen-1792091812-0lGbPF0LDwnEO33UO4X7`. Duration: 6.64s. Attempt cost: 0.00074693.

- Added explanation of registration behavior (PreRegisterSWEP hook, ClassNameOverride, spawnmenu list entry, duplicator, reload refresh) directly from the supplied source in lua/includes/modules/weapons.lua lines 46 to 109.
- The example uses a minimal SWEP table with common fields; the exact required fields for a working weapon are documented on Structures/SWEP, which was not supplied, so the example should be checked against that page.
- The source file line range in the existing markup is 46-L106 while the supplied source spans lines 46 to 109; the existing file tag was preserved unchanged.

```diff
--- original/weapons.Register
+++ proposed/weapons.Register
@@ -1,19 +1,60 @@
 <function name="Register" parent="weapons" type="libraryfunc">
 	<description>
 Registers a Scripted Weapon (SWEP) class manually. When the engine spawns an entity, weapons registered with this function will be created if the class names match.
 
 See also <page>scripted_ents.Register</page> for Scripted Entities (SENTs)
+
+The registration does the following:
+
+* Runs the <page>PreRegisterSWEP</page> hook. If any hook returns `false`, the weapon is not registered.
+* If the SWEP table contains a string `ClassNameOverride`, that value is used as the classname instead of the second argument.
+* Stores the table in the weapon list and sets its `ClassName` field to the classname.
+* Adds an entry to the `Weapon` spawnmenu list so the weapon appears in the spawnmenu, using the table's `PrintName`, `Category`, `Spawnable`, `AdminOnly`, `ScriptedEntityType`, `IconOverride` and `SubCategory` fields. `PrintName` falls back to the classname and `Category` falls back to `#spawnmenu.category.other`.
+* Allows the weapon to be duplicated with the duplicator, unless the table sets `DisableDuplicator` to true.
+* If a weapon with the same classname was already registered, existing entities of that class are refreshed with the new table and derived classes are updated. Each affected entity has its `OnReloaded` method called if it has one.
 
 <bug pull="1300">Sub-tables provided in the first argument will not carry over their metatable, and will receive a BaseClass key if the table was merged with the base's. Userdata references, which includes Vectors, Angles, Entities, etc. will not be copied.</bug>
 	</description>
 	<realm>Shared</realm>

+<example name="Registering a simple SWEP">
+	<description>Registers a minimal scripted weapon on the server. Run this code once at load time, for example from a file in `lua/weapons/` or an autorun script. The weapon then appears in the spawnmenu under the given category and can be spawned and fired.</description>

+		Damage = 10

+
```
